sentences.zh: 列傳二百七十一

translations.literal: Biographies 271
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 271

sentences.zh: 文苑一

translations.literal: Literary Grove 1
translations.idiomatic: Literary Figures 1

sentences.zh: 魏禧侯方域申涵光吳嘉紀錢謙益吳偉業宋琬施閏章王士祿陳恭尹馮班胡承諾阿什垣汪琬計東彭孫遹朱彝尊尤侗陳維崧潘耒徐嘉炎萬斯同劉獻廷邵遠平喬萊陸葇龐塏陸圻孫枝蔚丁煒黃與堅吳雯梅清馮景姜宸英性德文昭趙執信黃儀查慎行史申義顧陳垿何焯戴名世

translations.literal: Wei Xi, Hou Fangyu, Shen Hanguang, Wu Jiaji, Qian Qianyi, Wu Weiye, Song Wan, Shi Runzhang, Wang Shilu, Chen Gongyin, Feng Ban, Hu Chengnuo, A Shen Yuan, Wang Wan, Ji Dong, Peng Sunyu, Zhu Yizun, You Dong, Chen Weisong, Pan Lei, Xu Jiayan, Wan Sitong, Liu Xianting, Shao Yuanping, Qiao Lai, Lu Rou, Pang Kai, Lu Qi, Sun Zhiwei, Ding Wei, Huang Yujian, Wu Wen, Mei Qing, Feng Jing, Jiang Chenying, Xingde, Wenzhao, Zhao Zhixin, Huang Yi, Cha Shenxing, Shi Shenyi, Gu Chenxu, He Chao, Dai Mingshi
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xi, Hou Fangyu, Shen Hanguang, Wu Jiaji, Qian Qianyi, Wu Weiye, Song Wan, Shi Runzhang, Wang Shilu, Chen Gongyin, Feng Ban, Hu Chengnuo, A Shen Yuan, Wang Wan, Ji Dong, Peng Sunyu, Zhu Yizun, You Dong, Chen Weisong, Pan Lei, Xu Jiayan, Wan Sitong, Liu Xianting, Shao Yuanping, Qiao Lai, Lu Rou, Pang Kai, Lu Qi, Sun Zhiwei, Ding Wei, Huang Yujian, Wu Wen, Mei Qing, Feng Jing, Jiang Chenying, Xingde, Wenzhao, Zhao Zhixin, Huang Yi, Cha Shenxing, Shi Shenyi, Gu Chenxu, He Chao, and Dai Mingshi

sentences.zh: 清代學術，超漢越宋。

translations.literal: Qing dynasty learning surpassed the Han and exceeded the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Qing scholarship surpassed that of the Han and exceeded that of the Song.

sentences.zh: 論者至欲特立「清學」之名，而文學並重，亦足於漢、唐、宋、明以外別樹一宗，嗚呼盛已！

translations.literal: Commentators even wished to establish the separate name "Qing Learning," and with literature equally esteemed, it was enough to set up a distinct school apart from Han, Tang, Song, and Ming—alas, how flourishing it was!
translations.idiomatic: Some scholars went so far as to propose a distinct label of "Qing Learning," and with literature held in equal regard, Qing culture could well stand as a separate tradition alongside those of the Han, Tang, Song, and Ming—what an age of brilliance!

sentences.zh: 明末文衰甚矣！

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming, literature had declined greatly!
translations.idiomatic: By the late Ming, letters had fallen into deep decline!

sentences.zh: 清運既興，文氣亦隨之而一振。

translations.literal: Once the Qing fortune arose, the literary spirit also revived with it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing dynasty rose, the literary spirit revived in turn.

sentences.zh: 謙益歸命，以詩文雄於時，足負起衰之責；

translations.literal: Qianyi submitted to the new order and, with his poetry and prose dominant in the age, was fully able to bear the responsibility of reviving a fallen tradition;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qianyi submitted to the new regime and towered over his age in poetry and prose, bearing the burden of reviving a fallen literary tradition;

sentences.zh: 而魏、侯、申、吳，山林遺逸，隱與推移，亦開風氣之先。

translations.literal: while Wei, Hou, Shen, and Wu, recluses of mountain and forest, quietly moved with the times and also opened the way for new trends.
translations.idiomatic: while Wei Xi, Hou Fangyu, Shen Hanguang, and Wu Jiaji, recluses dwelling in the hills, quietly moved with the changing times and helped open the new literary climate.

sentences.zh: 康、乾盛治，文教大昌。

translations.literal: Under the flourishing rule of Kangxi and Qianlong, culture and education greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Under the prosperous reigns of Kangxi and Qianlong, culture and learning flourished as never before.

sentences.zh: 聖主賢臣，莫不以提倡文化為己任。

translations.literal: Sage rulers and worthy ministers all took the promotion of culture as their own duty.
translations.idiomatic: Sage emperors and capable ministers alike made the advancement of culture their personal charge.

sentences.zh: 師儒崛起，尤盛一時。

translations.literal: Master-scholars rose up, especially flourishing for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Men of letters and learning rose in great numbers, reaching a peak unrivaled in their day.

sentences.zh: 自王、朱以及方、惲，各擅其勝。

translations.literal: From Wang and Zhu to Fang and Yun, each excelled in his own strength.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Shilu and Zhu Yizun to Fang Bao and Yun Jing, each mastered his own field of excellence.

sentences.zh: 文運盛衰，實通世運。

translations.literal: The rise and fall of literary fortune in fact corresponds to the fortune of the age.
translations.idiomatic: The fortunes of literature rise and fall in step with those of the dynasty itself.

sentences.zh: 此當舉其全體，若必執一人一地言之，轉失之隘，豈定論哉？

translations.literal: This should be discussed as a whole; if one insists on speaking of a single person or place, one instead becomes narrow—is that a settled judgment?
translations.idiomatic: Such matters must be judged as a whole; to fix on one figure or one region alone is to take too narrow a view—how could that be a final verdict?

sentences.zh: 道、咸多故，文體日變。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns there were many troubles, and literary forms changed day by day.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang and Xianfeng reigns, amid constant upheaval, literary styles changed by the day.

sentences.zh: 龔、魏之徒，乘時立說。

translations.literal: Men such as Gong and Wei seized the moment to set forth their doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Figures such as Gong Zizhen and Wei Yuan seized the moment to advance new doctrines.

sentences.zh: 同治中興，文風又起。

translations.literal: In the Tongzhi revival, literary style rose again.
translations.idiomatic: With the Tongzhi revival, literary culture flourished once more.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓立言有體，濟以德功，實集其大成。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan established words with proper form, complemented by virtue and achievement, and in truth gathered their great completion.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan wrote with disciplined form and backed his words with moral stature and practical achievement, bringing the tradition to its fullest expression.

sentences.zh: 光、宣以後，支離龐雜，不足言文久矣。

translations.literal: After Guangxu and Xuantong, writing became fragmented and sprawling, and has long been unworthy of being called literature.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guangxu and Xuantong reigns, letters grew fragmented and chaotic, and have scarcely deserved the name of literature for some time.

sentences.zh: 茲為文苑傳，但取詩文有各能自成家者，彙為一編，以著有清一代文學之盛。

translations.literal: This Literary Grove biography takes only those whose poetry and prose each could form a school of their own, gathers them in one compilation, and thereby records the flourishing of Qing literature for a generation.
translations.idiomatic: This Literary Figures chapter selects only those poets and prose writers who each established a distinctive voice of their own, gathering them in one volume to show the brilliance of Qing letters.

sentences.zh: 派別異同，皆置勿論。

translations.literal: Differences and similarities among schools are all set aside and not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Questions of literary faction and affiliation are deliberately left aside.

sentences.zh: 其已見大臣及儒林各傳者，則不復著焉。

translations.literal: Those already appearing in the biographies of great ministers and the Confucian scholars are not recorded again here.
translations.idiomatic: Those already treated in the biographies of eminent officials and Confucian scholars are not included again here.

sentences.zh: 魏禧，字冰叔，寧都人。

translations.literal: Wei Xi, styled Bingshu, was a native of Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xi, courtesy name Bingshu, was a native of Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 父兆鳳，諸生。

translations.literal: His father Zhao Feng was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao Feng was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 明亡，號哭不食，翦發為頭陀，隱居翠微峰。

translations.literal: When the Ming fell, he wailed and refused food, cut his hair to become a Buddhist mendicant, and retired to Cuiwei Peak.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell, he wailed and refused to eat, shaved his head to become a Buddhist mendicant, and withdrew to Cuiwei Peak.

sentences.zh: 是冬，筮離之乾，遂名其堂為易堂。

translations.literal: That winter, divining the hexagram Li changing to Qian, he therefore named his hall the Hall of Change.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, having divined the hexagram Li changing into Qian, he named his hall the Hall of Change.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 禧兒時嗜古，論史斬斬見識議。

translations.literal: From childhood Xi loved antiquity, and in discussing history he showed sharp insight and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Xi was devoted to antiquity, and when he discussed history his judgments were sharp and incisive.

sentences.zh: 年十一，補縣學生。

translations.literal: At age eleven he became a supplemental county student.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he enrolled as a supplemental county student.

sentences.zh: 與兄際瑞、弟禮，及南昌彭士望、林時益，同邑李騰蛟、邱維屏、彭任、曾燦等九人為易堂學。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother Jirui, younger brother Li, Peng Shiwang and Lin Shiyi of Nanchang, and fellow townsmen Li Tengjiao, Qiu Weiping, Peng Ren, and Zeng Can—nine men in all—they formed the Hall of Change school.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his elder brother Jirui, his younger brother Li, Peng Shiwang and Lin Shiyi of Nanchang, and fellow townsmen Li Tengjiao, Qiu Weiping, Peng Ren, and Zeng Can—nine men in all—he formed the Hall of Change school.

sentences.zh: 皆躬耕自食，切劘讀書，「三魏」之名遍海內。

translations.literal: All tilled the fields to feed themselves, studied with tireless diligence, and the name of the "Three Weis" spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They all worked their own fields for their livelihood, studied with tireless diligence, and the fame of the "Three Weis" spread across the land.

sentences.zh: 禧束身砥行，才學尤高。

translations.literal: Xi restrained himself and polished his conduct; his talent and learning were especially lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Xi held himself to the strictest standards of conduct, and his talent and learning stood above the rest.

sentences.zh: 門前有池，顏其居曰勺庭，學者稱勺庭先生。

translations.literal: There was a pond before his gate; he inscribed his residence Shao Ting, and scholars called him Master Shao Ting.
translations.idiomatic: A pond lay before his gate, and he named his residence Spoon Court; scholars addressed him as Master Spoon Court.

sentences.zh: 為人形幹修頎，目光射人。

translations.literal: As a man his frame was tall and slender, and his gaze struck people forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and slender in build, with a gaze that seemed to pierce those before him.

sentences.zh: 少善病，參術不去口。

translations.literal: From youth he was prone to illness, and ginseng and atractylodes never left his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was frequently ill and rarely went without ginseng and atractylodes on his lips.

sentences.zh: 性仁厚，寬以接物，不記人過。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and generous, broad-minded in dealing with others, and did not remember people's faults.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was kind and magnanimous, generous in his dealings with others, and never kept account of others' faults.

sentences.zh: 與人以誠，雖見欺，怡如也。

translations.literal: He treated people with sincerity; even when deceived, he remained at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He dealt with others in good faith, and even when deceived remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 然多奇氣，論事每縱橫排奡，倒注不窮。

translations.literal: Yet he possessed much extraordinary spirit; in discussing affairs he always ranged freely and forcefully, pouring forth without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he possessed a bold and unconventional spirit; when discussing affairs he spoke with sweeping force, pouring out argument after argument without end.

sentences.zh: 事會盤錯，指畫灼有經緯。

translations.literal: When affairs were tangled and complex, his plans showed clear method and design.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs grew tangled and complex, his plans showed clear method and design.

sentences.zh: 思患豫防，見幾於蚤，懸策而後驗者十嘗八九。

translations.literal: He thought ahead to prevent trouble, saw the signs early, and of strategies proposed beforehand and later verified, eight or nine out of ten proved true.
translations.idiomatic: He anticipated trouble before it arose, read the signs early, and of the policies he proposed in advance, eight or nine times out of ten events proved him right.

sentences.zh: 流賊起，承平久，人不知兵，且謂寇遠猝難及。

translations.literal: When bandits arose, peace had lasted long; people knew nothing of war and even said the rebels were far away and could not suddenly reach them.
translations.idiomatic: When rebel armies rose, the land had known peace so long that people were ignorant of war and assumed the bandits were too distant to strike suddenly.

sentences.zh: 禧獨憂之，移家山中。

translations.literal: Xi alone was worried and moved his family into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Xi alone was alarmed and moved his family into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 山距城四十里，四面削起百餘丈。

translations.literal: The mountain was forty li from the city; on all sides it rose sheer more than a hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain stood forty li from the city, its cliffs rising sheer on every side more than a hundred zhang high.

sentences.zh: 中徑坼，自山根至頂若斧劈然。

translations.literal: A path split through the middle; from the foot of the mountain to the summit it was as if split by an axe.
translations.idiomatic: A fissure ran straight through it from base to summit, as though the mountain had been cleaved by an axe.

sentences.zh: 緣坼鑿磴道梯而登，因置閘為守望。

translations.literal: Along the fissure they carved steps and ladders to ascend, and set up gates for watch and guard.
translations.idiomatic: They carved steps and ladders along the fissure for ascent and erected gates for watch and defense.

sentences.zh: 士友稍稍依之。

translations.literal: Scholars and friends gradually came to rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and friends gradually gathered there for refuge.

sentences.zh: 後數年，寧都被寇，翠微峰獨完。

translations.literal: Several years later, Ningdu was overrun by bandits, but Cuiwei Peak alone remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later, when Ningdu was overrun by bandits, Cuiwei Peak alone remained unscathed.

sentences.zh: 喜讀史，尤好左氏傳及蘇洵文。

translations.literal: He loved reading history, especially favoring the Zuo Commentary and the writings of Su Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading history, especially the Zuo Commentary and the prose of Su Xun.

sentences.zh: 其為文凌厲雄傑。

translations.literal: His writing was fierce, bold, and heroic.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was fierce, bold, and commanding.

sentences.zh: 遇忠孝節烈事，則益感激，摹畫淋漓。

translations.literal: When encountering matters of loyalty, filial piety, and steadfast integrity, he became all the more moved and depicted them with overflowing emotion.
translations.idiomatic: When treating themes of loyalty, filial devotion, and heroic integrity, he grew all the more impassioned and rendered them with overflowing force.

sentences.zh: 年四十，乃出遊。

translations.literal: At age forty he finally set out on travels.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he finally set out on his travels.

sentences.zh: 於蘇州交徐枋、金俊明，杭州交汪渢，乍浦交李天植，常熟交顧祖禹，常州交惲日初、楊瑀，方外交藥地、槁木，皆遺民也。

translations.literal: In Suzhou he befriended Xu Fang and Jin Junming; in Hangzhou Wang Fen; in Zhapu Li Tianzhi; in Changshu Gu Zuyu; in Changzhou Yun Richu and Yang Yu; among Buddhist monks Yaodi and Gaomu—all loyalists of the fallen dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In Suzhou he befriended Xu Fang and Jin Junming; in Hangzhou, Wang Fen; in Zhapu, Li Tianzhi; in Changshu, Gu Zuyu; in Changzhou, Yun Richu and Yang Yu; among Buddhist monks, Yaodi and Gaomu—all loyalists of the fallen Ming.

sentences.zh: 當是時，南豐謝文洊講學程山，星子宋之盛講學髻山，弟子著錄者皆數十百人，與易堂相應和。

translations.literal: At that time Xie Wenjin of Nanfeng lectured on Cheng Mountain and Song Zhisheng of Xingzi on Ji Mountain; registered disciples numbered in the dozens and hundreds, responding in harmony with the Hall of Change.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xie Wenjin of Nanfeng taught on Cheng Mountain and Song Zhisheng of Xingzi on Ji Mountain, each with dozens or hundreds of registered disciples, their schools answering the spirit of the Hall of Change.

sentences.zh: 易堂獨以古人實學為歸，而風氣之振，由禧為之領袖。

translations.literal: The Hall of Change alone took the practical learning of the ancients as its goal, and the revival of the climate was led by Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Change alone took the practical learning of the ancients as its ideal, and Xi stood at the head of the movement that revived the age.

sentences.zh: 僧無可嘗至山中，歎曰：「易堂真氣，天下無兩矣！」

translations.literal: The monk Wuke once came to the mountain and sighed: "The true spirit of the Hall of Change—under heaven there is no second!"
translations.idiomatic: The monk Wuke once visited the mountain and exclaimed, "The Hall of Change has a vital spirit unmatched anywhere under heaven!"

sentences.zh: 無可，明檢討方以智也。

translations.literal: Wuke was the Ming Hanlin reviewer Fang Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wuke was Fang Yizhi, Hanlin reviewer under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 友人亡，其孤不能自存，禧撫教安業之。

translations.literal: When a friend died and his orphan could not support himself, Xi raised, taught, and settled him in a livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: When a friend died leaving an orphan who could not fend for himself, Xi took the boy in, educated him, and helped him establish a livelihood.

sentences.zh: 凡戚友有難進之言，或處人骨肉間，禧批郤導窾，一言輒解其紛。

translations.literal: Whenever relatives and friends had words difficult to speak, or when mediating between close kin, Xi would pierce the obstruction and guide to the vital point; a single word often resolved the dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever kin or friends faced words too delicate to speak, or when he stood between feuding relatives, Xi would cut to the heart of the matter with a single remark and dissolve the quarrel.

sentences.zh: 或訝之，禧曰：「吾每遇難言事，必積誠累時，待其精神與相貫注，夫然後言。」

translations.literal: When someone expressed surprise, Xi said: "Whenever I encounter matters hard to speak of, I must accumulate sincerity over time and wait until our spirits are fully joined; only then do I speak."
translations.idiomatic: When someone expressed surprise at this, Xi said, "Whenever I face something difficult to say, I must build up sincerity over time and wait until our minds are fully attuned—only then do I speak."

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，詔舉博學鴻儒，禧以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi, an edict summoned men of broad learning and great talent; Xi declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi, when an edict summoned men of broad learning and eminent talent, Xi declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 有司催就道，不得已，舁疾至南昌就醫。

translations.literal: The local officials pressed him to take the road; having no choice, he was carried, ill, to Nanchang to seek medical treatment.
translations.idiomatic: When officials pressed him to set out, he had no choice but to be carried, feigning illness, to Nanchang for medical treatment.

sentences.zh: 巡撫舁驗之，禧蒙被臥稱疾篤，乃放歸。

translations.literal: The governor had him carried in for inspection; Xi lay covered with a quilt claiming grave illness, and was then released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The governor had him brought in for inspection; Xi lay wrapped in quilts claiming grave illness, and was sent home.

sentences.zh: 後二年卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: Two years later he died, at age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died two years later, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 妻謝氏，絕食殉。

translations.literal: His wife, née Xie, starved herself to death in martyrdom.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Xie, starved herself to death in devotion to him.

sentences.zh: 著有文集二十二卷、日錄三卷、詩八卷、左傳經世十卷。

translations.literal: He authored a collected works in twenty-two juan, a daily record in three juan, poetry in eight juan, and Applying the Zuo Commentary to Statecraft in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works include a collected prose in twenty-two juan, a daily record in three juan, poetry in eight juan, and Applying the Zuo Commentary to Statecraft in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 際瑞，原名祥，字善伯，禧兄。

translations.literal: Jirui, originally named Xiang, styled Shanbo, was Xi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Jirui, originally named Xiang, courtesy name Shanbo, was Xi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 明亡後，禧、禮並謝諸生。

translations.literal: After the Ming fell, Xi and Li both resigned their status as licentiates.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Ming, both Xi and Li renounced their status as licentiates.

sentences.zh: 際瑞歎曰：「吾為長子，祖宗祠墓，父母屍饔，將誰責乎？」

translations.literal: Jirui sighed and said: "As the eldest son, the ancestral temples and tombs, my parents' burial and sacrificial offerings—upon whom shall these duties fall?"
translations.idiomatic: Jirui sighed and said, "As the eldest son, who will tend the ancestral temples and tombs, who will see to our parents' burial and sacrificial offerings?"

sentences.zh: 遂出就試。

translations.literal: He therefore went out to take the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: So he went out and entered the examinations.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年歲貢生。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi he became a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi he qualified as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 寧都民亂，贛軍進討，索餉於山砦。

translations.literal: When the people of Ningdu rose in revolt, the Ganzhou army marched to suppress them and demanded supplies from the mountain strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Ningdu rose in revolt, the Ganzhou army marched to suppress them and demanded supplies from the mountain strongholds.

sentences.zh: 際瑞身冒險阻，往來任其事，屢瀕於死。

translations.literal: Jirui personally braved danger and obstruction, going back and forth to handle the matter, repeatedly coming near death.
translations.idiomatic: Jirui personally braved danger and obstruction, going back and forth to handle the matter, repeatedly coming near death.

sentences.zh: 際瑞重信義，翠微峰諸隱者暨族戚倚際瑞為安危者三十餘年。

translations.literal: Jirui valued faith and righteousness; the recluses of Cuiwei Peak and his kinsmen relied on Jirui for their safety and peril for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Jirui was a man of faith and honor; for more than thirty years the recluses of Cuiwei Peak and his kinsmen looked to him for their safety in times of peril.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，滇將韓大任踞贛，當事議撫之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi the Yunnan general Han Daren held Ganzhou, and the authorities discussed pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi the Yunnan general Han Daren held Ganzhou, and the authorities discussed offering him terms of surrender.

sentences.zh: 大任曰：「非魏際瑞至，吾不信也！」

translations.literal: Daren said: "Unless Wei Jirui comes, I will not believe it!"
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren said, "Unless Wei Jirui comes in person, I will not believe a word of it!"

sentences.zh: 時際瑞館總鎮哲爾肯所，遂遣之。

translations.literal: At that time Jirui was lodging with the regional commander Zhe'erken, who therefore dispatched him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jirui was staying with the regional commander Zhe'erken, who sent him on the mission.

sentences.zh: 家人泣勸毋往，際瑞曰：「此鄉邦宗族所關也，吾不行，恐禍及。

translations.literal: His family wept and urged him not to go; Jirui said: "This concerns our homeland and clans; if I do not go, I fear disaster will reach them.
translations.idiomatic: His family wept and begged him not to go. Jirui said, "This concerns our homeland and our clans; if I do not go, I fear disaster will fall on them.

sentences.zh: 行而無成，吾自當之。」

translations.literal: If I go and nothing is achieved, I alone shall bear the responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: If I go and fail, I alone shall bear the blame."

sentences.zh: 遂往。

translations.literal: He therefore went.
translations.idiomatic: And so he went.

sentences.zh: 甫入營。

translations.literal: He had just entered the camp.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely entered the camp

sentences.zh: 官兵遽從東路急攻。

translations.literal: when government troops suddenly launched a swift attack from the eastern route.
translations.idiomatic: when government troops suddenly launched a swift attack from the east.

sentences.zh: 大任疑賣己，因拘留之。

translations.literal: Daren suspected he had been betrayed and therefore detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren suspected he had been betrayed and had him detained.

sentences.zh: 大任變計走降閩，際瑞遂遇害，年五十八。

translations.literal: Daren changed his plan and fled to surrender in Fujian; Jirui was then killed, at age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Han Daren changed his plan and fled to surrender in Fujian; Jirui was killed in the affair, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子世傑殉焉。

translations.literal: His son Shijie died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shijie died with him.

sentences.zh: 際瑞篤治古文，喜漆園、太史公書。

translations.literal: Jirui devoted himself to ancient prose and loved the writings of Master Zhuang and the Grand Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Jirui devoted himself to ancient-style prose and loved the writings of Zhuangzi and Sima Qian.

sentences.zh: 著有文集十卷、五雜俎五卷。

translations.literal: He authored a collected works in ten juan and Miscellaneous Notes in five juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works include a collected prose in ten juan and Miscellaneous Notes in five juan.

sentences.zh: 禮，字和公，禧弟。

translations.literal: Li, styled Hegong, was Xi's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Li, courtesy name Hegong, was Xi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 少魯鈍，受業於禧。

translations.literal: In youth he was dull and slow; he received instruction from Xi.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he seemed slow and dull, and studied under Xi.

sentences.zh: 禧嘗笞詈之，禮弗憾，曰：「兄固愛弟也！」

translations.literal: Xi once beat and scolded him; Li bore no resentment and said: "My elder brother truly loves his younger brother!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi once beat and scolded him, but Li bore no resentment and said, "My elder brother truly loves his younger brother!"

sentences.zh: 禧喜過望。

translations.literal: Xi was delighted beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was delighted beyond all expectation.

sentences.zh: 方九歲，父將析產，持一田券躊躇曰：「與祥，則禮損矣。

translations.literal: When he was nine, his father was about to divide the estate and, holding a land deed, hesitated and said: "If I give it to Xiang, then Li will be shortchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When he was nine, his father was about to divide the family property and, holding a land deed, hesitated. "If I give this to Xiang," he said, "Li will be shortchanged.

sentences.zh: 奈何？」

translations.literal: What is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 禮適在旁，應聲曰：「任損我，毋損伯兄。」

translations.literal: Li happened to be at his side and immediately replied: "Let me bear the loss; do not shortchange my elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: Li, who happened to be nearby, answered at once, "Let me take the loss; do not shortchange my elder brother."

sentences.zh: 父笑曰：「是固魯鈍者耶？」

translations.literal: His father laughed and said: "Is this really the dull one?"
translations.idiomatic: His father laughed and said, "And this is the dull one?"

sentences.zh: 禮寡言，急然諾，喜任難事，以鬱鬱不得志，乃益事遠遊。

translations.literal: Li spoke little, was quick to promise, and liked to take on difficult tasks; because he was depressed at failing to realize his ambitions, he devoted himself all the more to distant travels.
translations.idiomatic: Li spoke little, was quick to keep his word, and liked to take on hard tasks; frustrated in his ambitions, he devoted himself increasingly to long journeys.

sentences.zh: 所至必交其賢豪，物色窮岩遺佚之士。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he sought out the worthy and heroic, searching out recluses in remote cliffs and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went he sought out men of talent and spirit, tracking down recluses in remote hills and valleys.

sentences.zh: 年五十，倦遊返，於翠微左幹之巔構屋五楹。

translations.literal: At age fifty, weary of travel, he returned and built a five-bay house on the summit of Zuogan on the left flank of Cuiwei.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty, weary of travel, he returned and built a five-bay house on the summit of Zuogan on the left flank of Cuiwei.

sentences.zh: 是時伯叔踵逝，石閣、勺庭久虛無人。

translations.literal: At that time his elder and younger uncles died in succession; Shige and Shao Ting had long stood empty with no one there.
translations.idiomatic: By then his uncles had died in succession, and the halls of Stone Pavilion and Spoon Court had long stood empty.

sentences.zh: 諸子各散處，不復居易堂。

translations.literal: The various sons each scattered to live elsewhere and no longer dwelt at the Hall of Change.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers had each gone their separate ways and no longer gathered at the Hall of Change.

sentences.zh: 禮獨身率妻子居十七年，未他徙。

translations.literal: Li alone led his wife and children in residence for seventeen years and did not move elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Li lived there alone with his wife and children for seventeen years and never moved elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 著有詩文集十六卷。

translations.literal: He authored a collected poetry and prose in sixteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected poetry and prose in sixteen juan.

sentences.zh: 子世效、世儼。

translations.literal: His sons were Shi Xiao and Shi Yan.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Shi Xiao and Shi Yan.

sentences.zh: 世效，字昭士。

translations.literal: Shi Xiao, styled Zhaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiao, styled Zhaoshi.

sentences.zh: 生二十餘月，母口授九歌，輒能成誦。

translations.literal: When he was a little over twenty months old, his mother orally taught him the Nine Songs, and he could at once recite them completely.
translations.idiomatic: At barely twenty months old, he could already recite the Nine Songs from memory after his mother taught them to him orally.

sentences.zh: 稍長，從仲父禧讀。

translations.literal: When he grew a little older, he studied under his second uncle Xi.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older, he studied under his second uncle, Wei Xi.

sentences.zh: 性狷急，勇於任事。

translations.literal: By nature he was impatient and narrow-minded, yet bold in taking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was impatient and quick-tempered, but bold in taking on responsibility.

sentences.zh: 禧嘗謂其文一如其人，鋒銳所及，往往有沒羽之力。

translations.literal: Xi once said that his writing was just like the man himself: wherever its sharp edge reached, it often had the force of an arrow buried to the feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Xi once remarked that his writing matched the man—wherever its edge fell, it often struck with the force of an arrow buried to the feathers.

sentences.zh: 以多病不應試。

translations.literal: Because of frequent illness he did not sit for the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Chronic illness kept him from sitting for the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 遍遊燕、楚、吳、越，一至嶺南。

translations.literal: He traveled widely through Yan, Chu, Wu, and Yue, and once went as far as Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled widely through Yan, Chu, Wu, and the Yue regions, and once journeyed as far south as Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 適王士禎使粵，見所作，原折節與交。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Shizhen was on a mission to Guangdong; when he saw Shi Xiao's writings, he willingly lowered himself to befriend him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shizhen was dispatched to Guangdong, he read Shi Xiao's work and willingly set aside his own rank to befriend him.

sentences.zh: 著有耕廡文稿十卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Gengwu Drafts in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Gengwu Drafts in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 世儼，字敬士。

translations.literal: Shi Yan, styled Jingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yan, styled Jingshi.

sentences.zh: 善病如​​其兄，然不廢翰墨。

translations.literal: He was prone to illness like his elder brother, yet he did not abandon brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Like his elder brother, he was often ill, yet he never abandoned his literary pursuits.

sentences.zh: 與世傑、世效時稱「小三魏」。

translations.literal: Together with Shi Jie and Shi Xiao he was at the time called the "Little Three Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Together with Shi Jie and Shi Xiao, he was known at the time as the "Little Three Wei."

sentences.zh: 著有為谷文稿八卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Weigu Drafts in eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Weigu Drafts in eight juan.

sentences.zh: 李騰蛟，字咸齋，亦寧都人。

translations.literal: Li Tengjiao, styled Xianzhai, was also a native of Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tengjiao, styled Xianzhai, was also from Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of licentiate.

sentences.zh: 於易堂中年最長，諸子皆兄事之，嚴敬無敢斁。

translations.literal: Among the members of the Yi Hall he was the eldest in years; all the younger men treated him as an elder brother, with strict reverence and none daring to show disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yi Hall he was the eldest in years, and the younger men all treated him as an elder brother, with such strict reverence that none dared show disrespect.

sentences.zh: 後居三巘峰，以經學教授。

translations.literal: Later he lived on San Yan Peak and taught the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Later he settled on San Yan Peak and made his living teaching the classics.

sentences.zh: 著周易賸言。

translations.literal: He authored Remaining Words on the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Remaining Words on the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 年六十，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of sixty he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 邱維屏，字邦士，寧都人，三魏姊壻也。

translations.literal: Qiu Weiping, styled Bangshi, was a native of Ningdu and the husband of a sister of the Three Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Weiping, styled Bangshi, was from Ningdu and had married a sister of the Three Wei brothers.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: He was a Ming licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a licentiate under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 為人高簡率穆。

translations.literal: As a man he was lofty, spare, straightforward, and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: He was lofty and reserved in manner, plain and dignified in bearing.

sentences.zh: 讀書多玄悟，禧嘗從之學。

translations.literal: In reading he often attained profound insight; Xi once studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: He read with deep intuitive insight, and Wei Xi once studied under him.

sentences.zh: 晚為歷數、易學及泰西算法。

translations.literal: In his later years he took up calendrical studies, the learning of the Changes, and Western mathematics.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned to calendrical science, the Book of Changes, and Western mathematics.

sentences.zh: 僧無可與布算，退語人曰：「此神人也！」

translations.literal: The monk Wuke calculated with him; afterward he withdrew and said to others: "This man is a spirit!"
translations.idiomatic: The monk Wuke worked through calculations with him and, afterward, told others, "This man is a prodigy!"

sentences.zh: 彭士望與維屏交三十餘年，未嘗見其毀一人。

translations.literal: Peng Shiwang was acquainted with Weiping for more than thirty years and never once saw him speak ill of anyone.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shiwang had known Weiping for more than thirty years and never once heard him speak ill of anyone.

sentences.zh: 然維屏獨推服禧，嘗貽禧書曰：「拒諫飾非者大惡也，不拒諫而嘗自拒諫，不飾非而嘗自飾非，尤惡之惡也。

translations.literal: Yet Weiping alone held Xi in deep admiration and once sent Xi a letter saying: "Those who reject remonstrance and gloss over their faults are greatly wicked; those who do not reject remonstrance yet often reject it themselves, and who do not gloss over faults yet often gloss over their own—this is wickedness within wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Weiping alone held Xi in the highest regard and once wrote to him: "To reject remonstrance and cover one's faults is a great evil; but to accept remonstrance in principle yet habitually reject it in practice, and to condemn self-deception yet persistently deceive oneself—that is evil compounded.

sentences.zh: 足下敢於自信，自處有故，而持之以堅，拒諫飾非，蓋有如此者！」

translations.literal: You, sir, dare to trust yourself; you have reasons for how you conduct yourself and hold to them with firmness—rejecting remonstrance and glossing over faults are just such things!"
translations.idiomatic: You dare to trust yourself utterly; you have your reasons for how you conduct yourself and hold to them unyieldingly—rejecting remonstrance and covering one's faults are precisely such things!"

sentences.zh: 禧得之痛服。

translations.literal: When Xi received it, he was deeply moved and fully convinced.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi read it, he was deeply moved and fully convinced.

sentences.zh: 維屏教授弟子，手批口講，日夜不輟業。

translations.literal: Weiping instructed his disciples, annotating by hand and lecturing orally, day and night without ceasing their studies.
translations.idiomatic: Weiping taught his disciples, annotating their work by hand and lecturing orally, and day and night they never ceased their studies.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi he died at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year of the Kangxi reign, at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 垂歿，示子曰：「食有菜飯，穿可補衣，無譎戾行，堪句讀師。」

translations.literal: Near death, he instructed his sons: "To eat there is plain rice and vegetables; to wear, clothes that can be patched; with no deceitful or perverse conduct—one can serve as a teacher of elementary reading."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his sons, "With plain rice and vegetables to eat and patched clothes to wear, and without deceitful or perverse conduct, one can make a living as a teacher of elementary reading."

sentences.zh: 士望服其言。

translations.literal: Shiwang admired his words.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwang admired what he had said.

sentences.zh: 著有周易剿說十二卷、松下集十二卷、邦士文集十八卷。

translations.literal: He authored Explanatory Notes on the Book of Changes in twelve juan, the Songxia Collection in twelve juan, and the Bangshi Collected Writings in eighteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left Explanatory Notes on the Book of Changes in twelve juan, the Songxia Collection in twelve juan, and the Bangshi Collected Writings in eighteen juan.

sentences.zh: 曾燦，字青藜，亦寧都人，給事中應遴仲子。

translations.literal: Zeng Can, styled Qingli, was also a native of Ningdu and the second son of the censor Ying Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Can, styled Qingli, was also from Ningdu and was the second son of the censor Ying Lin.

sentences.zh: 歲乙酉，楊廷麟竭力保南贛。

translations.literal: In the yiyou year, Yang Tinglin strove with all his strength to defend southern Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiyou year, Yang Tinglin fought with all his strength to hold southern Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 應遴以閩嶠山澤間有眾十萬，命燦往撫之。

translations.literal: Ying Lin, because there were a hundred thousand men among the mountains and marshes of the Fujian ranges, ordered Can to go and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that a hundred thousand men had gathered in the mountains and marshes of the Fujian ranges, Ying Lin sent Can to win them over.

sentences.zh: 既行，而應遴病卒，贛亦破，乃解散。

translations.literal: After Can had set out, Ying Lin fell ill and died, Ganzhou also fell, and Can then disbanded his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Can had barely set out when Ying Lin fell ill and died; Ganzhou soon fell as well, and Can disbanded his forces.

sentences.zh: 尋祝髮為僧，遊閩、浙、兩廣間。

translations.literal: Before long he tonsured his hair and became a monk, traveling between Fujian, Zhejiang, and the two Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he shaved his head and became a monk, traveling through Fujian, Zhejiang, and Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 大母及母念燦成疾，乃歸寧都。

translations.literal: His grandmother and mother, longing for Can until they fell ill, caused him to return to Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother and mother pined for him until they fell ill, and so he returned to Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 以大母命受室，築六松草堂，躬耕不出者數年。

translations.literal: At his grandmother's command he took a wife, built the Six Pines Thatched Hall, and for several years personally farmed the land without going out.
translations.idiomatic: At his grandmother's command he married, built the Six Pines Thatched Hall, and for several years farmed the land himself without leaving home.

sentences.zh: 後僑居吳下二十餘年，客遊燕市以卒。

translations.literal: Later he lived as a sojourner in the Wu region for more than twenty years and died while traveling as a guest in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later lived as a sojourner in the Wu region for more than twenty years and died while visiting the capital.

sentences.zh: 著有六松草堂文集、西崦草堂詩集。

translations.literal: He authored the Six Pines Thatched Hall Collected Writings and the Xiyan Thatched Hall Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Six Pines Thatched Hall Collected Writings and the Xiyan Thatched Hall Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 林時益，本明宗室，名議霶，字確齋，南昌人。

translations.literal: Lin Shiyi was originally of the Ming imperial clan; his original name was Yi Piao, styled Quezhai, and he was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shiyi was originally a member of the Ming imperial clan; his birth name was Yi Piao, styled Quezhai, and he was from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 與彭士望同里。

translations.literal: He was from the same district as Peng Shiwang.
translations.idiomatic: He was from the same home district as Peng Shiwang.

sentences.zh: 兩人謀居。

translations.literal: The two men planned where to live.
translations.idiomatic: The two men planned where to settle.

sentences.zh: 士望與魏禧一見定交，極言金精諸山可為嶺北耕種處，乃攜家偕士望往。

translations.literal: Shiwang and Wei Xi became friends at first meeting; Xi spoke at length of how the mountains around Jin Jing could serve as farmland north of the ranges, and so Shiyi took his family and went there together with Shiwang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiwang and Wei Xi became friends at first meeting; Xi spoke at length of how the mountains around Jin Jing could serve as farmland north of the ranges, and so Shiyi took his family and went there with Shiwang.

sentences.zh: 僑居十餘年，與魏氏昆弟相講習。

translations.literal: He lived as a sojourner for more than ten years, studying together with the Wei brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He lived there as a sojourner for more than ten years, studying together with the Wei brothers.

sentences.zh: 康熙七年，詔明故宗室子孫眾多，竄伏山林者還田廬，復姓氏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Kangxi, an edict declared that among the many descendants of the former Ming imperial clan, those who had hidden themselves in mountains and forests should return to their fields and homes and resume their surnames.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Kangxi reign, an edict declared that the many descendants of the former Ming imperial clan who had hidden in the mountains should return to their fields and homes and resume their original surnames.

sentences.zh: 時益久客寧都，弗樂歸。

translations.literal: Shiyi had long been a guest in Ningdu and was not pleased to return.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi had long lived as a guest in Ningdu and had no wish to go back.

sentences.zh: 卜居冠石，結廬傭田，非其力不食。

translations.literal: He chose to live at Guanshi, built a hut, and rented fields; he would not eat what his own labor had not produced.
translations.idiomatic: He settled at Guanshi, built a hut, and rented fields to farm; he would eat only what his own labor had produced.

sentences.zh: 冠石宜茶，時益以意制之，香味擬陽羨，所謂林茶者也。

translations.literal: Guanshi was suited to tea; Shiyi devised his own method of preparing it, and its fragrance and flavor rivaled Yangxian tea—this was what was called Lin Tea.
translations.idiomatic: Guanshi was well suited to tea; Shiyi devised his own method of preparing it, and its fragrance and flavor rivaled Yangxian tea—this was the tea known as Lin Tea.

sentences.zh: 晚好禪悅。

translations.literal: In his later years he delighted in Chan meditation.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he took delight in Chan Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 著有冠石詩集五卷、確齋文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Guanshi Poetry Collection in five juan and the Quezhai Collected Writings.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Guanshi Poetry Collection in five juan and the Quezhai Collected Writings.

sentences.zh: 梁份，字質人，南豐人。

translations.literal: Liang Fen, styled Zhiren, was a native of Nanfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Fen, styled Zhiren, was from Nanfeng.

sentences.zh: 少從彭士望、魏禧遊，講經世之學。

translations.literal: In youth he associated with Peng Shiwang and Wei Xi, studying statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied with Peng Shiwang and Wei Xi, learning the arts of statecraft.

sentences.zh: 工古文辭。

translations.literal: He was skilled in ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 嘗隻身遊萬里，西盡武威、張掖，南極黔、滇，遍歷燕、趙、秦、晉、齊、魏之墟，覽山川形勢，訪古今成敗得失，遐荒軼事，一發之於文。

translations.literal: He once traveled ten thousand li alone, reaching as far west as Wuwei and Zhangye and as far south as Qian and Dian; he traversed the old lands of Yan, Zhao, Qin, Jin, Qi, and Wei, surveyed the terrain of mountains and rivers, inquired into the successes and failures of past and present, and set forth in writing even remote and little-known events.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled ten thousand li alone, reaching as far west as Wuwei and Zhangye and as far south as Guizhou and Yunnan; he traversed the old lands of Yan, Zhao, Qin, Jin, Qi, and Wei, surveyed mountains and rivers, investigated the successes and failures of past ages, and committed even remote and little-known events to writing.

sentences.zh: 方苞、王源皆重之。

translations.literal: Fang Bao and Wang Yuan both held him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Bao and Wang Yuan both held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 其論山海關，謂：「關自明洪武間始設，隋置臨榆於西，唐為榆關。

translations.literal: In his discussion of Shanhai Pass he said: "The pass was first established in the Hongwu reign of the Ming; in the Sui the Lin Yu post was placed to the west, and in the Tang it was called Yu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In his discussion of Shanhai Pass he wrote: "The pass was first established in the Hongwu reign of the Ming; in the Sui the Lin Yu post was placed to the west, and in the Tang it was called Yu Pass.

sentences.zh: 東北古長城，燕、秦所築，距關遠，皆不足輕重。

translations.literal: The ancient Great Wall to the northeast, built by Yan and Qin, stood far from the pass and was of no real consequence.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient Great Wall to the northeast, built by Yan and Qin, stood far from the pass and mattered little.

sentences.zh: 金之伐遼，自取遷民始。

translations.literal: The Jin conquest of the Liao began with taking in relocated commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin conquest of the Liao began with absorbing relocated commoners.

sentences.zh: 李自成席捲神京，敗石河而失之。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng swept through the divine capital, was defeated at the Shi River, and lost it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng swept through the capital, was defeated at the Shi River, and lost everything.

sentences.zh: 天之廢興，人之成敗，而決於山海一隅。

translations.literal: The rise and fall ordained by Heaven and the success or failure of men were decided in this one corner at the mountains and sea.
translations.idiomatic: The rise and fall of dynasties and the success or failure of men were decided at this one corner where mountains meet the sea.

sentences.zh: 荒榛千百年之上，偏重於三百年間。

translations.literal: Over wilderness and thicket for more than a thousand years, its importance was concentrated in the last three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a thousand years it lay in wilderness and neglect, yet its decisive importance was concentrated in the last three hundred.

sentences.zh: 天下定則山海安，山海困則天下舉困，其安危之重如此。」

translations.literal: When the realm was settled, the mountains and sea were secure; when the mountains and sea were beset, the whole realm was beset—such was the weight of its safety and peril."
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was settled, the pass was secure; when the pass was threatened, the whole realm was threatened—such was its strategic weight."

sentences.zh: 生平以未遊山海為憾。

translations.literal: Throughout his life he regretted never having visited the mountains and sea.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he regretted never having visited Shanhai Pass.

sentences.zh: 為人樸摯強毅，守窮約至老不少挫。

translations.literal: As a man he was plain, sincere, strong, and steadfast, keeping to poverty and restraint until old age without the least weakening.
translations.idiomatic: Plain, sincere, and steadfast, he held to poverty and restraint until old age without the least weakening.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-nine.

sentences.zh: 著有懷葛堂文集十五卷、西陲今略八卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Huaige Hall Collected Writings in fifteen juan and the Brief Account of the Western Frontier in eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Huaige Hall Collected Writings in fifteen juan and the Brief Account of the Western Frontier in eight juan.

sentences.zh: 侯方域，字朝宗，商丘人。

translations.literal: Hou Fangyu, styled Chaozong, was a native of Shangqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Fangyu, styled Chaozong, was from Shangqiu.

sentences.zh: 父恂，明戶部尚書；

translations.literal: His father Xun was a Ming Minister of Revenue;
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun had been Minister of Revenue under the Ming;

sentences.zh: 季父恪，官祭酒：皆以東林忤閹黨。

translations.literal: his younger uncle Ke held the post of Chancellor of the National University: both had offended the eunuch faction through their association with the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: his younger uncle Ke had served as Chancellor of the National University: both had clashed with the eunuch faction through their Donglin affiliations.

sentences.zh: 方域師倪元璐。

translations.literal: Fangyu studied under Ni Yuanlu.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu studied under Ni Yuanlu.

sentences.zh: 性豪邁不羈，為文有奇氣。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold, free-spirited, and unrestrained; in writing he had a singular force.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and unrestrained by nature, he wrote with singular force.

sentences.zh: 時太倉張溥主盟復社，青浦陳子龍主盟幾社，咸推重方域，海內名士爭與之交。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Pu of Taicang led the Fushe society and Chen Zilong of Qingpu led the Jishe society; both held Fangyu in high esteem, and famous men throughout the realm vied to befriend him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Pu of Taicang led the Fushe society and Chen Zilong of Qingpu led the Jishe society; both held Fangyu in high esteem, and celebrated scholars throughout the realm vied to befriend him.

sentences.zh: 方恂之督師援汴也，方域進曰：「大人受詔討賊，廟堂議論多牽制。

translations.literal: When Xun was appointed supreme commander to relieve Bian, Fangyu advanced and said: "Father, you have received an edict to suppress the rebels, yet deliberations at court impose many restraints.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun was appointed supreme commander to relieve Bian, Fangyu urged him: "Father, you have received an edict to suppress the rebels, yet court deliberations impose many restraints.

sentences.zh: 今宜破文法，取賜劍誅一甲科守令之不應徵辦者，而晉帥許定國師噪，亟斬以徇。

translations.literal: Now you should break through bureaucratic convention, take the imperial sword and execute one prefect or magistrate of jinshi rank who fails to respond to levies and supplies, and as for the Shanxi commander Xu Dingguo, whose troops are in an uproar, swiftly behead him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: You should set bureaucratic convention aside, take the imperial sword, and execute one prefect or magistrate of jinshi rank who fails to meet levies and supplies; and as for the Shanxi commander Xu Dingguo, whose troops are in an uproar, behead him at once as a warning.

sentences.zh: 如此則威立，軍事辦，然後渡河收中原土寨團結之眾，以合左良玉於襄陽，約陝督孫傳庭犄角並進，則汴圍不救自解。」

translations.literal: If you do this, authority will be established and military affairs will be managed; then cross the river to gather the fortified communities of the Central Plain, join Zuo Liangyu at Xiangyang, and arrange with the Shaanxi governor Sun Chuanting to advance in pincer formation—then the siege of Bian will lift without need of relief."
translations.idiomatic: Do this, and authority will be established and the army brought to order; then cross the river to rally the fortified communities of the Central Plain, join Zuo Liangyu at Xiangyang, and coordinate with the Shaanxi governor Sun Chuanting for a pincer advance—the siege of Bian will lift of its own accord."

sentences.zh: 恂叱其跋扈，不用，趣遣之歸。

translations.literal: Xun rebuked him for arrogance, paid no heed, and hurried him home.
translations.idiomatic: Xun rebuked him for arrogance, rejected his advice, and sent him home at once.

sentences.zh: 方域既負才無所試，一放意聲伎，流連秦淮間。

translations.literal: Fangyu, having talent yet no scope to prove it, gave himself over to music and entertainers and lingered along the Qinhuai.
translations.idiomatic: With his talent unused, Fangyu gave himself over to music and entertainers and lingered along the Qinhuai.

sentences.zh: 閹黨阮大鋮時亦屏居金陵，謀復用。

translations.literal: The eunuch faction member Ruan Dacheng was also living in retirement in Jinling at the time, scheming for reinstatement.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Dacheng of the eunuch faction was also living in retirement in Jinling at the time, scheming for reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 諸名士共檄大鋮罪，作留都防亂揭，宜興陳貞慧、貴池吳應箕二人主之。

translations.literal: The leading scholars jointly issued a denunciation of Dacheng's crimes and composed the "Manifesto Against Disorder in the Southern Capital," with Chen Zhenhui of Yixing and Wu Yingji of Guichi as its chief authors.
translations.idiomatic: Leading scholars jointly denounced Dacheng's crimes and composed the Manifesto Against Disorder in the Southern Capital, chiefly authored by Chen Zhenhui of Yixing and Wu Yingji of Guichi.

sentences.zh: 大鋮知方域與二人善，私念因侯生以交於二人，事當已，乃囑其客來結驩。

translations.literal: Dacheng knew that Fangyu was on good terms with the two men and privately thought that by befriending Hou Sheng he could reach them and settle the matter; he therefore instructed his clients to come and establish overtures.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng knew Fangyu was close to the two men and privately thought that by winning over Hou Sheng he could reach them and settle the matter; he sent clients to offer friendship.

sentences.zh: 方域覺之，卒謝客，大鋮恨次骨。

translations.literal: Fangyu perceived this and ultimately declined the visitors; Dacheng hated him to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu saw through the scheme and declined the visitors; Dacheng hated him to the bone.

sentences.zh: 已而驟柄用，將盡殺黨人，捕貞慧下獄。

translations.literal: Before long Dacheng was suddenly restored to power and was about to kill all the faction members; he arrested Zhenhui and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dacheng was suddenly restored to power and set about killing his factional enemies; he arrested Zhenhui and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 方域夜走依鎮帥高傑，得免。

translations.literal: Fangyu fled by night and took refuge with the regional commander Gao Jie, thereby escaping harm.
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu fled by night to the regional commander Gao Jie and escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 順治八年，出應鄉試，中式副榜。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shunzhi he sat for the provincial examination and placed on the supplementary list.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Shunzhi he sat for the provincial examination and placed on the supplementary list.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒，年三十七。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died at the age of thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year of Shunzhi, at the age of thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 方域健於文，與魏禧、汪琬齊名，號「國初三家」。

translations.literal: Fangyu was strong in letters and was famed alongside Wei Xi and Wang Wan as the "Three Masters at the Founding of the Dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: Fangyu excelled in letters and was famed alongside Wei Xi and Wang Wan as the Three Masters at the Founding of the Dynasty.

sentences.zh: 有壯悔堂集。

translations.literal: He had the Zhuanghui Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Zhuanghui Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 同時江西以文名者，南昌王猷定，新建陳宏緒、徐士溥、歐陽斌元。

translations.literal: At the same time, those in Jiangxi famed for letters included Wang Youding of Nanchang and Chen Hongxu, Xu Shipu, and Ouyang Binyuan of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, Jiangxi writers of note included Wang Youding of Nanchang and Chen Hongxu, Xu Shipu, and Ouyang Binyuan of Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 猷定，字於一。

translations.literal: Youding, styled Yuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Youding, styled Yuyi.

sentences.zh: 選拔貢生。

translations.literal: He was a selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a selected tribute student.

sentences.zh: 父時熙，進士，官太僕卿，名在東林。

translations.literal: His father Shixi was a jinshi who served as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and was known among the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shixi was a jinshi who served as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and was known as a Donglin associate.

sentences.zh: 猷定好奇，有辯口，文亦如之。

translations.literal: Youding was fond of the unusual and had a gift for debate; his writing was the same.
translations.idiomatic: Youding was fond of the unusual and had a gift for debate, and his writing showed the same quality.

sentences.zh: 著四照堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Sizhao Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Sizhao Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 宏緒，字士業。

translations.literal: Hongxu, styled Shiye.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu, styled Shiye.

sentences.zh: 父道亨，進士，官兵部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Daoheng was a jinshi who served as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: His father Daoheng was a jinshi who served as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 疏救楊漣，罷歸。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial to save Yang Lian, was dismissed, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting a memorial to save Yang Lian, he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 藏書萬卷。

translations.literal: He collected ten thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed a library of ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 宏緒不仕，輯宋遺民錄以見志，有石莊集。

translations.literal: Hongxu did not take office; he compiled the Record of Song Loyalists to express his convictions, and had the Shizhuang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu refused office, compiled the Record of Song Loyalists to declare his convictions, and left the Shizhuang Collection.

sentences.zh: 士溥，字巨源。

translations.literal: Shipu, styled Juyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shipu, styled Juyuan.

sentences.zh: 父良彥，進士。

translations.literal: His father Liangyan was a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangyan was a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 忤崔、魏削籍，戍清浪。

translations.literal: Having offended Cui and Wei, he was struck from the rolls and exiled to guard Qinglang.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing Cui and Wei, he was struck from the rolls and exiled to Qinglang.

sentences.zh: 溧陽陳名夏聞士溥善古文，手書招之，拒不納。

translations.literal: Chen Mingxia of Liyang, hearing that Shipu excelled in ancient-style prose, wrote to summon him by hand; Shipu refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Mingxia of Liyang, hearing that Shipu excelled in ancient-style prose, wrote to summon him in his own hand; Shipu refused the invitation.

sentences.zh: 有榆溪集。

translations.literal: He had the Yuxi Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Yuxi Collection.

sentences.zh: 斌元，字憲萬。

translations.literal: Binyuan, styled Xianwan.
translations.idiomatic: Binyuan, styled Xianwan.

sentences.zh: 嘗為南司馬呂大器草奏劾馬士英二十四大罪，又佐史可法幕府。

translations.literal: He once drafted for the Southern Vice Censor Lu Daqi a memorial impeaching Ma Shiying on twenty-four major counts, and also served on Shi Kefa's staff.
translations.idiomatic: He once drafted for the Southern Vice Censor Lu Daqi a memorial impeaching Ma Shiying on twenty-four major counts, and also served on Shi Kefa's staff.

sentences.zh: 有文集十二卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twelve juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twelve juan.

sentences.zh: 申涵光，字孚孟，號鳧盟，永年人，明太僕寺丞佳胤子。

translations.literal: Shen Hanguang, styled Fumeng, sobriquet Fumeng, was a native of Yongnian and the son of Jiaoyin, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Hanguang, styled Fumeng, sobriquet Fumeng, was a native of Yongnian and the son of Jiaoyin, Vice Director of the Imperial Stud under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 年十五，補諸生。

translations.literal: At the age of fifteen he was enrolled as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he was enrolled as a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 文名藉藉，顧不屑為舉子業。

translations.literal: His literary fame was widespread, yet he disdained the work of examination candidates.
translations.idiomatic: His literary fame was widespread, yet he disdained the grind of examination essays.

sentences.zh: 日與諸同志論文立社，載酒豪遊為樂。

translations.literal: Day after day he discussed letters and formed literary societies with like-minded companions, taking wine and bold excursions for his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day he discussed letters and formed literary societies with kindred spirits, finding his joy in wine and spirited outings.

sentences.zh: 萬曆六年亂起，議城守，出家貲四百金、錢二十萬犒士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli disorder broke out; when the city defense was discussed, he contributed from his family wealth four hundred taels of gold and two hundred thousand cash to reward the troops.
translations.idiomatic: When disorder broke out in the sixth year of Wanli, he contributed four hundred taels of gold and two hundred thousand cash from his family fortune to reward the troops defending the city.

sentences.zh: 甲申，奉母避亂西山，誅茅廣羊絕頂。

translations.literal: In the jiashen year he took his mother to escape the turmoil in the Western Hills, cutting thatch on the summit of Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1644 he took his mother to the Western Hills to escape the turmoil, building a thatched hut on the summit of Mount Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 與鉅鹿楊思聖，雞澤殷岳、殷淵，定患難交。

translations.literal: With Yang Sisheng of Julu and Yin Yue and Yin Yuan of Jize he formed bonds of hardship friendship.
translations.idiomatic: With Yang Sisheng of Julu and Yin Yue and Yin Yuan of Jize he forged bonds of friendship in adversity.

sentences.zh: 京師破，佳胤殉國難，涵光痛絕復甦。

translations.literal: When the capital fell, Jiaoyin died for the national calamity; Hanguang was stricken with grief to the point of death and then revived.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, Jiaoyin died in the national calamity; Hanguang was stricken with grief to the point of death, then revived.

sentences.zh: 因渡江而南，謁陳子龍、夏允彝、徐石麟諸名宿，為父志、傳。

translations.literal: He therefore crossed the river southward and visited eminent elders such as Chen Zilong, Xia Yunyi, and Xu Shilin, seeking a biography and memorial account for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed the river south and visited eminent elders such as Chen Zilong, Xia Yunyi, and Xu Shilin, seeking a biography and memorial account for his father.

sentences.zh: 歸里，事親課弟，足跡絕城市。

translations.literal: Returning home, he served his parents and tutored his younger brothers, and his footsteps never reached the city.
translations.idiomatic: Back home, he cared for his parents and tutored his younger brothers, keeping his footsteps far from the cities.

sentences.zh: 日與殷岳及同里張蓋相往來酬和，人號為「廣平三君」。

translations.literal: Day after day he exchanged visits and poetic responses with Yin Yue and Zhang Gai of his home district, and people called them the "Three Lords of Guangping."
translations.idiomatic: Day after day he exchanged visits and poetic responses with Yin Yue and Zhang Gai of his home district, and people called them the Three Lords of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 清初，詔訪明死難諸臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, an edict was issued to seek out Ming officials who had died in the national calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, an edict was issued to seek out Ming officials who had died in the national calamity.

sentences.zh: 柏鄉魏裔介上褎忠疏，列佳胤名，格於部議。

translations.literal: Wei Yijie of Baixiang submitted a memorial honoring the loyal dead and listed Jiaoyin's name, but it was blocked by deliberation in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yijie of Baixiang submitted a memorial honoring the loyal dead and listed Jiaoyin's name, but the Ministry blocked it in deliberation.

sentences.zh: 涵光徒跣赴京師，踔泥水中，幾瀕於死。

translations.literal: Hanguang went barefoot to the capital, wading through mud and water, and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Hanguang went barefoot to the capital, wading through mud and water, and nearly died on the way.

sentences.zh: 麻衣絰帶，號哭東華道上，觀者皆飲泣。

translations.literal: Wearing hemp mourning garments and a hemp headband, he wailed along the Donghua Road, and all who saw him wept.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing hemp mourning garments and a hemp headband, he wailed along Donghua Road, and all who saw him wept.

sentences.zh: 裔介再疏爭之，卒與祀卹如例。

translations.literal: Yijie submitted another memorial to argue the case, and in the end Jiaoyin received posthumous honors and relief according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yijie submitted another memorial to press the case, and in the end Jiaoyin received posthumous honors and relief according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 一時士大夫高其行，皆傾心納交，宴遊贈答無虛日。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials of the time admired his conduct and all opened their hearts to befriend him; feasts, excursions, and exchanges of gifts and poems left no day empty.
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials of the time admired his conduct and sought his friendship; feasts, excursions, and exchanges of gifts and poems filled his days.

sentences.zh: 涵光為詩，吞吐眾流，納之爐治。

translations.literal: In composing poetry, Hanguang took in every current and refined it in his furnace.
translations.idiomatic: In composing poetry, Hanguang took in every current of the tradition and refined it in his own forge.

sentences.zh: 一以少陵為宗，而出入於高、岑、王、孟諸家。

translations.literal: He took Shaoling as his sole master, yet moved in and out among the schools of Gao, Cen, Wang, and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: He took Du Fu as his sole master, yet moved freely among the schools of Gao Shi, Cen Shen, Wang Wei, and Meng Haoran.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「詩以道性情，性情之真者，可以格帝天，泣神鬼。

translations.literal: He once said: "Poetry expresses one's nature and feelings; when nature and feelings are true, they can move the Emperor of Heaven and make spirits and ghosts weep.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "Poetry expresses one's nature and feelings; when those feelings are true, they can move Heaven itself and make spirits and ghosts weep.

sentences.zh: 若專事附會，寸寸而效之，則啼笑皆偽，不能動一人矣。」

translations.literal: If one devotes oneself solely to imitation, copying inch by inch, then laughter and tears alike are false and cannot move a single person."
translations.idiomatic: If one devotes oneself solely to imitation, copying line by line, then laughter and tears alike are false and cannot move a single person."

sentences.zh: 尚書王士禎稱涵光開河朔詩派。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Shizhen said that Hanguang founded the Hebei school of poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Shizhen said that Hanguang founded the Hebei school of poetry.

sentences.zh: 學士熊伯龍謂今世詩人吾甘為之下者，鳧盟一人而已。

translations.literal: Academician Xiong Bolong said that among the poets of this age, the one beneath whom I am willing to place myself is Fumeng alone.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Xiong Bolong said that among the poets of his age, Fumeng alone was one he would gladly rank above himself.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁孫奇逢，執弟子禮。

translations.literal: He once visited Sun Qifeng and performed the rites of a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: He once visited Sun Qifeng and performed the rites of a disciple.

sentences.zh: 奇逢恨得之晚，以聖賢相敦勉。

translations.literal: Qifeng regretted having found him so late and urged him on with the example of sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng regretted having found him so late and urged him on with the example of sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 自是始聞天人性命之旨，究心理學，不復為詩。

translations.literal: From then on he first heard the teaching on Heaven, human nature, and life's purpose; he pursued the learning of principle and mind and no longer wrote poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he first heard the teaching on Heaven, human nature, and life's purpose; he pursued Neo-Confucian learning and wrote no more poetry.

sentences.zh: 順治十七年，詔郡縣舉孝行，有司以涵光應，力辭之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi an edict ordered the prefectures and counties to recommend men of filial conduct; the local officials nominated Hanguang, but he forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Shunzhi an edict ordered the prefectures and counties to recommend men of filial conduct; the local officials nominated Hanguang, but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 再舉隱逸之士，堅辭不就。

translations.literal: When recluses were recommended again, he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When recluses were recommended again, he firmly declined and would not accept office.

sentences.zh: 嘗自悔為名累，謝絕交遊。

translations.literal: He once regretted that fame had become a burden and cut off social relations.
translations.idiomatic: He once regretted that fame had become a burden and withdrew from society.

sentences.zh: 晚年取諸儒語錄昕夕研究。

translations.literal: In his later years he took the recorded sayings of various Confucians and studied them morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he studied the recorded sayings of various Confucians morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 作性習圖、義利說及荊園小語、進語諸書。

translations.literal: He wrote such works as Diagrams of Nature and Habit, Discourse on Righteousness and Profit, Small Talk from Jing Garden, and Advancing Words.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote such works as Diagrams of Nature and Habit, Discourse on Righteousness and Profit, Small Talk from Jing Garden, and Advancing Words.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「主靜不如主敬，敬，自靜也。

translations.literal: He once said: "To uphold reverence is better than to uphold stillness; reverence is stillness of itself.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "To uphold reverence is better than to uphold stillness; reverence is stillness of itself.

sentences.zh: 朱、陸同適於道，朱由大路，雖遲而穩；

translations.literal: Zhu and Lu alike lead to the Way; Zhu takes the great road—though slow, it is steady;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi and Lu Xiangshan alike lead to the Way; Zhu takes the great road—though slow, it is steady;

sentences.zh: 陸由便徑，似捷而危：在人自擇耳。」

translations.literal: Lu takes the shortcut—though it seems quick, it is perilous: each person chooses for himself."
translations.idiomatic: Lu takes the shortcut—though it seems quick, it is perilous: each person must choose for himself."

sentences.zh: 奇逢謂其苦心積慮，閱歷深而動忍熟。

translations.literal: Qifeng said that his painstaking thought and accumulated reflection came from deep experience and mature forbearance in action.
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng said that his painstaking thought and accumulated reflection came from deep experience and mature forbearance in action.

sentences.zh: 裔介則讚之曰：「年少文壇，老來理路，聖賢之所謂博文而約禮也。」

translations.literal: Yijie then praised him, saying: "In youth he stood on the literary stage; in old age he pursued the path of principle—this is what the sages call broad learning disciplined by ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Yijie then praised him, saying: "In youth he stood on the literary stage; in old age he pursued the path of principle—this is what the sages call broad learning disciplined by ritual."

sentences.zh: 其推重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 康熙十六年，卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kangxi he died at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Kangxi, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 涵光又解琴理。

translations.literal: Hanguang also understood the principles of the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Hanguang also understood the principles of the zither.

sentences.zh: 書法顏魯公，尤工漢隸。

translations.literal: In calligraphy he followed Yan Lugong and was especially skilled in Han clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: In calligraphy he followed Yan Zhenqing and was especially skilled in Han clerical script.

sentences.zh: 間作山水木石，落落有雅緻。

translations.literal: From time to time he painted landscapes, trees, and rocks, with an open, refined elegance.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he painted landscapes, trees, and rocks with an open, refined elegance.

sentences.zh: 著有聰山詩集八卷，文集四卷，說杜一卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Congshan Poetry Collection in eight juan, a prose collection in four juan, and On Du Fu in one juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Congshan Poetry Collection in eight juan, a prose collection in four juan, and On Du Fu in one juan.

sentences.zh: 蓋，字覆輿。

translations.literal: Gai, styled Fuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Gai, styled Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 明亡後，謝諸生，悲吟侘傺，遂成狂疾。

translations.literal: After the fall of the Ming he resigned his status as licentiate, mourned in verse with desolate lament, and eventually developed a mad affliction.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Ming he resigned his status as licentiate, mourned in verse with desolate lament, and eventually developed a mad affliction.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊齊、晉、楚、豫間，歸自閉土室中，雖妻子不得見。

translations.literal: He once traveled among Qi, Jin, Chu, and Yu, and upon returning shut himself in an earthen chamber where even his wife and children could not see him.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled among Qi, Jin, Chu, and Yu, and upon returning shut himself in an earthen chamber where even his wife and children could not see him.

sentences.zh: 唯涵光、岳至則延入，談甚洽。

translations.literal: Only when Hanguang and Yue came would he invite them in, and their talk was very congenial.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Hanguang and Yue came would he admit them, and their talk was always congenial.

sentences.zh: 其詩哀憤過情，恆自毀其稿。

translations.literal: His poetry was grief-stricken and indignant beyond measure, and he constantly destroyed his own drafts.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was grief-stricken and indignant beyond measure, and he constantly destroyed his own drafts.

sentences.zh: 卒後，涵光為刊遺詩，曰柿葉集。

translations.literal: After his death Hanguang published his remaining poems under the title Persimmon Leaf Collection.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Hanguang published his remaining poems as the Persimmon Leaf Collection.

sentences.zh: 岳，字宗山，雞澤人。

translations.literal: Yue, styled Zongshan, was a native of Jize.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, styled Zongshan, was a native of Jize.

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: He was a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，入西山，與其弟淵謀舉義。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he entered the Western Hills and with his younger brother Yuan plotted to raise a righteous force.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he entered the Western Hills and with his younger brother Yuan plotted to raise a righteous force.

sentences.zh: 事泄，淵被害，岳匿涵光家得免。

translations.literal: When the plot leaked out, Yuan was killed; Yue hid in Hanguang's home and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot leaked out, Yuan was killed; Yue hid in Hanguang's home and escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 其為詩自魏、晉以下屏不觀，尤不喜律詩，所作唯古體，莽莽然肖其為人。

translations.literal: In composing poetry he shut out everything from Wei and Jin downward, especially disliked regulated verse, and wrote only in ancient forms—vast and rugged, matching his character.
translations.idiomatic: In composing poetry he shut out everything from Wei and Jin downward, especially disliked regulated verse, and wrote only in ancient forms—vast and rugged, matching his character.

sentences.zh: 有留耕堂集。

translations.literal: He had the Liugeng Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Liugeng Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 吳嘉紀，字賓賢，泰州人。

translations.literal: Wu Jiaji, styled Binxian, was a native of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jiaji, styled Binxian, was a native of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 布衣。

translations.literal: He was a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was a commoner.

sentences.zh: 家安豐鹽場之東淘。

translations.literal: His family lived at Dongtao by the Anfeng salt works.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived at Dongtao by the Anfeng salt works.

sentences.zh: 地濱海，無交遊。

translations.literal: The place bordered the sea and he had no social contacts.
translations.idiomatic: The place bordered the sea and he had no social contacts.

sentences.zh: 自名所居曰陋軒。

translations.literal: He named his dwelling the Humble Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He named his dwelling the Humble Studio.

sentences.zh: 貧甚，雖豐歲常乏食。

translations.literal: He was extremely poor; even in abundant years he often lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: He was extremely poor; even in abundant years he often lacked food.

sentences.zh: 獨喜吟詩，晨夕嘯詠自適，不交當世。

translations.literal: He alone delighted in composing poetry, chanting and singing morning and evening for his own contentment, and kept no company with men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He alone delighted in composing poetry, chanting and singing morning and evening for his own contentment, and kept no company with men of the age.

sentences.zh: 郡人汪楫、孫枝蔚與友善，時稱道之，遂為王士禎所知。

translations.literal: Wang Ji and Sun Zhiwei of his prefecture were on friendly terms with him and often spoke of him, and thus he came to be known to Wang Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji and Sun Zhiwei of his prefecture were his friends and often spoke of him, and thus he came to be known to Wang Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 尤賞其五言清冷古淡，雪夜酌酒，為之序，馳使三百里致之。

translations.literal: Shizhen especially admired his five-character lines for their cool clarity and ancient plainness; on a snowy night he poured wine, wrote a preface for him, and sent a messenger three hundred li to deliver it.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen especially admired his five-character lines for their cool clarity and ancient plainness; on a snowy night he poured wine, wrote a preface for him, and sent a messenger three hundred li to deliver it.

sentences.zh: 嘉紀因買舟至揚州謁謝定交，由是四方知名士爭與之倡和。

translations.literal: Jiaji therefore bought a boat and went to Yangzhou to pay his respects and establish friendship; from then on renowned men from all quarters vied to exchange poems with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaji therefore bought a boat and went to Yangzhou to pay his respects and establish friendship; from then on renowned men from all quarters vied to exchange poems with him.

sentences.zh: 嘉紀工為危苦嚴冷之詞，嘗撰今樂府，淒急幽奧，能變通陳跡，自為一家。
