translations.literal: Jiaji was skilled at writing words of peril, hardship, severity, and cold; he once composed New Music Bureau poems—desolate, urgent, hidden, and abstruse—able to transform stale forms and establish a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaji was skilled at writing words of peril, hardship, severity, and cold; he once composed New Music Bureau poems—desolate, urgent, hidden, and abstruse—able to transform stale forms and establish a school of his own.

sentences.zh: 所著陋軒集多散佚，友人復裒集之為四卷。

translations.literal: Most of his Humble Studio Collection was scattered and lost; friends later gathered the remaining pieces into four juan.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his Humble Studio Collection was scattered and lost; friends later gathered the remaining pieces into four juan.

sentences.zh: 其詩風骨頗遒，運思亦復劖刻。

translations.literal: His poetry had a vigorous bone and sinew, and his working of thought was likewise incised and refined.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry had vigorous bone and sinew, and his working of thought was likewise incised and refined.

sentences.zh: 由所遭不偶，每多怨咽之音，而篤行潛修，特為一時推重云。

translations.literal: Because his fate was unkind, his work often bore notes of grievance and lament; yet his earnest conduct and quiet cultivation were especially esteemed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Because fortune had been unkind to him, his work often bore notes of grievance and lament; yet his earnest conduct and quiet cultivation were especially esteemed in his time.

sentences.zh: 徐波，字元嘆，吳縣人。

translations.literal: Xu Bo, styled Yuantan, was a native of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bo, styled Yuantan, was a native of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 少任俠。

translations.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and bold.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was chivalrous and bold.

sentences.zh: 明亡後，居天池，構落木菴，以枯禪終。

translations.literal: After the fall of the Ming he lived at Tianchi, built the Falling Tree Hermitage, and ended his days in dry Chan meditation.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Ming he lived at Tianchi, built the Falling Tree Hermitage, and ended his days in dry Chan meditation.

sentences.zh: 詩多感喟，虞山錢謙益與之善，贈以詩，頗推重之。

translations.literal: His poetry was full of sighs and emotion; Qian Qianyi of Yushan was on good terms with him, presented him with poems, and held him in considerable esteem.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was full of sighs and emotion; Qian Qianyi of Yushan was his friend, presented him with poems, and held him in considerable esteem.

sentences.zh: 有諡簫堂、染香菴等集。

translations.literal: He had such collections as Yi Xiao Hall and Dyed Fragrance Hermitage.
translations.idiomatic: He left such collections as Yi Xiao Hall and Dyed Fragrance Hermitage.

sentences.zh: 錢謙益，字受之，常熟人。

translations.literal: Qian Qianyi, styled Shouzhi, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qianyi, styled Shouzhi, was a native of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 明萬曆中進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign of the Ming he became a jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign he became a jinshi and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 博學工詞章，名隸東林黨。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and skilled in belles-lettres, his name was listed among the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and skilled in belles-lettres, he was known as a Donglin associate.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，御史陳以瑞劾罷之。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign the censor Chen Yirui impeached him and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign the censor Chen Yirui impeached him and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起官，不數月至禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was restored to office and within a few months reached Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was restored to office and within a few months reached Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會推閣臣，謙益慮尚書溫體仁、侍郎周延儒並推，則名出己上，謀沮之。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretaries were to be jointly recommended, Qianyi feared that if Minister Wen Tiren and Vice Minister Zhou Yanru were recommended together, their names would rank above his own, and he plotted to obstruct it.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Secretaries were to be jointly recommended, Qianyi feared that if Minister Wen Tiren and Vice Minister Zhou Yanru were recommended together, their names would rank above his own, and he plotted to obstruct it.

sentences.zh: 體仁追論謙益典試浙江取錢千秋關節事，予杖論贖。

translations.literal: Tiren pursued the matter of Qianyi's chief examining in Zhejiang and accepting Qian Qianqiu's examination irregularities; Qianyi was sentenced to beating and redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren pursued the matter of Qianyi's chief examining in Zhejiang and accepting Qian Qianqiu's examination irregularities; Qianyi was sentenced to beating and redemption.

sentences.zh: 體仁复賄常熟人張漢儒訐謙益貪肆不法。

translations.literal: Tiren again bribed Zhang Hanru of Changshu to accuse Qianyi of greed, excess, and unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren again bribed Zhang Hanru of Changshu to accuse Qianyi of greed, excess, and unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 謙益求救於司禮太監曹化淳，刑斃漢儒。

translations.literal: Qianyi sought rescue from the Director of Ceremonial eunuch Cao Huachun, and Hanru was executed by punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi sought rescue from the Director of Ceremonial eunuch Cao Huachun, and Hanru was executed.

sentences.zh: 體仁引疾去，謙益亦削籍歸。

translations.literal: Tiren cited illness and withdrew; Qianyi was also struck from the rolls and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren cited illness and withdrew; Qianyi was also struck from the rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 流賊陷京師，明臣議立君江寧。

translations.literal: When the bandits took the capital, Ming officials discussed enthroning a ruler at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits took the capital, Ming officials discussed enthroning a ruler at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 謙益陰推戴潞王，與馬士英議不合。

translations.literal: Qianyi secretly favored enthroning the Prince of Lu, and his views did not agree with those of Ma Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi secretly favored enthroning the Prince of Lu, and his views did not agree with those of Ma Shiying.

sentences.zh: 已而福王立，懼得罪，上書誦士英功，士英引為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long the Prince of Fu was enthroned; fearing punishment, Qianyi submitted a memorial praising Shiying's merits, and Shiying had him appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Prince of Fu was enthroned; fearing punishment, Qianyi submitted a memorial praising Shiying's merits, and Shiying had him appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 复力荐閹黨阮大鋮等，大鋮遂為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Again he strongly recommended eunuch-faction men such as Ruan Dacheng, and Dacheng accordingly became Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He again vigorously recommended eunuch-faction figures such as Ruan Dacheng, and Dacheng was duly appointed Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，豫親王多鐸定江南，謙益迎降，命以禮部侍郎管秘書院事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, Prince Regent Dodo pacified Jiangnan; Qianyi welcomed the surrender and was ordered to serve as Vice Minister of Rites overseeing the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shunzhi, Prince Regent Dodo pacified the south; Qianyi surrendered and was appointed Vice Minister of Rites in charge of the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 馮銓充明史館正總裁，而謙益副之。

translations.literal: Feng Quan served as chief director of the Ming History Bureau, with Qianyi as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan was chief director of the Ming History Bureau, with Qianyi as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 俄乞歸。

translations.literal: Before long he requested to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 五年，鳳陽巡撫陳之龍獲黃毓祺，謙益坐與交通，詔總督馬國柱逮訊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Chen Zhilong, governor of Fengyang, captured Huang Yuqi; Qianyi was implicated for having had dealings with him, and an edict ordered Governor-General Ma Guozhu to arrest and interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Chen Zhilong, governor of Fengyang, captured Huang Yuqi; Qianyi was implicated for having communicated with him, and the emperor ordered Governor-General Ma Guozhu to arrest and question him.

sentences.zh: 謙益訴辨，國柱遂以謙益、毓祺素非相識定讞。

translations.literal: Qianyi pleaded in his defense; Guozhu thereupon fixed the verdict on the grounds that Qianyi and Yuqi had never known each other.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi pleaded in his own defense, and Ma Guozhu ruled that he and Yuqi had never been acquainted.

sentences.zh: 得放還，以箸​​述自娛，越十年卒。

translations.literal: He was released to return home and amused himself with writing; more than ten years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was released and returned home, devoting himself to writing for his remaining years; he died ten years later.

sentences.zh: 謙益為文博贍，諳悉朝典，詩尤擅其勝。

translations.literal: Qianyi's prose was broad and rich; he was thoroughly versed in court rites and regulations, and in poetry he was especially unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi's prose was broad and learned, he knew court rites inside out, and his poetry was the field in which he truly excelled.

sentences.zh: 明季王、李號稱復古，文體日下，謙益起而力振之。

translations.literal: In the late Ming, the Wang and Li schools styled themselves restorers of the ancients, and literary style daily declined; Qianyi rose and strove vigorously to revive it.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, the Wang and Li schools claimed to be restoring classical style even as literary standards sank; Qianyi stepped forward and tried hard to reverse the decline.

sentences.zh: 家富藏書，晚歲絳雲樓火，惟一佛像不燼，遂歸心釋教，著。

translations.literal: His household was rich in stored books; in his later years the Jiangyun Pavilion burned, and only a Buddhist statue was not consumed by the flames; he thereupon gave his heart to Buddhism and authored the Exegetical Notes on the Śūraṅgama Sūtra.
translations.idiomatic: He maintained a great library at home. In his old age the Jiangyun Pavilion burned down, leaving only a Buddhist image unscathed; he then turned to Buddhism and wrote his Exegetical Notes on the Śūraṅgama Sūtra.

sentences.zh: 其自為詩文，曰，曰、。

translations.literal: His own poetry and prose he titled the Collected Works of Muzhai, the Chuxue Collection, and the Youxue Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His own writings included the Collected Works of Muzhai, the Chuxue Collection, and the Youxue Collection.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十四年，詔毀板，然傳本至今不絕。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong, an edict ordered the destruction of the printing blocks, yet copies in circulation have not ceased to this day.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 34 an edict ordered the blocks destroyed, yet circulated copies survive to this day.

sentences.zh: 龔鼎孳，字孝升，合肥人。

translations.literal: Gong Dingzi, styled Xiaosheng, was a native of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Dingzi, styled Xiaosheng, was from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎七年進士，授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen of the Ming he became a jinshi and was appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of War.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Chongzhen 7, he was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of War.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷都城，以鼎孳為直指使，巡視北城。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng seized the capital, Dingzi was made direct censor and assigned to patrol the northern city.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng took the capital, Dingzi was made a direct censor and charged with patrolling the northern city.

sentences.zh: 及睿親王至，遂迎降，授吏科給事中。

translations.literal: When the Prince Regent arrived, he welcomed the surrender and was appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Regent Dorgon arrived, he surrendered and was appointed supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 改禮科，遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Bureau of Rites and promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Bureau of Rites and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，丁父憂，請賜卹典。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi, upon mourning for his father, he petitioned for the grant of condolence rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3, while mourning his father, he petitioned for imperial condolences.

sentences.zh: 給事中孫自齡疏言：「鼎孳辱身流賊，蒙朝廷擢用，曾不聞夙夜在公，惟飲酒醉歌，俳優角逐。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Sun Ziling memorialized, saying: "Dingzi debased himself under the bandit rebels; the court raised him to office, yet one never hears of his working day and night in public service—only of drinking, drunken singing, and competing with actors.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Sun Ziling memorialized: "Dingzi debased himself serving the rebels; honored with office by the court, he has shown none of the tireless dedication a minister owes—only drinking, drunken song, and jousting with actors.

sentences.zh: 聞訃仍復歌飲留連，冀邀非分之典，虧行滅倫，莫此為甚！」

translations.literal: On hearing of mourning he still indulged in song and drink at length, hoping to invite unmerited rites—a breach of conduct and annihilation of human bonds; nothing exceeds this!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of his father's death, he still caroused and lingered over wine and song, hoping to secure undeserved honors—a violation of propriety and filial duty without equal!"

sentences.zh: 部議降二級。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and reduced him two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry recommended demoting him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 尋遇恩詔獲免，累遷左都御史。

translations.literal: Soon he benefited from an amnesty edict and was spared; he was successively promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon pardoned under an amnesty and rose to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 先是大學士馮銓被劾，睿親王集科道質訊。

translations.literal: Earlier Grand Secretary Feng Quan had been impeached, and the Prince Regent assembled censorial officials for examination.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Grand Secretary Feng Quan had been impeached, and the Prince Regent assembled the censorate for a formal inquiry.

sentences.zh: 鼎孳斥銓閹黨，為忠賢義兒。

translations.literal: Dingzi denounced Quan as an eunuch-faction man and an adopted son of Wei Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi denounced Feng Quan as a eunuch-faction ally and adoptive son of Wei Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 銓曰：「何如逆賊御史？」

translations.literal: Quan said: "How does that compare with the rebel-bandit censor?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Quan retorted: "And how does that compare with a censor who served the rebel bandits?"

sentences.zh: 鼎孳以魏徵歸順太宗自解，王笑曰：「惟無瑕者可以戮人。

translations.literal: Dingzi explained himself by comparing himself to Wei Zheng's submission to Emperor Taizong of Tang; the Prince laughed and said: "Only the flawless may punish others.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi defended himself by citing Wei Zheng's turn to Emperor Taizong of Tang; the Prince laughed and said, "Only those without blemish may judge others.

sentences.zh: 奈何以闖賊擬太宗！」

translations.literal: How can one liken the marauding rebels to Taizong!"
translations.idiomatic: How dare you compare Li Zicheng's bandits to Emperor Taizong!"

sentences.zh: 遂罷不問。

translations.literal: The matter was thereupon dismissed without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 坐事降八級調用，補上林苑丞，旋罷。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted eight ranks and reassigned, appointed as director of the Imperial Park, and soon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After an offense he was demoted eight ranks and reassigned as director of the Imperial Park, then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，起左都御史，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi he was restored as Left Censor-in-Chief and transferred to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kangxi reign he was restored as Left Censor-in-Chief and later became Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡「端毅」。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously titled "Duanyi."
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given the title "Duanyi" (Steadfast and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十四年，詔削其諡。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Qianlong, an edict stripped his posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 34 an edict stripped his posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 鼎孳天才宏肆，千言立就。

translations.literal: Dingzi's native talent was vast and unrestrained; a thousand-character piece he could finish on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzi was prodigiously gifted; he could produce a thousand-character essay in a single sitting.

sentences.zh: 世祖在禁中見其文，歎曰：「真才子也！」

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor saw his writing while in the inner palace and sighed: "A true literary genius!"
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu Emperor read his work in the inner palace and exclaimed, "A true literary genius!"

sentences.zh: 嘗兩典會試，汲引英雋如不及。

translations.literal: He twice served as chief examiner of the metropolitan examination, drawing forth talented young men as though he could not do so fast enough.
translations.idiomatic: He twice presided over the metropolitan examinations, advancing talented scholars as if he could never reach them soon enough.

sentences.zh: 朱彝尊、陳維崧遊京師，貧甚，資給之。

translations.literal: Zhu Yizun and Chen Weisong traveled to the capital extremely poor; he supplied them with funds.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yizun and Chen Weisong came to the capital in dire poverty, he provided for them.

sentences.zh: 傅山、閻爾梅陷獄，皆賴其力得免。

translations.literal: Fu Shan and Yan Ermei fell into prison; all relied on his efforts to gain release.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shan and Yan Ermei were imprisoned; both owed their release to his intervention.

sentences.zh: 臨歿，以徐釚囑梁清標曰：「負才如虹亭，可使之不成名耶？」

translations.literal: On the verge of death he entrusted Xu Chi to Liang Qingbiao, saying: "One with talent like Hongting—can one let him fail to win fame?"
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he commended Xu Chi to Liang Qingbiao, saying, "A man of talent like Hongting—can we let him go unrecognized?"

sentences.zh: 釚後以清標薦試鴻博，入史館。

translations.literal: Chi later, through Qingbiao's recommendation, took the Special Examination and entered the History Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chi later entered the History Bureau after Liang Qingbiao recommended him for the Special Examination.

sentences.zh: 自謙益卒後，在朝有文藻負士林之望者，推鼎孳雲。

translations.literal: After Qian Qianyi died, among those at court possessed of literary talent who bore the hopes of the scholarly community, Gong Dingzi was ranked foremost.
translations.idiomatic: After Qian Qianyi's death, Gong Dingzi stood at the head of those at court whose literary gifts commanded the respect of the scholarly world.

sentences.zh: 著有定山堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Ding Shan Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Ding Shan Tang Collection.

sentences.zh: 吳偉業，字駿公，太倉人。

translations.literal: Wu Weiye, styled Jungong, was a native of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Weiye, styled Jungong, was from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎四年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen of the Ming he became a jinshi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Chongzhen 4, he was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 充東宮講讀官，再遷左庶子。

translations.literal: He served as lecturer to the Eastern Palace and was twice promoted to Left Subprefect of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as lecturer to the crown prince and was twice promoted to Left Subprefect of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弘光時，授少詹事，乞假歸。

translations.literal: During the Hongguang reign he was appointed Junior Mentor and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Hongguang regime he was appointed Junior Mentor and asked for leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，用兩江總督馬國柱薦，詔至京。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi, on the recommendation of Governor-General Ma Guozhu of the Two Jiangs, an edict summoned him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9, on the recommendation of Governor-General Ma Guozhu of the Two Jiangs, he was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 侍郎孫承澤、大學士馮銓相繼論薦，授秘書院侍講，充修太祖、太宗聖訓纂修官。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Sun Chengze and Grand Secretary Feng Quan successively urged his appointment; he was made Secretariat Reader and appointed compiler of the Sacred Instructions of Taizu and Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Sun Chengze and Grand Secretary Feng Quan both recommended him in turn; he was made Secretariat Reader and compiler of the Sacred Instructions of Taizu and Taizong.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷祭酒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was promoted to Libationer.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂歸。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 10.

sentences.zh: 偉業學問博贍，或從質經史疑義及朝章國故，無不洞悉原委。

translations.literal: Weiye's learning was broad and rich; whether one questioned him on doubtful points in the classics and histories or on court regulations and national lore, he understood the origins and particulars of all without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Weiye's erudition was vast; ask him about any knot in the classics or histories, or any point of court ritual and state precedent, and he could trace every thread to its source.

sentences.zh: 詩文工麗，蔚為一時之冠，不自標榜。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were finely wrought and ranked foremost of the age, yet he did not boast of himself.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were exquisitely crafted and stood at the summit of his generation, though he never flaunted it.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，生際鼎革，有親在，不能不依違顧戀，俯仰身世，每自傷也。

translations.literal: Deeply filial by nature, born at the moment of dynastic transition, with parents still living he could not but waver and linger in indecision; looking up and down at his life in the world, he often wounded himself over it.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, he came of age amid dynastic upheaval; with parents still alive he could not but hesitate and cling to both old and new worlds, and as he surveyed his life he often grieved over it.

sentences.zh: 臨歿，顧言：「吾一生遭際，萬事憂危，無一時一境不歷艱苦。

translations.literal: On the verge of death he left word: "Throughout my life I have met with every sort of trial and peril—not a single hour or circumstance without hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Facing death he said: "In all my days I have known nothing but worry and danger—there was never a moment or a place free of hardship.

sentences.zh: 死後斂以僧裝，葬我鄧尉、靈巖之側。

translations.literal: After death let me be dressed in monk's garb and bury me beside Dengwei and Lingyan.
translations.idiomatic: When I am dead, dress me in monk's robes and bury me beside Dengwei and Lingyan.

sentences.zh: 墳前立一圓石，題曰『詩人吳梅村之墓』。

translations.literal: Before the grave set up a round stone and inscribe it "The Grave of the Poet Wu Meicun."
translations.idiomatic: Place a round stone before the grave and inscribe it: "The Grave of the Poet Wu Meicun."

sentences.zh: 勿起祠堂，勿乞銘。」

translations.literal: Do not build a memorial hall; do not seek an epitaph."
translations.idiomatic: Do not raise a memorial hall; do not ask anyone to write my epitaph."

sentences.zh: 聞其言者皆悲之。

translations.literal: Those who heard his words were all moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard him were deeply saddened.

sentences.zh: 著有春秋地理志、氏族志，綏寇紀略及梅村集。

translations.literal: He authored the Gazetteer of Spring and Autumn Geography, Record of Clans, Chronicle of Pacifying the Bandits, and the Meicun Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works included the Gazetteer of Spring and Autumn Geography, Record of Clans, Chronicle of Pacifying the Bandits, and the Meicun Collection.

sentences.zh: 曹溶，字鑑躬，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Cao Rong, styled Jiangong, was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Rong, styled Jiangong, was from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎十年進士，官御史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen of the Ming he became a jinshi and served as censor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Chongzhen 10, he served as censor.

sentences.zh: 清定京師，仍原職。

translations.literal: When the Qing pacified the capital he retained his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qing took the capital he kept his original post.

sentences.zh: 尋授順天學政。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed educational commissioner of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed educational commissioner of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 疏薦明進士王崇簡等五人，又請旌殉節明大學士苑景文、尚書倪元璐等二十八人，孝子徐基、義士王良翰等及節婦十餘人。

translations.literal: In a memorial he recommended five Ming jinshi including Wang Chongjian, and also requested honors for twenty-eight Ming figures who died in loyalty, including Grand Secretary Yuan Jingwen and Minister Ni Yuanlu, as well as the filial son Xu Ji, the righteous man Wang Lianghan, and more than ten chaste widows.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he recommended five Ming jinshi including Wang Chongjian, and asked that honors be granted to twenty-eight Ming loyalists who died for the dynasty, including Grand Secretary Yuan Jingwen and Minister Ni Yuanlu, as well as the filial son Xu Ji, the righteous man Wang Lianghan, and more than ten chaste widows.

sentences.zh: 試竣，擢太僕寺少卿。

translations.literal: When the examinations concluded he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: After the examinations he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 坐前學政任內失察，降二級。

translations.literal: For failure to detect misconduct during his earlier term as educational commissioner, he was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted two ranks for failing to detect misconduct during his earlier term as educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 久之，稍遷左通政，上言：「通政之官職在納言，請嗣後凡遇挾私違例章疏即予駮還，仍許隨事建議。」

translations.literal: After a long interval he was gradually promoted to Left Vice Minister of Communications and submitted: "The duty of the Office of Transmission lies in receiving remonstrance; hereafter, whenever a memorial is submitted in violation of rules through private interest, let it be returned with rejection, while still permitting suggestions on matters as they arise."
translations.idiomatic: After some time he rose to Left Vice Minister of Communications and memorialized: "The transmission office exists to channel remonstrance; hereafter, whenever a memorial violates the rules out of private interest, return it at once—but still allow ad hoc proposals on current affairs."

sentences.zh: 又言：「王師入關，各處駐兵，乃一時權宜。

translations.literal: He also said: "When the imperial army entered the passes, troops were stationed in various places as a temporary expedient.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "When the imperial army entered the passes, garrisons were posted across the realm only as a temporary measure.

sentences.zh: 今當歸併於盜賊出沒險阻之地，則兵不患少。

translations.literal: Now they should be consolidated in places where bandits and rebels emerge in rugged terrain; then troops need not be feared too few.
translations.idiomatic: They should now be concentrated where bandits and rebels haunt difficult country; then numbers will cease to be a worry.

sentences.zh: 其閒散無事之兵，遇缺勿補，遇調即遣，則餉不虛糜。

translations.literal: As for idle troops with nothing to do, when vacancies occur do not fill them; when transfers are needed dispatch them at once—then pay will not be wasted in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Idle troops with no duties should go unfilled when vacancies arise and be sent out the moment they are needed—so rations are not squandered.

sentences.zh: 且當裁提鎮，增副將，以專責成。」

translations.literal: Moreover, regional commanders should be cut back and vice generals increased, so that responsibility may be fixed."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged reducing provincial commanders and adding vice generals, so that accountability would be clear."

sentences.zh: 又言：「諸司職掌無成書，請以近年奉旨通行者，參之前朝會典，編為簡明則例，以重官守。」

translations.literal: He further said: "The various ministries have no comprehensive code of duties; I request that recent edicts issued for general application be collated with the precedents of the former dynasty's administrative statutes and compiled into concise regulations, to strengthen official responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed compiling a concise code of office from recent imperial edicts and Ming administrative precedents, since the ministries lacked any authoritative handbook of duties.

sentences.zh: 擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏請時禦便殿，召大臣入對，賜筆札以辨其才識，有切中利弊者，即飭力行，勿概下部議，帝並嘉納。

translations.literal: In a memorial he requested that the emperor regularly hold audience in the informal hall and summon ministers for direct discussion, granting them writing materials to test their talent and insight; when any proposal struck at real advantages and disadvantages, let it be ordered carried out at once and not routinely referred to the ministries for deliberation—and the emperor approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the emperor should hold informal audiences, summon ministers for direct discussion, and supply paper and brush to test their judgment; proposals that hit real strengths and weaknesses should be enforced immediately rather than routinely sent down for departmental debate—and the emperor accepted every point.

sentences.zh: 擢戶部侍郎，出為廣東布政使，降山西陽和道。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, then sent out as provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong, and was demoted to intendant of Yanghe in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, then posted as provincial administration commissioner of Guangdong, and later demoted to intendant of Yanghe in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，裁缺歸里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kangxi, when his post was abolished, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kangxi his post was abolished and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 十八年，舉鴻博，丁憂未赴，學士徐元文薦修明史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was nominated for the Special Examination, but mourning prevented his attendance; Academician Xu Yuanwen recommended him to compile the Ming History.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he was nominated for the Special Examination but could not attend because of mourning; Academician Xu Yuanwen recommended him to help compile the Ming History.

sentences.zh: 又數年，卒，有倦圃詩集。

translations.literal: Several years later he died; he left the Juanpu Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He died several years later, leaving the Juanpu Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 宋琬，字玉叔，萊陽人。

translations.literal: Song Wan, styled Yushu, was a native of Laiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wan, styled Yushu, was from Laiyang.

sentences.zh: 父應亨，明天啟中進士。

translations.literal: His father Yingheng became a jinshi in the Tianqi reign of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingheng was a jinshi in the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 令清豐，有惠政，民為立祠。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Qingfeng he governed with benevolence, and the people built a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Qingfeng he ruled with kindness, and the people erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 崇禎末殉節，贈太僕寺卿。

translations.literal: At the end of Chongzhen he died loyal to the dynasty and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Chongzhen he died loyal to the dynasty and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 琬少能詩，有才名。

translations.literal: From youth Wan could compose poetry and had a reputation for talent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Song Wan wrote poetry and was known for his talent.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士，授戶部主事，累遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shunzhi he became a jinshi and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; he was successively promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 4, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 出為隴西道，過清豐，民遮至應亨祠，款留竟日，述往事至泣下。

translations.literal: Sent out as intendant of Longxi, he passed through Qingfeng; the people blocked his path to Yingheng's shrine and detained him for a whole day, recounting old events until they wept.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as intendant of Longxi, he passed through Qingfeng, where the people stopped him at Yingheng's shrine and kept him a full day, recalling the past until they wept.

sentences.zh: 琬益自刻厲，期不墜先緒。

translations.literal: Wan redoubled his self-discipline, resolving not to fall short of his forebears' legacy.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wan redoubled his efforts, determined not to disgrace his family's name.

sentences.zh: 調永平道，又調寧紹台道，皆有績。

translations.literal: Transferred to intendant of Yongping, then to intendant of Ning-Shao-Tai, he achieved merit in each post.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yongping and then to Ning-Shao-Tai, he distinguished himself in every assignment.

sentences.zh: 十八年，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時登州於七為亂。

translations.literal: At the time Yu Qi was in rebellion at Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu Qi had risen in rebellion at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 琬同族子懷宿憾，因告變，誣琬與於七通，立逮下獄，並系妻子。

translations.literal: A clansman of Wan's, nursing an old grudge, denounced him; Wan was falsely accused of collusion with Yu Qi, immediately arrested and imprisoned, and his wife and children were detained as well.
translations.idiomatic: A kinsman of Song Wan's, nursing an old grievance, denounced him; Wan was falsely accused of colluding with Yu Qi, seized and thrown into prison, and his wife and children were imprisoned too.

sentences.zh: 逾三載，下督撫外訊。

translations.literal: More than three years passed before the case was tried outside the provincial jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: After more than three years the case was tried outside provincial jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 巡撫蔣國柱白其誣，康熙三年放歸。

translations.literal: Governor Jiang Guozhu cleared him of the false charge, and in the third year of Kangxi he was released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Guozhu established his innocence, and in Kangxi 3 he was released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 十一年，有詔起用，授四川按察使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict restored him to office and appointed him provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year an edict recalled him to office as provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，入覲，家屬留官所。

translations.literal: The following year he went to court for audience, leaving his family at his post.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he went to court for audience, leaving his family at his post.

sentences.zh: 值吳三桂叛，成都陷，聞變驚悸卒。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, Chengdu fell; on hearing the news he died of shock and terror.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled and Chengdu fell, the news struck him with such shock that he died.

sentences.zh: 始琬官京師，與嚴沆、施閏章、丁澎輩酬倡，有「燕台七子」之目。

translations.literal: When Wan first served at the capital he exchanged poems with Yan Hang, Shi Runzhang, Ding Peng, and others, and was known as one of the "Seven Masters of the Yan Capital."
translations.idiomatic: When Song Wan first served in the capital he exchanged verses with Yan Hang, Shi Runzhang, Ding Peng, and others, and was counted among the "Seven Masters of the Yan Capital."

sentences.zh: 其詩格合聲諧，明靚溫潤。

translations.literal: His poetry combined structure with harmonious sound, bright, clear, warm, and polished.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry married form to melody—bright, lucid, warm, and refined.

sentences.zh: 既構難，時作淒清激宕之調，而亦不戾於和。

translations.literal: After he suffered calamity he sometimes wrote in a desolate, stirring key, yet never lost harmony.
translations.idiomatic: After his ordeal he sometimes wrote in a desolate, impassioned vein, yet never lost his sense of balance.

sentences.zh: 王士禎點定其集為三十卷。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen edited his collection into thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen edited his collected works into thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 嘗舉閏章相況，目為「南施北宋」。

translations.literal: He once compared Runzhang to himself, calling them "Southern Shi and Northern Song."
translations.idiomatic: He once paired himself with Runzhang under the epithet "Southern Shi and Northern Song."

sentences.zh: 歿後詩散佚，族孫邦憲綴輯之為六卷。

translations.literal: After his death his poems were scattered and lost; a clansman grandson, Bangxian, collected and arranged them into six juan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his poems were scattered and lost; his clansman grandson Bangxian gathered and edited them into six juan.

sentences.zh: 沆，字子餐，餘杭人。

translations.literal: Hang, styled Zican, was a native of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hang, styled Zican, was from Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，官至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi and rose to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Shunzhi, he rose to serve as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 性退讓，或譏彈其詩，輒應時改定。

translations.literal: By nature he was modest and yielding; if anyone criticized his poems, he would promptly revise them on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Modest and yielding by nature, he would revise his poems on the spot whenever anyone criticized them.

sentences.zh: 有皋園集。

translations.literal: He had the Gaoyuan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection entitled Gaoyuan ji.

sentences.zh: 施閏章，字尚白，號愚山，宣城人。

translations.literal: Shi Runzhang, styled Shangbai and known as Yushan, was a native of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Runzhang, styled Shangbai and known as Yushan, was from Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 祖鴻猷，以儒學著。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hongyou was renowned for Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hongyou was noted for scholarly accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 子姓傳業江南，言家法者推施氏。

translations.literal: For generations his descendants carried on the family vocation in Jiangnan; among those who spoke of household discipline, the Shi clan was held up as a model.
translations.idiomatic: His family kept up its scholarly tradition in the south for generations; when people spoke of exemplary household discipline, the Shi were always cited.

sentences.zh: 閏章少孤，事叔父如父。

translations.literal: Runzhang lost his father early and served his uncle as he would a father.
translations.idiomatic: Runzhang was orphaned young and treated his uncle with the respect due a father.

sentences.zh: 從沈壽民遊，博綜群籍，善詩古文辭。

translations.literal: He associated with Shen Shoumin, broadly mastered numerous texts, and was skilled in poetry and ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with Shen Shoumin, read widely across many texts, and excelled in poetry and classical prose.

sentences.zh: 順治六年進士，授刑部主事，以員外郎試高等。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Shunzhi, was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice, and ranked at the top in the assistant department director examination.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the sixth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice and placed at the top of the assistant department director examination.

sentences.zh: 擢山東學政，崇雅黜浮，有冰鑑之譽。

translations.literal: He was promoted to educational commissioner of Shandong; he honored solid elegance and dismissed shallow showmanship, earning a reputation as an icy mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to educational commissioner of Shandong, he favored solid elegance over shallow display and won a reputation as an incorruptible judge of talent—as a "mirror of ice."

sentences.zh: 秩滿，遷江西參議，分守湖西道。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he was transferred to assistant administrator of Jiangxi, stationed to guard the Huxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he was made assistant administrator of Jiangxi with charge of the western Jiangxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 屬郡殘破多盜，遍歷山谷撫循之，人呼為施佛子。

translations.literal: The subordinate prefectures were ravaged and banditry was rife; he traveled through every valley and hill to soothe and rule them, and the people called him "Bodhisattva Shi."
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures under his charge were devastated and infested with bandits; he traveled through hill and valley to restore order, and the people called him "Bodhisattva Shi."

sentences.zh: 嘗作彈子嶺、大阬嘆等篇告長吏，讀者皆曰：「今之元道州也。」

translations.literal: He once wrote pieces such as "Lament at Danzi Ridge" and "Lament at the Great Pit" to admonish senior officials; readers all said, "This is today's Yuan Daozhou."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote such pieces as "Lament at Danzi Ridge" and "Lament at the Great Pit" to reprove local officials; readers said of him, "He is the Yuan Daozhou of our age."

sentences.zh: 尤崇獎風教，所至輒葺書院，會講常數百人。

translations.literal: He especially honored and promoted moral teaching; wherever he went he repaired academies, and lecture gatherings often numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: He made a special point of promoting moral instruction; wherever he went he restored academies, and his lecture gatherings routinely drew hundreds.

sentences.zh: 新淦民兄弟忿戾不睦，一日聞講禮讓孝弟之言，遂相持哭，詣堦下服罪。

translations.literal: Two brothers in Xingan were fierce and at odds; one day, hearing a lecture on ritual, deference, filial piety, and brotherly affection, they embraced and wept, then came before the steps to confess their fault.
translations.idiomatic: Two brothers in Xingan had grown hostile to each other; one day, upon hearing a lecture on ritual, deference, and filial duty, they fell into each other's arms weeping and came before the hall to confess their wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 峽江患虎，製文祝之，俄有虎墮深塹，患遂絕。

translations.literal: Xiajiang suffered from tigers; he composed a prayer-text to them, and soon a tiger fell into a deep ditch—the plague was ended.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiajiang was troubled by tigers, he composed a ritual prayer against them; soon afterward a tiger fell into a deep ditch, and the menace ceased.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，禱雨輒應。

translations.literal: In years of drought, his prayers for rain were invariably answered.
translations.idiomatic: In drought years his prayers for rain were answered without fail.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，裁缺歸。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi reign, his post was abolished and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign his office was abolished and he returned home.

sentences.zh: 民留之不，得，乃醵金創龍岡書院祀之。

translations.literal: The people tried to keep him but could not; thereupon they pooled money to build Longgang Academy and enshrined him there.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to keep him from leaving, the people pooled funds to found Longgang Academy and enshrined him there.

sentences.zh: 初，閏章駐臨江，有清江環城下，民過者咸曰：「是江似使君。」

translations.literal: At first, when Runzhang was stationed at Linjiang, a clear river encircled the base of the city wall; passersby all said, "This river is like the prefect."
translations.idiomatic: When Runzhang was first posted at Linjiang, a clear river wound below the city walls; people passing by would say, "This river is like our prefect."

sentences.zh: 因改名使君江。

translations.literal: For this reason it was renamed Prefect's River.
translations.idiomatic: It was accordingly renamed "Prefect's River."

sentences.zh: 及是傾城送江上，又送至湖。

translations.literal: On this occasion the whole city saw him off on the river, then sent him off again at the lake.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion the whole city turned out to see him off on the river and followed him as far as the lake.

sentences.zh: 以官舫輕，民爭買石膏載之，乃得渡。

translations.literal: Because the official boat was too light, the people competed to buy gypsum to load it, and only then could it cross.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the official boat too light to cross safely, the people vied to buy gypsum and load it aboard so he could get across.

sentences.zh: 十八年，召試鴻博，授翰林院侍講，纂修明史，典試河南。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was summoned to the Special Examination of Eminent Scholars, appointed Hanlin Academy Reader-in-Waiting, compiled the Ming History, and presided over examinations in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was summoned to the poetics examination, appointed Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy, assigned to compile the Ming History, and put in charge of the Henan provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，轉侍讀，尋病卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to Reader, and soon after died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Reader; before long he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 閏章之學，以體仁為本。

translations.literal: Runzhang's learning took embodied benevolence as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Runzhang's scholarship took practical humanity as its foundation.

sentences.zh: 置義田，贍族好，扶掖後進。

translations.literal: He established charity fields, supported clansmen in need, and helped and guided younger scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He set up charity fields to support needy kinsmen and took pains to encourage younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 為文意樸而氣靜，詩與宋琬齊名。

translations.literal: His prose was plain in intention and tranquil in tone; his poetry ranked with Song Wan's in fame.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was plain in thought and calm in spirit; in poetry he ranked with Song Wan.

sentences.zh: 王士禎愛其五言詩，為作摘句圖。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen loved his five-character poems and made for him an "Extracted Lines" painting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen admired his pentameter verse and painted an "Extracted Lines" scroll in his honor.

sentences.zh: 士禎門人問詩法於閏章，閏章曰：「阮亭如華嚴樓閣，彈指即見。

translations.literal: A disciple of Shizhen asked Runzhang about poetic method; Runzhang said, "Ruanting is like the towers and pavilions of the Huayan Sutra—snap your fingers and they appear.
translations.idiomatic: When one of Shizhen's disciples asked Runzhang about the art of poetry, Runzhang replied, "Ruanting is like the jeweled towers of the Avatamsaka Sutra—you need only snap your fingers and they appear.

sentences.zh: 予則不然，如作室者，瓴甓木石，一一就平地築起。」

translations.literal: As for me, it is not so—I am like one who builds a house, raising each tile, brick, and stone up level by level from the ground."
translations.idiomatic: I am not like that. I am like someone building a house—laying each tile, brick, and stone in place from the ground up."

sentences.zh: 論者皆謂其允。

translations.literal: Commentators all said this was apt.
translations.idiomatic: Critics agreed that the comparison was just.

sentences.zh: 著有學餘堂集、矩齋雜記、蠖齋詩話，都八十餘卷。

translations.literal: His works include the Xueyu Tang Collection, Juzhai Miscellanies, and Huozhai Poetry Talk—altogether more than eighty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Xueyu Tang ji, Juzhai zaji, and Huozhai shihua—more than eighty juan in all.

sentences.zh: 閏章與同邑高詠友善，皆工詩，主東南壇坫數十年，時號「宣城體」。

translations.literal: Runzhang was close friends with Gao Yong of the same district; both were skilled in poetry and presided over the literary altars of the southeast for decades, their style being called the "Xuancheng manner."
translations.idiomatic: Runzhang was close friends with his fellow townsman Gao Yong; both were masters of poetry and for decades led literary circles in the southeast, their manner known as the "Xuancheng style."

sentences.zh: 詠，字阮懷。

translations.literal: Yong, styled Ruanhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, styled Ruanhuai.

sentences.zh: 幼稱神童。

translations.literal: As a child he was hailed as a prodigy.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he was hailed as a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 祖維岳，知興國州，清介無長物。

translations.literal: His grandfather Weiyue served as prefect of Xingguo Prefecture; he was upright and austere, with nothing superfluous to his name.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Weiyue, who served as prefect of Xingguo, was incorruptible and owned almost nothing beyond the essentials.

sentences.zh: 詠食貧勵學，屢躓名場，年近六十，始貢入太學。

translations.literal: Yong lived in poverty yet drove himself in study; he repeatedly stumbled on the examination path, and not until he was nearly sixty did he enter the Imperial Academy as a tribute scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Yong lived in poverty but studied hard; he failed repeatedly on the examination circuit and was nearly sixty before he entered the Imperial Academy as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 詞科之舉，詠與焉，授檢討。

translations.literal: When the Special Examination for Eminent Scholars was held, Yong participated and was appointed Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the special scholars' examination and was appointed a reviser.

sentences.zh: 閏章稱其討優入古人。

translations.literal: Runzhang praised him, saying his regulated verse entered the realm of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Runzhang said of his regulated verse that it rivaled the ancients.

sentences.zh: 兼工書畫，有遺山堂、若岩堂集。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in calligraphy and painting; he had the Yishan Tang and Ruoyan Tang collections.
translations.idiomatic: He was also accomplished in calligraphy and painting and left the Yishan Tang and Ruoyan Tang collections.

sentences.zh: 時同舉鴻博又有泰州鄧漢儀，字孝威。

translations.literal: At that time another who was recommended for the poetics examination was Deng Hanyi of Taizhou, styled Xiaowei.
translations.idiomatic: Among those recommended for the special examination at the same time was Deng Hanyi of Taizhou, styled Xiaowei.

sentences.zh: 以年老授中書舍人。

translations.literal: Because of his advanced age, he was granted the post of Secretariat Drafting Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his age, he was appointed a drafting clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 亦工詩。

translations.literal: He too was skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He too was a skilled poet.

sentences.zh: 遊跡所至，輒以名集，逐年編紀，凡七集。

translations.literal: Wherever his travels took him, he would title a collection after the place; compiled year by year, there were seven collections in all.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he traveled he titled a collection after the place, arranging them year by year—seven volumes in all.

sentences.zh: 詩家咸推重之。

translations.literal: Poets all held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Poets everywhere held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 王士祿，字子底，濟南新城人。

translations.literal: Wang Shilu, styled Zidi, was a native of Xincheng in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shilu, styled Zidi, was from Xincheng in Jinan.

sentences.zh: 少工文章，清介有守。

translations.literal: From youth he was adept at literature; he was upright and principled.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he excelled at literary composition and was known for his integrity and self-restraint.

sentences.zh: 弟士祜、士禎從之學詩。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Shihu and Shizhen learned poetry from him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Shihu and Shizhen studied poetry under him.

sentences.zh: 士禎遂為詩家大宗，官尚書，自有傳。

translations.literal: Shizhen in time became a great master among poets; he rose to Minister and has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen went on to become a leading figure in poetry, rose to minister, and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 士祿，順治九年進士。

translations.literal: Shilu became a jinshi in the ninth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu was a jinshi of the ninth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 投牒改官，選萊州府教授，遷國子監助教，擢吏部主事。

translations.literal: He submitted a petition to change office and was selected as instructor of Laizhou Prefecture; he was transferred to assistant instructor of the Imperial Academy, then promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to change posts, was appointed instructor at Laizhou Prefecture, then assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy, and was eventually promoted to a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，以員外郎典試河南，磨勘罣吏議下獄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, serving as an assistant department director he presided over the Henan examinations; in the follow-up review he was implicated by an official censure and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi, while presiding over the Henan examinations as an assistant department director, he was caught up in a post-examination investigation, censured, and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 久之得雪，免歸。

translations.literal: After a long while his name was cleared; he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was cleared, dismissed from office, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 居數年，起原官。

translations.literal: After several years at home, he was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 學士張貞生、御史李棠先後建言獲咎，力直之，人以為難。

translations.literal: Academician Zhang Zhensheng and censor Li Tang successively offered remonstrance and were punished; he spoke up forcefully on their behalf—people regarded this as a difficult thing to do.
translations.idiomatic: When Academician Zhang Zhensheng and Censor Li Tang were punished in turn for their memorials, he spoke out forcefully on their behalf—an act people considered brave.

sentences.zh: 尋又免歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was again dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed again and sent home.

sentences.zh: 母喪，以毀卒，年四十有八。

translations.literal: Upon mourning his mother, he died from grief-induced exhaustion at the age of forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-eight, worn away by grief during mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 其文去雕飾，詩尤閒澹幽肆。

translations.literal: His prose eschewed ornamental flourish; his poetry was especially leisurely, plain, and quietly expansive.
translations.idiomatic: His prose avoided ornament; his poetry was especially calm, understated, and spacious in spirit.

sentences.zh: 有西樵、十笏山房諸集。

translations.literal: He had the Xiqiao and Shihu Shanfang collections.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Xiqiao and Shihu Shanfang collections.

sentences.zh: 士祜，字子測。

translations.literal: Shihu, styled Zice.
translations.idiomatic: Shihu, styled Zice.

sentences.zh: 十歲時，客或疑焦竑字弱侯何耶？

translations.literal: When he was ten, a guest asked in puzzlement why Jiao Hong styled himself Ruohou?
translations.idiomatic: When he was ten, a guest wondered aloud why the scholar Jiao Hong took the style Ruohou?

sentences.zh: 坐客未對，即應聲曰：「此出考工記，'竑其幅廣以為之弱'也。

translations.literal: Before those seated could answer, he replied on the spot: "This comes from the Record of Crafts: 'Broaden the width of the cloth to make the selvage.
translations.idiomatic: Before anyone at the table could answer, he replied at once: "It comes from the Record of Crafts—'Broaden the width of the cloth to make the selvage.

sentences.zh: 咸驚其夙慧。

translations.literal: All were astonished at his precocious brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was astonished by his precocious wit.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，第進士，未仕卒。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi reign he passed the jinshi examination but died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign he passed the jinshi examination but died before he could take office.

sentences.zh: 士禎輯其詩為古缽山人遺集。

translations.literal: Shizhen compiled his poems into the Posthumous Collection of the Old Bowl Mountain Man.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen edited his poems into the Gubo Shanren yiji, the Posthumous Collection of the Hermit of the Old Bowl.

sentences.zh: 當是時，山左詩人王氏兄弟外，有田雯、顏光敏、曹貞吉、王蘋、張篤慶、徐夜皆知名。

translations.literal: At that time, among poets of Shandong aside from the Wang brothers, Tian Wen, Yan Guangmin, Cao Zhenji, Wang Ping, Zhang Duqing, and Xu Ye were all well known.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, apart from the Wang brothers, Shandong poets of note included Tian Wen, Yan Guangmin, Cao Zhenji, Wang Ping, Zhang Duqing, and Xu Ye.

sentences.zh: 雯，字紫綸，號山薑，德州人。

translations.literal: Wen, styled Zilun and known as Shangjiang, was a native of Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, styled Zilun and known as Shangjiang, was from Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年進士，授中書。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the third year of Kangxi and was appointed Secretariat Drafting Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the third year of Kangxi, he was appointed a drafting clerk in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 先是中書以貲郎充，是年始改用進士，遂為例。

translations.literal: Previously the drafting clerk post had been filled by purchased offices; from this year jinshi began to be used instead, and this became the established practice.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Secretariat draftsmen had been purchased offices; from this year on jinshi were appointed instead, and the practice became standard.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to become a director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 督江南學政，所取士多異才。

translations.literal: As superintendent of Jiangnan education, most of the scholars he selected were exceptional talents.
translations.idiomatic: As educational superintendent of Jiangnan, he selected many exceptionally gifted scholars.

sentences.zh: 每按試，從兩騾，二僕隨之，戒有司勿供張。

translations.literal: Whenever he conducted examinations on circuit, he took only two mules and two servants, and warned local officials not to prepare lavish receptions.
translations.idiomatic: On examination tours he traveled with only two mules and two servants, and warned local officials not to put on display for him.

sentences.zh: 授湖廣督糧道，遷光祿寺卿，巡撫江寧，調貴州。

translations.literal: He was appointed grain-intendant of Huguang, transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, served as governor of Jiangning, and was transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Huguang grain intendant, was promoted to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, governed Jiangning, and was later transferred to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 時苗、仲猖獗，粵督議會剿，雯謂：「制苗之法，犯則治之，否則防之而已，無庸動眾勞民也。」

translations.literal: At the time the Miao and Zhong were rampant; the Guangdong governor-general proposed a joint expedition to suppress them. Wen said, "The way to control the Miao is: if they offend, punish them; if not, simply guard against them—that is all. There is no need to mobilize armies and exhaust the people."
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao and Zhong were acting up, the governor-general of Guangdong proposed a joint punitive campaign. Wen argued: "The way to handle the Miao is to punish offenses and otherwise keep them in check—there is no need to mobilize armies and wear out the people."

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was thereupon shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 丁憂，起補刑部侍郎，調戶部，以疾歸。

translations.literal: Upon completing mourning, he was recalled to serve as Vice Minister of Justice, transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and then retired home on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was recalled as Vice Minister of Justice, transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and later retired home because of illness.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，士禎負海內重名，其論詩主風調。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era, Shizhen bore a great reputation throughout the empire; his theory of poetry emphasized tonal grace.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kangxi era Shizhen enjoyed a towering national reputation, and his poetics emphasized tone and modulation.

sentences.zh: 雯負其縱橫排奡之氣，欲以奇麗抗之。

translations.literal: Wen relied on his sweeping, forceful spirit and wished to oppose him with the strange and gorgeous.
translations.idiomatic: Wen, relying on his bold, forceful temperament, sought to counter him with poetry that was strange and gorgeous.

sentences.zh: 有古懽堂集。

translations.literal: He had the Guhuan Tang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Guhuan Tang ji.

sentences.zh: 貞吉，字升六，安丘人。

translations.literal: Zhenji, styled Shengliu, was a native of Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji, styled Shengliu, was from Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 與雯同年進士，禮部郎中。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the same year as Wen and served as director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the same year as Wen, he served as a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 詩格遒練，有實庵詩略。

translations.literal: His poetic style was forceful and refined; he had the Shian Poetry Outline.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was taut and polished; he left the Shian shilue.

sentences.zh: 兼工倚聲，吳綺選名家詞，推為壓卷。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in lyric poetry; when Wu Qi compiled Selected Lyrics of Eminent Masters, his work was chosen to lead the volume.
translations.idiomatic: He was also an accomplished lyricist; when Wu Qi compiled an anthology of master lyricists, Zhenji's piece was placed at the head of the volume.

sentences.zh: 光敏，字遜甫，曲阜人，顏子六十七世孫也。

translations.literal: Guangmin, styled Xunfu, was a native of Qufu and the sixty-seventh-generation descendant of Yan Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Guangmin, styled Xunfu, was from Qufu and a sixty-seventh-generation descendant of Yan Hui.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年進士，除國史院中書舍人。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi and was appointed drafting clerk of the State History Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the sixth year of Kangxi, he was appointed a drafting clerk of the State History Bureau.

sentences.zh: 帝幸太學，加恩四氏子孫，授禮部主事，歷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy, he bestowed favor on descendants of the Four Sages and appointed Guangmin a secretary in the Ministry of Rites; he later served as director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy and extended favor to descendants of the Four Sages, Guangmin was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Rites and later served as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其為詩秀逸深厚，出入錢、劉。

translations.literal: His poetry was elegant, unfettered, and profound, moving within the sphere of Qian Qi and Liu Yuxi.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was graceful, spirited, and richly layered, in the vein of Qian Qi and Liu Yuxi.

sentences.zh: 吳江計東謂足以鼓吹休明。

translations.literal: Ji Dong of Wujiang said it was sufficient to proclaim and glorify the age's brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Dong of Wujiang said his poetry was worthy to celebrate the golden age.

sentences.zh: 雅善鼓琴，精騎射蹋鞠。

translations.literal: He was refined and skilled at the zither, and accomplished at horseback archery and cuju.
translations.idiomatic: He was an elegant zither player and adept at mounted archery and cuju.

sentences.zh: 嘗西登太華，循伊闕，南浮江、淮，觀濤錢塘，溯三衢。

translations.literal: He once climbed Mount Hua in the west, followed the Yique Pass, floated south along the Yangtze and Huai, watched the tidal bore at Qiantang, and traveled upstream through Sanqu.
translations.idiomatic: He once climbed Mount Hua in the west, passed through the Yique Gate, traveled south along the Yangtze and Huai, watched the Qiantang bore, and went upriver through the Sanqu region.

sentences.zh: 所至輒命工為圖，得金石文恆懸之屋壁。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he had artisans make pictures, and any epigraphic texts he obtained he always hung on his walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he traveled he commissioned artists to paint the scenes, and inscribed stones he acquired he always hung on his walls.

sentences.zh: 有樂圃集、舊雨堂集。

translations.literal: He had the Lepu Collection and Jiuyu Tang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Lepu ji and Jiuyu Tang ji.

sentences.zh: 蘋，字秋史，歷城人。

translations.literal: Ping, styled Qiushi, was a native of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ping, styled Qiushi, was from Licheng.

sentences.zh: 少落拓不偶，人目為狂。

translations.literal: In youth he was unmoored and unrestrained; people regarded him as eccentric.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he lived unconstrained and unlucky in life; people considered him unhinged.

sentences.zh: 雯見其詩，為延譽。

translations.literal: When Wen saw his poems, he spoke well of him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Wen read his poetry and lent him his reputation.

sentences.zh: 嘗賦「黃葉」句絕工，人稱為王黃葉。

translations.literal: He once composed a line on yellow leaves of consummate craft; people called him Wang Yellow-Leaf.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote an exceptionally fine line on yellow leaves, and people nicknamed him "Wang Yellow Leaf."

sentences.zh: 康熙四十五年進士，當為令，以母老改成山衛教授。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the forty-fifth year of Kangxi; he was to be appointed a magistrate, but because his mother was elderly he changed to instructor of Chengshan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the forty-fifth year of Kangxi, he was slated to become a county magistrate but, because his mother was old, sought and received appointment as instructor at Chengshan Guard instead.

sentences.zh: 閉門耽吟，介節彌著。

translations.literal: He closed his doors and devoted himself to composing poetry; his upright integrity became even more conspicuous.
translations.idiomatic: He shut himself in to write poetry, and his principled integrity became all the more celebrated.

sentences.zh: 有二十四泉草堂集。

translations.literal: He had the Collection of the Twenty-Four Springs Thatched Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Ershisi Quan Caotang ji.

sentences.zh: 篤慶，字歷久，淄川人。

translations.literal: Duqing, styled Lijiu, was a native of Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Duqing, styled Lijiu, was from Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 拔貢生。

translations.literal: He was a selected tribute graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a selected tribute graduate.

sentences.zh: 早受知施閏章。

translations.literal: From early on he won the recognition of Shi Runzhang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he won the patronage of Shi Runzhang.

sentences.zh: 會徵鴻博，有欲薦之者，辭不應。

translations.literal: When the Special Examination was announced, some wished to recommend him, but he declined and did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When the Special Examination was announced, some wanted to recommend him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 詩以盛唐為宗，有崑崙山房集。

translations.literal: His poetry took the High Tang as its model; he had the Kunlun Mountain Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled his poetry on the High Tang masters and left the Kunlun Shanfang ji.

sentences.zh: 夜，字東痴，新城人，本名元善。

translations.literal: Ye, styled Dongchi, was a native of Xincheng; his original name was Yuanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, styled Dongchi, was from Xincheng; his original name was Yuanshan.

sentences.zh: 舉鴻博，不赴。

translations.literal: He was nominated for the Special Examination but did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated for the Special Examination but did not go.

sentences.zh: 有詩集。

translations.literal: He had a poetry collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left a poetry collection.

sentences.zh: 陳恭尹，字元孝，順德人。

translations.literal: Chen Gongyin, styled Yuanxiao, was a native of Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Gongyin, styled Yuanxiao, was from Shunde.

sentences.zh: 父邦彥，明末殉國難，贈尚書。

translations.literal: His father Bangyan died for the country at the end of the Ming and was posthumously made Minister.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bangyan died for the dynasty at the fall of the Ming and was posthumously made Minister of a department.

sentences.zh: 恭尹少孤，能為詩，習聞忠孝大節。

translations.literal: Gongyin was orphaned young, could compose poetry, and from childhood heard of the great principles of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, Gongyin wrote poetry and grew up steeped in stories of loyalty and filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 棄家出遊，賦姑蘇懷古諸篇，傾動一時。

translations.literal: He abandoned his home to wander abroad, composing such pieces as Recalling Antiquity at Gusu, which stirred the age.
translations.idiomatic: He left home to travel, and poems such as his Recalling Antiquity at Gusu shook the literary world of his day.

sentences.zh: 留閩、浙者七年。

translations.literal: He remained in Fujian and Zhejiang for seven years.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed in Fujian and Zhejiang for seven years.

sentences.zh: 一日，父友遇諸塗，責之曰：「子不歸葬，奈何徒欲一死塞責耶！」

translations.literal: One day a friend of his father met him on the road and rebuked him, saying, "You do not return to bury your father—why do you merely wish to die to discharge your duty!"
translations.idiomatic: One day a friend of his father met him on the road and rebuked him: "You have not returned to bury your father—do you think dying alone will satisfy your obligation?"

sentences.zh: 恭尹泣謝之，乃歸。

translations.literal: Gongyin wept and apologized, then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyin wept and apologized, then went home.

sentences.zh: 既葬父增城，遂渡銅鼓洋訪故人於海外。

translations.literal: After burying his father at Zengcheng, he crossed the Tonggu Sea to visit an old friend overseas.
translations.idiomatic: After burying his father at Zengcheng, he crossed the Tonggu Sea to visit an old friend abroad.

sentences.zh: 久之歸，主何衡家。

translations.literal: After a long time he returned and lodged with the He Heng household.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he came back and lived in the home of He Heng.

sentences.zh: 與陶窳、梁無技及衡弟絳相砥礪，世稱「北田五子」。

translations.literal: Together with Tao Yu, Liang Wuji, and Heng's younger brother Jiang he encouraged one another in study; the world called them the "Five Sons of Beitian."
translations.idiomatic: With Tao Yu, Liang Wuji, and He Heng's younger brother Jiang he spurred one another on in letters, and they were known as the "Five Sons of Beitian."

sentences.zh: 已，复遊贛州，轉泛洞庭，再遊金陵，至汴梁，北渡黃河，徘徊大行之下。

translations.literal: Later he again traveled to Ganzhou, then wandered on Lake Dongting, visited Jinling once more, reached Bianliang, crossed the Yellow River northward, and lingered below the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Later he traveled again to Ganzhou, sailed on Lake Dongting, revisited Nanjing, went on to Kaifeng, crossed the Yellow River northward, and wandered beneath the Taihang range.

sentences.zh: 於是南歸，築室羊城之南以詩文自娛，自稱羅浮布衣。

translations.literal: Then he returned south, built a house south of Yangcheng to amuse himself with poetry and prose, and styled himself the Commoner of Luofu.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned south, built a house south of Guangzhou, and amused himself with poetry and prose, calling himself the Luofu Commoner.

sentences.zh: 恭尹修髯偉貌，氣幹沉深。

translations.literal: Gongyin had a long beard and imposing appearance; his bearing was deep and steady.
translations.idiomatic: Gongyin wore a long beard and had a commanding presence, with a grave and steady air.

sentences.zh: 其為詩激昂頓挫，足以發其哀怨之思。

translations.literal: His poetry was stirring and forceful, sufficient to express his thoughts of resentment and sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: His verse rose and fell with passionate force, enough to give voice to his grief and indignation.

sentences.zh: 自言平生文辭多取諸胸臆，僕僕道塗，稽古未遑也。

translations.literal: He said himself that his life's writings mostly came from his own breast; always on the road, he had no leisure to study antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He said that most of his life's writing came straight from the heart; always on the road, he had never had time for scholarly antiquarianism.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 著獨漉堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Dulutang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Dulutang ji.

sentences.zh: 王隼取恭尹詩合屈大均、梁佩蘭共刻之，為嶺南三家集。

translations.literal: Wang Sun took Gongyin's poems together with those of Qu Dajun and Liang Peilan and printed them jointly as the Collection of the Three Masters of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sun collected Gongyin's poems together with those of Qu Dajun and Liang Peilan and published them as the Lingnan Sanjia ji.

sentences.zh: 大均，字介子，番禺人。

translations.literal: Dajun, styled Jiezi, was a native of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Dajun, styled Jiezi, was from Panyu.

sentences.zh: 初名紹隆，遇變為僧，中年返初服。

translations.literal: His original name was Shaolong; when calamity struck he became a monk, and in middle age he returned to lay dress.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Shaolong, he became a monk when disaster struck and returned to lay life in middle age.

sentences.zh: 工詩，高渾兀奡，有翁山詩文集。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry—lofty, full-bodied, and boldly unconstrained—and had the Wengshan Poetry and Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: A fine poet, his verse was lofty, resonant, and boldly free; he left the Wengshan shiwen ji.

sentences.zh: 佩蘭，字芝五，南海人。

translations.literal: Peilan, styled Zhiwu, was a native of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: Peilan, styled Zhiwu, was from Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 童時日記數千言。

translations.literal: As a child he could memorize several thousand characters each day.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he could memorize several thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 順治十四年鄉試第一，又三十一年始成進士，年六十矣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi he placed first in the provincial examination; only thirty-one years later did he become a jinshi, at the age of sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the provincial examination in Shunzhi 14, but did not pass the palace examination until thirty-one years later, when he was sixty.

sentences.zh: 佩蘭夙負詩名。

translations.literal: Peilan had long borne a reputation in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Peilan had been famous for his poetry from early on.

sentences.zh: 既選庶吉士，館中推為祭酒。

translations.literal: After selection as a Hanlin bachelor, he was acclaimed in the academy as its toastmaster.
translations.idiomatic: Once chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, he was regarded as the leading spirit of the academy.

sentences.zh: 不一年假歸，里居十五載。

translations.literal: Within a year he took leave to return home and lived locally for fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he took leave and went home, where he lived for fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 會詔飭詞臣就職，復入都。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered literary officials to take up their posts, he again entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered literary officials back to duty, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 踰月散館，以不習國書罷歸。

translations.literal: After a month the Hanlin probation ended; because he had not mastered Manchu script he was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: A month later, when the Hanlin probation ended, he was dismissed for failing to master Manchu and sent home.

sentences.zh: 結蘭湖社，與同邑程可則，番禺王邦畿、方殿元及恭尹等稱「嶺南七子」。

translations.literal: He formed the Orchid Lake Society, and together with his fellow townsman Cheng Keze, Wang Bangji and Fang Dianyuan of Panyu, and Gongyin and others he was called the "Seven Masters of Lingnan."
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Lanhu Society, and with his fellow townsman Cheng Keze, Wang Bangji and Fang Dianyuan of Panyu, Chen Gongyin, and others he was known as one of the "Seven Masters of Lingnan."

sentences.zh: 有六瑩堂集。

translations.literal: He had the Liuyingtang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Liuyingtang ji.

sentences.zh: 可則，字週量。

translations.literal: Keze, styled Zhouliang.
translations.idiomatic: Keze, styled Zhouliang.

sentences.zh: 順治九年會試第一。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shunzhi he placed first in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the metropolitan examination in Shunzhi 9.

sentences.zh: 以磨勘停殿試歸，益恣探經史。

translations.literal: Because of a document review his palace examination was suspended and he returned home, where he explored the classics and history even more freely.
translations.idiomatic: A document review halted his palace examination and sent him home, where he threw himself even more freely into the classics and history.

sentences.zh: 十七年，始應閣試，授內閣中書，累遷兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he at last took the palace examination, was appointed a Secretariat drafter, and was successively promoted to Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he finally took the palace examination, was appointed a Secretariat drafter, and rose to Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 出知桂林府，以敏幹稱。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Guilin, he was known for quick competence.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as prefect of Guilin, he was praised for sharp and capable administration.

sentences.zh: 其官都下，與宋琬、施閏章、王士祿、士禎、陳廷敬、沈荃、曹爾堪輩為文酒之會，吳之振合刻八家詩選。

translations.literal: While serving at court he joined Song Wan, Shi Runzhang, Wang Shilu, Wang Shizhen, Chen Tingjing, Shen Quan, Cao Erkan, and others in literary gatherings over wine; Wu Zhizhen compiled and printed the Eight Masters Poetry Selection.
translations.idiomatic: While at court he joined Song Wan, Shi Runzhang, Wang Shilu, Wang Shizhen, Chen Tingjing, Shen Quan, Cao Erkan, and others in literary gatherings over wine, and Wu Zhizhen published their Eight Masters Poetry Selection.

sentences.zh: 可則詩曰海日堂集。

translations.literal: Keze's poetry collection is called the Hairi Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Keze's poetry is collected in the Hairi Tang ji.

sentences.zh: 殿元，字蒙章。

translations.literal: Dianyuan, styled Mengzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Dianyuan, styled Mengzhang.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the third year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Kangxi 3.

sentences.zh: 歷知剡城、江寧等縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Shancheng, Jiangning, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Shancheng, Jiangning, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 置祭田以贍兄弟，而自攜長子還、次子朝僑寓蘇州。

translations.literal: He established sacrificial fields to support his brothers, but himself took his eldest son Huan and second son Chao to live abroad in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He set aside sacrificial land to support his brothers, but took his eldest son Huan and second son Chao to live in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 父子皆有詩名。

translations.literal: Father and sons all had reputations in poetry.
