translations.idiomatic: Father and sons were all known for their poetry.

sentences.zh: 所稱「嶺南七子」，併其二子數之也。

translations.literal: The so-called "Seven Masters of Lingnan" counted his two sons among the number.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called "Seven Masters of Lingnan" included his two sons in the count.

sentences.zh: 殿元著九谷集；

translations.literal: Dianyuan authored the Jiugu Collection;
translations.idiomatic: Dianyuan wrote the Jiugu ji;

sentences.zh: 還，靈州集；

translations.literal: Huan, the Lingzhou Collection;
translations.idiomatic: Huan, the Lingzhou ji;

sentences.zh: 朝，勺園集。

translations.literal: Chao, the Shaoyuan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Chao, the Shaoyuan ji.

sentences.zh: 佩蘭之友又有南海吳文煒，字山帶。

translations.literal: Among Peilan's friends was also Wu Wenwei of Nanhai, styled Shandai.
translations.idiomatic: Among Peilan's friends was Wu Wenwei of Nanhai, styled Shandai.

sentences.zh: 十歲工詩，兼善繪事。

translations.literal: At ten he was skilled at poetry and also good at painting.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he was already an accomplished poet and painter.

sentences.zh: 時初效長吉體，務為險語取快。

translations.literal: At first he imitated Li He's style, striving for startling phrases to win quick effect.
translations.idiomatic: At first he wrote in the manner of Li He, chasing daring lines for instant effect.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年舉人。

translations.literal: He became a juren in the thirty-second year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A juren of Kangxi 32.

sentences.zh: 計偕，卒於旅舍。

translations.literal: On the journey to the capital for the examination he died at an inn.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey to the capital for the examination he died at an inn.

sentences.zh: 有金茅山堂集，恭尹為之序。

translations.literal: He had the Jinmao Mountain Hall Collection, for which Gongyin wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Jinmaoshantang ji, with a preface by Chen Gongyin.

sentences.zh: 王隼，字蒲衣，番禺人。

translations.literal: Wang Sun, styled Puyi, was a native of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sun, styled Puyi, was from Panyu.

sentences.zh: 父邦畿，明副貢生。

translations.literal: His father Bangji was a supplemental tribute graduate of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bangji was a supplemental tribute graduate under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 隱居羅浮，嶺南七子之一也。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion on Mount Luofu and was one of the Seven Masters of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion on Mount Luofu and was one of the Seven Masters of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 有耳鳴集。

translations.literal: He had the Ermimg Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Ermimg ji.

sentences.zh: 隼七歲能詩。

translations.literal: Sun at seven could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Sun was writing poetry by the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 慕道術，早歲棄家入丹霞，尋入匡廬，居太乙峰，六七年始歸。

translations.literal: He admired Daoist arts; in early youth he abandoned his family and entered Danxia, then went on to Mount Lu, lived at Taiyi Peak, and only returned after six or seven years.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn to Daoist practice, he left home young for Danxia, then Mount Lu, where he lived on Taiyi Peak and did not return for six or seven years.

sentences.zh: 性喜琵琶，終日理書卷，生事窘不顧，惟取琵琶彈之。

translations.literal: By nature he loved the pipa; all day he managed his books, paid no heed to his straitened livelihood, and only took up the pipa to play.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the pipa; he spent his days among books, ignored his poverty, and played nothing but the pipa.

sentences.zh: 琵琶聲急，即其窘益甚。

translations.literal: When the pipa sounded urgently, his straits grew even worse.
translations.idiomatic: The more urgently the pipa sounded, the worse his poverty became.

sentences.zh: 著大樗堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Dachu Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Dachu Tang ji.

sentences.zh: 妻潘，女瑤湘，並工詩。

translations.literal: His wife Pan and his daughter Yaoxiang were both skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Pan and his daughter Yaoxiang were both accomplished poets.

sentences.zh: 馮班，字定遠，常熟人。

translations.literal: Feng Ban, styled Dingyuan, was a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ban, styled Dingyuan, was from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 淹雅善持論，顧性不諧俗。

translations.literal: Deeply cultured and good at holding forth in debate, yet by nature he did not harmonize with the world.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply learned and sharp in debate, he was by nature at odds with conventional society.

sentences.zh: 說詩力牴嚴羽，尤不取江西宗派，出入義山、牧之、飛卿之間。

translations.literal: In discussing poetry he strongly opposed Yan Yu, especially rejected the Jiangxi school, and moved between the styles of Yishan, Muzhi, and Feiqing.
translations.idiomatic: In poetics he fiercely opposed Yan Yu, rejected the Jiangxi school above all, and ranged between Li Shangyin, Du Mu, and Wen Tingyun.

sentences.zh: 書四體皆精。

translations.literal: He was accomplished in all four script styles.
translations.idiomatic: He was master of all four major calligraphic scripts.

sentences.zh: 著鈍吟集。

translations.literal: He authored the Dunyin Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Dunyin ji.

sentences.zh: 趙執信於近代文家少許可者，見班所著獨折服，至具衣冠拜之。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhixin rarely approved any writer of recent times, but on seeing Ban's works he alone was won over, even dressing in full formal robes to pay him homage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhixin seldom approved any writer of his day, but Ban's work alone won him over—so much so that he put on full formal dress to pay him homage.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁其墓，寫「私淑門人」刺焚塚前。

translations.literal: Once he visited Ban's tomb, wrote the card "Private Disciple," and burned it before the grave.
translations.idiomatic: Once he visited Ban's tomb, wrote "Private Disciple" on a card, and burned it before the grave.

sentences.zh: 其為名流所傾仰類此。

translations.literal: The esteem shown him by famous men was like this.
translations.idiomatic: The admiration he won from leading men of letters was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 宗元鼎，字定九，江都人。

translations.literal: Zong Yuanding, styled Dingjiu, was a native of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yuanding, styled Dingjiu, was from Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 七歲詠梅，遠近傳誦其句。

translations.literal: At seven he composed a poem on plum blossoms, and near and far people circulated his lines.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he wrote a poem on plum blossoms, and his lines were passed around far and wide.

sentences.zh: 堂有古梅一株，人謂之「宗郎梅」。

translations.literal: In his hall stood an ancient plum tree; people called it "Young Master Zong's Plum."
translations.idiomatic: An ancient plum tree stood in his hall, and people called it "Young Master Zong's Plum."

sentences.zh: 性狷而孝，釜甑屢空，未嘗以貧告人。

translations.literal: By nature stern and filial; pots and pans were often empty, yet he never complained of poverty to others.
translations.idiomatic: Stern in temperament and deeply filial, he often had nothing in the larder, yet never complained of poverty to anyone.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，貢太學，銓注州同知。

translations.literal: In early Kangxi he entered the Imperial Academy as a tribute student and was selected for appointment as sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kangxi he was sent as a tribute student to the Imperial Academy and selected for appointment as sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 未仕卒。

translations.literal: He died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 元鼎與從弟元豫、觀，從子之瑾、之瑜皆工詩，有「廣陵五宗」之目。

translations.literal: Yuanding, together with his younger cousins Yuan Yu and Yuan Guan and his nephews Zhi Jin and Zhi Yu, were all skilled at poetry; they were known as the "Five Zongs of Guangling."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanding, his younger cousins Yuan Yu and Yuan Guan, and his nephews Zhi Jin and Zhi Yu were all accomplished poets and were known as the "Five Zongs of Guangling."

sentences.zh: 劉體仁，字公霝，潁州人。

translations.literal: Liu Tiren, styled Gongyin, was a native of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tiren, styled Gongyin, was from Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 順治中進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the Shunzhi reign.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the Shunzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 有家難，棄官從孫奇逢講學。

translations.literal: When family trouble arose he abandoned office to study under Sun Qifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When family trouble struck he resigned his post to study under Sun Qifeng.

sentences.zh: 後官考功郎中。

translations.literal: Later he served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel's merit-evaluation bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 體仁喜作畫，鑑識其精，又工鼓琴。

translations.literal: Tiren loved painting and had refined connoisseurship; he was also skilled at playing the zither.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren loved to paint and had a sharp eye for art; he was also an accomplished zither player.

sentences.zh: 與汪琬、王士禎友善，著七頌堂集。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Wang Wan and Wang Shizhen and authored the Qisong Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: A friend of Wang Wan and Wang Shizhen, he left the Qisong Tang ji.

sentences.zh: 士禎稱其詩似孟東野；

translations.literal: Shizhen said his poetry resembled that of Meng Dongye;
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen said his poetry resembled Meng Jiao's;

sentences.zh: 又言今日善學才調集者無如元鼎，學西昆體者無如吳殳。

translations.literal: He also said that today none equals Yuanding in learning from the Caidiaoji, and none equals Wu Shu in learning the Xikun style.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that among living poets none matched Yuanding in mastering the Caidiaoji tradition, and none matched Wu Shu in the Xikun manner.

sentences.zh: 殳，字修齡，原名喬，亦常熟人也。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Xiuling, original name Qiao, was also a native of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Xiuling, originally named Qiao, was also from Changshu.

sentences.zh: 著圍爐詩話，云：「意喻則米，炊而為飯者文，釀而為酒者詩乎？」

translations.literal: He authored Weilu shihua, saying, "Meaning is like rice—is what is cooked into food prose, and what is fermented into wine poetry?"
translations.idiomatic: In his Weilu shihua he wrote: "Meaning is like rice—is prose the cooked grain, and poetry the wine brewed from it?"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「詩之中須有人在。」

translations.literal: He also said, "In poetry there must be a person present."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "A poem must have a living person in it."

sentences.zh: 執信嘆為知言。

translations.literal: Zhixin sighed that this was true insight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhixin sighed that this was the voice of genuine understanding.

sentences.zh: 胡承諾，字君信，天門人。

translations.literal: Hu Chengnuo, styled Junxin, was a native of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Chengnuo, styled Junxin, was from Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時舉人。

translations.literal: He was a juren in the Chongzhen reign.
translations.idiomatic: A juren of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 明亡後，隱居不仕，臥天門巾、柘間。

translations.literal: After the fall of the Ming he lived in seclusion and did not take office, dwelling between the Jin and Zhe hills of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: After the Ming fell he lived in seclusion and refused office, dwelling among the Jin and Zhe hills near Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，部銓縣職。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi the ministry selected him for a county post.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12 the ministry selected him for a county appointment.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，檄徵入都，六年，至京師，未幾告歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kangxi a summons ordered him to the capital; in the sixth year he reached the capital, and before long he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 he was summoned to the capital by official order; he arrived in Kangxi 6 and before long asked to go home.

sentences.zh: 構石莊於西村，窮年誦讀，著繹志二十餘萬言。

translations.literal: He built the Stone Villa in West Village, spent year after year reading and reciting, and wrote the Yizhi in more than two hundred thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Stone Villa in West Village, devoted himself to reading year round, and wrote the Yizhi, more than two hundred thousand characters in all.

sentences.zh: 繹志者，繹己所志也。

translations.literal: Yizhi means to unfold what one sets one's heart upon.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi means to unfold one's own aspirations.

sentences.zh: 原本道德，切近人事，為有體有用之學。

translations.literal: It was rooted in morality and virtue, close to human affairs, and constituted learning with both substance and practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Rooted in moral principle and grounded in human affairs, it was learning with both substance and practical application.

sentences.zh: 其吏治篇曰：「古之人不敢輕言變法也。

translations.literal: Its chapter on governance of officials says, "The ancients did not dare speak lightly of changing the laws.
translations.idiomatic: Its chapter on official administration says: "The ancients did not dare speak lightly of changing the laws.

sentences.zh: 必有明哲之德，於精粗之理無所不昭，不獨精者為之地，即粗者亦為之地，有和悅之氣，於異同之見無所不容，不獨同者樂其然，即異者亦樂其然；

translations.literal: There must be the virtue of clear wisdom, illuminating all principles fine and coarse alike—not only making room for the refined but also for the coarse; there must be a spirit of harmony and ease, embracing all views whether alike or different—not only making those who agree rejoice in it, but also those who differ.
translations.idiomatic: One must possess the virtue of clear wisdom, illuminating every principle fine and coarse alike—not only making room for the refined but for the coarse as well; one must have a spirit of harmony and ease, embracing every view whether alike or different—not only pleasing those who agree, but those who differ as well;

sentences.zh: 然後可奪其久安之法，授以更新之制，而民不驚顧不讙譁也。」

translations.literal: Only then could one take away their long-established laws and grant them renewed institutions, and the people would neither start in alarm nor break into clamor."
translations.idiomatic: only then could one take away long-established laws and grant new institutions, and the people would neither start in alarm nor break into clamor."

sentences.zh: 租庸篇曰：「欲富國者，當使君民之力皆常有餘。

translations.literal: The chapter on land tax and corvée labor says, "One who wishes to enrich the state should keep both the ruler's strength and the people's strength always in surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter on land tax and corvée says: "One who wishes to enrich the state should keep both the ruler's strength and the people's strength always in surplus.

sentences.zh: 民之餘力，生於君之約取；

translations.literal: The people's surplus strength comes from the ruler's restrained exactions;
translations.idiomatic: The people's surplus strength comes from the ruler's restraint in exactions;

sentences.zh: 君之餘力，生於民之各足。」

translations.literal: the ruler's surplus strength comes from each of the people having enough."
translations.idiomatic: the ruler's surplus strength comes from each of the people having enough for themselves."

sentences.zh: 他篇準此。

translations.literal: Other chapters follow this pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The other chapters follow the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 承諾自擬其書於徐幹中論、顏氏家訓。

translations.literal: Chengnuo himself compared his book to Xu Gan's Zhonglun and the Yan Family Instructions.
translations.idiomatic: Chengnuo himself likened his book to Xu Gan's Zhonglun and the Yan Family Instructions.

sentences.zh: 或頗譏其掇拾群言，未能如古人自成一家之說，然大體必軌於正。

translations.literal: Some criticized it for gathering sayings from many sources and failing, like the ancients, to form a school of thought of its own, but on the whole it always kept to the correct path.
translations.idiomatic: Some criticized it for assembling others' words rather than forming a school of thought of its own like the ancients, but on the whole it always kept to the correct path.

sentences.zh: 又有讀書錄，則鱗雜細碎，殆繹志取材之餘矣。

translations.literal: He also had the Reading Notes, which were miscellaneous and fragmentary—likely the leftover material gathered while composing the Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: He also left Reading Notes, a miscellaneous collection of fragments—likely leftover material gathered while composing the Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died, at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-sixth year, at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 同時篤志撰述，其學與承諾相上下者，又有賀貽孫，字子翼，永新人；

translations.literal: At the same time, devoted to writing and whose learning matched Chengnuo's, there was also He Yisun, styled Ziyi, a native of Yongxin;
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was He Yisun, styled Ziyi, of Yongxin, equally devoted to writing and Chengnuo's peer in learning;

sentences.zh: 唐甄，字鑄萬，達州人。

translations.literal: Tang Zhen, styled Zhuwan, was a native of Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: and Tang Zhen, styled Zhuwan, from Dazhou.

sentences.zh: 貽孫九歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Yisun at nine could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: Yisun was writing prose by the age of nine.

sentences.zh: 明季社事盛行，貽孫與萬茂先、陳士業、徐巨源、曾堯臣輩結社豫章。

translations.literal: In the late Ming, literary societies flourished; Yisun together with Wan Maoxian, Chen Shiye, Xu Juyuan, Zeng Yaochén, and others formed a society at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, when literary societies flourished, Yisun formed a society at Nanchang with Wan Maoxian, Chen Shiye, Xu Juyuan, Zeng Yaochén, and others.

sentences.zh: 及明亡，遂不出。

translations.literal: When the Ming fell, he then did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming fell, he withdrew from public life entirely.

sentences.zh: 順治初，學使者慕其名，特列貢榜，避不就。

translations.literal: In early Shunzhi the provincial education commissioner, admiring his name, specially placed him on the tribute list, but he avoided it and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shunzhi the provincial education commissioner, admiring his reputation, specially placed him on the tribute list, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史笪重光欲舉應鴻博，書至，貽孫愀然曰：「吾逃世而不逃名，名之累人實甚。

translations.literal: The touring censor Da Chongguang wished to recommend him for the Special Examination; when the letter arrived, Yisun said mournfully, "I fled the world but did not flee fame—how greatly fame burdens a man!
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor Da Chongguang wished to recommend him for the Special Examination; when the letter arrived, Yisun said mournfully: "I fled the world but not fame—how greatly fame burdens a man!

sentences.zh: 吾將從此逝矣！」

translations.literal: I shall depart from here!"
translations.idiomatic: I shall vanish from here!"

sentences.zh: 乃翦發衣緇，結茅深山，無復能踪蹟之者。

translations.literal: He then cut his hair, put on monastic garb, built a thatched hut deep in the mountains, and no one could track him down again.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut his hair, put on monastic garb, built a thatched hut deep in the mountains, and was never traced again.

sentences.zh: 晚年窮益甚。

translations.literal: In his later years his poverty grew even worse.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he grew even poorer.

sentences.zh: 著有易觸、詩觸、詩筏、騷筏，又著水田居激書。

translations.literal: He authored Yichu, Shichu, Shifa, and Saofa, and also wrote the Jishu of the Waterfield Dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Yichu, Shichu, Shifa, and Saofa, and also the Shuitian ju Jishu.

sentences.zh: 激書者，備名物以寄興，紀逸事以垂勸，援古鑑今，錯綜比類。

translations.literal: The Jishu assembles names and things to convey its inspiration, records unusual events to hand down admonition, draws on antiquity to mirror the present, and weaves comparisons together in intricate arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: The Jishu assembles names and things to convey its themes, records unusual events to hand down admonition, draws on antiquity to mirror the present, and weaves comparisons together in intricate arrangement.

sentences.zh: 言之不足，故長言之，長言之不足，故危悚惕厲，必暢所欲言而後已，激濁揚清。

translations.literal: When words were insufficient, he therefore spoke at length; when speaking at length was insufficient, he therefore wrote with urgency, alarm, vigilance, and sternness, never stopping until he had fully expressed himself, stirring up the muddy and raising up the clear.
translations.idiomatic: When words were not enough, he spoke at length; when length was not enough, he wrote with urgency, alarm, vigilance, and sternness, never stopping until he had fully expressed himself—stirring up the muddy and raising up the clear.

sentences.zh: 始自貴因，終於空明，凡四十一篇。

translations.literal: It begins with "Honoring Causation" and ends with "Empty Clarity," forty-one chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: It begins with "Honoring Causation" and ends with "Empty Clarity"—forty-one chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 甄性至孝，父喪，獨棲殯室三年。

translations.literal: Zhen was deeply filial by nature; when his father died, he lived alone in the mourning hall beside the coffin for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial by nature, Zhen lived alone in the mourning hall beside his father's coffin for three years.

sentences.zh: 以世亂不克還葬，遂葬父虎丘。

translations.literal: Because the age was in turmoil he could not return the body for burial at home, and so buried his father at Tiger Hill.
translations.idiomatic: Because the times were too chaotic to return the body home, he buried his father at Tiger Hill.

sentences.zh: 順治十四年舉人。

translations.literal: He became a juren in the fourteenth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: A juren of Shunzhi 14.

sentences.zh: 選長子令，下車，即導民樹桑凡八十萬本，民利賴焉。

translations.literal: Selected as magistrate of Changzi, as soon as he took office he guided the people to plant mulberry trees—eight hundred thousand in all—and the people relied on this for their livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as magistrate of Changzi, he immediately guided the people to plant eight hundred thousand mulberry trees, on which the people came to rely.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐逃人詿誤去官。

translations.literal: Before long, because of entanglement in a fugitive case, he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was dismissed over entanglement in a fugitive case.

sentences.zh: 僦居吳市，炊煙屢絕，至採枸杞葉為食，衣敗絮，著述不輟。

translations.literal: He rented a dwelling in the Wu market; cooking smoke often ceased altogether, until he gathered wolfberry leaves for food, wore tattered cotton padding, and yet never stopped writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rented a room in Suzhou; cooking fires often went out altogether, and he gathered wolfberry leaves for food and wore tattered cotton padding, yet never stopped writing.

sentences.zh: 始志在權衡天下，作衡書，後以連蹇不遇，更名潛書。

translations.literal: At first his aim was to weigh and balance the realm, and he wrote the Hengshu; later, because of repeated setbacks and lack of recognition, he renamed it the Qianshu.
translations.idiomatic: At first his aim was to weigh and balance the realm, and he wrote the Hengshu; later, after repeated setbacks and lack of recognition, he renamed it the Qianshu.

sentences.zh: 分上下篇，上篇論學，始辨儒，終博觀，凡五十篇；

translations.literal: It is divided into upper and lower sections; the upper section discusses learning, beginning with distinguishing the Ru and ending with broad observation—fifty chapters in all;
translations.idiomatic: It is divided into upper and lower sections: the upper discusses learning, beginning with distinguishing the Ru and ending with broad observation—fifty chapters in all;

sentences.zh: 下篇論政，始尚治，終潛存，凡四十七篇。

translations.literal: the lower section discusses governance, beginning with esteeming order and ending with hidden preservation—forty-seven chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: the lower discusses governance, beginning with esteeming order and ending with hidden preservation—forty-seven chapters in all.

sentences.zh: 上觀天道，下察人事，遠正古蹟，近度今宜，根於心而致之行，非虛言也。

translations.literal: Looking up it observes the Way of Heaven, looking down it examines human affairs; from afar it corrects ancient traces, from near it measures what suits the present; rooted in the heart and carried into action—it is not empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: Looking up it observes the Way of Heaven, looking down it examines human affairs; from afar it corrects ancient traces, from near it measures what suits the present—rooted in the heart and carried into action, not empty talk.

sentences.zh: 寧都魏禧見而歎之曰：「是周、秦之書也，今猶有此人乎！」

translations.literal: Wei Xi of Ningdu saw it and sighed, saying, "This is a book of Zhou and Qin times—can such a man still exist today!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xi of Ningdu saw it and sighed: "This is a book of Zhou and Qin times—can such a man still exist today!"

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 阿什坦，字金龍，完顏氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Ashitan, styled Jinlong, of the Wanyan clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ashitan, styled Jinlong, of the Wanyan clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，授刑科給事中。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of Shunzhi and was appointed a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 9, he was appointed a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 初繙譯大學、中庸、孝經諸書，詔刊行。

translations.literal: At first the Great Learning, Doctrine of the Mean, Classic of Filial Piety, and other books were translated, and an edict ordered their publication.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Learning, Doctrine of the Mean, Classic of Filial Piety, and other books were first translated, an edict ordered their publication.

sentences.zh: 阿什坦上言；

translations.literal: Ashitan submitted a memorial;
translations.idiomatic: Ashitan submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「學者宜以聖賢為期，經史為導，此外無益雜書當屏絕。」

translations.literal: "Students should take the sages as their goal and the classics and histories as their guide; aside from these, unprofitable miscellaneous books should be cast aside."
translations.idiomatic: "Students should take the sages as their goal and the classics and histories as their guide; aside from these, unprofitable miscellaneous books should be cast aside."

sentences.zh: 又請嚴旗人男女之別，定部院九品之制，俱報可。

translations.literal: He also requested strict separation between men and women among banner people and the establishment of a nine-rank system for ministries and boards—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested strict separation between men and women among banner people and the establishment of a nine-rank system for ministries and boards—all were approved.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，罷職家居。

translations.literal: In early Kangxi he was dismissed from office and lived at home.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kangxi he was dismissed and lived at home.

sentences.zh: 鰲拜專政，欲令一見終不往。

translations.literal: When Oboi monopolized power and wished to summon him for an audience, he never went.
translations.idiomatic: When Oboi monopolized power and wished to summon him for an audience, he never went.

sentences.zh: 嗣以薦起，聖祖召問節用愛人，對曰：「節用莫要於寡欲，愛人莫先於用賢。」

translations.literal: Later, through recommendation, he was restored to office; the Kangxi Emperor summoned him and asked about thrift and caring for the people. He replied, "In thrift nothing is more essential than few desires; in caring for the people nothing comes before employing the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Later, through recommendation, he was restored to office; the Kangxi Emperor summoned him and asked about thrift and caring for the people. He replied: "In thrift nothing is more essential than few desires; in caring for the people nothing comes before employing the worthy."

sentences.zh: 聖祖顧左右曰：「此我朝大儒也！」

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor turned to those beside him and said, "This is a great Confucian of our dynasty!"
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor turned to those beside him and said: "This is a great Confucian of our dynasty!"

sentences.zh: 著有大學中庸講義及奏稿。

translations.literal: He authored commentaries on the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, as well as memorial drafts.
translations.idiomatic: His works include commentaries on the Great Learning and Doctrine of the Mean, as well as memorial drafts.

sentences.zh: 孫留保，以掌院學士充明史總裁，附王蘭生傳。

translations.literal: His grandson Liubao served as chief compiler of the History of the Ming as a Grand Secretary of the Hanlin Academy; see the biography of Wang Lansheng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Liubao served as chief compiler of the History of the Ming as a Grand Secretary of the Hanlin Academy; see the biography of Wang Lansheng.

sentences.zh: 劉淇，字武仲，漢軍鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Liu Qi, styled Wuzhong, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi, styled Wuzhong, was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 弟汶，舉人。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wen was a juren.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wen was a juren.

sentences.zh: 受知世宗，時有二難之目。

translations.literal: Both won the recognition of the Yongzheng Emperor and at the time were known as the "Two Qis."
translations.idiomatic: Both won the Yongzheng Emperor's favor and at the time were known as the "Two Qis."

sentences.zh: 著周易通說、禹貢說、助字辨略、堂邑志、衛園集。

translations.literal: He authored Exposition of the Zhou Changes, Exposition of the Tribute of Yu, Brief Discrimination of Auxiliary Characters, Gazetteer of Tangyi, and the Weiyuan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Exposition of the Zhou Changes, Exposition of the Tribute of Yu, Brief Discrimination of Auxiliary Characters, Gazetteer of Tangyi, and the Weiyuan ji.

sentences.zh: 金德純，字素公，漢軍正紅旗人。

translations.literal: Jin Dechun, styled Sugong, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Dechun, styled Sugong, was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 著旗軍志。

translations.literal: He authored the Record of Banner Armies.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Record of Banner Armies.

sentences.zh: 傅澤洪，字育甫，漢軍旗人。

translations.literal: Fu Zehong, styled Yufu, was a Han Bannerman.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zehong, styled Yufu, was a Han Bannerman.

sentences.zh: 累官江南淮揚道。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Intendant of the Huai-Yang Circuit in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Intendant of the Huai-Yang Circuit in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 著行水金鑑百七十五卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Golden Mirror of Water Control in one hundred seventy-five juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Golden Mirror of Water Control in one hundred seventy-five juan.

sentences.zh: 汪琬，字苕文，長洲人。

translations.literal: Wang Wan, styled Tiaowen, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wan, styled Tiaowen, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，自奮於學，銳意為古文辭。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he applied himself vigorously to study and was intent on writing classical prose.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he drove himself in study and was intent on writing classical prose.

sentences.zh: 於易、詩、書、春秋、三禮、喪服咸有發明。

translations.literal: In the Changes, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, Three Rites, and Mourning Dress he all had original insights.
translations.idiomatic: He had original insights into the Changes, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, Three Rites, and Mourning Dress.

sentences.zh: 性狷介。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stern and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 深嘆古今文家好名寡實，鮮自重特立，故務為經世有用之學。

translations.literal: He deeply lamented that writers ancient and modern loved fame but lacked substance and rarely held themselves to independent integrity; therefore he devoted himself to learning useful for governing the age.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply lamented that writers ancient and modern loved fame but lacked substance and rarely held themselves to independent integrity; therefore he devoted himself to learning useful for governing the age.

sentences.zh: 其於當世人物，褒譏不少寬假。

translations.literal: In his treatment of people of his day, praise and censure alike were never sparing.
translations.idiomatic: In his judgments of contemporaries, praise and censure alike were never sparing.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，授主事，再遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi, was appointed a section chief, and was twice promoted to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 12, he was appointed a section chief and twice promoted to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 坐累降兵馬司指揮，能舉其職，不以秩卑自沮。

translations.literal: Because of entanglement in a case he was demoted to commander in the Horse Bureau, yet he could fulfill his duties and did not let his low rank discourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to commander in the Horse Bureau over entanglement in a case, he still fulfilled his duties and was not discouraged by his low rank.

sentences.zh: 任滿，稍遷戶部主事，民送之溢衢卷。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was gradually promoted to section chief in the Ministry of Revenue; the people saw him off until the streets overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was promoted to section chief in the Ministry of Revenue; the people saw him off until the streets overflowed.

sentences.zh: 榷江寧西新關，以疾假歸。

translations.literal: He supervised the West New Customs at Jiangning, then took sick leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the West New Customs at Nanjing, then took sick leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 結廬堯峰山，閉戶撰述，不交世事，學者稱堯峰先生。

translations.literal: He built a hut on Mount Yaofeng, closed his doors to write, had no dealings with worldly affairs, and scholars called him Master Yaofeng.
translations.idiomatic: He built a hut on Mount Yaofeng, closed his doors to write, kept aloof from worldly affairs, and scholars called him Master Yaofeng.

sentences.zh: 以宋德宜，陳廷敬薦博學鴻儒科，試列一等。

translations.literal: Through the recommendation of Song Deyi and Chen Tingjing he was nominated for the Erudite Special Examination and placed in the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Song Deyi and Chen Tingjing for the Erudite Special Examination, he placed in the first rank.

sentences.zh: 授編修，纂修明史，棘棘爭議不阿。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler, helped compile the History of the Ming, and in sharp disputes never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed compiler, he helped compile the History of the Ming and in sharp disputes never yielded.

sentences.zh: 在館六十日，再乞病歸。

translations.literal: After sixty days in the academy he again requested sick leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After sixty days in the academy he again requested sick leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 歸十年而卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: Ten years after returning home he died, at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years after returning home he died, at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 初，聖祖嘗問廷敬今世誰能為古文者，廷敬舉琬以對。

translations.literal: Earlier the Kangxi Emperor once asked Chen Tingjing who in the present age could write classical prose, and Chen Tingjing named Wan in reply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Kangxi Emperor once asked Chen Tingjing who in the present age could write classical prose, and Chen Tingjing named Wan.

sentences.zh: 及琬病歸，聖祖南巡駐無錫，諭巡撫湯斌曰：「汪琬久在翰林，有文譽。

translations.literal: When Wan returned home on sick leave, the Kangxi Emperor on his southern tour stopped at Wuxi and instructed the governor Tang Bin, "Wang Wan long served in the Hanlin and has a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan returned home on sick leave, the Kangxi Emperor on his southern tour stopped at Wuxi and instructed Governor Tang Bin: "Wang Wan long served in the Hanlin and has a literary reputation.

sentences.zh: 今聞其居鄉甚清正，特賜御書一軸。」

translations.literal: Now I hear that in his retirement he is very upright and pure; I specially bestow one scroll of imperial calligraphy."
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear that in retirement he is very upright and pure; I specially bestow one scroll of imperial calligraphy."

sentences.zh: 當時榮之。

translations.literal: At the time this was counted an honor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was counted a great honor.

sentences.zh: 琬為文原本六經，疏暢類南宋諸家，敘事有法。

translations.literal: Wan's writing was rooted in the Six Classics, lucid and flowing like the writers of the Southern Song, and his narrative had method.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's writing was rooted in the Six Classics, lucid and flowing like the Southern Song masters, and his narrative had method.

sentences.zh: 公卿志狀，皆爭得琬文為重。

translations.literal: For the memorial inscriptions and biographies of high officials, all vied to obtain Wan's writing as the weightiest part.
translations.idiomatic: For the memorial inscriptions and biographies of high officials, all vied to obtain Wan's writing as the crowning piece.

sentences.zh: 嘗自輯詩文為類稿、續稿各數十卷，又簡其尤精者，囑門人林佶繕刻之。

translations.literal: He once compiled his poetry and prose into categorized drafts and continued drafts, each of several dozen juan, then selected the finest pieces and entrusted his disciple Lin Ji to edit and print them.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled his poetry and prose into categorized drafts and continued drafts, each of several dozen juan, then selected the finest pieces and entrusted his disciple Lin Ji to edit and print them.

sentences.zh: 計東，字甫草，吳江人。

translations.literal: Ji Dong, styled Fucao, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Dong, styled Fucao, was from Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 少負經世才，自比馬周、王猛。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed talent for governing the age and compared himself to Ma Zhou and Wang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he possessed talent for statecraft and compared himself to Ma Zhou and Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 遭世變，著籌南五論，持謁史可法，可法奇之，弗能用也。

translations.literal: When calamity struck the age he wrote the Five Discourses on Planning for the South, took them to pay a visit to Shi Kefa, and Shi Kefa marveled at them but could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster struck he wrote the Five Discourses on Planning for the South, presented them to Shi Kefa, and Shi Kefa marveled at them but could not employ him.

sentences.zh: 順治十四年，舉順天鄉試，旋以江南奏銷案被黜。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi he passed the Shuntian provincial examination, but soon afterward was disqualified in the Jiangnan examination-fraud case.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 14 he passed the Shuntian provincial examination, but was soon disqualified in the Jiangnan examination-fraud case.

sentences.zh: 嘗從湯斌講學，又從汪琬受歐、曾古文義法，故其為文具有本原，而一出以和平溫雅。

translations.literal: He once studied under Tang Bin and also learned from Wang Wan the classical prose methods of Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong; therefore his writing had solid foundations, yet always came forth in peaceful and gentle elegance.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Tang Bin and learned classical prose from Wang Wan in the manner of Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong; his writing had solid foundations, yet always came forth in peaceful and gentle elegance.

sentences.zh: 既廢不用，貧無以養，縱遊四方，所至交其豪傑。

translations.literal: Once discarded and unused, too poor to support himself, he wandered freely in all directions and wherever he went befriended local heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Discarded and unemployed, too poor to support himself, he wandered freely and wherever he went befriended local heroes.

sentences.zh: 過鄴城，尋明詩人謝榛葬處，得之南門外二十里，為修墓立石，請有司禁樵牧。

translations.literal: Passing through Yecheng, he searched for the burial place of the Ming poet Xie Zhen, found it twenty li outside the south gate, restored the tomb and erected a stele, and requested the authorities to forbid woodcutting and grazing there.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Yecheng, he searched for the burial place of the Ming poet Xie Zhen, found it twenty li outside the south gate, restored the tomb and erected a stele, and asked the authorities to forbid woodcutting and grazing there.

sentences.zh: 又憩順德逆旅，念歸有光昔嘗佐郡，集中有廳壁記，求其遺址不得，乃即署旁廢圃中設瓣香，再拜流涕而去，觀者駭其狂。

translations.literal: Resting again at an inn in Shunde, he recalled that Gui Youguang had once served as assistant in the prefecture and that his collected works contained a Hall Wall Record; unable to find the site, he set out a single incense petal in the abandoned garden beside the yamen, bowed twice with tears streaming, and departed—onlookers were alarmed by his eccentricity.
translations.idiomatic: Resting at an inn in Shunde, he recalled that Gui Youguang had once served as assistant in the prefecture and that his collected works contained a Hall Wall Record; unable to find the site, he set out a single incense petal in the abandoned garden beside the yamen, bowed twice with tears streaming, and left—onlookers were alarmed by his eccentricity.

sentences.zh: 東外若不羈，內行謹，事母至孝。

translations.literal: Outwardly Dong seemed unrestrained, but inwardly his conduct was careful and his service to his mother deeply filial.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Dong seemed unrestrained, but inwardly his conduct was careful and his devotion to his mother deeply filial.

sentences.zh: 同邑友人吳兆騫流徙出關，為卹其家，且以女許配其弱子。

translations.literal: When his fellow townsman and friend Wu Zhaoqian was exiled beyond the pass, he provided for his family and even betrothed his daughter to Wu's young son.
translations.idiomatic: When his fellow townsman and friend Wu Zhaoqian was exiled beyond the pass, he provided for his family and even betrothed his daughter to Wu's young son.

sentences.zh: 大學士王熙素重東，屢欲薦之，未果。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Wang Xi had long valued Dong and repeatedly wished to recommend him, but never succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Wang Xi had long valued Dong and repeatedly wished to recommend him, but never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 會詔舉鴻博，而東已前一年卒，深悼惜焉。

translations.literal: Just as an edict was issued to recommend candidates for the Special Examination, Dong had already died the year before, and Wang deeply mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Just as an edict was issued to recommend candidates for the Special Examination, Dong had already died the year before, and Wang deeply mourned and regretted it.

sentences.zh: 初游河南，見商丘宋犖，輒引重。

translations.literal: On his first travels in Henan he met Song Luo of Shangqiu and was immediately held in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: On his first travels in Henan he met Song Luo of Shangqiu, who immediately held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 其後東歿二十餘年，犖至江蘇巡撫，為序其遺文，曰改亭集，刊行之。

translations.literal: More than twenty years after Dong died, Song became governor-general of Jiangsu, wrote a preface for his posthumous writings under the title Gaiting ji, and had them published.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty years after Dong's death, Song became governor-general of Jiangsu, wrote a preface for his posthumous writings titled the Gaiting ji, and had them published.

sentences.zh: 兆騫，字漢槎。

translations.literal: Zhao Qian, styled Hancha.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qian, styled Hancha.

sentences.zh: 亦十四年舉人。

translations.literal: He too was a juren in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: He too was a juren of Shunzhi 14.

sentences.zh: 以科場蜚語逮系，遣戍寧古塔。

translations.literal: Because of rumors in the examination halls he was arrested and imprisoned and sent into exile at Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: Because of rumors in the examination halls he was arrested and sent into exile at Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 兆騫與弟兆宜皆善屬文，居塞上二十年，侘傺不自聊，一發之於詩。

translations.literal: Zhao Qian and his younger brother Zhao Yi were both skilled at composition; living on the frontier for twenty years, despondent and unable to find solace, he poured it all out in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qian and his younger brother Zhao Yi were both skilled writers; after twenty years on the frontier, despondent and unable to find solace, he poured it all out in poetry.

sentences.zh: 已而友人顧貞觀言於納蘭成德、徐乾學，為納鍰，遂於康熙二十年赦還。

translations.literal: Before long his friend Gu Zhenguan spoke to Nalan Xingde and Xu Qianxue, who paid the ransom money, and so in the twentieth year of Kangxi he was pardoned and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his friend Gu Zhenguan spoke to Nalan Xingde and Xu Qianxue, who paid the ransom, and in Kangxi 20 he was pardoned and returned.

sentences.zh: 著秋笳集。

translations.literal: He authored the Qiujia ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Qiujia ji.

sentences.zh: 兆宜嘗注徐、庾二集，韓偓詩集，又注玉台新詠、才調集，並行於世。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi once annotated the two collections of Xu and Yu, Han Wo's poetry collection, and also annotated the Yutai xinyong and Caidiao ji, all of which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi annotated the two collections of Xu and Yu, Han Wo's poetry collection, and also the Yutai xinyong and Caidiao ji, all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 同邑顧我錡，廩生。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Gu Woqi was a government-sponsored student.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Gu Woqi was a government-sponsored student.

sentences.zh: 鄂爾泰任江蘇布政，試古學，得士五十三人，刻南邦黎獻集，推我錡為冠。

translations.literal: When Ortai served as financial commissioner of Jiangsu, he tested candidates in classical learning and selected fifty-three scholars, printing the Nibang lixian ji and ranking Woqi first.
translations.idiomatic: When Ortai served as financial commissioner of Jiangsu, he tested candidates in classical learning, selected fifty-three scholars, printed the Nibang lixian ji, and ranked Woqi first.

sentences.zh: 乾隆丙辰開詞科，鄂爾泰惜我錡前卒，不獲舉，人謂其遇與東同。

translations.literal: When the poetry special examination was opened in the bingchen year of Qianlong, Ortai regretted that Woqi had died earlier and could not be recommended; people said his fortune was the same as Dong's.
translations.idiomatic: When the poetry special examination was opened in Qianlong bingchen, Ortai regretted that Woqi had already died and could not be recommended; people said his fortune matched Dong's.

sentences.zh: 有湘南詩集。

translations.literal: He left the Xiangnan shiji.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Xiangnan shiji.

sentences.zh: 彭孫遹，字駿孫，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Peng Sunyu, styled Junsun, was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Sunyu, styled Junsun, was from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 父期生，明唐王時官太僕卿，死贛州。

translations.literal: His father Qisheng served as Minister of the Stud under the Prince of Tang in the Ming and died at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qisheng served as Minister of the Stud under the Ming Prince of Tang and died at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 長子孫貽以毀卒，孫遹其少子也。

translations.literal: The eldest son Sunyi died from grief-mourning; Sunyu was his youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Sunyi died from grief-mourning; Sunyu was the youngest son.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年進士，授中書。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the sixteenth year of Shunzhi and was appointed a secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 16, he was appointed a secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 素工詞章，與王士禎齊名，號曰「彭王」。

translations.literal: Skilled in lyrical composition, he was as famous as Wang Shizhen, and they were known as "Peng and Wang."
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in lyrical composition, he was as famous as Wang Shizhen, and the two were known as "Peng and Wang."

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，開博學鴻儒科，詔中外諸臣廣蒐幽隱，備禮敦勸，無論已仕未仕，徵詣闕下，月餼太倉米。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi the Erudite Special Examination was opened; an edict ordered officials throughout the realm to search widely for recluses, prepare rites and earnestly encourage them, and whether already in office or not, summon them to the capital with monthly rations of Taicang rice.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 the Erudite Special Examination was opened; an edict ordered officials throughout the realm to search widely for recluses, prepare rites and earnestly encourage them, and whether already in office or not, summon them to the capital with monthly rations of Taicang rice.

sentences.zh: 明年三月朔，召試太和殿。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month of the following year they were summoned for examination at the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month of the following year they were summoned for examination at the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 發賦、詩題各一，學士院給官紙，光祿布席，賜宴體仁閣下。

translations.literal: One fu and one poetry topic were issued; the Hanlin Academy supplied official paper, the Court of Imperial Entertainments laid out the seating mats, and a banquet was granted below the Hall of Embodying Benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: One fu and one poetry topic were issued; the Hanlin Academy supplied official paper, the Court of Imperial Entertainments laid out the seating mats, and a banquet was granted below the Hall of Embodying Benevolence.

sentences.zh: 於是天子親擢孫遹一等一名，授編修。

translations.literal: Thereupon the emperor personally selected Sunyu as first in the first rank and appointed him compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor personally selected Sunyu as first in the first rank and appointed him compiler.

sentences.zh: 自孫遹外，其籍隸浙江者，又有錢塘汪霦，秀水徐嘉炎、朱彝尊，平湖陸葇，海寧​​沈珩，仁和沈筠、吳任臣、邵遠平，遂安方象瑛、毛升芳，蕭山毛奇齡，鄞陳鴻績，凡十三人。

translations.literal: Apart from Sunyu, those whose registers were in Zhejiang included Wang Lin of Qiantang, Xu Jiayan and Zhu Yizun of Xiushui, Lu Rou of Pinghu, Shen Heng of Haining, Shen Jun, Wu Renchen, and Shao Yuanping of Renhe, Fang Xiangying and Mao Shengfang of Suian, Mao Qiling of Xiaoshan, and Chen Hongji of Yin—thirteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Sunyu, those registered in Zhejiang included Wang Lin of Qiantang, Xu Jiayan and Zhu Yizun of Xiushui, Lu Rou of Pinghu, Shen Heng of Haining, Shen Jun, Wu Renchen, and Shao Yuanping of Renhe, Fang Xiangying and Mao Shengfang of Suian, Mao Qiling of Xiaoshan, and Chen Hongji of Yin—thirteen in all.

sentences.zh: 江蘇二十三人，曰：上元倪燦，寶應喬萊，華亭王頊齡、吳元龍，無錫秦松齡、嚴繩孫，武進周清原，宜興陳維崧，長洲馮勳、汪琬、尤侗、範必英，吳錢中諧，儀真汪楫，淮安邱象隨，吳江潘耒、徐釚，太倉黃與堅，常熟周慶會，山陽李鎧、張鴻烈，上海錢金甫，江陰曹禾。

translations.literal: From Jiangsu there were twenty-three: Ni Can of Shangyuan, Qiao Lai of Baoying, Wang Xuling and Wu Yuanlong of Huating, Qin Songling and Yan Shengsun of Wuxi, Zhou Qingyuan of Wujin, Chen Weisong of Yixing, Feng Xun, Wang Wan, You Dong, and Fan Biying of Changzhou, Qian Zhongxie of Wu, Wang Ji of Yizhen, Qiu Xiangsui of Huai'an, Pan Lei and Xu Qiu of Wujiang, Huang Yujian of Taicang, Zhou Qinghui of Changshu, Li Kai and Zhang Honglie of Shanyang, and Qian Jinfu of Shanghai and Cao He of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangsu there were twenty-three: Ni Can of Shangyuan, Qiao Lai of Baoying, Wang Xuling and Wu Yuanlong of Huating, Qin Songling and Yan Shengsun of Wuxi, Zhou Qingyuan of Wujin, Chen Weisong of Yixing, Feng Xun, Wang Wan, You Dong, and Fan Biying of Changzhou, Qian Zhongxie of Wu, Wang Ji of Yizhen, Qiu Xiangsui of Huai'an, Pan Lei and Xu Qiu of Wujiang, Huang Yujian of Taicang, Zhou Qinghui of Changshu, Li Kai and Zhang Honglie of Shanyang, Qian Jinfu of Shanghai, and Cao He of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 直隸五人，曰：大興張烈，東明袁佑，宛平米漢雯，獲鹿崔如岳，任丘龐塏。

translations.literal: From Zhili there were five: Zhang Lie of Daxing, Yuan You of Dongming, Mi Hanwen of Wan, Cui Ruyue of Huolu, and Pang Kai of Renqiu.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhili there were five: Zhang Lie of Daxing, Yuan You of Dongming, Mi Hanwen of Wan, Cui Ruyue of Huolu, and Pang Kai of Renqiu.

sentences.zh: 安徽三人，曰：宣城施閏章、高詠，望江龍燮。

translations.literal: From Anhui there were three: Shi Runzhang and Gao Yong of Xuancheng, and Long Xie of Wangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: From Anhui there were three: Shi Runzhang and Gao Yong of Xuancheng, and Long Xie of Wangjiang.

sentences.zh: 江西二人，曰：臨川李來泰，清江黎騫。

translations.literal: From Jiangxi there were two: Li Laitai of Linchuan and Li Qian of Qingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiangxi there were two: Li Laitai of Linchuan and Li Qian of Qingjiang.

sentences.zh: 陝西一人，曰富平李因篤。

translations.literal: From Shaanxi there was one: Li Yindu of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: From Shaanxi there was one: Li Yindu of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 河南一人，曰睢州湯斌。

translations.literal: From Henan there was one: Tang Bin of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: From Henan there was one: Tang Bin of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 山東一人，曰諸城李澄中。

translations.literal: From Shandong there was one: Li Chengzhong of Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: From Shandong there was one: Li Chengzhong of Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 湖北一人，曰黃岡曹宜圃。

translations.literal: From Hubei there was one: Cao Yipu of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: From Hubei there was one: Cao Yipu of Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 凡五十人，皆以翰林入史館。

translations.literal: Fifty in all entered the Historiography Bureau as Hanlin scholars.
translations.idiomatic: All fifty entered the Historiography Bureau as Hanlin scholars.

sentences.zh: 其列二等者，亦多知名之士，稱極盛焉。

translations.literal: Those placed in the second rank were also mostly renowned figures—it was called an age of utmost flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Those placed in the second rank were also mostly renowned figures—the occasion was called an age of utmost flourishing.

sentences.zh: 孫遹歷官吏部侍郎，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: Sunyu rose through offices to Vice Minister of Personnel and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Sunyu rose to Vice Minister of Personnel and served as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 明史久未成，特命為總裁，賜專敕，異數也。

translations.literal: The History of the Ming had long gone unfinished; he was specially appointed chief compiler and granted a personal commission—an exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Ming had long gone unfinished; he was specially appointed chief compiler and granted a personal commission—an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 年七十，致仕歸，御書「松桂堂」額賜之，遂以名其集。

translations.literal: At the age of seventy he retired; the emperor bestowed the plaque "Pine and Cassia Hall," and he named his collection after it.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy he retired; the emperor bestowed the plaque "Pine and Cassia Hall," and he named his collection after it.

sentences.zh: 朱彝尊，字錫鬯，秀水人，明大學士國祚曾孫。

translations.literal: Zhu Yizun, styled Xichang, was a native of Xiushui and the great-grandson of Grand Secretary Guozuo of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yizun, styled Xichang, was from Xiushui and the great-grandson of Ming Grand Secretary Guozuo.

sentences.zh: 生有異秉，書經目不遺。

translations.literal: Born with exceptional talent, what he read he never forgot.
translations.idiomatic: Born with exceptional talent, he never forgot what he read.

sentences.zh: 家貧客遊，南踰嶺，北出雲朔，東泛滄海，登之罘，經甌越。

translations.literal: His family was poor and he traveled as a guest: south beyond the ranges, north to Yunshuo, east across the blue sea to climb Zhifu, and through Ou-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and traveling as a guest, he went south beyond the ranges, north to Yunshuo, east across the sea to climb Zhifu, and through Ou-Yue.

sentences.zh: 所至叢祠荒塚、破爐殘碣之文，莫不搜剔考證，與史傳參校同異。

translations.literal: Wherever he went, he searched out and collated inscriptions from shrines, desolate tombs, broken furnaces, and ruined steles, comparing them with historical biographies for discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, he searched out and collated inscriptions from shrines, desolate tombs, broken furnaces, and ruined steles, comparing them with historical biographies for discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 歸里，約李良年、週篔、繆泳輩為詩課，文名益噪。

translations.literal: After returning home he joined with Li Liangnian, Zhou Yun, Miao Yong, and others for poetry sessions, and his literary fame grew louder.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he joined Li Liangnian, Zhou Yun, Miao Yong, and others for poetry sessions, and his literary fame grew louder.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，試鴻博，除檢討。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi he passed the Special Examination and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he passed the Special Examination and was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 時富平李因篤、吳江潘耒、無錫嚴繩孫及彝尊皆以布衣入選，同修明史。

translations.literal: At that time Li Yindu of Fuping, Pan Lei of Wujiang, Yan Shengsun of Wuxi, and Yizun were all selected as commoners and jointly compiled the History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Yindu of Fuping, Pan Lei of Wujiang, Yan Shengsun of Wuxi, and Yizun were all selected as commoners and jointly compiled the History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 建議訪遺書，寬期限，毋效元史之迫時日。

translations.literal: He proposed searching for lost books and extending deadlines, and not forcing the work to match the Yuan History's compressed timeline.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed searching for lost books, extending deadlines, and not forcing the work to match the Yuan History's compressed timeline.

sentences.zh: 辨方孝孺之友宋仲珩、王孟缊、鄭叔度、林公輔諸人咸不及於難，則知從亡、致身錄謂誅九族，並戮其弟子朋友為一族不足據，所謂九族者，本宗一族也。

translations.literal: He showed that Fang Xiaoru's friends Song Zhongheng, Wang Mengyun, Zheng Shudu, Lin Gongfu, and others all escaped the calamity, proving that the Congwang and Zhishen lu claim that nine clans were executed and that disciples and friends were slaughtered as one clan cannot be relied upon—the so-called nine clans meant the original clan and its branches.
translations.idiomatic: He showed that Fang Xiaoru's friends Song Zhongheng, Wang Mengyun, Zheng Shudu, Lin Gongfu, and others all escaped the calamity, proving that the Congwang and Zhishen lu claim—that nine clans were executed and disciples and friends slaughtered as one clan—cannot be relied upon; the so-called nine clans meant the original clan and its branches.

sentences.zh: 又言東林不皆君子，異乎東林者，亦不皆小人。

translations.literal: He also said that not all Donglin were gentlemen, and that those unlike the Donglin were not all petty men.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that not all Donglin were gentlemen, and that those unlike the Donglin were not all petty men.

sentences.zh: 作史者未可存門戶之見，以同異分邪正。

translations.literal: Those writing history must not hold to factional views, dividing good and evil by allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Historians must not hold to factional views, dividing good and evil by allegiance.

sentences.zh: 二十年，充日講起居注官。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he served as daily lecturer and recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 20 he served as daily lecturer and recorder.

sentences.zh: 典試江南，稱得士。

translations.literal: He presided over the Jiangnan examination and was said to have selected worthy scholars.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Jiangnan examination and was said to have selected worthy scholars.

sentences.zh: 入值南書房，賜紫禁城騎馬。

translations.literal: He entered the Southern Library and was granted the privilege of riding a horse within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Southern Library and was granted the privilege of riding a horse within the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 數與內廷宴，被文綺、時果之賚，皆紀以詩。

translations.literal: He attended inner-court banquets many times and received gifts of brocade and seasonal fruit, all of which he recorded in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He attended inner-court banquets many times and received gifts of brocade and seasonal fruit, all of which he recorded in poetry.

sentences.zh: 旋坐私挾小胥入內寫書被劾，降一級，後復原官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was impeached for secretly bringing a clerk into the inner palace to copy books, was demoted one rank, and later had his original office restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was impeached for secretly bringing a clerk into the inner palace to copy books, was demoted one rank, and later had his original office restored.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，假歸。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 31 he took leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 聖祖南巡，迎駕無錫，御書「研經博物」額賜之。

translations.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor on his southern tour reached Wuxi, Yizun welcomed him and received the imperial plaque "Studying the Classics and Mastering Antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor on his southern tour reached Wuxi, Yizun welcomed him and received the imperial plaque "Studying the Classics and Mastering Antiquity."

sentences.zh: 當時王士禎工詩，汪琬工文，毛奇齡工考據，獨彝尊兼有眾長。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Shizhen excelled at poetry, Wang Wan at prose, and Mao Qiling at evidential scholarship; Yizun alone combined all these strengths.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Shizhen excelled at poetry, Wang Wan at prose, and Mao Qiling at evidential scholarship; Yizun alone combined all these strengths.

sentences.zh: 著經義考、日下舊聞、曝書亭集。

translations.literal: He authored the Inquiry into the Meaning of the Classics, Old Accounts of the Capital, and the Baoshu Ting Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Inquiry into the Meaning of the Classics, Old Accounts of the Capital, and the Baoshu Ting ji.

sentences.zh: 又嘗選明詩綜，或因人錄詩，或因詩存人，銓次為最當。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Comprehensive Ming Poetry, recording poets because of their poems or preserving men because of their poems, with the most judicious arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Comprehensive Ming Poetry, recording poets through their poems or preserving men through their poems, with the most judicious arrangement.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 子昆田，亦工詩文，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Kuntian was also skilled in poetry and prose but died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuntian was also skilled in poetry and prose but died young.

sentences.zh: 孫稻孫，舉乾隆丙辰鴻博，能世其家。

translations.literal: His grandson Daosun passed the Special Examination in the bingchen year of Qianlong and continued the family tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Daosun passed the Special Examination in Qianlong bingchen and continued the family tradition.

sentences.zh: 彝尊所與為詩課者，李良年，字武曹，同邑人。

translations.literal: Among those with whom Yizun held poetry sessions was Li Liangnian, styled Wucao, a fellow townsman.
translations.idiomatic: Among those with whom Yizun held poetry sessions was Li Liangnian, styled Wucao, a fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 與兄繩遠、弟符並著詩名。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother Shengyuan and younger brother Fu all had reputations in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Shengyuan and younger brother Fu all had reputations in poetry.

sentences.zh: 試鴻博，罷歸。

translations.literal: He took the Special Examination and returned home after failing.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Special Examination and returned home after failing.

sentences.zh: 有秋錦山房集。

translations.literal: He left the Qiujin shanfang ji.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Qiujin shanfang ji.

sentences.zh: 譚吉璁，字舟石，嘉興人，彝尊姑之子也。

translations.literal: Tan Jicong, styled Zhoushi, was a native of Jiaxing and the son of Yizun's paternal aunt.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Jicong, styled Zhoushi, was from Jiaxing and the son of Yizun's paternal aunt.

sentences.zh: 少遇寇，以身蔽父，寇舍之去。

translations.literal: In youth he encountered bandits and shielded his father with his body; the bandits spared them and left.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he encountered bandits and shielded his father with his body; the bandits spared them and left.

sentences.zh: 後以諸生試國子監第一，授弘文院撰文中書舍人，出為延安同知。

translations.literal: Later, as a licentiate he ranked first in the examination at the Imperial Academy and was appointed a drafting secretary in the Hongwen Academy, then went out to serve as vice-prefect of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as a licentiate he ranked first in the Imperial Academy examination and was appointed a drafting secretary in the Hongwen Academy, then went out to serve as vice-prefect of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂叛，守榆城獨完，論功加一級。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled he held Yucheng alone intact, and for his merit was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled he held Yucheng alone intact, and for his merit was promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 舉應鴻博，報罷。

translations.literal: He was nominated for the Special Examination but was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: He was nominated for the Special Examination but was rejected.

sentences.zh: 遷知登州府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 有嘉樹堂集。

translations.literal: He left the Jia shu tang ji.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Jia shu tang ji.

sentences.zh: 尤侗，字展成，長洲人。

translations.literal: You Dong, styled Zhancheng, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: You Dong, styled Zhancheng, was from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 少補諸生，以貢謁選。

translations.literal: In youth he became a licentiate and presented himself for selection through the tribute route.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he became a licentiate and presented himself for selection through the tribute route.

sentences.zh: 除永平推官，守法不撓。

translations.literal: He was appointed judicial assistant of Yongping and upheld the law without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial assistant of Yongping and upheld the law without yielding.

sentences.zh: 坐撻旗丁鐫級歸。

translations.literal: Because he flogged a banner soldier he was reduced in rank and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Because he flogged a banner soldier he was reduced in rank and returned home.

sentences.zh: 侗天才富贍，詩文多新警之思，雜以諧謔，每一篇出，傳誦遍人口。

translations.literal: Dong's native talent was rich and abundant; his poetry and prose were full of fresh and striking thought, mixed with wit and banter, and whenever a piece appeared it was recited from mouth to mouth throughout the land.
translations.idiomatic: Dong's native talent was rich and abundant; his poetry and prose were full of fresh and striking thought, mixed with wit and banter, and whenever a piece appeared it was recited throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，試鴻博列二等，授檢討，與修明史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi he placed in the second rank of the Special Examination, was appointed reviser, and helped compile the History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he placed in the second rank of the Special Examination, was appointed reviser, and helped compile the History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 居三年告歸。

translations.literal: After three years in office he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he requested leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 聖祖南巡至蘇州，侗獻詩頌。

translations.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor on his southern tour reached Suzhou, Dong presented congratulatory poetry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor on his southern tour reached Suzhou, Dong presented congratulatory poetry.

sentences.zh: 上嘉焉，賜御書「鶴棲堂」額，遷侍講。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, bestowed the imperial plaque "Crane Dwelling Hall," and promoted him to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, bestowed the imperial plaque "Crane Dwelling Hall," and promoted him to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖於禁中覽侗詩篇，​​以才子目之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Shunzhi Emperor in the palace had read Dong's poetry and regarded him as a literary genius.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Shunzhi Emperor in the palace had read Dong's poetry and regarded him as a literary genius.

sentences.zh: 後入翰林，聖祖稱之曰「老名士」。

translations.literal: Later, after entering the Hanlin, the Kangxi Emperor called him "the old man of letters."
translations.idiomatic: Later, after entering the Hanlin, the Kangxi Emperor called him "the old man of letters."

sentences.zh: 天下羨其榮遇。

translations.literal: All under Heaven envied his honored treatment.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven envied his honored treatment.

sentences.zh: 侗喜汲引才雋，性寬和，與物無忤。

translations.literal: Dong delighted in recommending talented men; by nature he was generous and mild and at odds with no one.
translations.idiomatic: Dong delighted in recommending talented men; by nature he was generous and mild and at odds with no one.

sentences.zh: 兄弟七人甚友愛，白首如垂髫。

translations.literal: The seven brothers were deeply affectionate, white-haired yet as close as in childhood.
translations.idiomatic: The seven brothers were deeply affectionate, white-haired yet as close as in childhood.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 著西堂集、鶴棲堂集，凡百餘卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Xitang ji and the Hexi tang ji, more than one hundred juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Xitang ji and the Hexi tang ji, more than one hundred juan in all.

sentences.zh: 秦松齡，字留仙，無錫人。

translations.literal: Qin Songling, styled Liuxian, was a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Songling, styled Liuxian, was from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，官檢討，罷歸。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi, served as reviser, and was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 12, he served as reviser, was dismissed, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 後舉鴻博，复授檢討。

translations.literal: Later he was nominated for the Special Examination and was again appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was nominated for the Special Examination and was again appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 典江西鄉試，歷左贊善，以諭德終。

translations.literal: He presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination, rose to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and ended his career as tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination, rose to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent, and ended his career as tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 松齡為庶常，召試詠鶴詩，有句云：「高鳴常向月，善舞不迎人。」

translations.literal: When Songling was a bachelor in the Hanlin, he was summoned to compose a poem on the crane and wrote a line saying, "It cries often toward the moon and dances well without courting men."
translations.idiomatic: When Songling was a bachelor in the Hanlin, he was summoned to compose a poem on the crane and wrote a line saying: "It cries often toward the moon and dances well without courting men."

sentences.zh: 世祖拔置第一，示閣臣曰：「是人必有品！」

translations.literal: The Shunzhi Emperor ranked him first and showed it to the grand secretaries, saying, "This man must have character!"
translations.idiomatic: The Shunzhi Emperor ranked him first and showed it to the grand secretaries, saying: "This man must have character!"

sentences.zh: 及告歸，里居二十餘年，專治毛詩。

translations.literal: When he returned home he lived in retirement for more than twenty years and devoted himself exclusively to the Mao Odes.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned home he lived in retirement for more than twenty years and devoted himself exclusively to the Mao Odes.

sentences.zh: 仿黃氏日鈔之例，著毛詩日箋六卷。

translations.literal: Following the example of Huang's Daily Notes, he authored the Daily Commentary on the Mao Odes in six juan.
translations.idiomatic: Following the example of Huang's Daily Notes, he wrote the Daily Commentary on the Mao Odes in six juan.

sentences.zh: 自為詩文曰蒼峴山人集。

translations.literal: His own poetry and prose he collected under the title Cangxian shanren ji.
translations.idiomatic: His own poetry and prose he collected under the title Cangxian shanren ji.

sentences.zh: 曹禾，字頌嘉，江陰人。

translations.literal: Cao He, styled Songjia, was a native of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Cao He, styled Songjia, was from Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the third year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Kangxi 3.

sentences.zh: 選鴻博，授檢討，官至祭酒。

translations.literal: Selected for the Special Examination, he was appointed reviser and rose to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for the Special Examination, he was appointed reviser and rose to Grand Master of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 與田雯、宋犖、汪懋麟、顏光敏、王又旦、謝重輝、曹貞吉、丁澎、葉封齊名，稱詩中十子。

translations.literal: Together with Tian Wen, Song Luo, Wang Maolin, Yan Guangmin, Wang Youdan, Xie Chonghui, Cao Zhenji, Ding Peng, and Ye Feng, he was equally renowned, and together they were called the Ten Masters of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He stood among the Ten Masters of Poetry—Tian Wen, Song Luo, Wang Maolin, Yan Guangmin, Wang Youdan, Xie Chonghui, Cao Zhenji, Ding Peng, and Ye Feng.

sentences.zh: 同時江西選鴻博一等者，李泰來，字石台，臨川人。

translations.literal: At the same time, among those from Jiangxi selected in the first class of the Special Examination was Li Tailai, styled Shitai, a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Among Jiangxi men chosen first class in the Special Examination at the same time was Li Tailai, styled Shitai, of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Shunzhi 9.

sentences.zh: 嘗督江南學政，除蘇松常道，以疾歸。

translations.literal: He once served as educational commissioner of Jiangnan, was appointed intendant of the Suzhou-Songjiang-Changzhou circuit, and returned home due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: He once supervised education in Jiangnan, was appointed intendant of the Suzhou-Songjiang-Changzhou circuit, and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 試詞科，授侍講。

translations.literal: He took the Literary Examination and was appointed lecturer-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Literary Examination and received appointment as lecturer-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 古文博奧，詩以和雅稱。

translations.literal: His classical prose was learned and profound; his poetry was renowned for its harmonious elegance.
translations.idiomatic: His classical prose was learned and profound, and his poetry was praised for its harmonious elegance.

sentences.zh: 有石台集。

translations.literal: He authored the Shitai ji collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Shitai ji collection.

sentences.zh: 陳維崧，字其年，宜興人。

translations.literal: Chen Weisong, styled Qinian, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Weisong, styled Qinian, was from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 祖於廷，明左都御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu Ting was Left Censor-in-Chief of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu Ting had been Left Censor-in-Chief under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 父貞慧，見遺逸傳。

translations.literal: His father Zhenhui is treated in the Biographies of Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhenhui appears in the Biographies of Recluses.

sentences.zh: 維崧天才絕艷，十歲，代大父撰楊忠烈像贊。

translations.literal: Weisong's genius was exceptionally brilliant; at the age of ten he composed an encomium for the portrait of Yang Zhonglie in place of his grandfather.
translations.idiomatic: Weisong possessed dazzling genius; at ten he wrote, in his grandfather's stead, an encomium for the portrait of Yang Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 比長，侍父側，每名流宴集，援筆作序記，千言立就，瑰瑋無比，皆折行輩與交。

translations.literal: When he came of age, attending at his father's side, at every gathering of eminent figures he would take up the brush and write prefaces and accounts—thousands of words completed in an instant, of unrivaled splendor—and men of rank and seniority all lowered themselves to befriend him.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown, he waited on his father; at every banquet of leading men he would take up his brush and draft prefaces and accounts—thousands of words at a stroke, gorgeously unmatched—and even his seniors sought his friendship.

sentences.zh: 補諸生，久之不遇。

translations.literal: He was enrolled as a licentiate but for a long time received no official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He became a licentiate, yet for years found no official opening.

sentences.zh: 因出遊，所在爭客之。

translations.literal: Therefore he went traveling, and everywhere he went men vied to receive him as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: He set out on the road, and wherever he went men competed to host him.

sentences.zh: 嘗由汴入都，與朱彝尊合刻一稿，名朱陳村詞，流傳至禁中，蒙賜問，時以為榮。

translations.literal: Once, entering the capital from Bian, he jointly published a collection with Zhu Yizun entitled Zhu-Cun Village Lyrics; it circulated even into the inner palace, and he was honored with imperial inquiry—a distinction regarded at the time as glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Once, traveling from Bian to the capital, he and Zhu Yizun jointly published Zhu-Cun Village Lyrics; the book reached the inner palace, and he received an imperial inquiry—a mark of honor in his day.

sentences.zh: 逾五十，始舉鴻博，授檢討，修明史。

translations.literal: After the age of fifty he finally passed the Special Examination, was appointed reviser, and worked on the Draft History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Not until past fifty did he pass the Special Examination, receive appointment as reviser, and join the compilation of the Draft History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 在館四年，病卒。

translations.literal: Four years in the Hanlin Academy, then he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in the academy he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 維崧清臞多鬚，海內稱陳髯。

translations.literal: Weisong was lean and bearded; throughout the realm he was known as Chen the Bearded.
translations.idiomatic: Lean and full-bearded, Weisong was known across the land as Chen the Bearded.

sentences.zh: 平生無疾言遽色，友愛諸弟甚。

translations.literal: In his life he never spoke harshly or showed sudden anger; he deeply loved his younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke in anger or flashed sudden temper, and he loved his younger brothers dearly.

sentences.zh: 遊公卿間，慎密，隨事匡正，故人樂近之，而卒莫之狎。

translations.literal: Among high officials he was discreet, correcting matters as they arose, so old friends were glad to be near him—yet in the end none presumed familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: Moving among ministers and grandees, he was careful and steady, setting things right as occasion arose; friends were glad to draw near him, yet none in the end took liberties.

sentences.zh: 著湖海樓詩集、迦陵文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Huhai lou shi ji and Jialing wen ji.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Huhai lou shi ji and Jialing wen ji.

sentences.zh: 時汪琬於同輩少許可者，獨推維崧駢體，謂自唐開、寶後無與抗矣。

translations.literal: Wang Wan, who rarely praised his contemporaries, singled out Weisong's parallel prose and said that since the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras of Tang, none could stand against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wan seldom approved anyone among his peers, yet he singled out Weisong's parallel prose and declared that since Tang Kaiyuan and Tianbao, no one could rival him.

sentences.zh: 詩雄麗沉鬱，詞至千八百首之多，尤前此未有也。

translations.literal: His poetry was bold, rich, and somber; his lyrics numbered as many as eighteen hundred—a scale unheard of before.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was bold, lush, and weighty; his song lyrics ran to some eighteen hundred pieces—more than anyone before him.

sentences.zh: 順、康間，以駢文稱者，又有吳綺，字次，江都人。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi and Kangxi reigns, another famed for parallel prose was Wu Qi, styled Ci, a native of Jiangdu.
