translations.idiomatic: During Shunzhi and Kangxi, Wu Qi, styled Ci, of Jiangdu, was also celebrated for parallel prose.

sentences.zh: 維崧導源庾信，氾濫於初唐四傑，故氣脈雄厚。

translations.literal: Weisong took Yu Xin as his source and drew broadly on the Four Talents of early Tang, so his style was powerfully robust.
translations.idiomatic: Weisong traced his line to Yu Xin and flooded outward into the Four Talents of early Tang, giving his style a deep, vigorous pulse.

sentences.zh: 綺則追步李商隱，才地視維崧為弱，而秀逸特甚。

translations.literal: Qi followed Li Shangyin; in breadth of talent he fell short of Weisong, yet he was exceptionally refined and graceful.
translations.idiomatic: Qi followed in Li Shangyin's steps; his range was slighter than Weisong's, yet he was surpassingly elegant and nimble.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年拔貢生，薦授中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi he was selected as a tribute student and recommended for appointment as secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 he was chosen as a tribute student and recommended as a secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奉詔譜楊繼盛樂府，遷兵部主事，即以繼盛官官之也。

translations.literal: By imperial order he composed Yang Jisheng's yuefu; he was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of War—the very post Yang Jisheng had held.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he set Yang Jisheng's yuefu to music; he was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of War—the office Yang Jisheng once held.

sentences.zh: 出知湖州府，有吏能。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Huzhou, he proved capable in administration.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed prefect of Huzhou, he showed real administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 人謂其多風力，尚風節，饒風趣，稱為「三風太守」。

translations.literal: People said he had force of character, upheld integrity, and abounded in wit, calling him the Three-Winds Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Men praised his force of character, his regard for principle, and his store of wit, and called him the Three-Winds Prefect.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷歸。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was removed from office and went home.

sentences.zh: 貧無田屯，購廢圃以居。

translations.literal: Poor and without farmland, he bought a ruined garden to live in.
translations.idiomatic: Without land or fields, he bought an abandoned garden and made it his home.

sentences.zh: 有匄詩文者，以花木潤筆，因顏其圃曰種字林。

translations.literal: When people sought poems or essays from him, he accepted flowers and plants as payment, and therefore named his garden the Character-Planting Grove.
translations.idiomatic: Those who asked him for poems or essays paid him in flowers and plants; he named the garden Character-Planting Grove for that reason.

sentences.zh: 著林蕙堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Linhuitang ji collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Linhuitang ji collection.

sentences.zh: 詞最有名，婦孺皆能習之。

translations.literal: His lyrics were the most famous; even women and children could learn them by heart.
translations.idiomatic: His song lyrics were best known of all—women and children alike could sing them from memory.

sentences.zh: 以有「把酒祝東風，種出雙紅豆」之句，又稱「紅豆詞人」。

translations.literal: Because of the line "Raise the cup and toast the east wind—planting twin red beans," he was also called the Red-Bean Lyricist.
translations.idiomatic: For the line "Raise the cup and toast the east wind—planting twin red beans," he was also known as the Red-Bean Lyricist.

sentences.zh: 徐釚，字電發，吳江人。

translations.literal: Xu Qian, styled Dianfa, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qian, styled Dianfa, was from Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 應鴻博，授檢討。

translations.literal: He answered the Special Examination and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Special Examination and received appointment as reviser.

sentences.zh: 會當外轉，遽乞歸。

translations.literal: When the time came for an outside transfer, he abruptly asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was due for transfer outside the capital, he suddenly petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 後起原官，不就。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled to his former post but declined.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned back to his former office but refused.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 著南州草堂集、本事詩。

translations.literal: He authored the Nanzhou caotang ji and Benshi shi.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Nanzhou caotang ji and Benshi shi.

sentences.zh: 又嘗刻菊莊樂府。

translations.literal: He also published the Juzhuang yuefu.
translations.idiomatic: He also printed the Juzhuang yuefu.

sentences.zh: 崑山葉方靄稱其綿麗幽深，耐人尋繹。

translations.literal: Ye Fang'ai of Kunshan praised his work as lush, subtle, and deep—rewarding prolonged reflection.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Fang'ai of Kunshan called his writing lush and deep, subtle enough to repay long pondering.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮貢使以兼金購之。

translations.literal: Korean tribute envoys bought copies with fine gold.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys from Korea paid in fine gold to obtain copies.

sentences.zh: 釚既工倚聲，因輯詞苑叢談，具有裁鑑。

translations.literal: Skilled in regulated song lyrics, he compiled the Ciyuan congtan, showing sure critical judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Already masterful in regulated lyrics, he compiled the Ciyuan congtan, displaying keen critical taste.

sentences.zh: 潘耒，字次耕，吳江人。

translations.literal: Pan Lei, styled Cigeng, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Lei, styled Cigeng, was from Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 生而奇慧，讀書十行並下，自經史、音韻、算數及宗乘之學，無不通貫。

translations.literal: Born with extraordinary intelligence, he read ten lines at once; from the classics, histories, phonology, and mathematics to Buddhist doctrine, nothing was beyond his mastery.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted from birth, he read ten lines at a glance; whether classics, history, phonology, mathematics, or Buddhist learning, he mastered them all.

sentences.zh: 康熙時，以布衣試鴻博，授檢討，纂修明史。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he took the Special Examination as a commoner, was appointed reviser, and helped compile the Draft History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he entered the Special Examination as a commoner, became reviser, and joined the compilation of the Draft History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 上書總裁，言要義八端：「宜搜採博而考證精；

translations.literal: He memorialized the chief compilers on eight essential points: "Collection should be broad and verification meticulous;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the chief compilers setting forth eight essentials: "Gather widely and verify with precision;

sentences.zh: 職任分而義例一；

translations.literal: duties divided yet principles unified;
translations.idiomatic: divide labor yet keep one standard of method;

sentences.zh: 秉筆直而持論平；

translations.literal: the pen upright and judgments even;
translations.idiomatic: write plainly and argue fairly;

sentences.zh: 歲月寬而卷帙簡。」

translations.literal: time ample and volumes concise.
translations.idiomatic: allow ample time and keep the work concise."

sentences.zh: 總裁善其說，令撰食貨志，兼他紀傳。

translations.literal: The chief compilers approved his proposal and had him write the Treatise on Food and Money, along with other annals and biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs approved and assigned him the Treatise on Food and Money, along with other annals and biographies.

sentences.zh: 尋充日講起居注官，修實錄、聖訓。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served as diarist of the imperial lectures and worked on the Veritable Records and Sacred Instructions.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became diarist of the imperial lectures and helped compile the Veritable Records and Sacred Instructions.

sentences.zh: 嘗應詔陳言，謂：「建言古無專責，梅福以南昌尉言外戚，柳伉以太常博士言程元振，陳東以太學生攻六賊，楊繼盛以部曹劾嚴嵩。

translations.literal: Once, answering an imperial call for counsel, he said: "In antiquity memorializing had no fixed office—Mei Fu, as magistrate of Nanchang, spoke against imperial in-laws; Liu Kang, as Grand Astrologer, inveighed against Cheng Yuanzhen; Chen Dong, as an Imperial Academy student, attacked the Six Traitors; Yang Jisheng, as a ministry clerk, impeached Yan Song.
translations.idiomatic: Once, responding to an imperial request for counsel, he argued: "Memorializing was never a single office—Mei Fu as magistrate of Nanchang spoke against imperial in-laws; Liu Kang as Grand Astrologer denounced Cheng Yuanzhen; Chen Dong as an academy student attacked the Six Traitors; Yang Jisheng as a ministry clerk impeached Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 本朝舊制，京官並許條陳。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's old rule allowed all capital officials to submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The old custom of this dynasty permitted every capital official to submit memorials.

sentences.zh: 自康熙十年憲臣奏請停止，凡非言官而言事為越職。

translations.literal: Since the tenth year of Kangxi, when censorial officials petitioned to stop it, any non-censor who speaks on policy is deemed to have overstepped his office.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kangxi 10, when censorial officials petitioned to end the practice, any non-censor who speaks on affairs of state is treated as overstepping his rank.

sentences.zh: 夫人主明目達聰，宜導之使言。

translations.literal: A ruler should see clearly and hear acutely; he ought to be guided to hear speech.
translations.idiomatic: A sovereign should see and hear for himself; he should be led to welcome speech.

sentences.zh: 今乃禁之，豈盛世事？

translations.literal: Now it is forbidden—is that fitting for an age of flourishing?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now it is forbidden—can that be the way of a flourishing age?

sentences.zh: 臣請弛其禁，俾大小臣工各得獻替，庶罔上行私之徒，有所忌而不敢肆。

translations.literal: I ask that the ban be lifted so that officials great and small may each offer advice and remonstrance, so that those who deceive the throne for private gain may fear and not act freely.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the ban be relaxed so officials at every rank may speak and remonstrate, giving those who mislead the throne for private ends something to fear.

sentences.zh: 於此輩甚不便，於國家甚便也。

translations.literal: This would be very inconvenient for such men, but very convenient for the state.
translations.idiomatic: That would be hard on such men, but a great benefit to the realm.

sentences.zh: 其在外監司守令，遇地方大利弊，許其條奏。

translations.literal: As for provincial commissioners and local magistrates abroad, when they encounter great benefit or harm in their regions, they should be allowed to submit memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial commissioners and local magistrates, when they see great benefit or harm in their jurisdictions, should also be allowed to memorialize.

sentences.zh: 水旱災荒，州縣官得上聞。

translations.literal: In flood, drought, or famine, district officials should be permitted to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: In flood, drought, or famine, county and district officials should be able to report upward.

sentences.zh: 如此，則民間疾苦無不周知矣。」

translations.literal: In this way none of the people's hardships would go unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Then no hardship among the people would fail to reach the throne.

sentences.zh: 更請許臺諫官得風聞言事，有能奮擊姦回者，不次超擢，以作敢言之氣。

translations.literal: He further asked that censors and remonstrators be permitted to speak on hearsay, and that those who boldly strike at treacherous villains be promoted out of turn to encourage a spirit of fearless speech.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked that censors be allowed to speak on hearsay, and that men who boldly attack villainy be promoted out of turn to revive the courage to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，甄別議起，坐浮躁降調，遂歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year a personnel review was launched; judged frivolous, he was demoted and transferred, and then returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three a talent review began; deemed rash, he was demoted and sent away, then went home.

sentences.zh: 耒有至性，初被徵，辭以母老，不獲命，乃行。

translations.literal: Lei had deep filial feeling; when first summoned he declined on the grounds that his mother was old, could not obtain permission, and so went.
translations.idiomatic: Lei was deeply filial; when first called to office he pleaded his aged mother, was refused, and went all the same.

sentences.zh: 既徐官，三牒吏部以獨子請終養，卒格於議不果歸。

translations.literal: After slow advancement in office, he thrice petitioned the Ministry of Personnel as an only son requesting leave to nurse his parent, but debate blocked him each time and he never obtained permission to return.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, promotion came slowly; three times he petitioned the Ministry of Personnel as an only son to return and care for his parent, but each time debate blocked him.

sentences.zh: 逮居喪，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning, his grief wasted him to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning came upon him, grief wore him down to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 少受學同郡徐枋、顧炎武。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Xu Fang and Gu Yanwu of his own prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied under Xu Fang and Gu Yanwu, men of his own prefecture.

sentences.zh: 枋歿，周恤其孤孫，而刻炎武所著書，師門之誼甚篤焉。

translations.literal: After Fang's death he supported his orphaned grandson and published the books Gu had written—his devotion to his teachers' circle was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang died he cared for his orphaned grandson and printed Gu's writings—his loyalty to his teachers' circle ran very deep.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，聖祖南巡，復原官。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, on the emperor's southern tour, his former rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-two, during the emperor's southern tour, his former office was restored.

sentences.zh: 大學士陳廷敬欲薦起之，力辭而止。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Chen Tingjing wished to recommend him for reappointment, but he firmly declined and stopped there.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Tingjing wanted to recommend him back to service, but he refused firmly and would not return.

sentences.zh: 平生嗜山水，登高賦詠，名流折服。

translations.literal: All his life he loved mountains and rivers; climbing high and composing verse, he won the admiration of leading men.
translations.idiomatic: He loved landscape all his life; composing on high places, he made eminent men bow to his talent.

sentences.zh: 有遂初堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Suichu tang ji.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Suichu tang ji.

sentences.zh: 又因炎武音學五書為類音八卷。

translations.literal: Following Gu Yanwu's Yinxue wushu, he produced eight juan of Leiyin.
translations.idiomatic: On the basis of Gu Yanwu's Yinxue wushu he compiled eight juan of Leiyin.

sentences.zh: 炎武復古，耒則務窮後世之變雲。

translations.literal: Gu looked back to antiquity; Lei, by contrast, sought to exhaust the transformations of later ages.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanwu looked back to antiquity; Lei, by contrast, traced the changes of later ages to their end.

sentences.zh: 當時詞科以史才稱者，朱彝尊、汪琬、吳任臣及耒為最著。

translations.literal: Among those of the Literary Examination famed at the time for historical talent, Zhu Yizun, Wang Wan, Wu Renchen, and Lei were the most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Special Examination men celebrated for historical talent in that age, Zhu Yizun, Wang Wan, Wu Renchen, and Lei stood foremost.

sentences.zh: 又有倪燦，字闇公，上元人。

translations.literal: There was also Ni Can, styled Angong, a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Also Ni Can, styled Angong, of Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 以舉人授檢討，撰藝文志序，與姜宸英刑法志序並推傑構。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he was appointed reviser; his preface to the Treatise on Literature, together with Jiang Chenying's preface to the Treatise on Penal Law, were both praised as masterworks.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate appointed reviser, he wrote the preface to the Treatise on Literature; with Jiang Chenying's preface to the Treatise on Penal Law, both were hailed as outstanding compositions.

sentences.zh: 書法詩格秀出一時，有雁園集。

translations.literal: His calligraphy and poetic style stood above his age; he authored the Yanyuan ji.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy and poetic style stood out in his time; he left the Yanyuan ji.

sentences.zh: 嚴繩孫，字蓀友，無錫人，明尚書一鵬孫。

translations.literal: Yan Sun, styled Sunyou, was a native of Wuxi and grandson of Yan Yipeng, a minister of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Sun, styled Sunyou, of Wuxi, was grandson of the Ming minister Yan Yipeng.

sentences.zh: 六歲能作擘窠大書。

translations.literal: At the age of six he could write large seal-style characters.
translations.idiomatic: At six he could write large seal-script characters.

sentences.zh: 試日，目疾作，第賦一詩，亦授檢討，撰明史隱逸傳。

translations.literal: On the day of the examination his eyes afflicted him; he wrote only one poem, yet still received appointment as reviser and drafted the Biographies of Recluses for the Draft History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: On exam day eye trouble struck; he submitted only one poem, yet still became reviser and wrote the Recluses biography for the Draft History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 典試江西，尋遷中允，假歸。

translations.literal: He presided over the Jiangxi examinations, was soon promoted to middle attendant, and took leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted examinations in Jiangxi, was soon promoted to middle attendant, and went home on leave.

sentences.zh: 有秋水集。

translations.literal: He authored the Qiushui ji.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Qiushui ji.

sentences.zh: 子泓曾，亦善畫工詩。

translations.literal: His son Hongzeng was also skilled at painting and poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hongzeng also painted and wrote poetry well.

sentences.zh: 徐嘉炎，字勝力，秀水人，明兵部尚書必達曾孫。

translations.literal: Xu Jiayan, styled Shengli, was a native of Xiushui and great-grandson of Xu Bida, Minister of War of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jiayan, styled Shengli, of Xiushui, was great-grandson of the Ming War Minister Xu Bida.

sentences.zh: 幼警敏，強記絕人。

translations.literal: As a child he was alert and clever, with a memory surpassing other men.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was quick and clever, with a memory beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 既，試鴻博，授檢討。

translations.literal: Later he took the Special Examination and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the Special Examination and became reviser.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十年，王師收滇、黔，嘉炎仿鐃歌鼓吹曲，撰聖人出至文德舞二十四章以獻；

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kangxi, as the imperial armies recovered Yunnan and Guizhou, Jiayan modeled drum-and-bugle songs and composed twenty-four pieces from "The Sage Appears" through "The Dance of Civil Virtue" to present to the throne;
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 20, when imperial forces recovered Yunnan and Guizhou, Jiayan modeled the drum-and-bugle songs and presented twenty-four pieces from "The Sage Appears" through "The Dance of Civil Virtue";

sentences.zh: 又四年元夕，聖祖於南海大放燈火，縱臣民使觀，嘉炎复應制撰記：皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Four years later, on the Lantern Festival, the emperor lit the South Sea with lanterns and opened the spectacle to officials and commoners alike; Jiayan again wrote an imperial commission—both pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, on Lantern Festival night, the emperor lit the South Sea with lanterns and let officials and people look on freely; Jiayan again wrote on imperial command—and both works pleased the emperor.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍直，命背誦咸有一德，終篇不失一字。

translations.literal: Once, while on palace duty, he was ordered to recite "There Is One Virtue" from memory and did not miss a single word through the whole text.
translations.idiomatic: Once on palace duty he was told to recite "There Is One Virtue" from memory and did not err in a single word.

sentences.zh: 至「厥德靡常」數語，則斂容讀之，帝為悚異。

translations.literal: When he reached the passage "Its virtue is inconstant," he read with solemn mien, and the emperor was struck with awe.
translations.idiomatic: At the lines "Its virtue is inconstant," he read with grave countenance, and the emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 又嘗問宋元祐黨人是非，嘉炎舉諸人姓名始末，及先儒評騭語其悉。

translations.literal: The emperor once asked about the rights and wrongs of the Yuanyou partisans; Jiayan listed each man's name and story, together with earlier scholars' judgments, with complete thoroughness.
translations.idiomatic: Asked once about the Yuanyou partisan faction, Jiayan gave each man's name and story and the verdicts of earlier scholars with full detail.

sentences.zh: 特賜御臨蘇軾詩一卷，廷臣拜賜御書自此始也。

translations.literal: He was specially granted a scroll of Su Shi's poetry copied by the emperor's own hand—the bestowal of imperial writing upon court ministers began with this.
translations.idiomatic: He received a special gift of Su Shi poems in the emperor's own hand—the court's receipt of imperial calligraphy began here.

sentences.zh: 累擢內閣學士，兼禮部侍郎，充三朝國史及會典、一統志副總裁。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Grand Secretary, concurrent Vice Minister of Rites, and deputy chief compiler of the national history of three reigns, the institutional statutes, and the unified gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to Grand Secretary and concurrent Vice Minister of Rites, and served as deputy chief compiler of the three-reign national history, the statutes, and the unified gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 有抱經齋集。

translations.literal: He authored the Baojing zhai ji.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Baojing zhai ji.

sentences.zh: 方象瑛，字渭仁，遂安人。

translations.literal: Fang Xiangying, styled Weiren, was a native of Suian.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xiangying, styled Weiren, was from Suian.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Kangxi 6.

sentences.zh: 試鴻博，授編修，典試蜀中。

translations.literal: He took the Special Examination, was appointed compiler, and served as chief examiner in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Special Examination and became a compiler, then served as chief examiner in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸。

translations.literal: Soon after he requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 象瑛性簡靜，早慧，十歲作遠山淨賦，驚其長老。

translations.literal: Xiangying's nature was plain and quiet; he was precocious, and at ten years wrote the "Distant Mountains Clear" fu, astonishing the elders.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangying was plain and reserved by nature. Precocious as a child, at ten he wrote the fu "Clear Distant Mountains" and astounded the elders.

sentences.zh: 致仕家居，望益重。

translations.literal: After retiring he lived at home, and his reputation grew ever weightier.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement he lived at home, and his standing only grew.

sentences.zh: 邑有大利弊，則岳岳爭言，歲省脂膏萬計，邑人建思賢祠祀之。

translations.literal: When the district had great benefit or harm at stake, he would speak out forthrightly in contention; each year he saved tens of thousands in levies, and the people of the district erected the Sixian Shrine to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the district faced matters of great public benefit or harm, he spoke out boldly; each year he saved the people tens of thousands in taxes and levies, and they built the Sixian Shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 著健松齋集、封長白山記、松窗筆乘。

translations.literal: He authored the Jiansong zhai ji, Feng Changbai shan ji, and Songchuang biji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Jiansong zhai ji, Record of Ascending Changbai Mountain, and Songchuang biji.

sentences.zh: 萬斯同，字季野，鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Wan Sitong, styled Jiye, was a native of Yin County.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sitong, styled Jiye, was from Yin County.

sentences.zh: 父泰，生八子，斯同其季也。

translations.literal: His father Tai had eight sons; Sitong was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wan Tai had eight sons; Sitong was the youngest.

sentences.zh: 兄斯大，儒林有傳。

translations.literal: His elder brother Sida has a biography in the Confucian scholars section.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Sida has a biography in the Confucian Scholars section.

sentences.zh: 性彊記，八歲，客坐中能背誦揚子法言。

translations.literal: By nature he had a powerful memory; at eight, seated among guests, he could recite Yang Xiong's Fayan from memory.
translations.idiomatic: He had an extraordinarily strong memory; at eight, sitting among guests, he could recite Yang Xiong's Fayan by heart.

sentences.zh: 後從黃宗羲遊，得聞蕺山劉氏學說，以慎獨為宗。

translations.literal: Later he followed Huang Zongxi in study, heard the teachings of the Jishan Liu school, and took watchfulness in solitude as his creed.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied under Huang Zongxi, learned the Jishan Liu school's teachings, and made vigilance in solitude his guiding principle.

sentences.zh: 以讀書勵名節與同志相劘切，月有會講。

translations.literal: He took reading to encourage reputation and integrity, mutually admonishing with like-minded men; each month they held assembly lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He urged moral integrity through study, exchanged frank counsel with fellow scholars, and held monthly lectures.

sentences.zh: 博通諸史，尤熟明代掌故。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in the various histories, especially familiar with Ming-era institutional lore.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the histories and knew Ming institutional precedent especially well.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，薦鴻博，辭不就。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi he was recommended for the Special Examination and declined the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 he was recommended for the Special Examination but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 初，順治二年詔修明史，未幾罷。

translations.literal: At first, in the second year of Shunzhi an edict ordered the compilation of the Ming History; before long it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At first, in Shunzhi 2 an edict ordered work on the Ming History, but the project was halted before long.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，又詔修之，亦止。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi it was again ordered to be compiled, and again stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 the order came again, and again work ceased.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命徐元文為監修，取彭孫遹等五十人官翰林，與右庶子盧君琦等十六人同為纂修。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Xu Yuanwen was appointed supervising compiler; fifty men including Peng Sunyu who held Hanlin posts, together with sixteen including Right Sub-Reader Lu Junqi, were made compilers.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 Xu Yuanwen was named supervising compiler; fifty Hanlin officials including Peng Sunyu and sixteen others including Right Sub-Reader Lu Junqi were appointed compilers.

sentences.zh: 斯同嘗病唐以後史設局分修之失，以謂專家之書，才雖不逮，猶未至如官修者之雜亂，故辭不膺選。

translations.literal: Sitong once criticized the flaw of Tang-era and later histories being divided among bureaus for separate compilation, holding that works by individual scholars, though their talent did not match, still did not reach the disorderliness of official compilations; therefore he declined selection.
translations.idiomatic: Sitong had criticized the practice since Tang times of dividing historical compilation among offices; individual scholars' histories, he argued, though less gifted, were never as chaotic as official ones—so he declined appointment.

sentences.zh: 至三十二年，再召王鴻緒於家，命偕陳廷敬、張玉書為總裁。

translations.literal: By the thirty-second year, Wang Hongxu was again summoned from his home, and ordered together with Chen Tingjing and Zhang Yushu to serve as chief compilers.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 32 Wang Hongxu was summoned home again and appointed chief compiler together with Chen Tingjing and Zhang Yushu.

sentences.zh: 陳任本紀，張任志，而鴻緒獨任列傳。

translations.literal: Chen took charge of the annals, Zhang of the treatises, while Hongxu alone took charge of the biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Chen handled the annals, Zhang the treatises, and Hongxu the biographies alone.

sentences.zh: 乃延斯同於家，委以史事，而武進錢名世佐之。

translations.literal: He then invited Sitong to his home and entrusted him with the historical work, with Qian Mingshi of Wujin assisting him.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Sitong to his home, put him in charge of the history, and had Qian Mingshi of Wujin assist.

sentences.zh: 每覆審一傳，曰某書某事當參校，顧小史取其書第幾卷至，無或爽者。

translations.literal: Each time he reviewed a biography he would say such-and-such book, such-and-such matter should be collated; he would look to a junior clerk to fetch the book by volume—never once was there error.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing each biography he would say which book and passage needed checking; a clerk would fetch the right volume without fail.

sentences.zh: 士大夫到門諮詢，了辯如響。

translations.literal: When scholar-officials came to his door to inquire, his clear answers came like echoes.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who came to consult him received answers as prompt and clear as an echo.

sentences.zh: 嘗書抵友人，自言：「少館某所，其家有列朝實錄，吾默識暗誦，未敢有一言一事之遺也。

translations.literal: Once he wrote to a friend, saying himself: "In youth I lodged at a certain place; the family had the Veritable Records of successive reigns. I memorized them silently and recited them in secret, not daring to let a single word or incident slip.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote a friend: "As a young man I lodged in a household that owned the Veritable Records of successive reigns. I memorized them in silence—I did not let a single word or event slip.

sentences.zh: 長游四方，輒就故家耆老求遺書，考問往事。

translations.literal: Growing up he traveled the four quarters, always going to old families and venerable elders to seek lost books and examine past events.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he traveled widely, seeking lost books from old families and questioning elders about the past.

sentences.zh: 旁及郡志、邑乘，私家撰述，靡不搜討，而要以實錄為指歸。

translations.literal: Extending to prefectural gazetteers, county records, and private compositions, none he did not search out and investigate, yet he always took the Veritable Records as his guide.
translations.idiomatic: He searched prefectural and county gazetteers and private writings of every kind, but always kept the Veritable Records as his standard.

sentences.zh: 蓋實錄者，直載其事與言，而無可增飾者也。

translations.literal: For the Veritable Records directly record events and words and admit no embellishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records record events and words directly, without embellishment.

sentences.zh: 因其世以考其事，覈其言而平心察之，則其人本末可八九得矣。

translations.literal: By their age to examine events, verify their words and examine with even mind, then a person's beginning and end may be got eight or nine parts out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: By dating events, checking words, and judging with impartial care, one can recover eight or nine tenths of a person's life.

sentences.zh: 然言之發或有所由，事之端或有所起，而其流或有所激，則非他書不能具也。

translations.literal: Yet the issuing of words sometimes has its causes, the beginnings of events sometimes have their origins, and their currents sometimes have what stirred them—then only other books can supply the full account.
translations.idiomatic: Yet words have their motives, events their origins, and consequences their provocations—matters only other books can fully supply.

sentences.zh: 凡實錄之難詳者，吾以他書證之。

translations.literal: Where the Veritable Records are hard to detail, I verify them with other books.
translations.idiomatic: Where the Veritable Records are obscure, I corroborate them with other works.

sentences.zh: 他書之誣且濫者，吾以所得於實錄者裁之。

translations.literal: Where other books are false and excessive, I judge them by what I have obtained from the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Where other books are false or exaggerated, I trim them against what the Veritable Records provide.

sentences.zh: 雖不敢具謂可信，而是非之枉於人者蓋鮮矣。

translations.literal: Though I dare not claim them altogether trustworthy, wrong judgments of right and wrong upon persons are probably few.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not claim full reliability, yet wrongful judgments of men are probably rare.

sentences.zh: 昔人於宋史已病其繁蕪，而吾所述將倍焉。

translations.literal: Men of old already complained that the Song History was prolix, yet what I relate will be twice as much.
translations.idiomatic: Critics already found the Song History too verbose; my account will be twice as long.

sentences.zh: 非不知簡之為貴也，吾恐後之人務博而不知所裁，故先為之極，使知吾所取者有所捐，而​​所不取，必非其事與言之真，而不可溢也。」

translations.literal: It is not that I do not know brevity is prized; I fear later men will pursue breadth without knowing how to cut, so I first take it to the extreme, making them know that what I take has what is discarded, and what I do not take must not be the truth of event and word, and cannot be overflowed."
translations.idiomatic: I do not undervalue brevity—but I fear later writers will chase comprehensiveness without knowing what to cut. So I first go to the limit, so they know what I include I also discard, and what I omit is not the true event or word and cannot be added."

sentences.zh: 又以：「馬、班史皆有表，而後漢、三國以下無之。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ma and Ban's histories all have tables, but from Later Han and Three Kingdoms onward there are none.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Ma and Ban's histories all have tables, but from Later Han and Three Kingdoms onward there are none.

sentences.zh: 劉知幾謂得之不為益，失之不為損。

translations.literal: Liu Zhiji held that gaining them would not be gain, losing them would not be loss.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhiji argued that adding them would add nothing and omitting them would lose nothing.

sentences.zh: 不知史之有表，所以通紀、傳之窮者。

translations.literal: He did not understand that tables in history are what extend the limits of annals and biographies.
translations.idiomatic: He failed to see that historical tables exist precisely to extend what annals and biographies cannot cover.

sentences.zh: 有其人已入紀、傳而表之者，有未入紀、傳而牽連以表之者。

translations.literal: Some men already entered in annals and biographies are also tabulated; some not entered in annals and biographies are linked in by tables.
translations.idiomatic: Some figures already in annals or biographies appear again in tables; others not given full entries are brought in through tables.

sentences.zh: 表立而後紀、傳之文可省，故表不可廢。

translations.literal: Once tables are established, then annals and biographies' text can be abbreviated, so tables cannot be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: With tables in place, annals and biographies can be shorter—tables must not be dropped.

sentences.zh: 讀史而不讀表，非深於史者也。」

translations.literal: To read history without reading tables is not to be deep in history."
translations.idiomatic: To read history without reading the tables is not to know history deeply."

sentences.zh: 嘗作明開國訖唐、桂功臣將相年表，以備採擇。

translations.literal: He once composed a chronological table of Ming founding ministers and generals from beginning through the Tang and Gui regimes, to supply material for selection.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a chronological table of founding ministers and generals through the Tang and Gui regimes for use in compilation.

sentences.zh: 其後明史至乾隆初大學士張廷玉等奉詔刊定，即取鴻緒史藁為本而增損之。

translations.literal: Later the Ming History, when at the early Qianlong Grand Secretary Zhang Tingyu and others received edict to revise and fix it, took Hongxu's draft history as the base and added and subtracted from it.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Tingyu and other grand secretaries revised the Ming History under Qianlong, they took Hongxu's draft as their base and revised it.

sentences.zh: 鴻緒藁，大半出斯同手也。

translations.literal: Hongxu's draft was largely from Sitong's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Hongxu's draft came from Sitong's hand.

sentences.zh: 平生淡於榮利，脩脯所入，輒以以周宗黨。

translations.literal: All his life he was indifferent to glory and profit; tuition income that came in he always used to support his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for rank or gain all his life and used his stipends to support his clan.

sentences.zh: 故人馮京第死義，其子沒入不得歸，為醵錢贖之。

translations.literal: His old friend Feng Jingdi died for righteousness; his son was confiscated and could not return—he raised money jointly to redeem him.
translations.idiomatic: When his friend Feng Jingdi died a martyr, Feng's son was seized as property; Sitong collected funds to buy his freedom.

sentences.zh: 尤喜獎掖後進。

translations.literal: He especially liked to encourage and promote younger men.
translations.idiomatic: He especially loved to nurture younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 自王公以至下士，無不呼曰萬先生。

translations.literal: From princes and grandees down to humble scholars, none failed to call him Master Wan.
translations.idiomatic: From nobles to common scholars, all called him Master Wan.

sentences.zh: 李光地品藻人倫，以謂顧寧人、閻百詩及萬季野，此數子者，真足備石渠顧問之選。

translations.literal: Li Guangdi in judging men's character held that Gu Ningren, Yan Baishi, and Wan Jiye—these several men truly sufficed for selection as Shiqu advisers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi judged that Gu Yanwu, Yan Ruoju, and Wan Jiye were truly fit to serve as imperial advisers at Shiqu.

sentences.zh: 而斯同與人往還，其自署則曰「布衣万某」，未嘗有他稱也。

translations.literal: Yet when Sitong associated with men, what he signed himself was "Commoner Wan So-and-so," never using any other title.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in correspondence he signed himself only "Commoner Wan"—never any other title.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 著歷代史表，創為宦者侯表，大事年表二例。

translations.literal: He authored tables of successive dynasties' histories, creating two precedents: the eunuch marquis table and the great events chronological table.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote dynastic historical tables, pioneering the eunuch-marquis table and the great-events chronology.

sentences.zh: 又著儒林宗派。

translations.literal: He also authored Lineages of the Confucian Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Lineages of the Confucian Forest.

sentences.zh: 名世，字亮工。

translations.literal: Mingshi, styled Lianggong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Mingshi, styled Lianggong.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十二年一甲進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year of Kangxi a first-rank jinshi, appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A top-ranked jinshi in Kangxi 42, he became a compiler.

sentences.zh: 夙負文譽，王士禎見其詩激賞之。

translations.literal: From early he bore literary repute; Wang Shizhen saw his poetry and praised it enthusiastically.
translations.idiomatic: He had long enjoyed literary fame; Wang Shizhen read his verse and admired it greatly.

sentences.zh: 鴻緒聘修明史，斯同任考核，付名世屬辭潤色之。

translations.literal: Hongxu engaged him to compile the Ming History; Sitong undertook verification, and handed to Mingshi the task of composing and polishing the language.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxu engaged compilers for the Ming History, Sitong verified facts and gave the prose to Mingshi to compose and polish.

sentences.zh: 官至侍讀，坐投詩諂年羹堯奪職。

translations.literal: His office reached Reader-in-Waiting; he lost his post on account of submitting flattery poetry to Nian Gengyao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Reader-in-Waiting but was stripped of office for sending flattering poems to Nian Gengyao.

sentences.zh: 劉獻廷，字繼莊，大興人，先世本吳人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xianting, styled Jizhuang, was a native of Daxing; his forebears were originally people of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xianting, styled Jizhuang, was from Daxing; his ancestors were originally from Wu.

sentences.zh: 其學主經世，自象緯、律曆、音韻、險塞、財賦、軍政、以逮岐黃、釋老之書，無所不究習。

translations.literal: His learning took governing the age as its master; from astrology, calendrics, phonology, strategic passes, finance and taxation, military administration, down to medical and Buddhist-Daoist books—nothing he did not investigate and study.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship served practical governance; from astronomy and calendrics to phonology, frontier passes, finance, military affairs, and even medicine and Buddhist-Daoist texts—he studied them all.

sentences.zh: 與梁谿顧培、衡山王夫之、南昌彭士望為師友，而復往來崑山徐乾學之門。

translations.literal: With Gu Pei of Liangxi, Wang Fuzhi of Hengshan, and Peng Shiwang of Nanchang he was teacher and friend; he also came and went at the gate of Xu Qianxue of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Pei of Liangxi, Wang Fuzhi of Hengshan, and Peng Shiwang of Nanchang were his mentors and friends; he also studied with Xu Qianxue of Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 議論不隨人後。

translations.literal: In disputation he did not follow behind others.
translations.idiomatic: In debate he never merely followed others' lead.

sentences.zh: 萬斯同引參明史館事，顧祖禹、黃儀亦引參一統志事。

translations.literal: Wan Sitong brought him in to assist with Ming History Bureau affairs; Gu Zuyu and Huang Yi were also brought in to assist with the Unified Gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Sitong brought him into the Ming History project; Gu Zuyu and Huang Yi were enlisted for the Unified Gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 獻廷謂諸公考古有餘，實用則未也。

translations.literal: Xianting said the gentlemen had surplus in examining antiquity, but not yet in practical use.
translations.idiomatic: Xianting said they were strong on antiquarian research but weak on practical application.

sentences.zh: 其論方輿書：「當於各疆域前，測北極出地，定簡平儀制度，為正切線表，而節氣之後先，日食之分秒，五星之凌犯佔驗，皆可推矣。

translations.literal: His discourse on geographical books: "Before each territory one should measure polar altitude, fix the plane astrolabe's system, make a table of tangents—then the sequence of solar terms, the minutes and seconds of eclipses, the violations and prognostications of the five planets—all may be deduced.
translations.idiomatic: On geographical works he argued: "Before each region one should measure polar altitude, establish the plane astrolabe's system, and compile a tangent table—then the order of solar terms, the minutes and seconds of eclipses, and the conjunctions and portents of the five planets can all be calculated.

sentences.zh: 諸方七十二候不同，世所傳者本之月令。

translations.literal: The seventy-two seasonal periods differ among regions; what the world transmits is based on the Monthly Ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: The seventy-two seasonal periods differ by region; what is handed down derives from the Monthly Ordinances.

sentences.zh: 乃七國時中原之氣候，與今不合，則歷差為之。

translations.literal: Yet these were the climate of the Central Plain in Warring States times, not matching today—the calendrical discrepancy accounts for it.
translations.idiomatic: Those reflect the Central Plain climate of Warring States times, which no longer matches the present—the shift in the calendar explains the difference.

sentences.zh: 今宜細考南北諸方氣候，取其核者詳載之，然後天地相應，可以察其遷變之微矣。

translations.literal: Now one ought finely to examine the climates of northern and southern regions, take the verified and record them in detail—then Heaven and Earth will correspond, and one may discern the subtlety of their shifting changes.
translations.idiomatic: One should now examine the climates of north and south in detail, record what is verified, and then Heaven and Earth will correspond—so that subtle shifts may be observed.

sentences.zh: 燕京、吳下，水皆南流，故必東南風而後雨，衡、湘水北流，故必北風而後雨。

translations.literal: At Yanjing and Wu lands, waters all flow south, so there must be southeast wind before rain; at Heng and Xiang waters flow north, so there must be north wind before rain.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanjing and the lower Yangtze, waters flow south, so rain requires a southeast wind; at Heng and Xiang, waters flow north, so rain requires a north wind.

sentences.zh: 諸方山水向背分合，皆紀述之，而風土之剛柔，暨陰陽燥濕之徵，可次第而求矣。」

translations.literal: Each region's mountains and waters, facing and backing, division and joining—all should be recorded—and then the hardness and softness of wind and soil, together with the signs of yin-yang, dryness and damp, may be sought in sequence."
translations.idiomatic: Each region's mountains and waters, their orientations and confluences, should all be recorded—then the hardness or softness of local conditions and the signs of yin-yang, dryness and damp may be traced in order."

sentences.zh: 其論水利，謂：「西北乃先王舊都，二千餘年未聞仰給東南。

translations.literal: His discourse on water conservancy said: "The Northwest is the old capital region of former kings; for more than two thousand years one never heard of relying on supply from the Southeast.
translations.idiomatic: On water conservancy he said: "The Northwest was the ancient capital region; for more than two thousand years it never depended on grain from the Southeast.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 溝洫通，水利修也。

translations.literal: Because ditches and canals were connected and waterworks maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Because ditches and canals were connected and waterworks were maintained.

sentences.zh: 自劉、石雲擾，以訖金、元，千餘年未知水利為何事，不為民利，乃為民害。

translations.literal: From the Liu and Shi turmoil through Jin and Yuan, for over a thousand years men did not know what water conservancy meant—not for the people's benefit but for the people's harm.
translations.idiomatic: From the turmoil of the Liu and Shi regimes through Jin and Yuan, for over a thousand years men forgot what water conservancy meant—it brought the people harm rather than benefit.

sentences.zh: 故欲經理天下，必自西北水利始矣。

translations.literal: Therefore to order and govern the realm, one must begin with Northwest water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: To govern the realm properly, one must begin with waterworks in the Northwest.

sentences.zh: 西北水利，莫詳於水經酈注。

translations.literal: On Northwest waterworks, nothing is more detailed than Li Daoyuan's commentary on the Water Classic.
translations.idiomatic: On Northwest waterworks, nothing is more detailed than Li Daoyuan's Commentary on the Water Classic.

sentences.zh: 雖時移勢易，十猶可得六七。

translations.literal: Though times shift and conditions change, seven or eight parts of ten may still be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Though times have changed, six or seven parts in ten may still hold.

sentences.zh: 酈氏略於東南，人以此少之。

translations.literal: Master Li was brief on the Southeast; men for this reason slight his work.
translations.idiomatic: Li was brief on the Southeast, and critics for that reason undervalue his work.

sentences.zh: 不知水道之當詳，正在西北。」

translations.literal: They do not understand that waterways ought to be detailed precisely in the Northwest."
translations.idiomatic: They fail to see that waterways ought to be treated in detail precisely in the Northwest."

sentences.zh: 於是欲取二十一史關於水利農田戰守者，考其所以，附以諸家之說，為之疏證。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wished to take from the twenty-one histories passages concerning water conservancy, agriculture, war and defense, investigate their reasons, append various schools' explanations, and provide commentary and verification.
translations.idiomatic: He then planned to extract from the twenty-one histories all passages on waterworks, agriculture, and defense, investigate their grounds, add various scholars' views, and provide commentary and verification.

sentences.zh: 凡獻廷所撰著，類非一人一時所能成，故卒不就。

translations.literal: All that Xianting composed and authored—such things in general are not what one man in one time can complete, so in the end he did not finish.
translations.idiomatic: Everything Xianting planned to write was beyond what one man could finish in a lifetime, and in the end none of it was completed.

sentences.zh: 又嘗自謂於華嚴字母悟得聲音之道，作新韻譜，足窮造化之奧。

translations.literal: He also once said himself that from Huayan alphabet syllables he comprehended the way of sounds, composing the New Rhyme System, sufficient to exhaust creation's mysteries.
translations.idiomatic: He also claimed that from the Huayan syllabary he grasped the principles of sound, and wrote the New Rhyme System, sufficient to plumb nature's deepest mysteries.

sentences.zh: 證以遼人林益長之說，益自信。

translations.literal: Verified by the Liao man Lin Yichang's theory, he grew all the more confident.
translations.idiomatic: Corroborated by the Liao scholar Lin Yichang's theory, he grew all the more confident.

sentences.zh: 其法先立鼻音二，各轉陰、陽、上、去、入之五音共十聲，而不歷喉腭舌齒脣之七位。

translations.literal: His method first established two nasal sounds, each turning through the five tones yin, yang, rising, departing, entering—ten sounds in all—without passing through the seven positions of throat, palate, tongue, teeth, and lips.
translations.idiomatic: His method first posited two nasal sounds, each cycling through the five tones—level yin and yang, rising, departing, and entering—for ten sounds in all, without passing through the seven articulatory positions of throat, palate, tongue, teeth, and lips.

sentences.zh: 故有橫轉，無直送，則等韻重疊之失去。

translations.literal: Therefore there is horizontal turning without straight sending—then the overlapping losses of equal rhymes are removed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus there is lateral turning but no direct progression, eliminating the redundancies of equal-rhyme systems.

sentences.zh: 次定喉音四，為諸韻之宗，從此得半音、轉音、伏音、送音、變喉音。

translations.literal: Next he fixed four throat sounds as the lords of all rhymes; from these came half sounds, turning sounds, hidden sounds, sending sounds, and changing-throat sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Next he fixed four throat sounds as the root of all rhymes, from which derived half tones, turning tones, hidden tones, sending tones, and modified throat tones.

sentences.zh: 又以二鼻音分配之，一為東北韻宗，一為西南韻宗，八韻立，而四海之音可齊。

translations.literal: Again with the two nasal sounds he distributed them—one as northeast rhyme lord, one as southwest rhyme lord—eight rhymes established, and the four seas' sounds could be aligned.
translations.idiomatic: He then distributed the two nasal sounds—one governing northeast rhymes, one southwest—eight rhyme groups established, and the sounds of the four seas could be harmonized.

sentences.zh: 於是以喉音互相合，得音十七；

translations.literal: Thereupon combining throat sounds with each other, he obtained seventeen sounds;
translations.idiomatic: Combining throat sounds with one another yielded seventeen phonemes;

sentences.zh: 喉音鼻音互相合，得音十；

translations.literal: combining throat and nasal sounds with each other, he obtained ten sounds;
translations.idiomatic: combining throat and nasal sounds yielded ten;

sentences.zh: 又以有餘不盡者三合之，得音五：共三十二音，為韻父，而韻歷二十二位，為韻母。

translations.literal: again combining the remainder not fully used in threes, he obtained five sounds: thirty-two sounds in all as rhyme fathers, while rhymes passed through twenty-two positions as rhyme mothers.
translations.idiomatic: combining the remaining unused elements in threes yielded five more: thirty-two sounds in all served as rhyme fathers, and twenty-two positions as rhyme mothers.

sentences.zh: 橫轉各有五子，而萬有不齊之聲攝於此矣。

translations.literal: Horizontal turning each had five offspring, and the myriad uneven sounds were gathered within this.
translations.idiomatic: Each lateral turn produced five variants, and the myriad irregular sounds of speech were all encompassed within this system.

sentences.zh: 同時吳殳盛稱其書。

translations.literal: At the same time Wu Shu highly praised his book.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shu at the time praised the work highly.

sentences.zh: 他所著多佚。

translations.literal: His other compositions are mostly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his other works are lost.

sentences.zh: 歿後，弟子黃宗夏輯錄之，為廣陽雜記。

translations.literal: After his death, his disciple Huang Zongxia compiled and recorded them as the Guangyang zaji.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his disciple Huang Zongxia compiled the Guangyang zaji.

sentences.zh: 全祖望稱為薛季宣、王道父一流雲。

translations.literal: Quan Zuwang called him of the same stream as Xue Jixuan and Wang Daofu.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Zuwang ranked him with Xue Jixuan and Wang Daofu.

sentences.zh: 邵遠平，字戒三，仁和人。

translations.literal: Shao Yuanping, styled Jiesan, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yuanping, styled Jiesan, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the third year of Kangxi, selected as bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in Kangxi 3, he was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部郎中，出為江西學政，擢光祿寺少卿。

translations.literal: He passed through Ministry of Revenue director, went out as Jiangxi education intendant, and was promoted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue, then as Jiangxi education intendant, and was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 試鴻博，授侍讀，至少詹事，致仕歸。

translations.literal: He took the Special Examination, was appointed Reader-in-Waiting, reached Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, retired and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Special Examination and became Reader-in-Waiting, rose to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then retired.

sentences.zh: 以書史自娛，於世務泊如也。

translations.literal: He amused himself with books and history, indifferent to worldly affairs as if they were nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed his days among books and histories, utterly detached from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 聖祖南巡，賜御書「蓬觀」額，因自號蓬觀子。

translations.literal: When the Sage Ancestor toured the south, he was granted an imperial inscription reading "Pengguan," and thereby styled himself Master Pengguan.
translations.idiomatic: On the Kangxi Emperor's southern tour, Shao received the imperial inscription "Pengguan" and styled himself Master Pengguan.

sentences.zh: 遠平高祖經邦，明正德中進士，刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Yuanping's great-grandfather Jingbang, a jinshi in the Zhengde era of Ming, was an assistant department director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping's great-grandfather Jingbang, a Ming Zhengde-era jinshi, served as an assistant director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 以建言獲罪。

translations.literal: He was punished on account of submitting a memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished for offering forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 著弘簡錄，起唐迄宋，附以遼、金，未遑及元也。

translations.literal: He authored the Hongjian lu, running from Tang through Song, with Liao and Jin appended, not yet reaching Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Hongjian lu, covering Tang through Song with Liao and Jin added, but not extending to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遠平循其例續之，刊除舊​​史複重不雅馴者，入制誥於帝紀，採著作於儒林，而文苑分經學、文學、藝學三科，十三志則分載於紀傳，名曰元史類編。

translations.literal: Yuanping followed its precedent and continued it, excising from the old histories redundant passages that were inelegant or ill-arranged; placing edicts and enfeoffments in the imperial annals, collecting literary works in the Confucian scholars section, while the literary section was divided into three categories—classical learning, belles-lettres, and technical arts—and the thirteen treatises were distributed among annals and biographies; the work was titled the Yuan Shi leibian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanping continued in that vein, cutting redundant or clumsy passages from earlier histories, placing edicts in the annals and scholarly works in the Confucian Scholars section, dividing the Literary section into classical learning, literature, and technical arts, and distributing the thirteen treatises across annals and biographies—titling the work the Yuan Shi leibian.

sentences.zh: 朱彝尊稱其書非官局所能逮也。

translations.literal: Zhu Yizun declared his book beyond what an official bureau could achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yizun said the work surpassed anything an official compilation could match.

sentences.zh: 別著史學辨誤，京邸、粵行等集。

translations.literal: He separately authored Correcting Errors in Historical Studies, the Jingdi, Yuexing, and other collections.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Correcting Errors in Historical Studies and collections including Jingdi and Yuexing.

sentences.zh: 同邑吳任臣，字志伊。

translations.literal: From the same district, Wu Renchen, styled Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Wu Renchen, styled Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 志行端愨，強記博聞，為顧炎武所推。

translations.literal: His purpose and conduct were upright and sincere; with powerful memory and broad learning, he was recommended by Gu Yanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and sincere in character, with a formidable memory and wide learning, he won Gu Yanwu's esteem.

sentences.zh: 以精天官、樂律試鴻博，入翰林，承修明史曆志。

translations.literal: On account of mastery of celestial offices and musical pitch, he passed the Special Examination, entered the Hanlin, and undertook compilation of the Ming History's treatise on calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for the Special Examination for his expertise in astronomy and music, he joined the Hanlin and worked on the Ming History's calendrical treatise.

sentences.zh: 著周禮大義、禮通、春秋正朔考辨、山海經廣注、託園詩文集，而十國春秋百餘卷尤稱淹貫。

translations.literal: He authored the Zhouli dayi, Litong, Chunqiu zhengshuo kaobian, Expanded Commentary on the Shanhai jing, and the Tuoyuan shiwen ji, while his Ten Kingdoms Spring and Autumn in over a hundred juan was especially praised as comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Zhouli dayi, Litong, Chunqiu zhengshuo kaobian, Expanded Commentary on the Shanhai jing, and the Tuoyuan shiwen ji; his Ten Kingdoms Spring and Autumn of more than a hundred juan was especially admired for its breadth.

sentences.zh: 其後如謝啟昆之西魏書，周春之西夏書，陳鱣之續唐書，義例皆精審，非徒矜書法，類史鈔也。

translations.literal: Later works such as Xie Qikun's Western Wei History, Zhou Chun's Western Xia History, and Chen Shan's Continuation of the Tang History—all had careful principles and categories, not merely showing off calligraphic skill like historical anthologies.
translations.idiomatic: Later works such as Xie Qikun's Western Wei History, Zhou Chun's Western Xia History, and Chen Shan's Continuation of the Tang History were all judicious in method—not mere showpieces of compilation, like historical copybooks.

sentences.zh: 謝啟昆，字蘊山，南康人。

translations.literal: Xie Qikun, styled Yunshan, was a native of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qikun, styled Yunshan, was from Nankang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in Qianlong 25.

sentences.zh: 由編修簡鎮江知府，後至廣西巡撫，卒官。

translations.literal: From compiler he was selected as prefect of Zhenjiang, later rose to governor of Guangxi, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from compiler to prefect of Zhenjiang, he later became governor of Guangxi and died in office.

sentences.zh: 嘗築湘、漓二江之堤，詳見本傳。

translations.literal: He once built dikes on the Xiang and Li rivers; details appear in his main biography.
translations.idiomatic: He built dikes on the Xiang and Li rivers—described at length in his main biography.

sentences.zh: 又修廣西通志，阬元言可為省志法。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Guangxi gazetteer; its foundational principles could serve as a model for provincial gazetteers.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Guangxi gazetteer, whose basic principles could serve as a model for provincial gazetteers.

sentences.zh: 啟昆以魏書專主東魏，不載西魏四主，北史亦無糾正，乃作西魏書十二篇。

translations.literal: Qikun, because the Wei History favors Eastern Wei and omits the four Western Wei rulers, with the Northern History failing to correct this, wrote twelve chapters of a Western Wei History.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Wei History favors Eastern Wei and omits the four Western Wei rulers—and the Northern History never corrected the error—Qikun wrote twelve chapters of a Western Wei History.

sentences.zh: 周春，字芚兮，海寧人。

translations.literal: Zhou Chun, styled Chanxi, was a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chun, styled Chanxi, was from Haining.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十九年進士，選岑溪令，父憂去。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the nineteenth year of Qianlong, selected as magistrate of Cenxi, left office on father's death.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in Qianlong 19, he became magistrate of Cenxi and left office when his father died.

sentences.zh: 民懷其澤，合前令山陽劉信嘉、金壇於烜共祀之，曰岑溪三賢祠。

translations.literal: The people cherished his benevolence and jointly enshrined him with former magistrates Liu Xinjia of Shanyang and Yu Xuan of Jintan in the Three Worthies Shrine of Cenxi.
translations.idiomatic: The people honored his benevolence and, together with former magistrates Liu Xinjia of Shanyang and Yu Xuan of Jintan, enshrined him in the Three Worthies Shrine of Cenxi.

sentences.zh: 重宴鹿鳴，加六品銜。

translations.literal: At the repeat deer-ming banquet, he was granted sixth-rank title.
translations.idiomatic: At the repeat deer-ming banquet he received sixth-rank title.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十七。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 撰述甚多，而西夏書為最著。

translations.literal: He wrote extensively, but the Western Xia History was his most renowned work.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote extensively, but the Western Xia History was his best-known work.

sentences.zh: 春同州陳鱣，字仲魚。

translations.literal: Chun's fellow townsman Chen Shan, styled Zhongyu.
translations.idiomatic: Chun's fellow townsman Chen Shan, styled Zhongyu.

sentences.zh: 強於記誦，喜聚書。

translations.literal: Strong in memorization and recitation, he loved collecting books.
translations.idiomatic: He had a strong memory and loved collecting books.

sentences.zh: 州人吳騫拜經樓書亦富，得善木互相鈔藏。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Wu Qian's Baijing lou library was also rich; obtaining fine editions, they copied and kept one another's books.
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Wu Qian's Baijing lou library was also rich; when they found fine editions, they copied and exchanged them.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶改元，舉孝廉方正。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing's reign change, he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 1 he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 又明年，中式舉人。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 計偕入都，從錢大昕、翁方綱、段玉裁遊。

translations.literal: Traveling to the capital for the metropolitan examination, he associated with Qian Daxin, Weng Fanggang, and Duan Yucai.
translations.idiomatic: On his journey to the capital for the metropolitan examination, he studied with Qian Daxin, Weng Fanggang, and Duan Yucai.

sentences.zh: 後客吳門，與黃丕烈定交。

translations.literal: Later he sojourned in Suzhou and formed a close friendship with Huang Pilie.
translations.idiomatic: He later lived in Suzhou and became close friends with Huang Pilie.

sentences.zh: 精校勘之學。

translations.literal: He mastered the art of textual collation.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered textual collation.

sentences.zh: 嘗以朱梁無道，李氏既係賜姓，复奉天祐年號，至十年立廟太原，合高祖、太宗、懿宗、昭宗為七廟，唐亡而實存焉；

translations.literal: He once argued that Later Liang was without the Way; the Li clan, having been granted the imperial surname, still followed the Tianyou reign title; by the tenth year they established a temple at Taiyuan, combining Gaozu, Taizong, Yizong, and Zhaozong into seven temples—the Tang had perished yet in fact survived;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Later Liang was illegitimate; the Li clan, though granted the imperial surname, still used the Tianyou reign title, and by the tenth year had established a temple at Taiyuan enshrining Gaozu, Taizong, Yizong, and Zhaozong in seven temples—the Tang had fallen yet in truth endured;

sentences.zh: 南唐為憲宗五代孫建王之玄孫，祀唐配天，不失舊物，尤宜大書年號，以臨諸國：於是撰續唐書七十卷。

translations.literal: Southern Tang were great-great-grandsons of the fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Xianzong, Prince of Jian; they sacrificed to Tang and matched Heaven, not losing the old regalia—especially they should inscribe the reign title in large characters to preside over the states: therefore he compiled a Continuation of the Tang History in seventy juan.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang were great-great-grandsons of Prince Jian, fifth-generation descendant of Emperor Xianzong; they worshipped Tang and matched Heaven, preserving the old regalia—they above all should proclaim the reign title to rule the states: he therefore wrote a Continuation of the Tang History in seventy juan.

sentences.zh: 又有論語古訓、石經說、經籍跋文，恆言廣證諸書。

translations.literal: He also wrote Old Exegesis of the Analects, Studies on the Stone Classics, Colophons on Classics and Histories, and Expanded Verification of Colloquial Sayings, among other works.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Old Exegesis of the Analects, Studies on the Stone Classics, Colophons on Classics and Histories, and Expanded Verification of Colloquial Sayings.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 喬萊，字石林，寶應人。

translations.literal: Qiao Lai, styled Shilin, was a native of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Lai, styled Shilin, was from Baoying.

sentences.zh: 父可聘，明末為御史，有聲。

translations.literal: His father Keping, a censor in the late Ming, had a notable reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Keping had been a late-Ming censor of some renown.

sentences.zh: 萊，康熙六年進士，授內閣中書，乞養歸。

translations.literal: Lai, a jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi, was appointed Grand Secretariat secretary and requested leave to care for his parents and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in Kangxi 6, Lai became a Grand Secretariat secretary, then requested leave to care for his parents and went home.

sentences.zh: 十八年，試鴻博，授編修，與修明史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he passed the Special Examination, was appointed compiler, and joined compilation of the Ming History.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he passed the Special Examination, became a compiler, and worked on the Ming History.

sentences.zh: 典廣西鄉試，充實錄館纂修官，遷侍讀。

translations.literal: He presided over the Guangxi provincial examination, served as compiler at the Veritable Records Bureau, and was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Guangxi provincial examination, served as a Veritable Records compiler, and rose to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 時御史奏濬海口，瀉積水，而河道總督靳輔言其不便，請於邵伯、高郵間置閘洩水，复築長堤抵海口束之，使水勢高則趨海易，廷議多主河臣言。

translations.literal: At the time a censor memorialized dredging the estuary to drain accumulated water, while Grand Canal Director Jin Fu said it was impracticable and requested sluice gates between Shaobo and Gaoyou to release water, and rebuilding a long dike reaching the estuary to confine it, so that when the water level rose it would flow to the sea more easily; court discussion mostly favored the river official's view.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor proposed dredging the estuary to drain floodwater, Grand Canal Director Jin Fu argued against it, proposing sluices between Shaobo and Gaoyou and a long dike to the sea to raise the water level and speed its outflow; most court opinion sided with Jin Fu.

sentences.zh: 適萊入直，詔問萊，疏陳四不可行，略謂：「開河築堤，勢必壞隴畝，毀村落，不可行一。

translations.literal: It happened that Lai entered duty; the emperor questioned Lai, and in a memorial he set forth four reasons it could not be done, broadly saying: "Opening a canal and building dikes will inevitably ruin fields and destroy villages—reason one it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Lai happened to be on duty when the emperor asked him; in a memorial he set forth four reasons the plan would fail, saying in part: "Opening a canal and building dikes will inevitably ruin fields and destroy villages—that is the first reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚地卑，多積潦，今取濕土投深淵，工安得成？

translations.literal: Huai and Yang lands are low, with much accumulated flooding; now to throw wet earth into deep abysses—how can the work succeed?
translations.idiomatic: The Huai and Yang region is low and waterlogged; to throw wet earth into deep water—how can the work succeed?

sentences.zh: 不可行二。

translations.literal: Reason two it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 築丈六之堤，束水高一丈，秋雨驟至，勢必潰；

translations.literal: Building dikes one zhang six chi high, confining water one zhang higher, when autumn rains come suddenly they will inevitably burst;
translations.idiomatic: Building dikes one zhang six chi high to confine water a zhang higher—when autumn rains come suddenly, they will inevitably burst;

sentences.zh: 即當未潰，瀦水屋廬之上，豈能安枕？

translations.literal: Even before they burst, water dammed above houses and dwellings—how could one rest in peace?
translations.idiomatic: and even before they burst, water would stand above houses and dwellings—who could sleep in peace?

sentences.zh: 不可行三。

translations.literal: Reason three it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third reason it cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 至於七州縣之田，向沒於水，今更束河使高，則田水豈復能涸？

translations.literal: As for the fields of seven prefectures and counties, formerly submerged in water, now further confining the river to make it higher—how could the fields ever drain dry?
translations.idiomatic: As for the fields of seven prefectures and counties already submerged, to confine the river further and raise its level—how could those fields ever drain?

sentences.zh: 不可行四。」

translations.literal: Reason four it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth reason it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 帝是之，議乃寢。

translations.literal: The emperor approved this, and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，罷歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 he was dismissed and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，召來京。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was summoned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 旋卒。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 萊著易俟，雜採宋、元諸家易說，推求人事，參以古今治亂得失，蓋誠齋易傳之支流。

translations.literal: Lai authored the Yi si, drawing on Song and Yuan commentaries on the Changes, seeking application in human affairs and comparing gains and losses in governance through the ages—essentially a branch of Yang's Commentary on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Lai wrote the Yi si, drawing on Song and Yuan commentaries on the Changes to explore human affairs and weigh the gains and losses of governance through the ages—a line descended from Yang's Commentary on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 詩文有應制、直廬、使粵、歸田諸集。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose include collections titled Yingzhi, Zhilu, Shiyue, and Guitian.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose include the Yingzhi, Zhilu, Shiyue, and Guitian collections.

sentences.zh: 孫億，亦工詩。

translations.literal: His grandson Yi also excelled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yi also wrote fine poetry.

sentences.zh: 汪楫，字舟次，江都人，原籍休寧。

translations.literal: Wang Ji, styled Zhouci, was a native of Jiangdu, originally registered in Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, styled Zhouci, was from Jiangdu, originally registered in Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 性伉直，意氣偉然。

translations.literal: By nature upright and blunt, his spirit was bold and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and upright by nature, he had a bold and imposing spirit.

sentences.zh: 始以歲貢生署贛榆訓導。

translations.literal: At first, as an annual tribute student he served as acting director of studies in Ganyu.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as acting director of studies in Ganyu as an annual tribute student.

sentences.zh: 應鴻博，授檢討，入史館。

translations.literal: He passed the Special Examination, was appointed reviser, and entered the History Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Special Examination, became a reviser, and entered the History Bureau.

sentences.zh: 言於總裁，先仿宋李燾長編，匯集詔諭、奏議、邸報之屬，由是史材皆備。

translations.literal: He told the chief compilers to first follow Song Li Tao's comprehensive chronicle model, gathering edicts, memorials, court gazettes and the like—thereby historical materials were all prepared.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the chief compilers to follow Song Li Tao's comprehensive chronicle model, gathering edicts, memorials, and court gazettes—so that historical materials were fully assembled.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，充冊封琉球正使，宣布威德。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he served as chief envoy to invest Ryukyu, proclaiming imperial might and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 he served as chief envoy to invest Ryukyu, proclaiming imperial authority and virtue.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，不受例餽，國人建卻金亭誌之。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he refused customary gifts; the Ryukyuans built the Declining Gold Pavilion to commemorate this.
translations.idiomatic: Before departure he refused customary gifts, and the Ryukyuans built the Declining Gold Pavilion in his honor.

sentences.zh: 歸撰使琉球錄，載禮儀暨山川景物。

translations.literal: Returning, he compiled Record of an Embassy to Ryukyu, recording ceremonies and landscape features.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he wrote the Record of an Embassy to Ryukyu, recording ceremonies and local scenery.

sentences.zh: 又因諭祭故王，入其廟，默識所立主，兼得琉球世纘圖，參之明代事實，詮次為中山沿革志。

translations.literal: At the command to perform sacrifices for the former king, he entered the temple and silently noted the enshrined tablets; he also obtained the Ryukyu succession chart, compared it with Ming records, and arranged it as the Zhongshan yange zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to perform sacrifices for the former king, he entered the temple and silently noted the enshrined tablets; he also obtained the Ryukyu succession chart, checked it against Ming records, and compiled the Zhongshan yange zhi.

sentences.zh: 出知河南府，置學田，嵩陽書院聘詹事耿介主講席。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Henan, he established school lands and engaged the Mentor Geng Jie to head the lecture chair at Songyang Academy.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Henan he established school lands and invited Mentor Geng Jie to lecture at Songyang Academy.

sentences.zh: 治行為中州最。

translations.literal: His administrative conduct ranked first in the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: His record of governance ranked first in the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 擢福建按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: Promoted provincial surveillance commissioner of Fujian, then administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Fujian surveillance commissioner and then administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 楫少工詩，與三原孫枝蔚、泰州吳嘉紀齊名。

translations.literal: Ji from youth excelled at poetry and was equally renowned with Sun Zhiwei of Sanyuan and Wu Jiji of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ji wrote fine poetry and was ranked with Sun Zhiwei of Sanyuan and Wu Jiji of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 有悔齋集、觀海集。

translations.literal: He authored the Huizhai ji and Guanhai ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Huizhai ji and Guanhai ji.

sentences.zh: 同里汪懋麟，字季甪，並有詩名，時稱「二汪」。

translations.literal: Fellow townsman Wang Maolin, styled Jisu, shared poetic fame—they were called the "Two Wangs."
translations.idiomatic: Fellow townsman Wang Maolin, styled Jisu, shared his poetic fame; together they were called the "Two Wangs."

sentences.zh: 康熙六年進士，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi, appointed Grand Secretariat secretary.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in Kangxi 6, he became a Grand Secretariat secretary.

sentences.zh: 舉鴻博，持服不與試。

translations.literal: Recommended for the Special Examination, he was in mourning and did not take the test.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the Special Examination, he was in mourning and did not sit for it.

sentences.zh: 服闋，復用徐乾學薦，以刑部主事入史館為纂修官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, again through Xu Qianxue's recommendation he entered the History Bureau as compiler with the rank of principal in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Xu Qianxue recommended him again, and he entered the History Bureau as a compiler with the rank of principal in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 懋麟績學有幹才。

translations.literal: Maolin combined solid scholarship with practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Maolin combined solid learning with practical ability.

sentences.zh: 為中書時，楚人朱方旦挾邪說動公卿，懋麟作辨道論詆之。

translations.literal: As secretary, the Chu man Zhu Fangdan wielded heterodox doctrines to sway high officials; Maolin wrote Disputing the Way to denounce him.
translations.idiomatic: While a secretary, the Chu scholar Zhu Fangdan used heterodox teachings to sway high officials; Maolin wrote Disputing the Way to refute him.

sentences.zh: 熊賜履見其文，與定交。

translations.literal: Xiong Cilu read his essay and formed a lasting friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Cilu read his essay and became his close friend.

sentences.zh: 及居刑曹，勤於職事。

translations.literal: When he served in the Ministry of Justice, he was diligent in duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ministry of Justice he was diligent in his duties.

sentences.zh: 有武某乘車宿董之貴家，之貴利其貲，殺之。

translations.literal: A certain Wu rode in a carriage and lodged at Dong Zhigui's home; Zhigui coveted his wealth and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: A man surnamed Wu rode in a carriage and stayed at Dong Zhigui's house; Zhigui coveted his money and killed him.

sentences.zh: 車載而棄於道，鞭馬使馳。

translations.literal: He loaded the body in the carriage and abandoned it on the road, whipping the horse to make it gallop away.
translations.idiomatic: He loaded the body into the carriage, abandoned it on the road, and whipped the horse to send it galloping off.

sentences.zh: 武父得車馬劉氏之門，訟劉殺其子。

translations.literal: Wu's father found the carriage and horse at the Liu family's gate and sued Liu for killing his son.
translations.idiomatic: Wu's father found the carriage and horse at the Liu family's gate and sued Liu for murdering his son.

sentences.zh: 懋麟曰：「殺人而置其車馬於門，非理也。」

translations.literal: Maolin said: "To kill a man and leave his carriage and horse at the gate is unreasonable."
translations.idiomatic: Maolin said: "To kill a man and leave his carriage and horse at the gate makes no sense."

sentences.zh: 乃微行，縱其馬，馬至之貴門，駭躍悲鳴。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went out in plain clothes, released the horse, and when the horse reached Zhigui's gate it started in fright, leaping and crying mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: He then went out in plain clothes and released the horse; when it reached Zhigui's gate it started in fright, leaping and whinnying mournfully.

sentences.zh: 因收之貴，一訊得實，置於法。

translations.literal: He then arrested Zhigui; one interrogation brought out the truth, and the law was applied.
translations.idiomatic: He then arrested Zhigui; one interrogation established the facts, and the law was applied.

sentences.zh: 其發姦摘伏多類此。

translations.literal: His uncovering of hidden wrongdoing was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He uncovered hidden crimes in many cases like this.

sentences.zh: 懋麟從王士禎學詩，而才氣橫逸，視士禎為別格。

translations.literal: Maolin studied poetry under Wang Shizhen, yet his talent poured forth freely—he stood apart from Shizhen's style.
translations.idiomatic: Maolin studied poetry with Wang Shizhen, but his talent ran freely and formed a style apart from Shizhen's.

sentences.zh: 有百尺梧桐閣集。

translations.literal: He authored the Baichi wutong ge ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Baichi wutong ge ji.

sentences.zh: 陸葇，字次友，平湖人。

translations.literal: Lu Rong, styled Ciyou, was a native of Pinghu.
