translations.idiomatic: Lu Rong, styled Ciyou, was from Pinghu.

sentences.zh: 幼時值大軍收平湖，父被執，葇詣軍前乞代父。

translations.literal: As a child, when the great army took Pinghu, his father was seized; Rong went before the army to beg to take his father's place.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy, when the Qing army took Pinghu, his father was seized; Rong went to the camp and begged to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 軍將手詩★M3示之曰：「兒能讀是耶？

translations.literal: The general showed him a poem in hand and said: "Can you read this, boy?
translations.idiomatic: The general held out a poem and said: "Can you read this, boy?

sentences.zh: 吾赦汝父。」

translations.literal: I will pardon your father."
translations.idiomatic: I will pardon your father."

sentences.zh: 葇朗誦「收兵四解降王縛，教子三升上將台」，曰；

translations.literal: Rong recited clearly: "When the army withdrew, four bonds of the surrendering king were loosed; teaching one's son, thrice he ascended the general's platform," and said;
translations.idiomatic: Rong recited clearly: "When the army withdrew, four bonds of the surrendering king were loosed; teaching one's son, thrice he ascended the general's platform," and said;

sentences.zh: 「此宋人贈曹武惠王詩也。

translations.literal: "This is a Song poem presented to Marquis Wu of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: "This is a Song poem presented to Marquis Wu of Cao.

sentences.zh: 將軍不嗜殺，即今之武惠王矣！」

translations.literal: The general does not delight in killing—you are today's Marquis Wu of Cao!"
translations.idiomatic: The general does not delight in killing—you are today's Marquis Wu of Cao!"

sentences.zh: 將軍喜，挾與北行，善育之，為議婚。

translations.literal: The general was pleased, took him north, nurtured him kindly, and sought to arrange a marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The general was pleased, took him north, treated him well, and sought to arrange a marriage.

sentences.zh: 以先問名於楊，辭歸。

translations.literal: Because marriage had already been pledged to the Yang family, he declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had already been betrothed to the Yang family, he declined and returned home.

sentences.zh: 補諸生，入國學，試授中書。

translations.literal: Made up as a county student, entered the Imperial Academy, and on examination was appointed secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Restored as a county student, he entered the Imperial Academy and on examination was appointed secretary.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年進士，管內秘書院典藉。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the sixth year of Kangxi, he served as librarian of the Inner Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi in Kangxi 6, he served as librarian of the Inner Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 再試鴻博，授編修，分纂明史，命直南書房。

translations.literal: He took the Special Examination again, was appointed compiler, was assigned to compile the Ming History, and was ordered to serve in the Southern Library.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Special Examination again, became a compiler, helped compile the Ming History, and was assigned to the Southern Library.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，召試翰詹諸臣豐澤園，聖祖親置第一，謂曰：「連試詩文。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, Hanlin and Secretariat officials were summoned for examination at Fengzeyuan; the Sage Ancestor personally ranked him first and said: "Having tested your poetry and prose in succession,
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 33, Hanlin and Secretariat officials were tested at Fengzeyuan; the Kangxi Emperor ranked him first and said: "After testing your poetry and prose repeatedly,

sentences.zh: 無出汝右者。」

translations.literal: none surpass you."
translations.idiomatic: no one surpasses you."

sentences.zh: 一歲七遷，至內閣學士。

translations.literal: Within one year he was promoted seven times, reaching Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was promoted seven times, reaching Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 長至，奏句決本，請出矜疑二十餘人。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice, presenting the list for final capital sentences, he requested release of more than twenty cases of doubtful guilt.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice he reviewed death sentences and requested clemency for more than twenty doubtful cases.

sentences.zh: 後一年告歸。

translations.literal: One year later he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he retired.

sentences.zh: 葇性孝友，兄南雄知府世楷前卒，葇教養遺孤，俾成立，有名於時。

translations.literal: Rong was filial and fraternal by nature. His elder brother Shikai, prefect of Nanxiong, had died earlier; Rong raised and nurtured the orphaned children, enabling them to establish themselves, winning renown at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and devoted as a brother, Rong raised his late elder brother Shikai's orphaned children to maturity after Shikai, prefect of Nanxiong, had died earlier, winning renown at the time.

sentences.zh: 年七十，卒。

translations.literal: At age seventy he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 著雅坪詩文藁。

translations.literal: He authored the Yaping shi wen gao.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Yaping shi wen gao.

sentences.zh: 奎勳，字聚侯，世楷子也。

translations.literal: Kuixun, styled Juhou, was Shikai's son.
translations.idiomatic: Kuixun, styled Juhou, was Shikai's son.

sentences.zh: 少隨葇京師，以學行為公卿所推重，顧久困諸生中。

translations.literal: As a youth he followed Rong to the capital; for learning and conduct he was highly recommended by grandees, yet long remained stuck among county students.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he followed Rong to the capital; grandees respected his learning and conduct, yet he long remained a county student.

sentences.zh: 康熙末，年幾六十，始成進士，授檢討，充明史纂修官。

translations.literal: Near the end of Kangxi, at nearly sixty, he finally became a jinshi, was appointed reviser, and served as Ming History compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Kangxi, at nearly sixty, he finally passed the jinshi examination, became a reviser, and served as a Ming History compiler.

sentences.zh: 匄疾歸，主廣西秀峰書院。

translations.literal: Requesting leave on grounds of illness, he returned home and headed Xiufeng Academy in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, he returned home and headed Xiufeng Academy in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 奎勳篤於經學，忘飢渴寒暑。

translations.literal: Kuixun was devoted to classical learning, forgetting hunger, thirst, cold, and heat.
translations.idiomatic: Kuixun was devoted to classical learning, heedless of hunger, thirst, cold, or heat.

sentences.zh: 著陸堂易學，謂說卦一篇，足該全易。

translations.literal: He authored Lutang yixue, declaring that the Explaining the Trigrams chapter alone fully encompasses the entire Changes.
translations.idiomatic: In his Lutang yixue he argued that the Explaining the Trigrams chapter alone fully encompasses the entire Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 其詩學與明何楷詩世本古義相近。

translations.literal: His study of the Odes was close to Ming He Kai's Shishi ben gu yi.
translations.idiomatic: His Odes scholarship resembled Ming He Kai's Shishi ben gu yi.

sentences.zh: 尚書說，惟解伏生今文二十八篇、戴禮緒言，糾正漢人穿鑿附會之失。

translations.literal: In Shangshu shuo, he exclusively explicated Fu Sheng's twenty-eight New Text chapters and the preface of Dai's Rites, correcting Han scholars' forced and far-fetched errors.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangshu shuo he explicated only Fu Sheng's twenty-eight New Text chapters and Dai's Rites preface, correcting Han scholars' forced interpretations.

sentences.zh: 春秋義存錄，則凡經、傳、子、緯所載孔子語盡援為據，力主春秋非以一字褒貶。

translations.literal: In Chunqiu yi cun lu, he took as evidence all Confucian sayings recorded in classics, commentaries, masters, and weft texts, strongly maintaining that the Spring and Autumn does not praise and blame through single-character judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Chunqiu yi cun lu gathers every Confucian saying found in classics, commentaries, masters, and weft texts as evidence, arguing forcefully that the Spring and Autumn does not praise and blame through single-word judgments.

sentences.zh: 奎勳說經務新奇，使聽者忘倦。

translations.literal: Kuixun lectured on the classics seeking novelty, making listeners forget weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Kuixun's lectures on the classics were strikingly original, and listeners never grew weary.

sentences.zh: 最後撰古樂發微，未成而卒。

translations.literal: Finally he began Ancient Music Expounded, but died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: He finally began Ancient Music Expounded but died before finishing it.

sentences.zh: 龐塏，字霽公，任丘人。

translations.literal: Pang Kai, styled Jigong, was a native of Renqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Kai, styled Jigong, was from Renqiu.

sentences.zh: 生有至性。

translations.literal: He was born with utmost sincerity of nature.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed an exceptional nature from birth.

sentences.zh: 七歲時，父緣事被逮，母每夕禱天。

translations.literal: When he was seven, his father was seized on account of a legal matter; his mother prayed to Heaven every evening.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, when his father was seized on account of a legal matter, his mother prayed to Heaven every evening.

sentences.zh: 塏即隨母泣拜，無或間也。

translations.literal: Kai would follow his mother weeping and bowing, never missing a night.
translations.idiomatic: Kai would follow his mother weeping and bowing without fail.

sentences.zh: 稍長，工為文。

translations.literal: As he grew older, he became skilled at writing.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he became skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年舉人，試鴻博，授檢討，分修明史。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the fourteenth year of Kangxi; passed the Special Examination, was appointed reviser, and assigned to compile the Ming History.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in Kangxi 14, he passed the Special Examination, became a reviser, and helped compile the Ming History.

sentences.zh: 明都御史某諂附魏忠賢，其裔孫私餽金，匄閹黨傳諱其事勿書，力拒之。

translations.literal: A Ming censor had fawned on Wei Zhongxian; his descendant privately sent gold, begging that the eunuch faction biography omit this and not record it—Kai forcefully refused.
translations.idiomatic: A Ming censor had fawned on Wei Zhongxian; his descendant privately sent gold, begging that the eunuch faction biography omit the matter—Kai firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 大考降補中書，洊擢戶部郎中，出知建寧府。

translations.literal: Failing the grand evaluation he was demoted to secretary; repeatedly promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue; sent out as prefect of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: After failing the grand evaluation he was demoted to secretary, then rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and was sent out as prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 浦城民以令嚴苛激變，夜焚冊局，殺吏胥，罷市，令懼而逃。

translations.literal: Pucheng people rose in revolt over the magistrate's harshness; by night they burned the register office, killed clerks, closed the markets; the magistrate fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Pucheng people rose in revolt over the magistrate's harsh rule; by night they burned the register office, killed clerks, shut down the markets, and the magistrate fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 塏聞變即馳至浦城，集士民明倫堂，曉喻禍福，戮一人而事定。

translations.literal: Hearing of the disturbance Kai immediately rode to Pucheng, gathered gentry and people at the Hall of Bright Ethics, admonished them of fortune and calamity; executing one person, the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the disturbance, Kai rode at once to Pucheng, gathered gentry and people in the Hall of Bright Ethics, and admonished them of the consequences; after executing one man, the affair was settled.

sentences.zh: 民感其德，立書院祀之。

translations.literal: The people were grateful for his virtue and erected an academy to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful for his virtue, the people erected an academy in his honor.

sentences.zh: 九仙山多盜，至掠人索贖。

translations.literal: Jiuxian Mountain had many bandits, even kidnapping people for ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuxian Mountain swarmed with bandits who even kidnapped people for ransom.

sentences.zh: 掩捕數十人，境內帖然。

translations.literal: Ambushing and capturing dozens, the territory became peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: After ambushing and capturing dozens, the territory became peaceful.

sentences.zh: 未幾，告歸。

translations.literal: Before long he requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he retired.

sentences.zh: 塏嗜吟詠，與同里邊汝元以詩學相劘切。

translations.literal: Kai loved composing poetry; with fellow townsman Bian Ruyuan he mutually honed their poetry studies.
translations.idiomatic: Kai loved composing poetry and, with fellow townsman Bian Ruyuan, sharpened their craft through mutual critique.

sentences.zh: 其所作醇雅，以自然為宗。

translations.literal: His compositions were pure and elegant, taking naturalness as their principle.
translations.idiomatic: His work was pure and elegant, with naturalness as its guiding principle.

sentences.zh: 有叢碧山房集。

translations.literal: He authored the Congbi shanfang ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Congbi shanfang ji.

sentences.zh: 汝元子連寶，字趙珍。

translations.literal: Ruyuan's son Lianbao, styled Zhaozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyuan's son Lianbao, styled Zhaozhen.

sentences.zh: 世其家學。

translations.literal: He inherited the family learning.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family scholarship.

sentences.zh: 以諸生貢成均，廷試第一。

translations.literal: As a county student he was recommended to the Imperial Academy; ranked first in the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: As a county student he was recommended to the Imperial Academy and ranked first in the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 應乾隆元年博學鴻詞科，不中選。

translations.literal: He sat for the Qianlong 1 Broad Learning and Eminent Words Examination but was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: He sat for the Qianlong 1 Broad Learning and Eminent Words Examination but was not selected.

sentences.zh: 十四年，复薦經學，辭不赴。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, recommended again for classical learning, he declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 14, recommended again for classical learning, he declined to go.

sentences.zh: 或勸之行，曰：「吾自審不能如漢伏勝、董仲舒，安敢幸取哉？」

translations.literal: When some urged him to go, he said: "I know myself incapable of matching Han Fu Sheng or Dong Zhongshu—how dare I seek undeserved recognition?"
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him to go, he said: "I know I cannot match Han Fu Sheng or Dong Zhongshu—how dare I seek undeserved recognition?"

sentences.zh: 著有隨園集。

translations.literal: He authored the Suiyuan ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Suiyuan ji.

sentences.zh: 陸圻，字麗京，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Lu Qi, styled Lijing, was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi, styled Lijing, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 少與弟堦、培以文學、志行見重於時，稱曰「三陸」。

translations.literal: In youth with his younger brothers Jie and Pei, for literary talent and purposeful conduct he was respected in the age—they were called the "Three Lu."
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and his younger brothers Jie and Pei were respected for literary talent and upright character—they were called the "Three Lu."

sentences.zh: 所為詩號西​​陵體。

translations.literal: His poetry was called the Xiling style.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was known as the Xiling style.

sentences.zh: 性穎異，善思誤書。

translations.literal: His nature was sharp and unusual; he was skilled at reasoning from textual errors in books.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and unusual by nature, he was skilled at reasoning from textual errors in books.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀韓非子「一從而咸危」，曰：「是'一徙而成邑'也。」

translations.literal: Once reading Han Feizi "from one follow all are endangered," he said: "This is 'one removal and a town is formed.'
translations.idiomatic: Once reading in Han Feizi "from one follow all are endangered," he said: "This is 'one removal and a town is formed.'

sentences.zh: 戲令他人射覆，不得，惟弟廷中之。

translations.literal: In jest he had others guess the answer; none succeeded—only his younger brother guessed it.
translations.idiomatic: In jest he had others guess the answer; none succeeded—only his younger brother got it.

sentences.zh: 平生不喜言人過，有語及者，輒曰：「吾與汝，姑自淑。」

translations.literal: All his life he disliked speaking of others' faults; when someone did, he would say: "You and I—let us first improve ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: All his life he disliked speaking of others' faults; when someone did, he would say: "You and I had better improve ourselves first."

sentences.zh: 莊廷鑨史禍作，圻坐逮。

translations.literal: When the Zhuang Tinglong History Affair arose, Qi was implicated and arrested.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuang Tinglong History Affair arose, Qi was implicated and arrested.

sentences.zh: 以先嘗具狀自陳，事得白，歎曰：「今幸得不死，奈何不以餘年學道耶！」

translations.literal: Because he had previously submitted a written statement in self-defense, the matter was cleared; he sighed: "Now that I have thankfully escaped death, why not spend my remaining years pursuing the Way!"
translations.idiomatic: Because he had previously submitted a written statement in self-defense, the matter was cleared; he sighed: "Having thankfully escaped death, why not spend my remaining years pursuing the Way!"

sentences.zh: 親歿，遂棄家遠遊，不知所終。

translations.literal: After his parents died, he abandoned his home and wandered far away—his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: After his parents died, he abandoned his home and wandered far away—his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: 子寅，成進士。

translations.literal: His son Yin became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 往來萬里，尋父不得，竟悒悒以死，時稱其孝。

translations.literal: Traveling tens of thousands of li back and forth, he could not find his father, and finally died in dejection—they called it filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling tens of thousands of li in search of his father without success, he finally died in dejection—people praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 培死甲申之難。

translations.literal: Pei died in the disaster of jiashen.
translations.idiomatic: Pei died in the disaster of 1644.

sentences.zh: 丁澎，字飛濤，仁和人。

translations.literal: Ding Peng, styled Feitao, was a native of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Peng, styled Feitao, was from Renhe.

sentences.zh: 有雋才。

translations.literal: He had outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: He had outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 嗜飲，一石不亂，弟景鴻、溁並能文，時有「三丁」之目。

translations.literal: He loved drinking—a dan of wine did not unsettle him; younger brothers Jinghong and Rang were also capable writers—they were called the "Three Ding."
translations.idiomatic: He loved drinking—a full dan of wine did not unsettle him; his younger brothers Jinghong and Rang were also fine writers—they were called the "Three Ding."

sentences.zh: 澎，順治十二年進士，官禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Peng, jinshi in the twelfth year of Shunzhi, served as bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Peng, a Shunzhi 12 jinshi, served as bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 嘗典河南鄉試，得一卷奇之。

translations.literal: Once presiding over the Henan provincial examination, he found one exam paper remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: While presiding over the Henan provincial examination, he found one exam paper remarkable.

sentences.zh: 同考請置之乙，澎曰：「此名士也！」

translations.literal: A fellow examiner asked to place it in the second rank; Peng said: "This is a man of distinction!"
translations.idiomatic: A fellow examiner asked to place it in the second rank; Peng said: "This is a man of distinction!"

sentences.zh: 榜發，乃廬陽李天馥，出語人曰：「吾以世目衡文，幾失此士。」

translations.literal: When the list was published it was Li Tianfu of Luyang; Peng told people: "I nearly lost this scholar by judging the essay with conventional eyes."
translations.idiomatic: When the list was published it was Li Tianfu of Luyang; Peng told people: "I nearly lost this scholar by judging the essay with conventional eyes."

sentences.zh: 坐事謫居塞上五載，躬自飯牛，吟嘯自若。

translations.literal: Punished for an offense, he was banished to the frontier for five years, personally feeding cattle, singing and whistling at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for an offense, he was banished to the frontier for five years, personally tending cattle, singing and whistling at ease.

sentences.zh: 所作詩多忠愛，無怨誹之思。

translations.literal: His poems were mostly filled with loyal devotion, without resentful or slanderous thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: His poems were mostly filled with loyal devotion, without resentment or slander.

sentences.zh: 有扶​​荔堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Fuli tang ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Fuli tang ji.

sentences.zh: 先是陳子龍為登樓社，圻、澎及同里柴紹炳、毛先舒、孫治、張丹、吳百朋、沈謙、虞黃昊等並起，世號「西泠十子」。

translations.literal: Earlier Chen Zilong formed the Ascending the Tower Society; Qi, Peng, and fellow townsmen Chai Shaobing, Mao Xianshu, Sun Zhi, Zhang Dan, Wu Baipeng, Shen Qian, Yu Huanghao and others arose together—they were called the "Ten Masters of Xiling."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chen Zilong formed the Ascending the Tower Society; Qi, Peng, and fellow townsmen Chai Shaobing, Mao Xianshu, Sun Zhi, Zhang Dan, Wu Baipeng, Shen Qian, Yu Huanghao, and others rose together—they were called the "Ten Masters of Xiling."

sentences.zh: 紹炳，字虎臣。

translations.literal: Shaobing, styled Huchen.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobing, styled Huchen.

sentences.zh: 在十子中文名最著。

translations.literal: Among the Ten his literary name was most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Ten his literary reputation was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 持躬尤端謹。

translations.literal: His personal conduct was especially upright and careful.
translations.idiomatic: His personal conduct was especially upright and careful.

sentences.zh: 有省軒集。

translations.literal: He authored the Sheng xuan ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Sheng xuan ji.

sentences.zh: 先舒，字稚黃。

translations.literal: Xianshu, styled Zhihuang.
translations.idiomatic: Xianshu, styled Zhihuang.

sentences.zh: 嘗從劉宗周講學。

translations.literal: He once studied under Liu Zongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He once studied under Liu Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 其詩音節瀏亮，有七子餘風。

translations.literal: His poetry had flowing, bright rhythm, retaining traces of the Seven Masters style.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry had a flowing, bright rhythm, retaining traces of the Seven Masters style.

sentences.zh: 著思古堂集。

translations.literal: He wrote the Sigu tang ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Sigu tang ji.

sentences.zh: 治，字宇台。

translations.literal: Zhi, styled Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Yutai.

sentences.zh: 篤友誼，陸培死，以孤女託為擇婿，得吳任臣。

translations.literal: Deep in friendship: when Lu Pei died, he entrusted an orphaned daughter to Zhi to choose a son-in-law; Zhi found Wu Renchen.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply devoted in friendship, when Lu Pei died he entrusted an orphaned daughter to Zhi to choose a son-in-law; Zhi found Wu Renchen.

sentences.zh: 及立嗣，又以甥女嫁焉。

translations.literal: When establishing an heir, he also gave his niece in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: When an heir was established, he also gave his niece in marriage to him.

sentences.zh: 有鑑菴集。

translations.literal: He authored the Jian'an ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Jian'an ji.

sentences.zh: 丹，字綱孫。

translations.literal: Dan, styled Gangsun.
translations.idiomatic: Dan, styled Gangsun.

sentences.zh: 美鬚髯。

translations.literal: He had handsome beard and sideburns.
translations.idiomatic: He had a handsome beard and sideburns.

sentences.zh: 淡靜不樂交遊，而嗜山水。

translations.literal: Calm and quiet, he took no pleasure in socializing, but loved mountains and waters.
translations.idiomatic: Calm and quiet, he took little pleasure in society but loved mountains and rivers.

sentences.zh: 其詩悲涼沉遠，曰秦亭集。

translations.literal: His poetry was desolate, deep, and distant—it was called the Qinting ji.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was desolate, deep, and far-reaching—it was collected as the Qinting ji.

sentences.zh: 百朋，字錦雯。

translations.literal: Baipeng, styled Jinwen.
translations.idiomatic: Baipeng, styled Jinwen.

sentences.zh: 以舉人令南和，有異政，百姓祠祀之。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he served as magistrate of Nanhe; his exceptional governance led the people to worship him in a shrine.
translations.idiomatic: As a provincial graduate he served as magistrate of Nanhe; his exceptional governance led the people to enshrine him.

sentences.zh: 有襆庵集。

translations.literal: He authored the Fuan ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Fuan ji.

sentences.zh: 謙，字去矜。

translations.literal: Qian, styled Qujin.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, styled Qujin.

sentences.zh: 工詩，初喜溫、李，後乃循漢、魏以窺盛唐。

translations.literal: Skilled at poetry; at first he favored Wen and Li, later traced Han and Wei to glimpse High Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at poetry, he first favored Wen Tingyun and Li Shangyin, then traced Han and Wei poetry to glimpse the High Tang.

sentences.zh: 有東江草堂集。

translations.literal: He authored the Dongjiang caotang ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Dongjiang caotang ji.

sentences.zh: 謙與紹炳、先舒皆精韻學。

translations.literal: Qian, Shaobing, and Xianshu were all expert in rhyme studies.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, Shaobing, and Xianshu were all expert in rhyme studies.

sentences.zh: 紹炳作古韻通，先舒作韻學通指、南曲正韻，謙作東江詞韻。

translations.literal: Shaobing wrote Guyun tong, Xianshu wrote Yunxue tongzhi and Nanqu zhengyun, Qian wrote Dongjiang ciyun.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobing wrote Guyun tong, Xianshu wrote Yunxue tongzhi and Nanqu zhengyun, and Qian wrote Dongjiang ciyun.

sentences.zh: 陸圻歎曰：「恨孫偭、周德清曾無先覺。」

translations.literal: Lu Qi sighed: "It is a pity that Sun Mian and Zhou Deqing had no such foresight."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi sighed: "It is a pity that Sun Mian and Zhou Deqing lacked such foresight."

sentences.zh: 黃昊，字景明。

translations.literal: Huang Hao, styled Jingming.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hao, styled Jingming.

sentences.zh: 十歲即善屬文。

translations.literal: At ten he could already compose prose well.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could already compose prose well.

sentences.zh: 薄柳州乞巧，更作辭巧文，識者知其遠到。

translations.literal: He disdained Liu Zongyuan's Begging for Skillfulness and wrote instead a Rejecting Skillfulness essay—those who knew recognized his far-reaching talent.
translations.idiomatic: He disdained Liu Zongyuan's Begging for Skillfulness and wrote instead a Rejecting Skillfulness essay—those who knew recognized his far-reaching talent.

sentences.zh: 康熙中舉人，終教諭。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the Kangxi era; ended as director of studies.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in the Kangxi era, he ended his career as director of studies.

sentences.zh: 孫枝蔚，字豹人，三原人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhiwei, styled Baoren, was a native of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhiwei, styled Baoren, was from Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 少遭闖賊亂，結邑裡少年擊賊，墮坎埳，幸不死。

translations.literal: In youth during the rebel turmoil he gathered local youths to strike at bandits; he fell into a pit trap but fortunately did not die.
translations.idiomatic: In youth, during the rebel turmoil, he gathered local youths to fight bandits; he fell into a pit trap but fortunately survived.

sentences.zh: 乃走江都，習賈，屢致千金，輒散之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to Jiangdu, studied commerce, repeatedly earned a thousand gold, and each time gave it all away.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Jiangdu, took up trade, repeatedly amassed a thousand gold, and each time gave it all away.

sentences.zh: 既乃折節讀書，僦居董相祠，高不見之節。

translations.literal: Afterward he reformed his conduct and took up study, renting lodging at the Shrine of Chancellor Dong, with the lofty integrity of one who does not seek recognition.
translations.idiomatic: He then reformed his ways and devoted himself to study, renting rooms at the Shrine of Chancellor Dong and maintaining the lofty integrity of a man who shuns public notice.

sentences.zh: 王士禎官揚州，以詩先，遂定交，稱莫逆焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Shizhen served as prefect of Yangzhou, he sent poetry first; they formed a friendship and were called bosom companions.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shizhen was prefect of Yangzhou, he introduced himself with a poem; they became friends and were hailed as kindred spirits.

sentences.zh: 時左贊善徐乾學方激揚士類，才俊滿門，枝蔚弗屑也。

translations.literal: At the time Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Xu Qianxue was uplifting men of talent, and gifted scholars filled his house—but Zhiwei disdained it.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent Xu Qianxue was championing men of talent, and gifted scholars thronged his household—but Zhiwei would have none of it.

sentences.zh: 以布衣舉鴻博，自陳衰老，乞還山，遂不應試，授內閣中書。

translations.literal: Recommended for the Special Examination as a commoner, he declared his age and infirmity, begged to return to the mountains, and thus did not take the exam; he was appointed a Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the Special Examination though only a commoner, he pleaded old age and infirmity and begged to retire to the hills; he did not sit for the exam and was appointed a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 著溉堂集，詩詞多激壯之音，稱其高節。

translations.literal: He authored the Gaitang ji; his poetry and lyrics often had stirring, vigorous tones, and people praised his lofty integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Gaitang ji; his poetry and lyrics often rang with stirring vigor, and people praised his lofty character.

sentences.zh: 李念慈，字屺瞻，涇陽人。

translations.literal: Li Nianci, styled Qizhan, was a native of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Nianci, styled Qizhan, was from Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年進士，以河間府推官改知新城縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifteenth year of Shunzhi; as investigating censor of Hejian Prefecture he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Xincheng County.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 15 jinshi, he served as investigating censor of Hejian Prefecture before being transferred to magistrate of Xincheng County.

sentences.zh: 坐逋賦罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for arrears in tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for failing to collect taxes in full.

sentences.zh: 會有荊襄之役，敘運餉勞，再起，補天門。

translations.literal: When the Jingxiang campaign arose, his service in transporting supplies was credited; he was reinstated and appointed to Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jingxiang campaign broke out, he was credited for transporting supplies, reinstated, and appointed to Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 與枝蔚同舉鴻博，試不中選。

translations.literal: Together with Zhiwei he was recommended for the Special Examination, but failed to be selected.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended for the Special Examination together with Zhiwei but was not selected.

sentences.zh: 喜遊，好吟詠。

translations.literal: He loved travel and was fond of composing poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to travel and was fond of composing poetry.

sentences.zh: 有谷口山房集。

translations.literal: He authored the Gukou shanfang ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Gukou shanfang ji.

sentences.zh: 施閏章稱其雄爽之氣勃勃眉宇，蓋秦風而兼吳、楚者。

translations.literal: Shi Runzhang praised the bold, open spirit that brimmed in his features, saying he combined Qin vigor with Wu and Chu grace.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Runzhang praised the bold, open spirit that shone in his face, saying he combined the force of Qin with the grace of Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 丁煒，字瞻汝，晉江人。

translations.literal: Ding Wei, styled Zhanru, was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei, styled Zhanru, was from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: County student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county student.

sentences.zh: 工詩，有吏才。

translations.literal: Skilled at poetry; he had talent for administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at poetry and had a gift for administration.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，定遠大將軍濟度統師取漳州，詔便宜置郡縣吏，得試士幕下，拔煒第一。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi, Great General Jidu led troops to take Zhangzhou; the court authorized discretionary appointment of local officials, and scholars were tested under his command—Wei was ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12, Great General Jidu led troops to capture Zhangzhou; the court authorized him to appoint local officials at discretion, and scholars were tested under his command—Wei ranked first.

sentences.zh: 授漳平教諭，遷知直隸獻縣，內擢戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of studies at Zhangping, transferred to magistrate of Xian County in Zhili, and promoted internally to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of studies at Zhangping, then magistrate of Xian County in Zhili, and was promoted internally to secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時議稅閩鹽，煒力陳不可，事得寢。

translations.literal: At the time there was a proposal to tax Fujian salt; Wei forcefully argued against it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When a proposal arose to tax Fujian salt, Wei argued forcefully against it, and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 由郎中出為贛南分巡道。

translations.literal: From bureau director he was sent out as circuit intendant for southern Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted from bureau director, he was sent out as circuit intendant for southern Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 閩人佃贛者乘亂劫略，號「田賊」，捕治之，民情大洽。

translations.literal: Fujianese tenant farmers in Ganzhou took advantage of the turmoil to plunder and rob; they were called the "Field Bandits." After he captured and punished them, popular sentiment was greatly satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Fujianese tenant farmers in Ganzhou exploited the unrest to plunder and rob; they were called the "Field Bandits." After he captured and punished them, the people were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 遷湖北按察使，脫重囚為盜誣者二十餘人於獄。

translations.literal: Transferred to provincial judge of Hubei, he released from prison more than twenty convicts on capital charges who had been falsely accused as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to provincial judge of Hubei, he released from prison more than twenty men facing capital charges who had been falsely accused as bandits.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事謫官，居武昌，未發，武昌卒夏包子作亂，脅使署。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was demoted for an offense and was living in Wuchang before departing, when Wuchang soldier Xia Baozi rebelled and forced him to sign documents.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was demoted for an offense and was staying in Wuchang before his departure when Wuchang soldier Xia Baozi rebelled and forced him to sign official documents.

sentences.zh: 巡撫以死拒，東走安慶，乞師巡撫楊素蘊。

translations.literal: He refused even at the cost of death, fled east to Anqing, and begged Governor-General Yang Suyun for troops.
translations.idiomatic: He refused even at the cost of his life, fled east to Anqing, and begged Governor-General Yang Suyun for troops.

sentences.zh: 事平，降補知府雲南。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was demoted and reassigned as prefect of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the affair was settled, he was demoted and reassigned as prefect of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 會素蘊移撫湖廣，以煒事聞，复按察職。

translations.literal: When Suyun was transferred to govern Huguang, he reported on Wei's conduct, and Wei was restored to his provincial judge post.
translations.idiomatic: When Suyun was transferred to govern Huguang, he reported on Wei's conduct, and Wei was restored to his post as provincial judge.

sentences.zh: 俄以疾歸。

translations.literal: Before long he returned home due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he retired home due to illness.

sentences.zh: 煒論詩，以為詩貴合法，然法勝則離；

translations.literal: In discussing poetry, Wei held that poetry should value conformity to rules, yet when rules prevail it becomes detached;
translations.idiomatic: In discussing poetry, Wei held that poetry should honor formal rules, yet when rules dominate it grows remote;

sentences.zh: 貴近情，然情勝則俚。

translations.literal: it should value closeness to feeling, yet when feeling prevails it becomes vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: it should honor closeness to feeling, yet when feeling dominates it turns vulgar.

sentences.zh: 故其為詩，力追三唐、漢、魏。

translations.literal: Therefore in his own poetry he strove to follow the Three Tang periods, Han, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in his own poetry he strove to follow the Three Tang periods and the Han and Wei masters.

sentences.zh: 無詭薄之失。

translations.literal: He had no perverse or shallow lapses.
translations.idiomatic: His work never lapsed into perversity or shallowness.

sentences.zh: 有問山集。

translations.literal: He authored the Wenshan ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Wenshan ji.

sentences.zh: 林侗，字同人，閩人也。

translations.literal: Lin Tong, styled Tongren, was a native of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Tong, styled Tongren, was from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 縣貢生。

translations.literal: County tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a county tribute student.

sentences.zh: 喜金石。

translations.literal: He loved bronze and stone inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to bronze and stone inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十八。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 弟佶，字吉人。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ji, styled Jiren.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Ji, styled Jiren.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十二年進士，官中書​​，工楷法。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifty-second year of Kangxi; served as secretary; skilled in regular script.
translations.idiomatic: A Kangxi 52 jinshi, he served as secretary and was skilled in regular script.

sentences.zh: 文師汪琬，詩師陳廷敬、王士禎。

translations.literal: In prose he studied under Wang Wan; in poetry under Chen Tingjing and Wang Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: For prose he took Wang Wan as his master; for poetry, Chen Tingjing and Wang Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 此三人集皆佶手繕付雕，精雅為世所重。

translations.literal: All three men's collected works were copied by Ji's own hand for carving; their refinement and elegance were highly prized by the age.
translations.idiomatic: All three men's collected works were copied in Ji's own hand for printing; their refinement and elegance were highly prized.

sentences.zh: 家多藏書，徐乾學輯經解，朱彝尊選明詩，皆就傳鈔。

translations.literal: The family possessed many books; when Xu Qianxue compiled commentaries on the classics and Zhu Yizun selected Ming poetry, both came to borrow copies for transcription.
translations.idiomatic: The family owned a large library; when Xu Qianxue compiled commentaries on the classics and Zhu Yizun selected Ming poetry, both came to borrow copies for transcription.

sentences.zh: 有樸學齋集。

translations.literal: He authored the Puxue zhai ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Puxue zhai ji.

sentences.zh: 黃任，字莘田，永福人。

translations.literal: Huang Ren, styled Xintian, was a native of Yongfu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ren, styled Xintian, was from Yongfu.

sentences.zh: 工書。

translations.literal: Skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 口辯若懸河。

translations.literal: His eloquence flowed like a hanging river.
translations.idiomatic: His eloquence flowed like a torrent.

sentences.zh: 有硯癖，以舉人令四會，罷官歸，惟硯石壓裝。

translations.literal: He had a passion for inkstones; as a provincial graduate he served as magistrate of Sihui, and when dismissed and returning home, only inkstones weighed down his luggage.
translations.idiomatic: He had a passion for inkstones; as a provincial graduate he served as magistrate of Sihui, and when he was dismissed and returned home, only inkstones filled his baggage.

sentences.zh: 詩清新刻露，有香草齋集。

translations.literal: His poetry was fresh, clear, and incisive; he authored the Xiangcao zhai ji.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was fresh, clear, and incisive; he wrote the Xiangcao zhai ji.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十七年，重宴鹿鳴。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Qianlong, he was honored again at the Deer-Ming banquet.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 27, he was honored again at the Deer-Ming banquet.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: He died at over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 鄭方坤，字則厚，建安人。

translations.literal: Zheng Fangkun, styled Zehou, was a native of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Fangkun, styled Zehou, was from Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the first year of Yongzheng.
translations.idiomatic: A Yongzheng 1 jinshi.

sentences.zh: 為令邯鄲，屢擢至山東兗州知府。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Handan and was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Yanzhou in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Handan and rose through repeated promotions to prefect of Yanzhou in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 時禁人口出海，抵奉天而未入籍者，悉勒還本土。

translations.literal: At the time the population was forbidden to go to sea; those who reached Fengtian without registering were all compelled to return to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: At the time people were forbidden to go to sea; anyone who reached Fengtian without registering was forced to return home.

sentences.zh: 方坤適知登州，以為司牧者但當嚴姦宄之防，不得閉其謀生之路，為白大吏，弛其禁。

translations.literal: Fangkun happened to be prefect of Dengzhou; he held that local officials should only strictly guard against treachery and must not block people's paths to livelihood, and so reported this to the senior officials and had the prohibition relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Fangkun was then prefect of Dengzhou; he argued that local officials should guard strictly against treachery but must not block people's paths to livelihood, reported this to senior officials, and had the prohibition relaxed.

sentences.zh: 調武定，能盡心賑務。

translations.literal: Transferred to Wuding, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to relief work.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Wuding, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to famine relief.

sentences.zh: 兗州飢，复移治之。

translations.literal: When Yanzhou suffered famine, he was transferred back to govern it.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Yanzhou, he was transferred back to govern it.

sentences.zh: 方坤記誦博，詩才凌厲，與兄方城齊名。

translations.literal: Fangkun had broad memory and recitation; his poetic talent was forceful, and he was equally renowned with his elder brother Fangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fangkun had a prodigious memory; his poetic talent was forceful, and he was equally renowned with his elder brother Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 有蔗尾集，又著經稗、五代詩話、全閩詩話、國朝詩人小傳。

translations.literal: He authored the Zhewei ji, and also wrote Jing bai, Wudai shihua, Quan Min shihua, and Guochao shiren xiaozhuan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Zhewei ji, and also authored Jing bai, Wudai shihua, Quan Min shihua, and Guochao shiren xiaozhuan.

sentences.zh: 黃與堅，字廷表，太倉人。

translations.literal: Huang Yujian, styled Tingbiao, was a native of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yujian, styled Tingbiao, was from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 幼有奇慧，八歲，酷好唐人詩，錄小本，懷袖中諷誦之。

translations.literal: From childhood he had extraordinary intelligence; at eight he was passionately fond of Tang poetry, copied it into a small book, and kept it in his sleeve to recite.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he showed extraordinary intelligence; at eight he was passionately fond of Tang poetry, copied verses into a pocket book, and kept it in his sleeve to recite.

sentences.zh: 已而究心經術，遍讀週、秦古書。

translations.literal: Thereafter he devoted himself to classical learning and read widely in Zhou and Qin antiquities.
translations.idiomatic: He then devoted himself to classical learning and read widely in Zhou and Qin antiquities.

sentences.zh: 性落落，與人交有終始。

translations.literal: By nature he was free and easy; in friendship he was steadfast from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Free and easy by nature, he was steadfast in friendship from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年進士，後舉鴻博，授編修，遷贊善，分修明史及一統志。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the sixteenth year of Shunzhi; later recommended for the Special Examination, appointed compiler, promoted to tutor, and assigned to compile the Ming History and the Unified Gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 16 jinshi, he was later recommended for the Special Examination, became a compiler, was promoted to tutor, and helped compile the Ming History and the Unified Gazetteer.

sentences.zh: 寓居委巷，寂寞著書，如窮愁專一之士。

translations.literal: Living in a humble lane, he wrote in solitude like a poor scholar wholly devoted to one pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Living in a humble lane, he wrote in solitude like a poor scholar wholly devoted to his craft.

sentences.zh: 有忍菴集。

translations.literal: He authored the Ren'an ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Ren'an ji.

sentences.zh: 吳偉業選「婁東十子」詩，以與堅為冠。

translations.literal: Wu Weiye selected the poetry of the "Ten Masters of Loudong," placing Yujian at the head.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Weiye selected the poetry of the "Ten Masters of Loudong" and placed Yujian at the head.

sentences.zh: 十子者，周肇、許旭、王撰、王攄、王昊、王揆、王忭、王曜升、顧湄也。

translations.literal: The Ten were Zhou Zhao, Xu Xu, Wang Zhuan, Wang Shu, Wang Hao, Wang Kui, Wang Bian, Wang Yaosheng, and Gu Mei.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Masters were Zhou Zhao, Xu Xu, Wang Zhuan, Wang Shu, Wang Hao, Wang Kui, Wang Bian, Wang Yaosheng, and Gu Mei.

sentences.zh: 肇詩曰東岡集，旭曰秋水集，撰曰三餘集，攄曰蘆中集。

translations.literal: Zhao's poetry was called the Donggang ji, Xu's the Qiushui ji, Zhuan's the Sanyu ji, and Shu's the Luzhong ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's poetry was collected as the Donggang ji, Xu's as the Qiushui ji, Zhuan's as the Sanyu ji, and Shu's as the Luzhong ji.

sentences.zh: 昊，為世貞後，有文藻，下筆如宿構。

translations.literal: Hao was a descendant of Wang Shizhen; he had literary talent, and his writing seemed precomposed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was a descendant of Wang Shizhen; he had literary talent, and his writing seemed effortless.

sentences.zh: 康熙十八年，召試，授官正字。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kangxi he was summoned for examination and appointed proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he was summoned for examination and appointed proofreader.

sentences.zh: 所著曰碩園集。

translations.literal: His collected works were called the Shuoyuan ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Shuoyuan ji.

sentences.zh: 揆，順治中進士，所著曰芝廛集。

translations.literal: Kui, a jinshi of the Shunzhi era, authored the Zhichan ji.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, a Shunzhi-era jinshi, wrote the Zhichan ji.

sentences.zh: 忭曰健菴集，曜升曰東皋集。

translations.literal: Bian's was called the Jian'an ji, and Yaosheng's the Donggao ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bian's poetry was collected as the Jian'an ji, and Yaosheng's as the Donggao ji.

sentences.zh: 湄，字伊人，亦太倉人。

translations.literal: Mei, styled Yiren, was also from Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Mei, styled Yiren, was also from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 事母以孝聞，父夢麟，長於毛、鄭之學，湄傳其業。

translations.literal: He was known for filial service to his mother; his father Menglin was expert in the learning of Mao and Zheng, and Mei inherited his work.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion to his mother; his father Menglin was expert in the learning of Mao and Zheng, and Mei inherited his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 尤工詩，清麗婉約，陳瑚以為過元人。

translations.literal: Especially skilled at poetry, clear, beautiful, and graceful; Chen Hu held that he surpassed Yuan poets.
translations.idiomatic: Especially skilled at poetry, his work was clear, beautiful, and graceful; Chen Hu held that he surpassed Yuan poets.

sentences.zh: 其詩曰水鄉集。

translations.literal: His poetry was called the Shuixiang ji.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was collected as the Shuixiang ji.

sentences.zh: 吳雯，季天章，蒲州人，原籍遼陽。

translations.literal: Wu Wen, styled Tianzhang, was from Puzhou; his ancestral home was Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wen, styled Tianzhang, came from Puzhou; his family was originally from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 父允升，任蒲州學政，卒官，遂家焉。

translations.literal: His father Yun Sheng served as educational commissioner of Puzhou; he died in office, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun Sheng served as educational commissioner of Puzhou, died in office, and the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 雯少朗悟，記覽甚博，尤長於詩。

translations.literal: Wen from youth was bright and perceptive; his reading was very broad, and he was especially accomplished in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wen was bright and perceptive; he read widely and was especially accomplished in poetry.

sentences.zh: 遊京師，父執劉體仁、汪琬皆激賞之。

translations.literal: Traveling to the capital, his father's friends Liu Tiren and Wang Wan all praised him enthusiastically.
translations.idiomatic: When he traveled to the capital, his father's friends Liu Tiren and Wang Wan all praised him enthusiastically.

sentences.zh: 王士禎目為仙才。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen regarded him as a transcendent talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen called him a transcendent talent.

sentences.zh: 嘗與葉方靄同直，誦其警句，方靄下直即趨訪，名大噪。

translations.literal: Once while on duty with Ye Fang'ai, he recited a striking line; as soon as Fang'ai went off duty he hurried to visit him, and Wen's fame spread greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Once while on duty with Ye Fang'ai, he recited a striking line; as soon as Fang'ai went off duty he hurried to visit him, and Wen's fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 大學士馮溥出扇索詩，雯大書二絕句答之，其坦率類是。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Feng Pu sent out a fan requesting a poem; Wen wrote two quatrains in large characters in reply—his frankness was often like this.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Feng Pu sent out a fan requesting a poem; Wen answered with two quatrains written in large characters—his frankness was often like this.

sentences.zh: 卒以不遇，不悔也。

translations.literal: He ultimately went unrecognized, yet he did not regret it.
translations.idiomatic: He ultimately went unrecognized, yet he had no regrets.

sentences.zh: 試鴻博不中選。

translations.literal: He sat for the Special Examination but was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Special Examination but failed to be selected.

sentences.zh: 後居母憂，以毀卒。

translations.literal: Later, while observing mourning for his mother, he died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while mourning his mother, he died from grief.

sentences.zh: 雯著蓮洋集，詩體峻潔，有其鄉人元好問之風。

translations.literal: Wen authored the Lianyang ji; his poetic style was austere and pure, with the spirit of his fellow townsman Yuan Haowen.
translations.idiomatic: Wen wrote the Lianyang ji; his poetic style was austere and pure, with the spirit of his fellow townsman Yuan Haowen.

sentences.zh: 據名山記蓮洋村在華嶽下，取以名集。

translations.literal: According to the Record of Famous Mountains, Lianyang Village lies below Mount Hua; he took the name for his collection.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Record of Famous Mountains, Lianyang Village lies below Mount Hua, and he took the name for his collection.

sentences.zh: 陶季，寶應人。

translations.literal: Tao Ji was from Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Ji, a native of Baoying.

sentences.zh: 初名澂，字季深，以字行，复去其一，稱曰陶季。

translations.literal: Originally named Cheng, styled Jishen; he went by his style name, then dropped one character and was called Tao Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Cheng and styled Jishen, he went by his style name, then dropped one character and was known as Tao Ji.

sentences.zh: 負異才，鋒穎踔厲。

translations.literal: Endowed with unusual talent, his brilliance was sharp and soaring.
translations.idiomatic: Endowed with unusual talent, he wrote with sharp, soaring brilliance.

sentences.zh: 遊燕、趙、齊、魯之郊，逾太行，浮湘、沅，所至皆有詩。

translations.literal: He traveled through the regions of Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Lu, crossed the Taihang Mountains, and sailed the Xiang and Yuan rivers—wherever he went he wrote poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled through Yan, Zhao, Qi, and Lu, crossed the Taihang Mountains, and sailed the Xiang and Yuan rivers—wherever he went he wrote poetry.

sentences.zh: 士禎刪定其客滇南、閩中諸詩，以高、岑、龍標相況。

translations.literal: Shizhen edited his poems from Yunnan and Fujian, comparing him to Gao Shi, Cen Shen, and Li Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen edited his poems from Yunnan and Fujian and compared him to Gao Shi, Cen Shen, and Li Bai.

sentences.zh: 先是詔舉鴻博，公卿爭欲薦，季辭不就，以布衣終。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the court ordered recommendations for the Special Examination, grandees all competed to recommend him, but Ji declined and ended his days as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the court ordered recommendations for the Special Examination, grandees all competed to recommend him, but Ji declined and lived out his days as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 有湖邊草堂集及舟車集。

translations.literal: He authored the Hubian caotang ji and the Zhouche ji.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Hubian caotang ji and the Zhouche ji.

sentences.zh: 梅清，字瞿山，宣城人，宋梅堯臣後也。

translations.literal: Mei Qing, styled Qushan, was from Xuancheng; he was a descendant of Song Mei Yaochen.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Qing, styled Qushan, was from Xuancheng; he was a descendant of the Song poet Mei Yaochen.

sentences.zh: 清英偉豁達，自力於學，以淹雅稱。

translations.literal: Qing was heroic, open, and magnanimous; he applied himself to learning and was known for broad refinement.
translations.idiomatic: Heroic, open, and magnanimous, Qing applied himself to learning and was known for broad refinement.

sentences.zh: 順治十一年舉人，試禮部不第。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the eleventh year of Shunzhi; he sat for the Ministry of Rites examination but did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 11 provincial graduate, he sat for the Ministry of Rites examination but did not pass.

sentences.zh: 朝士爭與之交，王士禎、徐元文尤傾倒焉。

translations.literal: Court officials competed to associate with him; Wang Shizhen and Xu Yuanwen were especially devoted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials vied to befriend him, and Wang Shizhen and Xu Yuanwen were especially devoted.

sentences.zh: 詩凡數變，自訂天延閣前後集。

translations.literal: His poetry underwent several transformations; he compiled the Former and Later Collections of the Tianyan Pavilion himself.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry changed style several times over his career; he edited the Former and Later Collections of the Tianyan Pavilion himself.

sentences.zh: 年七十餘，復合編瞿山詩略。

translations.literal: In his seventies, he again compiled and edited the Qushan Selected Poems.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy, he compiled and edited the Qushan Selected Poems anew.

sentences.zh: 書法仿顏真卿、楊凝式。

translations.literal: His calligraphy imitated Yan Zhenqing and Yang Ningshi.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy followed the manner of Yan Zhenqing and Yang Ningshi.

sentences.zh: 畫尤盤薄多奇氣。

translations.literal: His paintings especially displayed sweeping boldness and an abundance of strange vigor.
translations.idiomatic: In painting he was especially bold and sweeping, full of uncanny energy.

sentences.zh: 嘗作黃山圖，極煙雲變幻之勝，為當時所重。

translations.literal: He once painted a picture of Mount Huang, capturing to the utmost the splendor of shifting mists and clouds, and it was highly valued in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He once painted Mount Huang with such mastery of shifting mists and clouds that the work was greatly prized in his time.

sentences.zh: 同族有梅庚者，生後於清。

translations.literal: Among his clansmen was one named Mei Geng, born later than Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Among his clansmen was Mei Geng, born after Qing.

sentences.zh: 善八分書，亦工詩畫，與清齊名。

translations.literal: Skilled in clerical script, he also excelled at poetry and painting, sharing fame with Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in clerical script, he also excelled at poetry and painting and shared Qing's renown.

sentences.zh: 庚，字耦長。

translations.literal: Geng, styled Ouchang.
translations.idiomatic: Geng, styled Ouchang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，承其祖鼎祚、父朗中之傳，益昌大之。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he inherited the learning handed down from his grandfather Dingzuo and his father Langzhong, and enlarged it still further.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he inherited the learning of his grandfather Dingzuo and his father Langzhong and carried it to new heights.

sentences.zh: 施閏章見其詩，引為忘年交。

translations.literal: When Shi Runzhang saw his poetry, he took him as a friend across the age gap.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Runzhang read his poetry, he took him as a friend despite the age difference.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十年舉人，為朱彝尊所得士。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the twentieth year of Kangxi; he was a favored disciple of Zhu Yizun.
translations.idiomatic: A Kangxi 20 provincial graduate, he was a favored disciple of Zhu Yizun.

sentences.zh: 性狷介，客遊京師，不妄投一刺。

translations.literal: By nature uncompromising and aloof, while visiting the capital as a guest he never casually presented a single calling card.
translations.idiomatic: Uncompromising by nature, he traveled to the capital as a guest yet never casually presented a single calling card.

sentences.zh: 士禎主禮闈，庚復被黜，士禎贈詩引為恨也。

translations.literal: Shizhen presided over the Ministry of Rites examination; Geng was rejected again, and Shizhen sent him a poem expressing this as a regret.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhen presided over the Ministry of Rites examination, Geng failed again; Shizhen sent him a poem lamenting the result.

sentences.zh: 後知泰順縣，有惠政，民德之。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of Taishun County; his benevolent governance won the people's gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Taishun County, he governed with kindness, and the people were grateful.

sentences.zh: 馮景，字山公，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Feng Jing, styled Shangong, was from Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing, styled Shangong, was a native of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 國子監生。

translations.literal: A student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，千言立就。

translations.literal: Skilled at composition; a thousand-character piece was completed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at prose composition, he could finish a thousand-character piece on the spot.

sentences.zh: 康熙時遊京師，侍郎項景襄、金鼐皆遣子弟從受學。

translations.literal: During the Kangxi era he traveled to the capital; Vice Ministers Xiang Jingxiang and Jin Nai both sent their sons and nephews to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he traveled to the capital; Vice Ministers Xiang Jingxiang and Jin Nai both sent sons and nephews to study under him.

sentences.zh: 會營宮室，求楠木樑不得，有請以他木易國子監彝倫堂梁者。

translations.literal: When palace construction was underway and nanmu beams could not be found, someone proposed replacing the beam of the Hall of Ethical Unity at the Imperial Academy with another kind of wood.
translations.idiomatic: During palace construction, when nanmu beams could not be found, someone proposed swapping the beam of the Imperial Academy's Hall of Ethical Unity for timber of another kind.

sentences.zh: 景上書尚書魏象樞，極陳不可，事得寢。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized the Minister Wei Xiangju, arguing forcefully that this must not be done, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized Minister Wei Xiangju, arguing forcefully against the plan, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 由是馮太學生之名盛傳京師。

translations.literal: From this the name of Feng, the Imperial Academy student, spread widely through the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From this the name of Feng, the Imperial Academy student, spread throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 大學士索額圖召欲見之，謝不往。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Songgotu summoned him wishing to see him, but he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Songgotu summoned him, but he declined the audience.

sentences.zh: 歸館淮安邱象隨家垂十年。

translations.literal: He returned and was retained in the household of Qiu Xiangsui in Huai'an for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and lived as a retainer in Qiu Xiangsui's household in Huai'an for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 宋犖撫江蘇，禮致幕府，或納金求為緩頰，峻卻之，人益欽其品。

translations.literal: Song Luo, as governor of Jiangsu, courteously brought him into his staff; some who offered gold asking him to speak on their behalf he sternly refused, and people admired his integrity all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Luo governed Jiangsu, he courteously brought Jing into his staff; when others offered gold to ask him to intercede for them, he sternly refused, and people admired his character all the more.

sentences.zh: 景篤師友風義，與仁和汪煜、湯右曾交最篤。

translations.literal: Jing was deeply devoted to the bonds of teacher and friend; his closest friendships were with Wang Yu of Renhe and Tang Youzeng.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was deeply devoted to the bonds of teacher and friend; his closest friendships were with Wang Yu of Renhe and Tang Youzeng.

sentences.zh: 二人為給事中，多所論列，亦由景數責善有以激厲之也。

translations.literal: The two became supervising secretaries and often submitted memorials criticizing affairs; this too was spurred by Jing's repeated demands for moral improvement.
translations.idiomatic: The two became supervising secretaries and often submitted critical memorials—partly because Jing repeatedly urged them toward moral rectitude.

sentences.zh: 王士禎轉左都御史，景以受知士禎，冀其大有匡濟，為書諷之。

translations.literal: When Wang Shizhen was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief, Jing, who had won Shizhen's esteem, hoped he would greatly set things right in the realm and wrote him a letter of admonition.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shizhen became Left Censor-in-Chief, Jing, whom Shizhen had favored, hoped he would greatly set the realm right and wrote him a letter of admonition.

sentences.zh: 景雖布衣，不求仕進，而未嘗忘當世之務。

translations.literal: Though Jing was a commoner who sought no office, he never forgot the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Though a commoner who sought no office, Jing never forgot the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 在淮安時，有水患，湯斌奉詔北上，作書陳災狀及所以致患之由，斌見書嗟賞，又嘗稱其文為不朽。

translations.literal: While in Huai'an there was flooding; Tang Bin was ordered north on imperial command, and Jing wrote describing the disaster and its causes; Bin read the letter with admiration, and also once praised his writings as immortal.
translations.idiomatic: While in Huai'an during a flood, he wrote to Tang Bin, who had been ordered north on imperial business, describing the disaster and its causes; Bin read the letter with admiration and once praised his prose as immortal.

sentences.zh: 其著述多佚，今存者解舂集。

translations.literal: Most of his writings are lost; what survives today is the Jiechun ji.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his writings are lost; only the Jiechun ji survives today.

sentences.zh: 邵長蘅，字子湘，武進人。

translations.literal: Shao Zhangheng, styled Zixiang, was from Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Zhangheng, styled Zixiang, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 十歲補諸生，因事除名，旋入太學。

translations.literal: At ten he was enrolled as a licentiate; he was stricken from the rolls for an affair and soon entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he became a licentiate; he was stricken from the rolls over an affair and soon entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 工詩，尤致力古文辭，陶鍊雅正。

translations.literal: Accomplished in poetry, he devoted himself especially to ancient-style prose, refining it to elegance and correctness.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplished in poetry, he devoted himself especially to ancient-style prose, refining it to elegance and correctness.

sentences.zh: 與景同客犖幕，長蘅亦觥觥持古義，無所貶損，時論賢之。

translations.literal: Together with Jing he was a guest in Luo's staff; Zhangheng likewise held to ancient principles with unyielding integrity, never compromising, and public opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Like Jing, he served as a retainer in Song Luo's staff; Zhangheng too held to ancient principles with unyielding integrity and never compromised, and public opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 著有青門稿。

translations.literal: He authored the Qingmen Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Qingmen Drafts.

sentences.zh: 姜宸英，字西溟，慈谿人，明太常卿應麟曾孫。

translations.literal: Jiang Chenying, styled Ximing, was from Cixi; he was a great-grandson of the Ming Chamberlain for Ceremonials, Yinglin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Chenying, styled Ximing, was from Cixi and a great-grandson of the Ming Chamberlain for Ceremonials Yinglin.

sentences.zh: 父晉珪，諸生，以孝聞。

translations.literal: His father Jin Gui was a licentiate renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin Gui was a licentiate renowned for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 宸英績學工文辭，閎博雅健。

translations.literal: Chenying was deeply learned and skilled in literary composition—broad, refined, and robust.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply learned and skilled in literary composition, Chenying wrote with breadth, refinement, and vigor.

sentences.zh: 屢躓於有司，而名達禁中。

translations.literal: He repeatedly failed before the examiners, yet his name reached the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly failed the examinations, yet his name reached the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 聖祖目宸英及朱彝尊、嚴繩孫為海內三布衣。

translations.literal: The Emperor designated Chenying, along with Zhu Yizun and Yan Shengsun, as the three commoners of note within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor named Chenying, Zhu Yizun, and Yan Shengsun the three celebrated commoners of the realm.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士葉方靄薦應鴻博，後期而罷。

translations.literal: Reader-in-Waiting Ye Fang'ai recommended him for the Special Examination, but he missed the deadline and was passed over.
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-Waiting Ye Fang'ai recommended him for the Special Examination, but he arrived late and was passed over.

sentences.zh: 方藹總裁明史，又薦充纂修，食七品俸，分撰刑法志。

translations.literal: When Fang'ai was chief editor of the History of Ming, he recommended Chenying again to serve as a compiler; Chenying received seventh-rank salary and was assigned to draft the monograph on penal law.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang'ai served as chief editor of the History of Ming, he recommended Chenying again as a compiler; Chenying received seventh-rank salary and was assigned to draft the monograph on penal law.

sentences.zh: 極言明詔獄，廷杖，立枷，東、西廠之害，辭甚愷至。

translations.literal: He spoke at length of the evils of Ming imperial prisons, court beatings, standing cangues, and the Eastern and Western Depots; his language was exceedingly earnest and forthright.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke at length of the evils of Ming secret prisons, court beatings, standing cangues, and the Eastern and Western Depots, in language that was earnest and forthright.

sentences.zh: 尚書徐乾學領一統志事，設局洞庭東山，疏請宸英偕行。

translations.literal: Minister Xu Qianxue oversaw the Comprehensive Gazetteer and established an office on East Dongting Mountain; he memorialized requesting Chenying accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xu Qianxue oversaw the Comprehensive Gazetteer and set up an office on East Dongting Mountain; he memorialized asking Chenying to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 久之，舉順天鄉試。

translations.literal: After some time, he passed the metropolitan provincial examination in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he passed the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，成進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year [of Kangxi], he became a metropolitan graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 36 he became a metropolitan graduate.

sentences.zh: 廷對李蟠第一，嚴虞惇第二，帝識宸英手書，親拔置第三人及第，授編修，年七十矣。

translations.literal: At the palace examination Li Pan ranked first and Yan Yudun second; the Emperor recognized Chenying's handwriting, personally raised him to third place and made him a Presented Scholar, appointing him compiler—he was seventy years old.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination Li Pan ranked first and Yan Yudun second; the Emperor recognized Chenying's handwriting, personally raised him to third place among the Presented Scholars, and appointed him compiler—he was seventy.

sentences.zh: 明年，副蟠典試順天，蟠被劾遣戍，宸英亦連坐。

translations.literal: The next year, as associate examiner for the Shuntian examination with Pan, Pan was impeached and sent to exile; Chenying was implicated as well.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, serving as associate examiner for the Shuntian examination with Pan, he was implicated when Pan was impeached and sent into exile.

sentences.zh: 事未白，卒獄中。

translations.literal: Before the matter was cleared, he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Before the matter was cleared, he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 宸英性孝友。

translations.literal: Chenying was filial and fraternal by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Chenying was filial and devoted to his brothers by nature.

sentences.zh: 與人交，坦夷而不阿。

translations.literal: In dealings with others he was open and straightforward and would not flatter.
translations.idiomatic: In his dealings with others he was open and straightforward and would not flatter.

sentences.zh: 祭酒翁叔元劾湯斌偽學，遽移書責之。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Weng Shuyuan impeached Tang Bin for false learning, he promptly sent a letter reproaching him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Weng Shuyuan impeached Tang Bin for false learning, Chenying promptly sent him a letter of reproach.

sentences.zh: 著湛園集、葦間集。

translations.literal: He authored the Zhan Garden Collection and the Weijian Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Zhan Garden Collection and the Weijian Collection.

sentences.zh: 書法得鍾、王遺意，世頗重之。

translations.literal: His calligraphy captured the spirit of Zhong and Wang, and the world held it in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy captured the spirit of Zhong You and Wang Xizhi, and the world held it in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 虞惇，字贊成，常熟人。

translations.literal: Yan Yudun, styled Zancheng, was from Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yudun, styled Zancheng, was a native of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 幼能背誦九經、三史。

translations.literal: As a child he could recite from memory the Nine Classics and the Three Histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he could recite the Nine Classics and the Three Histories from memory.

sentences.zh: 既官翰林，館閣文字多出其手。

translations.literal: Once in the Hanlin Academy, most of the court's literary compositions issued from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered the Hanlin Academy, most court compositions issued from his hand.

sentences.zh: 科場獄興，虞惇諸子是科獲雋，考官蟠、宸英皆其同年友。

translations.literal: When the examination scandal broke, Yudun's sons passed that year's examination with distinction; the chief examiners Pan and Chenying were both friends of his same cohort year.
translations.idiomatic: When the examination scandal broke, Yudun's sons passed that year's examination with distinction; the chief examiners Pan and Chenying were both friends from his cohort year.

sentences.zh: 用是罣吏議鐫級，閒居數年。

translations.literal: For this he was censured by the personnel office and reduced in rank; he lived in retirement for several years.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was censured by the personnel office and reduced in rank, and lived in retirement for several years.

sentences.zh: 起大理寺寺副，平反內務府殺人移獄被誣者，累遷太僕寺少卿，卒官。

translations.literal: He was recalled as vice director of the Grand Court of Revision, exonerating one wrongly accused when the Imperial Household Department shifted a murder case; he was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as vice director of the Grand Court of Revision, he exonerated a man wrongly accused after the Imperial Household Department shifted a murder case; he rose in succession to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud and died in office.

sentences.zh: 著有讀詩質疑。

translations.literal: He authored Doubts Raised on Reading the Classic of Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Doubts Raised on Reading the Classic of Poetry.

sentences.zh: 江南人刻其文曰嚴太僕集，以繼明歸太僕雲。

translations.literal: Men of Jiangnan printed his writings under the title Yan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud Collection, in succession to Gui You's Ming-era Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Men of Jiangnan printed his writings as the Yan, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Stud Collection, in succession to Gui You's Ming-era collection of the same title.

sentences.zh: 黃虞稷，字俞邰，上元人，本籍晉江。

translations.literal: Huang Yuji, styled Yu'ai, was from Shangyuan; his ancestral registration was Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yuji, styled Yu'ai, was from Shangyuan, with ancestral registration in Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 七歲能詩。

translations.literal: At seven he could compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 以諸生舉鴻博，遭母喪，不與試。

translations.literal: Recommended as a licentiate for the Special Examination, he was in mourning for his mother and did not take the test.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as a licentiate for the Special Examination, he was in mourning for his mother and did not sit for the test.

sentences.zh: 左都御史徐元文薦修明史，又修一統志，皆與宸英同。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Yuanwen recommended him to compile the History of Ming and also the Comprehensive Gazetteer—both assignments shared with Chenying.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Xu Yuanwen recommended him to compile the History of Ming and the Comprehensive Gazetteer, in both cases alongside Chenying.

sentences.zh: 家富藏書。

translations.literal: His household was rich in book collections.
translations.idiomatic: His household possessed a rich library.

sentences.zh: 著千頃堂書目，為明史藝文志所本。

translations.literal: He authored the Thousand-Mu Hall Bibliography, which became the basis for the bibliography monograph in the History of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Thousand-Mu Hall Bibliography, which became the basis for the bibliography monograph in the History of Ming.

sentences.zh: 性德，納喇氏，初名成德，以避皇太子允礽嫌名改，字容若，滿洲正黃旗人，明珠子也。

translations.literal: Xingde, of the Nara clan, was originally named Chengde; to avoid the taboo name of Crown Prince Yunreng he changed it, styled Rongruo, of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner; he was the son of Mingzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde of the Nara clan was originally named Chengde; to avoid the taboo name of Crown Prince Yunreng he changed it. Styled Rongruo, a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner, he was the son of Mingzhu.

sentences.zh: 性德事親孝，侍疾衣不解帶，顏色黧黑，疾愈乃復。

translations.literal: Xingde was filial toward his parents; attending them in illness he did not loosen his girdle, his complexion turned dark and sallow, and only when they recovered did he return to normal.
translations.idiomatic: Filial toward his parents, Xingde attended them in illness without loosening his girdle; his face grew dark and gaunt, and only when they recovered did he return to himself.

sentences.zh: 數歲即習騎射，稍長工文翰。

translations.literal: From several years of age he practiced riding and archery; as he grew older he became accomplished in letters.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he practiced riding and archery; as he grew older he became accomplished in letters.

sentences.zh: 康熙十四年成進士，年十六。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kangxi he became a metropolitan graduate at sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 he became a metropolitan graduate at sixteen.

sentences.zh: 聖祖以其世家子，授三等侍衛，再遷至一等。

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing him as a scion of a great house, appointed him a third-rank bodyguard and twice promoted him to first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, seeing him as a scion of a great house, appointed him a third-rank bodyguard and twice promoted him to first rank.

sentences.zh: 令賦乾清門應制詩，譯御製松賦，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Ordered to compose an imperial-assignment poem at the Gate of Heavenly Purity and to translate the imperial Pine Fu, both won the Emperor's approval.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to compose an imperial-assignment poem at the Gate of Heavenly Purity and to translate the imperial Pine Fu, he pleased the Emperor in both.

sentences.zh: 俄疾作，上將出塞避暑，遣中官將御醫視疾，命以疾增減告。

translations.literal: Soon illness set in; the Emperor was about to leave the pass for summer retreat and dispatched eunuchs with imperial physicians to attend him, ordering them to report whether his illness improved or worsened.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he fell ill; as the Emperor was about to leave the pass for summer retreat, he dispatched eunuchs with imperial physicians to attend him and ordered reports on whether his condition improved or worsened.

sentences.zh: 遽卒，年止三十一。

translations.literal: He suddenly died, only thirty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He died suddenly at only thirty-one.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉使塞外有所宣撫，卒後，受撫諸部款塞。

translations.literal: He had once been sent on mission beyond the pass to pacify certain regions; after his death the tribes under his reassurance came to the frontier in allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been sent beyond the pass on a pacification mission; after his death the tribes he had reassured came to the frontier in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 上自行在遣中官祭告，其眷睞如是。

translations.literal: From the traveling palace the Emperor sent eunuchs to offer sacrifices; such was the fond regard shown him.
translations.idiomatic: From the traveling palace the Emperor sent eunuchs to offer sacrifices—such was the fond regard shown him.

sentences.zh: 性德鄉試出徐乾學門。

translations.literal: Xingde's provincial examination success came through Xu Qianxue's tutelage.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde passed the provincial examination as a disciple of Xu Qianxue.

sentences.zh: 與從揅討學術，嘗裒刻宋、元人說經諸書，書為之序，以自撰禮記陳氏集說補正附焉，合為通志堂經解。

translations.literal: Together with his followers he pursued scholarly inquiry, once gathering and printing Song and Yuan commentaries on the classics, writing prefaces for the volumes and appending his own Rectifications to Chen's Collected Explanations of the Book of Rites; the whole was combined as the Tongzhi Hall Exegesis of the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: With his followers he pursued scholarship, once gathering and printing Song and Yuan commentaries on the classics, writing prefaces for them and appending his own Rectifications to Chen's Collected Explanations of the Book of Rites; the whole was published as the Tongzhi Hall Exegesis of the Classics.

sentences.zh: 性德善詩，尤長倚聲。

translations.literal: Xingde was skilled at poetry and especially excelled at ci lyric composition.
translations.idiomatic: Xingde was skilled at poetry and especially excelled at ci lyric composition.

sentences.zh: 遍涉南唐、北宋諸家，窮極要眇。

translations.literal: He ranged across the masters of Southern Tang and Northern Song, penetrating their subtlest essentials.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged across the masters of Southern Tang and Northern Song, penetrating their subtlest essentials.

sentences.zh: 所著飲水、側帽二集、清新秀雋，自然超逸。

translations.literal: His Yinshui and Cemao collections are fresh, elegant, and refined, naturally transcendent and unforced.
translations.idiomatic: His Yinshui and Cemao collections are fresh, elegant, and refined—naturally transcendent and unforced.

sentences.zh: 嘗讀趙松雪自寫照詩有感，即繪小像，仿其衣冠。

translations.literal: Once reading Zhao Songxue's poem on his own self-portrait moved him, and he immediately painted a small likeness, copying his dress and cap.
