translations.idiomatic: Reading Zhao Songxue's poem on his own self-portrait once moved him so deeply that he immediately painted a small likeness in imitation of Zhao's dress and cap.

sentences.zh: 坐客期許過當，弗應也。

translations.literal: Guests praised him beyond measure; he did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When guests praised him beyond measure, he would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 乾學謂之曰：「爾何似王逸少！」

translations.literal: Qianxue said to him: "How much you resemble Wang Yishao!"
translations.idiomatic: Qianxue said to him, "How much you resemble Wang Yishao!"

sentences.zh: 則大喜。

translations.literal: At this he was greatly delighted.
translations.idiomatic: At that he was greatly delighted.

sentences.zh: 好賓禮士大夫，與嚴繩孫、顧貞觀、陳維崧、姜宸英諸人遊。

translations.literal: He delighted in receiving guests and honoring scholar-officials, associating with Yan Shengsun, Gu Zhenguan, Chen Weisong, Jiang Chenying, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in receiving guests and honoring scholar-officials, keeping company with Yan Shengsun, Gu Zhenguan, Chen Weisong, Jiang Chenying, and others.

sentences.zh: 貞觀友吳江吳兆騫坐科場獄戍寧古塔，賦金縷曲二篇寄焉，性德讀之歎曰：「山陽思舊，都尉河梁，並此而三矣！」

translations.literal: Zhenguan's friend Wu Zhaoqian of Wujiang was implicated in the examination scandal and exiled to Ningguta; he composed two Jinlüqu lyrics and sent them. Xingde read them and sighed: "Shanyang reminiscences of old friends, the Commandant at the River Bridge, and this make three such laments!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan's friend Wu Zhaoqian of Wujiang was implicated in the examination scandal and exiled to Ningguta; he composed two Jinlüqu lyrics and sent them. Xingde read them and sighed, "The Shanyang lament for old friends, the Commandant at the River Bridge, and this make three such laments!"

sentences.zh: 貞觀因力請為兆騫謀，得釋還，士尤稱之。

translations.literal: Zhenguan then pressed hard on Zhaoqian's behalf; he was freed and returned home, and scholars especially praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan then pressed hard on Zhaoqian's behalf; he was freed and returned home, and scholars especially praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 貞觀，字梁汾，無錫人。

translations.literal: Zhenguan, styled Liangfen, was from Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenguan, styled Liangfen, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年舉人，官內閣中書。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the eleventh year of Kangxi; he served as secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A Kangxi 11 provincial graduate, he served as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 工詩，自定集僅五言三十餘篇，清微婉篤，上睎韋、柳；

translations.literal: Accomplished in poetry, his self-selected collection has only thirty-odd pentameter poems—subtle, gentle, and sincere, looking back to Wei and Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplished in poetry, his self-selected collection contains only thirty-odd pentameter poems—subtle, gentle, and sincere, looking back to Wei Yingwu and Liu Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 而世特傳其詞，與維崧及朱彝尊稱詞家三絕。

translations.literal: But the world especially transmitted his ci lyrics; together with Weisong and Zhu Yizun he was called one of the three unsurpassed ci poets.
translations.idiomatic: But the world chiefly transmitted his ci lyrics; together with Weisong and Zhu Yizun he was hailed as one of the three unsurpassed ci poets.

sentences.zh: 清世工詞者，往往以詩文兼擅，獨性德為專長，仁和譚獻嘗謂為詞人之詞。

translations.literal: Qing masters of ci often excelled equally in shi and prose; Xingde alone was a specialist, and Tan Xian of Renhe once called his work "ci of a true ci poet."
translations.idiomatic: Qing masters of ci often excelled equally in shi and prose; Xingde alone was a specialist, and Tan Xian of Renhe once called his work "ci of a true ci poet."

sentences.zh: 性德後，又得項鴻祚、蔣春霖三家鼎立。

translations.literal: After Xingde there emerged Xiang Hongzuo and Jiang Chunlin, and the three stood as a tripod.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingde came Xiang Hongzuo and Jiang Chunlin, and the three stood like a tripod.

sentences.zh: 鴻祚，字蓮生，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Hongzuo, styled Liansheng, was from Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzuo, styled Liansheng, was a native of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 道光十二年舉人。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the twelfth year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: A Daoguang 12 provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 善詞，上溯溫、韋，下逮周密、吳文英。

translations.literal: Skilled in ci, he traced upward to Wen and Wei and downward to Zhou Mi and Wu Wenying.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in ci, he traced his lineage upward to Wen Tingyun and Wei Zhuang and downward to Zhou Mi and Wu Wenying.

sentences.zh: 擷精棄滓，以自名其家。

translations.literal: He gathered the essence and discarded the dregs, thereby establishing a name for his own school.
translations.idiomatic: He distilled the finest and cast off the chaff, establishing a distinctive voice of his own.

sentences.zh: 屢應禮部試不第。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sat for the Ministry of Rites examination but never passed.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Ministry of Rites examination many times but never passed.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十八。

translations.literal: He died at the age of thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 自序憶雲詞，有曰：「不為無益之事，何以遣有涯之生！」

translations.literal: In the preface to his Reminiscences of Cloud Lyrics, he wrote: "If one does not do useless things, how can one pass one's finite life!"
translations.idiomatic: In the preface to his Reminiscences of Cloud Lyrics, he wrote, "If one does not do useless things, how can one pass one's finite life!"

sentences.zh: 學者誦而悲之。

translations.literal: Scholars recited it and mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who read it were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 春霖，字鹿潭，江陰人，寄籍大興。

translations.literal: Chunlin, styled Lutan, was from Jiangyin, with registered residence in Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Chunlin, styled Lutan, was a native of Jiangyin but registered as a resident of Daxing.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，官東台場鹽大使。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng reign, he served as salt intendant of the Dongtai salt station.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng era, he served as salt intendant at the Dongtai salt station.

sentences.zh: 工詞。

translations.literal: He was accomplished in ci lyrics.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in ci poetry.

sentences.zh: 時方亂離，傍徨沉鬱，高者直逼姜夔。

translations.literal: At a time of turmoil and separation, his work was haunted and somber; at its height it nearly rivaled Jiang Kui.
translations.idiomatic: In an age of chaos and upheaval, his lyrics were restless and brooding; at their best they nearly matched Jiang Kui.

sentences.zh: 困於卑官，孤介忤時，益侘傺。

translations.literal: Trapped in a lowly post, upright and at odds with the times, he grew ever more despondent.
translations.idiomatic: Stuck in a humble office, upright and out of step with the age, he grew ever more despondent.

sentences.zh: 舟經吳江，一夕暴卒。

translations.literal: While his boat passed through Wujiang, he died suddenly one night.
translations.idiomatic: While passing through Wujiang by boat, he died suddenly one night.

sentences.zh: 春霖慕性德飲水、鴻祚憶雲，自署水雲樓，即以名其詞。

translations.literal: Chunlin admired Xingde's Drinking Water and Hongzuo's Reminiscences of Cloud; he styled himself Master of the Water-and-Cloud Tower, and used that name for his ci collection.
translations.idiomatic: Chunlin admired Xingde's Drinking Water Lyrics and Hongzuo's Reminiscences of Cloud; he styled himself Master of the Water-and-Cloud Tower and gave that name to his ci collection.

sentences.zh: 宗室文昭，字子晉，饒餘親王阿巴泰曾孫，鎮國公百綬子。

translations.literal: Among the imperial clan, Wenzhao, styled Zijin, was a great-grandson of Prince Raoyu Abatai and son of Prince of the State Baoshou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhao of the imperial clan, styled Zijin, was a great-grandson of Prince Raoyu Abatai and son of Prince of the State Baoshou.

sentences.zh: 辭爵讀書，從王士禎遊。

translations.literal: He declined his title to devote himself to study, keeping company with Wang Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He declined his title to devote himself to study and kept company with Wang Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 工詩，才名藉甚。

translations.literal: He was accomplished in poetry, and his literary renown was great.
translations.idiomatic: Accomplished in poetry, he enjoyed great literary renown.

sentences.zh: 王式丹稱其詩以鮑、謝為胚胎，而又兼綜眾有，擷百家之精華，其味在酸鹹之外。

translations.literal: Wang Shidan said his poetry took Bao and Xie as its embryo, yet also synthesized all schools, gathering the essence of a hundred masters; its flavor lay beyond mere sweet and sour.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shidan said his poetry took Bao Zhao and Xie Lingyun as its foundation, yet also synthesized every school and distilled the essence of a hundred masters; its flavor transcended easy categories.

sentences.zh: 著有薌嬰居士集、紫幢詩鈔。

translations.literal: He authored the Xiangying Layman Collection and the Purple Banner Poetry Manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Xiangying Layman Collection and the Purple Banner Poetry Manuscript.

sentences.zh: 又宗室以詩名者，蘊端，初名岳端，字正子，號紅蘭主人，多羅安郡王岳樂子。

translations.literal: Another member of the imperial clan famed for poetry was Yun Duan, originally named Yue Duan, styled Zhengzi, sobriquet Master of the Red Orchid, son of Prince of the State of Duo'an Yuele.
translations.idiomatic: Another imperial clansman famed for poetry was Yun Duan, originally named Yue Duan, styled Zhengzi and known as Master of the Red Orchid, son of Prince Duo'an Yuele.

sentences.zh: 封貝子。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as a beizi.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of beizi.

sentences.zh: 有玉池生稿。

translations.literal: He had the Jade Pool Drafts.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Jade Pool Drafts.

sentences.zh: 博爾都，字問亭，號東皋漁父，恪僖公拔都海子，蘊端從弟。

translations.literal: Bo'erdu, styled Wenting, sobriquet Fisherman of Eastern Mound, was a son of Prince Kexi Badu and a younger cousin of Yun Duan.
translations.idiomatic: Bo'erdu, styled Wenting and known as the Fisherman of Eastern Mound, was a son of Prince Kexi Badu and a younger cousin of Yun Duan.

sentences.zh: 封輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Defender Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of Defender Prince of the State.

sentences.zh: 有問亭詩集。

translations.literal: He had the Wenting Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Wenting Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 永忠，字良輔，又字臞仙，多羅貝勒弘明子。

translations.literal: Yongzhong, styled Liangfu and also styled Quxian, was a son of Prince Duo Luo Hongming.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhong, styled Liangfu and also known as Quxian, was a son of Prince Duo Luo Hongming.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Defender Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of Defender Prince of the State.

sentences.zh: 有延芬室集。

translations.literal: He had the Yanfen Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Yanfen Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 詩體秀逸，書法遒勁，頗有晉人風味。

translations.literal: His poetry was elegant and unfettered, his calligraphy forceful and vigorous, with much of the flavor of Jin-dynasty masters.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was elegant and unfettered, his calligraphy bold and vigorous, with much of the flavor of Jin-dynasty masters.

sentences.zh: 常不衫不履，散步市衢。

translations.literal: He often went about without coat or shoes, strolling through the city streets.
translations.idiomatic: He often walked the streets without coat or shoes.

sentences.zh: 遇奇書異籍，必買之歸，雖典衣絕食不顧也。

translations.literal: When he encountered rare books and unusual texts, he always bought them and took them home, even if it meant pawning his clothes or going without food.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came upon rare books and unusual texts, he bought them and carried them home, even if it meant pawning his clothes or going without food.

sentences.zh: 書諴，字實之，號樗仙，鄭獻親王濟爾哈朗六世孫，輔國將軍長恆子。

translations.literal: Shu Shen, styled Shizhi, sobriquet Chuxian, was a sixth-generation descendant of Prince Zhengxian Jirhalang and son of Defender Prince of the State Changheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Shen, styled Shizhi and known as Chuxian, was a sixth-generation descendant of Prince Zhengxian Jirhalang and son of Defender Prince of the State Changheng.

sentences.zh: 奉國將軍。

translations.literal: Bulwark Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of Bulwark Prince of the State.

sentences.zh: 有靜虛堂集。

translations.literal: He had the Quiet Void Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Quiet Void Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 性慷慨，不欲嬰世俗情。

translations.literal: By nature he was generous and did not wish to entangle himself in worldly attachments.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was generous and wished to keep clear of worldly entanglements.

sentences.zh: 年四十，即託疾去官。

translations.literal: At the age of forty he pleaded illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he pleaded illness and resigned from office.

sentences.zh: 邸有餘隙地，盡種蔬果，手執畚鎛，從事習勞以為樂。

translations.literal: There was spare ground at his residence, which he planted entirely with fruits and vegetables; he took hoe and spade in hand and found joy in manual labor.
translations.idiomatic: On spare ground at his residence he planted nothing but fruits and vegetables; hoe and spade in hand, he took joy in manual labor.

sentences.zh: 永諲，字嵩山，康修親王崇安子。

translations.literal: Yongyin, styled Songshan, was a son of Prince Kangxiu Chong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyin, styled Songshan, was the son of Prince Kangxiu Chong'an.

sentences.zh: 鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: Pacifying Prince of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of Pacifying Prince of the State.

sentences.zh: 詩宗盛唐，書法趙文敏。

translations.literal: In poetry he followed the High Tang; in calligraphy he followed Zhao Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry he followed the High Tang; in calligraphy he followed Zhao Mengfu.

sentences.zh: 晚年獨居一室，不與人接。

translations.literal: In his later years he lived alone in one room and received no visitors.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he shut himself in a single room and saw no one.

sentences.zh: 詩多散佚。

translations.literal: Most of his poems were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his poetry has not survived.

sentences.zh: 裕瑞，字思元，豫通親王多鐸裔。

translations.literal: Yurui, styled Siyuan, was a descendant of Prince Yutong Dodo.
translations.idiomatic: Yurui, styled Siyuan, descended from Prince Yutong Dodo.

sentences.zh: 封輔國公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke Defender of the State.
translations.idiomatic: He held the title of Duke Defender of the State.

sentences.zh: 工詩善畫，通西番語。

translations.literal: He was accomplished in poetry and painting, and understood the Western Barbarian language.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in poetry and painting and understood Tibetan.

sentences.zh: 常畫鸚鵡地圖，即西洋地球圖。

translations.literal: He often painted parrot maps—that is, Western terrestrial globes.
translations.idiomatic: He often painted "parrot maps"—that is, Western terrestrial globes.

sentences.zh: 又以佛經自唐時流入西藏，近日佛藏皆出一本，無可校讎。

translations.literal: He also noted that Buddhist scriptures had flowed into Tibet since the Tang, yet recent Buddhist canons all derived from a single text and could not be collated.
translations.idiomatic: He also noted that Buddhist scriptures had flowed into Tibet since the Tang, yet recent Buddhist canons all derived from a single text and offered nothing to collate against.

sentences.zh: 乃取唐古特字譯校，以復佛經唐本之舊，凡數百卷。

translations.literal: He therefore took Tangut-script translations for collation, restoring the Tang originals of the Buddhist canon, several hundred scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore collated Tangut-script translations to restore the Tang originals of the Buddhist canon—several hundred scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 著有思元齋集。

translations.literal: He authored the Siyuan Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Siyuan Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 趙執信，字仲符，益都人。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhixin, styled Zhongfu, was from Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhixin, styled Zhongfu, was a native of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 從祖進美，官福建按察使，詩名甚著。

translations.literal: His father's cousin Jinmei served as Fujian Surveillance Commissioner and was greatly famed for poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His father's cousin Jinmei served as Fujian Surveillance Commissioner and enjoyed great renown as a poet.

sentences.zh: 執信承其家學，自少即工吟詠。

translations.literal: Zhixin inherited the family learning and from youth was accomplished in verse.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin inherited the family tradition and from youth was accomplished in verse.

sentences.zh: 年十九，登康熙十八年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: At nineteen he passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Kangxi and was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he passed the jinshi examination in Kangxi 18 and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 時方開鴻博科，四方雄文績學者皆集輦下，執信過從談宴，一座盡傾。

translations.literal: At that time the Special Examination was being held, and eminent scholars from all quarters gathered at the capital; Zhixin joined their gatherings and banquets, and every company was captivated by him.
translations.idiomatic: The Special Examination had just been opened, and eminent scholars from every quarter gathered at the capital; Zhixin joined their conversations and banquets, and every gathering was won over by him.

sentences.zh: 朱彝尊、陳維崧、毛奇齡尤相引重，訂為忘年交。

translations.literal: Zhu Yizun, Chen Weisong, and Mao Qiling especially valued him, and they formed friendships across the gap in age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yizun, Chen Weisong, and Mao Qiling especially valued him, and they became close friends despite the gap in their ages.

sentences.zh: 出典山西鄉試，遷右贊善。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as chief examiner for the Shanxi provincial examination, then was promoted to Right Director of the Court of Studious Endeavor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief examiner for the Shanxi provincial examination, then was promoted to Right Director of the Court of Studious Endeavor.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，坐國卹中宴飲觀劇，為言者所劾，削籍歸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, because he feasted and watched plays during the period of national mourning, he was impeached by censors, struck from the rolls, and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 28, because he feasted and watched plays during the period of national mourning, he was impeached by censors, struck from the rolls, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: He died in his eighties.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 執信為人峭峻褊衷，獨服膺常熟馮班，自稱私淑弟子。

translations.literal: Zhixin was by nature stern, severe, and narrow-minded; he alone revered Feng Ban of Changshu and called himself a private disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin was sharp-tempered and narrow in conviction; he revered none but Feng Ban of Changshu, whom he called his private master.

sentences.zh: 娶王士禎甥女，初頗相引重。

translations.literal: He married Wang Shizhen's niece, and at first they held each other in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: He married Wang Shizhen's niece, and at first the two men held each other in the highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 後求士禎序其詩，士禎不時作，遂相詬厲。

translations.literal: Later he asked Shizhen for a preface to his poetry, but Shizhen did not produce one promptly, and the two exchanged bitter reproaches.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked Shizhen for a preface to his poetry; when Shizhen did not produce one promptly, the two fell into bitter mutual abuse.

sentences.zh: 嘗問詩聲調於士禎，士禎靳之，乃歸取唐人集排比鉤稽，竟得其法，為聲調譜一卷。

translations.literal: Once he asked Shizhen about tonal patterns in poetry; Shizhen was stingy with his knowledge, so Zhixin returned home, arranged and collated Tang collections, and finally mastered the method, producing one scroll of a Tonal Pattern Manual.
translations.idiomatic: Once he asked Shizhen about tonal patterns in poetry; Shizhen was stingy with his knowledge, so Zhixin returned home, arranged and collated Tang collections, and finally mastered the method, producing a one-scroll Tonal Pattern Manual.

sentences.zh: 又以士禎論詩，比之神龍不見首尾，雲中所露一鱗一爪而已，遂著談龍錄，云：「詩以言志，詩之中須有人在，詩之外尚有事在。」

translations.literal: He also said that Shizhen's discourse on poetry was like a divine dragon whose head and tail one never sees—only a scale or a claw glimpsed through the clouds—and therefore wrote Discourse on the Dragon, saying: "Poetry expresses intent; within poetry there must be a person, and beyond poetry there must still be events."
translations.idiomatic: He also said that Shizhen's discourse on poetry was like a divine dragon whose head and tail one never sees—only a scale or a claw glimpsed through the clouds—and therefore wrote Discourse on the Dragon, saying, "Poetry expresses intent; within poetry there must be a person, and beyond poetry there must still be events.

sentences.zh: 意蓋詆士禎也。

translations.literal: The intent was plainly to denigrate Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: His aim was clearly to attack Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 說者謂士禎詩尚神韻，其弊也膚；

translations.literal: Commentators said Shizhen's poetry prized spiritual resonance, but its fault lay in superficiality;
translations.idiomatic: Critics held that Shizhen's poetry valued spiritual resonance, yet its weakness was shallowness;

sentences.zh: 執信以思路​​劖刻為主，其失也纖。

translations.literal: Zhixin made laborious carving of poetic thought his main principle, and his fault lay in fineness carried too far.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin made laborious carving of thought his guiding principle, and his failing was excessive fineness.

sentences.zh: 兩家才性不同，實足相資濟雲。

translations.literal: The talents and temperaments of the two schools differed, yet truly complemented each other.
translations.idiomatic: Their gifts and temperaments diverged, yet in truth they could profit each other.

sentences.zh: 執信所著詩文曰飴山堂集。

translations.literal: The poetry and prose Zhixin authored were called the Yishan Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: The poetry and prose Zhixin authored were collected as the Yishan Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 當是時，海內以詩名者推士禎，以文名者推汪琬。

translations.literal: At that time, within the realm Shizhen was regarded as foremost in poetry, and Wang Wan as foremost in prose.
translations.idiomatic: In those days Shizhen was reckoned the leading poet in the empire and Wang Wan the leading prose writer.

sentences.zh: 而嘉興葉燮，字星期，其論文亦與琬不合，往復論難，互譏嘲焉。

translations.literal: But Ye Xie of Jiaxing, styled Xingqi, also disagreed with Wan in literary theory; they exchanged arguments back and forth and mocked each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Xie of Jiaxing, styled Xingqi, also clashed with Wan over literary theory; they debated back and forth and taunted one another.

sentences.zh: 及琬歿，慨然曰：「吾失一諍友矣！

translations.literal: When Wan died, Ye said with emotion: "I have lost a friend who spoke truth to me!
translations.idiomatic: When Wan died, Ye said with emotion, "I have lost a friend who spoke truth to me!

sentences.zh: 今誰復彈吾文者？」

translations.literal: Who now will criticize my writing?"
translations.idiomatic: Who is left to find fault with my writing?

sentences.zh: 取向所短汪者悉焚之。

translations.literal: He then took everything he had written to criticize Wang and burned it all.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered everything he had written against Wang and burned it all.

sentences.zh: 燮父紹袁，明進士，官工部主事，國亡後為僧。

translations.literal: Ye's father Shaoyuan was a Ming jinshi who served as a secretary in the Ministry of Works; after the dynasty fell he became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's father Shaoyuan, a Ming jinshi who had served as a secretary in the Ministry of Works, took holy orders after the fall of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 燮生四歲，授以楚辭，即成誦。

translations.literal: When Ye was four years old, he was taught the Songs of Chu and could recite them at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye was four, he was taught the Songs of Chu and could recite them at once.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年進士，選授寶應令。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the ninth year of Kangxi; he was selected and appointed magistrate of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: A Kangxi 9 jinshi, he was selected and appointed magistrate of Baoying.

sentences.zh: 值三籓亂，又歲饑，民不堪苦。

translations.literal: It happened during the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, and famine followed year after year; the people could not endure the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: This fell in the time of the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, with famine year after year, until the people could bear no more.

sentences.zh: 累以伉直失上官意，坐累落職。

translations.literal: Repeatedly, through his upright and blunt manner, he lost the favor of his superiors and was dismissed from office through implicated guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again his blunt, upright ways cost him his superiors' favor, and he was removed from office on a trumped-up charge.

sentences.zh: 時嘉定​​知縣陸隴其亦被劾，燮以與隴其同罷為幸。

translations.literal: At that time Lu Longqi, magistrate of Jiading, was also impeached, and Ye considered himself fortunate to be dismissed together with Longqi.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Longqi, magistrate of Jiading, was also impeached, Ye counted it an honor to fall from office alongside him.

sentences.zh: 性喜山水，縱遊宇內名勝幾遍。

translations.literal: By nature he loved mountains and rivers, and he traveled freely to famous sites throughout the realm almost everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He loved mountains and rivers by nature and wandered freely to famed scenic places across the empire, leaving few unvisited.

sentences.zh: 年七十六，猶以會稽、五洩近在數百里獨未遊為憾。

translations.literal: At seventy-six he still regretted that Kuaiji and the Five Cascades, though only a few hundred li away, were the only famous places he had not yet visited.
translations.idiomatic: Even at seventy-six he regretted that Kuaiji and the Five Cascades—only a few hundred li distant—remained among the celebrated sites he had never seen.

sentences.zh: 复裹糧往，歸遂疾。

translations.literal: He again packed provisions and went; upon returning he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He packed food once more and made the journey; when he returned he took ill.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: More than a year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died.

sentences.zh: 寓吳時，以吳中論詩多獵範、陸皮毛，而遺其實，著原詩內外篇，力破其非。

translations.literal: While living in Wu, he observed that poetry discussions there often hunted only the surface of Fan and Lu while abandoning their substance, and therefore wrote the Inner and Outer Chapters of Original Poetry, forcefully refuting that error.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Wu, he observed that poetry discussions there often hunted only the surface of Fan Zhongyan and Lu You while abandoning their substance, and therefore wrote the Inner and Outer Chapters of Original Poetry, forcefully refuting that error.

sentences.zh: 吳士始而訾謷，久乃更從其說。

translations.literal: Wu scholars at first denounced and mocked him, but in time they came around to his view.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of Wu first jeered at him, but before long they adopted his position.

sentences.zh: 著已畦詩文集。

translations.literal: He authored the Yiqu Poetry and Prose Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Yiqu Poetry and Prose Collection.

sentences.zh: 士禎謂其鎔鑄往昔，獨立起衰。

translations.literal: Shizhen said that he fused and cast the past and alone stood forth to revive a declining tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen said he had smelted the past into something new and alone roused a fading tradition.

sentences.zh: 馮廷櫆，字大木，德州人。

translations.literal: Feng Tingkai, styled Damu, was from Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Tingkai, styled Damu, was a native of Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十一年進士，授中書。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-first year of Kangxi; he was appointed Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: A Kangxi 21 jinshi, he was appointed a Secretariat Secretary.

sentences.zh: 幼有奇童之目，讀書一覽輒記，尤長於詩。

translations.literal: From childhood he was regarded as a prodigy; what he read once he remembered, and he was especially accomplished in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was hailed as a prodigy; a single reading fixed a text in memory, and poetry was his especial gift.

sentences.zh: 嘗充湖廣副考官，試畢，登黃鶴樓，俯江、漢之流，南望瀟湘、洞庭，慨然遠想，賦詩百餘篇，識者以為騷之遺也。

translations.literal: Once, while serving as associate examiner in Huguang, after the examination he ascended Yellow Crane Tower, looked down on the Yangzi and Han rivers, and gazed south toward the Xiao and Xiang and Lake Dongting; moved by distant thoughts, he composed more than a hundred poems, which connoisseurs regarded as inheritors of the sao tradition.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while serving as associate examiner in Huguang, he climbed Yellow Crane Tower after the examinations, looked down on the Yangzi and Han rivers, and gazed south toward the Xiao and Xiang and Lake Dongting; stirred by distant thoughts, he composed more than a hundred poems that connoisseurs took for heirs to the sao tradition.

sentences.zh: 平生深契者惟執信，其詩孤峭亦相類，歿後散佚。

translations.literal: The only person with whom he was deeply close in life was Zhixin; their poetry, austere and steep, was also similar, and after his death it was scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: In life his sole intimate was Zhixin; their poetry alike was austere and steep, and after his death it was scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 其孫德培搜輯得五百篇，名馮舍人遺詩。

translations.literal: His grandson Depei gathered and edited five hundred poems, titled the Posthumous Poetry of Secretary Feng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Depei collected five hundred poems and published them as the Posthumous Poetry of Secretary Feng.

sentences.zh: 黃儀，字六鴻，常熟人。

translations.literal: Huang Yi, styled Liuhong, was from Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yi, styled Liuhong, was a native of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 精輿地之學。

translations.literal: He was expert in the study of geography.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master of geography.

sentences.zh: 嘗以班固地誌所載諸川，第詳水出入，其中間經歷之地，備著於水經，然讀者非繪圖不能了，乃反覆尋究，每水各為一圖。

translations.literal: He once observed that the rivers recorded in Ban Gu's Treatise on Geography detailed only where waters entered and exited, while the places they passed through in between were fully set forth in the Water Classic—but readers could not understand without maps; he therefore investigated repeatedly and made a separate map for each river.
translations.idiomatic: He observed that Ban Gu's Treatise on Geography recorded rivers only at their points of entry and exit, whereas the places they traversed in between were fully set forth in the Water Classic—yet readers could grasp this only with maps; he therefore investigated repeatedly and drew a separate map for each river.

sentences.zh: 凡都邑建署沿革、山川險易皆具焉，條縷分析，各得其理。

translations.literal: All changes in the founding and relocation of cities and offices, and the hazards and ease of mountains and rivers, were fully included; each thread was analyzed until its principle was clear.
translations.idiomatic: Every change in the siting of towns and offices, and every hazard or ease of mountain and river, was set down; strand by strand he analyzed each until its logic stood clear.

sentences.zh: 閻若璩見之，歎曰：「酈道元千古後一知己也！」

translations.literal: When Yan Ruoqu saw it, he sighed and said: "Li Daoyuan has found, a thousand years later, one who truly understands him!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Ruoqu saw it, he sighed and said, "Li Daoyuan has found, a thousand years later, one who truly understands him!"

sentences.zh: 若璩嘗問儀：「後漢志溫縣濟水出，王莽時大旱，遂枯絕。

translations.literal: Ruoqu once asked Yi: "The Treatise on the Later Han says the Ji River issued from Wen County, but during Wang Mang's reign there was a great drought and it dried up completely.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoqu once asked Yi, "The Treatise on the Later Han says the Ji River issued from Wen County, but during Wang Mang's reign there was a great drought and it dried up completely.

sentences.zh: 是河南無濟矣，何酈氏言之詳也？」

translations.literal: So there was no Ji in Henan—why then does Master Li speak of it in such detail?"
translations.idiomatic: If there was no Ji in Henan, why does Li Daoyuan describe it at such length?"

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「新莽時雖枯，後復見，酈氏所謂其後水流迳通，津渠勢改，尋梁脈水，不與昔同是也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Although it dried up in the Xin Mang period, it later reappeared; this is what Master Li meant when he said that afterward the water's course ran through again, the force of channels and sluices changed, and one traced the pulse of the riverbed—no longer the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Although it dried up in the Xin Mang period, it later reappeared; this is what Master Li meant when he said that afterward the water's course ran through again, the force of channels and sluices changed, and one traced the pulse of the riverbed—no longer the same as before.

sentences.zh: 杜君卿乃不信水經，專憑彪志，竊以彪特紀一時災變耳，非謂永不截河南過也。」

translations.literal: Du Junqing did not trust the Water Classic and relied solely on Ban Biao's Treatise; I suspect Ban Biao was merely recording a temporary disaster of that time, not saying that the river would never again cross through Henan."
translations.idiomatic: Du You did not trust the Water Classic and relied solely on Ban Biao's Treatise; I suspect Ban Biao was merely recording a temporary disaster of that time, not saying that the river would never again cross through Henan."

sentences.zh: 徐乾學修一統志，儀與若璩、胡渭、顧祖禹任分纂，皆地學專家。

translations.literal: When Xu Qianxue compiled the Comprehensive Gazetteer, Yi together with Ruoqu, Hu Wei, and Gu Zuyu were assigned as section compilers—all were experts in geography.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Qianxue compiled the Comprehensive Gazetteer, Yi served as a section compiler alongside Yan Ruoqu, Hu Wei, and Gu Zuyu—all masters of geographical studies.

sentences.zh: 儀又訂正晉書地理志。

translations.literal: Yi also revised the Geography Monograph of the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also corrected the Geography Monograph in the Book of Jin.

sentences.zh: 兼工詩詞，著有紉蘭集。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in shi and ci poetry, and authored the Ren Lan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He was also accomplished in shi and ci poetry and left the Ren Lan Collection.

sentences.zh: 鄭元慶，字芷畦，歸安人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yuanqing, styled Zhikai, was from Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuanqing, styled Zhikai, was a native of Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 通史傳，旁及金石文字。

translations.literal: He mastered historical biographies and extended his studies to epigraphy and bronze inscriptions.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in historical biographies and ranged widely into epigraphy and bronze inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 李紱、張伯行雅重其學，欲薦於朝未得也。

translations.literal: Li Fu and Zhang Boxing held his learning in high esteem and wished to recommend him to the court, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fu and Zhang Boxing greatly admired his scholarship and wished to recommend him to the throne, but never managed to do so.

sentences.zh: 顏魯公書湖州石柱記，元慶為之箋釋，甚博贍。

translations.literal: Yan the Duke of Lu wrote the Record on the Huzhou Stone Pillar; Yuanqing wrote exegesis for it, exceedingly rich and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing wrote a commentary on Yan Zhenqing's Record on the Huzhou Stone Pillar—a work of extraordinary breadth and erudition.

sentences.zh: 又著湖錄百二十卷，七易藁而後成，自謂平生精力殫於是書。

translations.literal: He also wrote the Hu Lu in one hundred and twenty juan, revising the draft seven times before completion, and said he had exhausted his life's energy on this book.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Hu Lu in one hundred and twenty juan, revising the manuscript seven times before he was satisfied, and declared that he had poured his life's strength into that book alone.

sentences.zh: 平生慕鄭子真之為人，自號鄭谷口。

translations.literal: All his life he admired the character of Zheng Zizhen and styled himself Zheng Gukou.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he admired the conduct of Zheng Zizhen and took the sobriquet Zheng Gukou.

sentences.zh: 晚更治經，其著書處名魚計亭。

translations.literal: In his later years he turned to studying the Classics; the place where he wrote was called Yuji Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In later life he turned to the Classics; the study where he wrote was named Yuji Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 著有周易集說、詩序傳異同、禮記集說參同、官禮經典參同、家禮經典參同、喪服古今異同考、春王正月考、海運議。

translations.literal: He authored Collected Notes on the Book of Changes, Differences in the Preface Traditions of the Book of Songs, Comparative Study of the Collected Notes on the Book of Rites, Comparative Study of the Classic of Official Rites, Comparative Study of the Classic of Family Rites, Examination of Ancient and Modern Differences in Mourning Dress, Examination of the First Month of the Spring King's Calendar, and Discourse on Sea Transport.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Collected Notes on the Book of Changes, Differences in the Preface Traditions of the Book of Songs, Comparative Study of the Collected Notes on the Book of Rites, Comparative Study of the Classic of Official Rites, Comparative Study of the Classic of Family Rites, Examination of Ancient and Modern Differences in Mourning Dress, Examination of the First Month of the Spring King's Calendar, and Discourse on Sea Transport.

sentences.zh: 查慎行，字悔餘，海寧人。

translations.literal: Zha Shenxing, styled Huiyu, was from Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Zha Shenxing, styled Huiyu, was a native of Haining.

sentences.zh: 少受學黃宗羲。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Huang Zongxi.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied under Huang Zongxi.

sentences.zh: 於經邃於易。

translations.literal: Among the Classics he was especially deep in the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Of the Classics he was deepest in the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 性喜作詩，遊覽所至，輒有吟詠，名聞禁中。

translations.literal: By nature he loved composing poetry; wherever he traveled he would sing what he saw, and his fame reached within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved to write poetry; wherever he traveled he would compose on what he saw, and his name reached even within the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年，舉鄉試。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 其後聖祖東巡，以大學士陳廷敬薦，詔詣行在賦詩。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the Sagely Ancestor toured east, on Grand Secretary Chen Tingjing's recommendation an edict summoned him to the traveling palace to compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Kangxi Emperor toured the east, Chen Tingjing, Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory, recommended him, and an edict summoned him to the imperial encampment to compose poetry.

sentences.zh: 又詔隨入都，直南書房。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered him to accompany the court to the capital and serve in the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to accompany the court to the capital and serve in the Southern Studio.

sentences.zh: 尋賜進士出身，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted jinshi status, selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was granted jinshi status, selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 時族子升以諭德直內廷，宮監呼慎行為老查以別之。

translations.literal: At the time his clansman Sheng served as tutor in the inner court; eunuchs called Shenxing "Old Zha" to distinguish him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his clansman Sheng served as tutor in the inner court, so the palace eunuchs called Shenxing "Old Zha" to tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 帝幸南苑，捕魚賜近臣，命賦詩。

translations.literal: The emperor visited the Southern Park, caught fish and bestowed them on close ministers, and ordered them to compose poems.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the Southern Park, caught fish and bestowed them on his close ministers, and ordered them to compose poems.

sentences.zh: 慎行有句云：「笠簷蓑袂平生夢，臣本煙波一釣徒。」

translations.literal: Shenxing had a couplet that read: "Bamboo hat and straw cloak—the dream of my whole life; your servant was originally a fishing recluse on misty waters."
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing had a couplet that ran: "Bamboo hat and straw sleeves—the dream of my whole life; your servant was always a fishing recluse on misty waters."

sentences.zh: 俄宮監傳呼「煙波釣徒查翰林」。

translations.literal: Shortly after, a eunuch called out, "Where is Academician Zha, the Fishing Recluse on Misty Waters?"
translations.idiomatic: Presently a palace eunuch called out, "Where is Academician Zha, the Fishing Recluse on Misty Waters?"

sentences.zh: 時以比「春城寒食」之韓翃雲。

translations.literal: At the time this was compared to the story of Han Hong and "Spring City, Cold Food Festival."
translations.idiomatic: At the time people compared it to the tale of Han Hong and his line "Spring City, Cold Food Festival."

sentences.zh: 充武英殿書局校勘，乞病還。

translations.literal: He served as collator in the Wuying Hall book office, then requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He served as collator in the Wuying Hall book office, then pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 坐弟嗣庭得罪，闔門就逮。

translations.literal: Because his younger brother Siting was punished for an offense, the whole family was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother Siting was condemned for an offense, the entire household was taken into custody.

sentences.zh: 世宗識其端謹，特許於歸田裡，而弟嗣瑮謫遣關西，卒於戍所。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor recognized his upright discretion and specially permitted him to return to his fields, while his younger brother Simi was banished to the northwest and died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor recognized his upright discretion and specially allowed him to return to his fields, while his younger brother Simi was banished to the northwest and died in exile.

sentences.zh: 嗣瑮，字德尹。

translations.literal: Simi, styled Deyin.
translations.idiomatic: Simi, styled Deyin.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十九年進士，官至侍講。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi; he rose to Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the thirty-ninth year of Kangxi, he rose to Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 性警敏，數歲即解切韻諧聲。

translations.literal: Quick and sharp by nature, from a few years old he understood rhyme classification and harmonic sound.
translations.idiomatic: Alert and quick-witted by nature, from childhood he understood rhyme categories and harmonic sound.

sentences.zh: 詩名與慎行相埒。

translations.literal: His poetic fame matched Shenxing's.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation as a poet rivaled Shenxing's.

sentences.zh: 慎行著敬業堂集、周易玩辭集解，又補注蘇詩，行於世。

translations.literal: Shenxing authored the Jingye Tang Collection and Collected Explications Playing with the Words of the Book of Changes, and also supplemented annotations on Su Shi's poetry—all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Shenxing authored the Jingye Tang Collection and Collected Explications Playing with the Words of the Book of Changes, and also supplemented annotations on Su Shi's poetry—all of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 嗣瑮著查浦詩鈔、音類通考。

translations.literal: Simi authored the Cha Pu Poetry Selection and Comprehensive Examination of Sound Categories.
translations.idiomatic: Simi authored the Cha Pu Poetry Selection and Comprehensive Examination of Sound Categories.

sentences.zh: 升，字仲韋。

translations.literal: Sheng, styled Zhongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, styled Zhongwei.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 官少詹事。

translations.literal: He served as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 詩筆清麗。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were clear and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were lucid and graceful.

sentences.zh: 尤工書，似董其昌。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in calligraphy, resembling Dong Qichang.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially accomplished in calligraphy, in a manner reminiscent of Dong Qichang.

sentences.zh: 有澹遠堂集。

translations.literal: He left the Danyuan Tang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Danyuan Tang Collection.

sentences.zh: 史申義，字叔時，江都人。

translations.literal: Shi Shenyi, styled Shushi, was from Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Shenyi, styled Shushi, was a native of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 少工詩，與同里顧圖河齊名，稱維揚二妙。

translations.literal: Skilled in poetry from youth, he was equally famed with his townsman Gu Tuhe—they were called the Two Wonders of Weiyang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was accomplished in poetry and shared equal fame with his townsman Gu Tuhe; together they were called the Two Wonders of Weiyang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二十七年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi; appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Kangxi, he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 充雲南鄉試考官，改御史、禮科給事中，乞病歸。

translations.literal: He served as examiner for the Yunnan provincial examination, transferred to censor and Supervisor in the Ministry of Rites, then requested leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He served as examiner for the Yunnan provincial examination, then transferred to censor and Supervisor in the Ministry of Rites before pleading illness and retiring home.

sentences.zh: 王士禎以風雅詔後進，嘗謂申義及湯右曾足傳己衣缽，人稱「王門二弟子」。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen instructed later generations in refined poetry, once saying Shenyi and Tang Youzeng were sufficient to carry on his mantle—they were called "Wang's Two Disciples."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen instructed later generations in refined poetry and once declared that Shenyi and Tang Youzeng were fit to inherit his mantle; people called them "Wang's Two Disciples."

sentences.zh: 在翰林時，聖祖以後進詩人詢大學士陳廷敬，廷敬舉申義、週起渭對，故又有「翰苑兩詩人」之目。

translations.literal: While in the Hanlin, the Sagely Ancestor asked Grand Secretary Chen Tingjing about rising poets; Chen named Shenyi and Zhou Qiwei—hence they were also called "the Two Poets of the Hanlin Academy."
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Hanlin, the Kangxi Emperor asked Grand Secretary Chen Tingjing which poets among the younger generation were worth noting; Chen named Shenyi and Zhou Qiwei, and so they were also known as "the Two Poets of the Hanlin Academy."

sentences.zh: 起渭，字漁塘，貴陽人。

translations.literal: Qiwei, styled Yutang, was from Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qiwei, styled Yutang, was a native of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十三年進士，由檢討累遷詹事府詹事。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirty-third year of Kangxi; from Reviser he rose through promotion to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the thirty-third year of Kangxi, he rose from Reviser through successive promotions to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 詩才雋逸，尤肆力於蘇軾、元好問、高啟諸家。

translations.literal: His poetic talent was spare and soaring; he especially devoted himself to the styles of Su Shi, Yuan Haowen, Gao Qi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His poetic talent was spare and soaring; he especially devoted himself to the styles of Su Shi, Yuan Haowen, Gao Qi, and others.

sentences.zh: 貴州自明始隸版圖，清詩人以起渭為冠，而銅仁張元臣、平遠潘淳亦並有詩名。

translations.literal: Since the Ming, Guizhou had belonged to the empire; among Qing poets Qiwei stood foremost, while Zhang Yuanchen of Tongren and Pan Chun of Pingyuan also shared poetic renown.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou had been part of the empire since the Ming; among Qing poets Qiwei stood at the head, while Zhang Yuanchen of Tongren and Pan Chun of Pingyuan also enjoyed poetic fame.

sentences.zh: 元臣，字志伊。

translations.literal: Yuanchen, styled Zhiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchen, styled Zhiyi.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十六年進士，由檢討累遷左諭德。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi; from Reviser he rose through promotion to Left Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the thirty-sixth year of Kangxi, he rose from Reviser through successive promotions to Left Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 有豆村詩鈔。

translations.literal: He left the Doucun Poetry Selection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Doucun Poetry Selection.

sentences.zh: 淳，字元亮。

translations.literal: Chun, styled Yuanliang.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, styled Yuanliang.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十四年進士，官檢討。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi; he served as Reviser.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi, he served as Reviser.

sentences.zh: 文安陳儀與同榜，一時咸推潘詩陳筆。

translations.literal: Chen Yi of Wen'an graduated in the same cohort; for a time all praised Pan's poetry and Chen's prose.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yi of Wen'an graduated in the same cohort, and for a time everyone praised Pan's poetry and Chen's prose.

sentences.zh: 有椽林詩集。

translations.literal: He left the Chuanlin Poetry Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He left the Chuanlin Poetry Collection.

sentences.zh: 顧陳垿，字玉停，鎮洋人。

translations.literal: Gu Chenxu, styled Yuting, was from Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chenxu, styled Yuting, was a native of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 少有文名，嘗得徐光啟曆書，精求一月，通其術。

translations.literal: Famed for literary talent from youth; once he obtained Xu Guangqi's calendrical treatise and for a month pursued it intensively until he mastered its methods.
translations.idiomatic: He won a literary reputation early; once he obtained Xu Guangqi's calendrical treatise and for a full month pursued it intensively until he mastered its methods.

sentences.zh: 康熙五十四年舉人，以薦入湛凝齋修書。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi; on recommendation he entered the Zhanning Studio to compile books.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in the fifty-fourth year of Kangxi, he entered the Zhanning Studio on recommendation to compile books.

sentences.zh: 書成，議敘行人司行人。

translations.literal: When the work was complete, he was nominated for the rank of Secretary in the Department of Foreign Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the compilation was finished, he was nominated for appointment as Secretary in the Department of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時外廷送算學三百餘員候試，聖祖親策之，得七十二人，陳垿為冠。

translations.literal: At the time the outer court sent over three hundred candidates in mathematics to await examination; the Sagely Ancestor personally examined them—seventy-two passed, and Chenxu ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the outer court sent more than three hundred candidates in mathematics to await examination; the Kangxi Emperor personally tested them, seventy-two passed, and Chenxu ranked first.

sentences.zh: 又充樂館纂修。

translations.literal: He also served as compiler in the Music Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as compiler in the Music Office.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，出使山東、浙江，還督通州倉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng he was dispatched as envoy to Shandong and Zhejiang; returning, he oversaw the Tongzhou granary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongzheng he was dispatched as envoy to Shandong and Zhejiang; on his return he oversaw the Tongzhou granary.

sentences.zh: 三年，以目疾乞歸，閉門撰述，四方走書幣乞文者踵至。

translations.literal: In the third year, on account of eye disease he requested retirement, closed his doors to write, and letter-carriers bearing gifts begging for compositions arrived in unbroken succession from all directions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he pleaded eye disease and retired, shut his doors to write, and messengers bearing letters and gifts begging for compositions arrived in an unbroken stream from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 性耿介，敦於內行。

translations.literal: Upright and uncompromising by nature, strict in private conduct.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and unyielding, strict in his private conduct.

sentences.zh: 居喪不飲酒食肉，不處內。

translations.literal: During mourning he neither drank nor ate meat, and did not enter the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: While in mourning he neither drank nor ate meat and did not enter the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 沈起元官河南，延主大樑書院，引範文正憂中掌學睢陽以勸；

translations.literal: Shen Qiyuan, posted in Henan, invited him to head the Daliang Academy, citing Fan Zhongyan's holding office at the Suiyang Academy while in mourning as encouragement;
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Qiyuan was posted to Henan he invited Chenxu to head the Daliang Academy, citing Fan Zhongyan's directing the Suiyang Academy while still in mourning as encouragement;

sentences.zh: 陳垿執象山責東萊故事，謝不往也。

translations.literal: Chenxu cited the precedent of Lu Jiuyuan's rebuke of Lu Donglai and declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxu invoked the precedent of Lu Jiuyuan's rebuke of Lu Donglai and politely refused.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，詔起官，又舉鴻博，及六年設樂部，復以洞曉音律宣召，皆辭不赴，時論高之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was summoned to office; he was also nominated for the Poet-Laureate examination; in the sixth year, when the Music Bureau was established, he was again summoned for his mastery of pitch and rhythm—all he declined; contemporary opinion held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he was summoned back to office and also nominated for the Poet-Laureate examination; in the sixth year, when the Music Bureau was established, he was again summoned for his mastery of pitch and rhythm—all of which he declined, and contemporary opinion held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 年七十，卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 陳垿精字學、算學、樂律，時稱三絕。

translations.literal: Chenxu was master of philology, mathematics, and music theory—called the Three Unmatched Excellences of his time.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxu mastered philology, mathematics, and music theory, and his contemporaries called these his Three Unmatched Excellences.

sentences.zh: 嘗造八矢注守圖說，謂字學居六藝之末，聲音，樂也，形體，書也，而口出耳入，手運目存，則皆有數焉。

translations.literal: He once wrote Illustrated Explanations of the Eight Arrows Principle, holding that philology stands last among the Six Arts: sound is music, form is writing, yet when the mouth emits and the ear receives, the hand moves and the eye retains—all involve measure.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote Illustrated Explanations of the Eight Arrows Principle, arguing that philology stands last among the Six Arts—sound belongs to music, form belongs to writing—yet when mouth emits and ear receives, hand moves and eye retains, all are governed by number.

sentences.zh: 學士惠士奇、通政孫勷得其書，置酒延陳垿請其說。

translations.literal: Academicians Hui Shiqi and Sun Rang obtained his book, set out wine, and invited Chenxu to explain his theory.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Hui Shiqi and Vice Minister of Communications Sun Rang obtained his book, set out wine, and invited Chenxu to expound his theory.

sentences.zh: 陳垿為言經聲緯音開發收閉之旨，及每矢實義，一矢未​​發，則聲不能出，字有所避，八矢盡而音定字死矣。

translations.literal: Chenxu explained the principles of warp-sounds and woof-sounds, opening, developing, receiving, and closing, and the real meaning of each arrow—until one arrow is released sound cannot emerge; when a character has something to avoid, all eight arrows spent, the sound is fixed and the character dies.
translations.idiomatic: Chenxu explained the principles of warp-sounds and woof-sounds—opening, developing, receiving, and closing—and the real meaning of each arrow: until one arrow is released, sound cannot emerge; when a character must avoid something, all eight arrows are spent, the sound is fixed, and the character is dead.

sentences.zh: 二人嘆為天授。

translations.literal: The two men sighed that this was heaven-endowed talent.
translations.idiomatic: The two men sighed that such talent could only be heaven-endowed.

sentences.zh: 少與同里王時翔為性命交，並工詩。

translations.literal: In youth he and his townsman Wang Shixiang were sworn friends of life and death, both skilled in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he and his townsman Wang Shixiang were sworn friends bound for life and death, and both were accomplished poets.

sentences.zh: 婁東詩人大率宗吳偉業，陳序晚出，乃自闢町畦。

translations.literal: Lou Dong poets mostly followed Wu Weiye; Chen Xu emerged late and carved his own ground.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Dong poets mostly followed Wu Weiye, but Chen Xu emerged later and carved out a path of his own.

sentences.zh: 著洗桐集、抱桐集。

translations.literal: He authored the Xi Tong Collection and the Bao Tong Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Xi Tong Collection and the Bao Tong Collection.

sentences.zh: 何焯，字屺瞻，長洲人。

translations.literal: He Chao, styled Qizhan, was from Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Chao, styled Qizhan, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 通經史百家之學。

translations.literal: He mastered the learning of the Classics, histories, and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in the Classics, histories, and the learning of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 藏書數万卷，得宋、元舊槧，必手加讎校，粲然盈帙。

translations.literal: His library held tens of thousands of volumes; whenever he obtained Song or Yuan old imprints he would personally collate them, and the volumes stood radiant on the shelves.
translations.idiomatic: His library held tens of thousands of volumes; whenever he obtained Song or Yuan old imprints he would personally collate them until the volumes stood radiant and complete on the shelves.

sentences.zh: 學者稱義門先生，傳錄其說為義門讀書記。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Yimen; his teachings were transcribed as Yimen's Reading Notes.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars called him Master Yimen, and his teachings were transcribed as Yimen's Reading Notes.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十一年，直隸巡撫李光地以草澤遺才薦，召入南書房。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Kangxi, Li Guangdi, Governor-General of Zhili, recommended him as a hidden talent from the wilds, and he was summoned into the Southern Studio.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Kangxi, Li Guangdi, Governor-General of Zhili, recommended him as a hidden talent from the wilds, and he was summoned to the Southern Studio.

sentences.zh: 明年，賜舉人，試禮部下第，复賜進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: The next year he was granted provincial graduate status, failed the metropolitan examination at the Ministry of Rites, was then granted jinshi status, and was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was granted provincial graduate status, failed the metropolitan examination at the Ministry of Rites, was then granted jinshi status, and was made a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 仍直南書房，授皇八子讀，兼武英殿纂修。

translations.literal: He continued to serve in the Southern Studio, instructing the Eighth Imperial Son in reading, and also compiled in the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to serve in the Southern Studio, tutoring the Eighth Imperial Son in reading while also compiling in the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 連丁內外艱。

translations.literal: He mourned in succession for both parents.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned in succession for both parents.

sentences.zh: 久之，復以光地薦，召授編修。

translations.literal: After a long interval, on Guangdi's recommendation again, he was summoned and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was again recommended by Guangdi, summoned to court, and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 尚書徐乾學、翁叔元爭延致焯。

translations.literal: Ministers Xu Qianxue and Weng Shuyuan vied to invite He Chao into their households.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xu Qianxue and Minister Weng Shuyuan vied to bring He Chao into their households.

sentences.zh: 尋遘讒，與乾學失歡，而叔元劾湯斌，焯上書請削門下籍，天下快之。

translations.literal: Soon he encountered slander and fell out with Qianxue; when Shuyuan impeached Tang Bin, He Chao submitted a memorial asking to be removed from Shuyuan's roster of disciples, and the realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he encountered slander and fell out with Qianxue; when Shuyuan impeached Tang Bin, He Chao submitted a memorial asking to be struck from Shuyuan's roster of disciples, and people throughout the realm applauded.

sentences.zh: 聖祖幸熱河，或以蜚語上聞，還京即命收系。

translations.literal: When the Sagely Ancestor went to Rehe, slander may have reached him; upon returning to the capital he ordered He Chao seized.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor went to Rehe, slander may have reached his ears; as soon as he returned to the capital he ordered He Chao seized.

sentences.zh: 盡籍其卷冊文字，帝親覽之，曰：「是固讀書種子也！」

translations.literal: All his scrolls and writings were confiscated; the emperor personally examined them and said: "This is truly a seed of learning!"
translations.idiomatic: All his scrolls and writings were confiscated; the emperor read them himself and said, "This is truly a seed of learning!"

sentences.zh: 無失職觖望語，又見其草藁有手簡吳縣令卻金事，益異之。

translations.literal: There was no language of disgruntlement over lost office; moreover he saw in the drafts a personal letter refusing gold from the magistrate of Wu County, and was all the more struck.
translations.idiomatic: There was no language of disgruntlement over lost office; moreover he found among the drafts a personal letter refusing a bribe from the magistrate of Wu County, and was all the more impressed.

sentences.zh: 命還所籍書，解官，仍參書局。

translations.literal: He ordered the confiscated books returned, removed him from office, but still had him participate in the book office.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the confiscated books returned, dismissed He Chao from office, but still had him participate in the book office.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he died, at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year of Kangxi he died, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 帝深悼惜，特贈侍講學士。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned and regretted his loss, specially posthumously granting him the title of Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply mourned his loss and specially posthumously granted him the title of Reader-in-Waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 贈金，給符傳歸喪，命有司存卹其孤。

translations.literal: He bestowed gold, provided travel passes for the return of the coffin, and ordered officials to care for and relieve his orphaned children.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed gold, provided travel passes for the return of the coffin, and ordered officials to care for his orphaned children.

sentences.zh: 焯工楷法，手所校書，人爭傳寶。

translations.literal: He Chao was skilled in regular script; books he collated by hand people competed to treasure.
translations.idiomatic: He Chao excelled in regular script, and books he collated by hand were treasured and passed from hand to hand.

sentences.zh: 門人著錄者四百人，吳江沈彤、吳縣陳景雲為尤著。

translations.literal: Four hundred disciples were recorded; Shen Tong of Wujiang and Chen Jingyun of Wuxian were especially distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred disciples were recorded under his name; Shen Tong of Wujiang and Chen Jingyun of Wuxian were especially distinguished.

sentences.zh: 景雲，字少章。

translations.literal: Jingyun, styled Shaozhang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyun, styled Shaozhang.

sentences.zh: 博聞彊識，能背誦通鑑。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with strong memory, he could recite the Comprehensive Mirror from memory.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned with a formidable memory, he could recite the Comprehensive Mirror from memory.

sentences.zh: 年十七，湯斌撫吳，試士拔第一。

translations.literal: At age seventeen, when Tang Bin governed Wu, he was tested among scholars and ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, when Tang Bin governed Jiangsu, he was tested among local scholars and placed first.

sentences.zh: 應京兆試，不遇。

translations.literal: He sat for the Capital Metropolitan examination but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He took the Capital Metropolitan examination but did not pass.

sentences.zh: 館籓邸三年，以母老辭歸，遂不出，以諸生終。

translations.literal: He served as a retainer in a princely residence for three years, then pleaded his aged mother and returned home; he never went out again and ended his days as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He served three years as a retainer in a princely household, then returned home on grounds of his aged mother and never went out again, ending his days as a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 少從焯遊，焯歿，獨系吳中文獻幾二十年。

translations.literal: From youth he studied with Chao; after Chao died, he alone preserved the literary records of Wu for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied under He Chao; after Chao's death he alone kept the literary tradition of Suzhou alive for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 著有讀書紀聞及綱目、通鑑、兩漢書、三國志、文選、韓、柳集皆有訂誤，共三十餘卷。

translations.literal: He authored Reading Notes and also corrected errors in the Outline and Mirror, the Two Han Histories, the Records of the Three Kingdoms, the Wen Xuan, and the collected works of Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan—more than thirty juan in all.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Reading Notes and textual corrections to the Outline and Mirror, the Two Han Histories, the Records of the Three Kingdoms, the Wen Xuan, and the collected works of Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan—more than thirty juan in all.

sentences.zh: 文集四卷，亦簡嚴有法。

translations.literal: His collected prose in four juan was likewise concise, rigorous, and methodical.
translations.idiomatic: His collected prose in four juan was likewise concise, rigorous, and well ordered.

sentences.zh: 子黃中，字和叔。

translations.literal: His son Huang Zhong, styled Heshu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huang Zhong, courtesy name Heshu.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 父子皆長史學，而黃中尤以才略自負。

translations.literal: Father and son both excelled in historical studies, but Huang Zhong especially prided himself on talent and strategic insight.
translations.idiomatic: Father and son both excelled in historical studies, but Huang Zhong especially prided himself on talent and strategic insight.

sentences.zh: 舉乾隆元年博學鴻詞，入都上書，論用人、理財、治兵三端。

translations.literal: Recommended in the Qianlong 1 Erudite Special Examination, he went to the capital and submitted a memorial discussing three matters: appointing men, managing finances, and governing the military.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for the Qianlong 1 Erudite Special Examination, he went to the capital and submitted a memorial on three matters: appointing men, managing finances, and governing the military.

sentences.zh: 大學士陳世倌韙其言。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Chen Shiguan approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Chen Shiguan endorsed his views.

sentences.zh: 頃之，詔求骨鯁之士，如古馬周、陽城者，世倌欲薦之，謝不應。

translations.literal: Soon an edict sought blunt-spirited men like the ancients Ma Zhou and Yang Cheng; Shiguan wished to recommend him, but he declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict sought blunt-spirited men in the mold of Ma Zhou and Yang Cheng of old; Shiguan wished to recommend him, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 胡天遊傲睨群士，獨推服黃中。

translations.literal: Hu Tianyou looked down on all other scholars but alone acknowledged Huang Zhong's superiority.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tianyou looked down on all other scholars but alone acknowledged Huang Zhong's superiority.

sentences.zh: 示以文，每發其瑕璺，未嘗有忤也。

translations.literal: When he showed him his writings, Tianyou always pointed out their flaws, yet Huang Zhong never took offense.
translations.idiomatic: When he showed Tianyou his writings, Tianyou always pointed out their flaws, yet Huang Zhong never took offense.

sentences.zh: 嘗病宋史蕪雜，別撰紀傳表百七十卷。

translations.literal: Finding the Song History cluttered and diffuse, he separately composed annals, biographies, and tables in one hundred seventy juan.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the Song History cluttered and diffuse, he separately composed annals, biographies, and tables in one hundred seventy juan.

sentences.zh: 又著國朝諡法考、閣部督撫年表。

translations.literal: He also wrote A Study of Posthumous Titles of Our Dynasty and Chronological Tables of Grand Secretaries, Ministries, Governors-General, and Governors.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote A Study of Posthumous Titles of Our Dynasty and Chronological Tables of Grand Secretaries, Ministries, Governors-General, and Governors.

sentences.zh: 其卒也貧不能葬，或賻以金，妻張氏固卻之，曰：「奈何以貧故，傷夫子義！」

translations.literal: When he died he was too poor to bury him; someone offered money for the funeral, but his wife, née Zhang, firmly refused and said: "How can we, because of poverty, wound my husband's integrity!"
translations.idiomatic: When he died they were too poor to bury him; someone offered money for the funeral, but his wife, née Zhang, firmly refused. "How can we," she said, "because of poverty, wound my husband's integrity!"

sentences.zh: 遂賣所居宅以營葬。

translations.literal: She therefore sold their house to arrange the burial.
translations.idiomatic: So she sold their house to arrange the burial.

sentences.zh: 戴名世，字田有，桐城人。

translations.literal: Dai Mingshi, styled Tianyou, was from Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Mingshi, courtesy name Tianyou, was a native of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 生而才辨雋逸，課徒自給。

translations.literal: From birth he was gifted in talent and eloquence; he taught pupils to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: From birth he was gifted with talent and eloquence and supported himself by teaching pupils.

sentences.zh: 以製舉業發名廩生，考得貢，補正藍旗教習。

translations.literal: Through examination essays he became a noted stipend student, qualified as a tribute student, and was appointed instructor in the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Through examination essays he became a noted stipend student, qualified as a tribute student, and was appointed instructor in the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 授知縣，棄去。

translations.literal: He was granted the post of county magistrate but abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered the post of county magistrate but declined it.

sentences.zh: 自是往來燕、趙、齊、魯、河、洛、吳、越之間，賣文為活。

translations.literal: From then on he traveled among Yan, Zhao, Qi, Lu, the Yellow River region, Luoyang, Wu, and Yue, making his living by selling his writing.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he traveled across Yan, Zhao, Qi, Lu, the Yellow River lands, Luoyang, Wu, and Yue, making his living by selling his writing.

sentences.zh: 喜讀太史公書，考求前代奇節瑋行。

translations.literal: He loved reading the Grand Historian's work and sought out the extraordinary integrity and remarkable conduct of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: He loved reading Sima Qian and sought out the extraordinary integrity and remarkable deeds of former ages.

sentences.zh: 時時著文以自抒湮鬱，氣逸發不可控禦。

translations.literal: From time to time he wrote to release his pent-up grief; his spirit surged forth beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time he wrote to release his pent-up grief; his spirit surged forth beyond restraint.

sentences.zh: 諸公貴人畏其口，尤忌嫉之。

translations.literal: Great lords and eminent men feared his tongue and especially envied and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Great lords and eminent men feared his sharp tongue and especially envied and resented him.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇方苞京師，言曰：「吾非役役求有得於時也，吾胸中有書數百卷，其出也，自忖將有異於人人。

translations.literal: Once in the capital he met Fang Bao and said: "I am not busily seeking gain from the age; I have several hundred juan of books in my breast, and when they come forth I reckon they will differ from everyone else's.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital he met Fang Bao and said, "I am not busily seeking gain from the age; I have several hundred juan of books in my breast, and when they come forth I reckon they will differ from everyone else's.

sentences.zh: 然非屏居深山，足衣食，使身無所累，未能誘而出之也。」

translations.literal: Yet unless I withdraw to deep mountains with food and clothing enough and my person free of burdens, I cannot draw them forth."
translations.idiomatic: Yet unless I withdraw to deep mountains with food and clothing enough and my person free of burdens, I cannot draw them forth."

sentences.zh: 因太息別去。

translations.literal: He sighed deeply and parted from him.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed deeply and took his leave.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十八年，年五十七，始中式會試第一，殿試一甲二名及第，授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi, at age fifty-seven, he finally placed first in the metropolitan examination, ranked second in the first class of the palace examination, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-eighth year of Kangxi, at fifty-seven, he finally placed first in the metropolitan examination, ranked second in the first class of the palace examination, and was appointed Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 又二年而南山集禍作。

translations.literal: Two years later the calamity of the Southern Mountain Collection arose.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the calamity of the Southern Mountain Collection erupted.

sentences.zh: 先是門人尤雲鶚刻名世所著南山集，集中有與餘生書，稱明季三王年號，又引及方孝標滇黔紀聞。

translations.literal: Earlier his disciple You Yunhe had printed Mingshi's Southern Mountain Collection; in it was a letter to Yu Sheng that used the reign titles of the three Ming princes of the late dynasty, and it also cited Fang Xiaobiao's Records of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his disciple You Yunhe had printed Mingshi's Southern Mountain Collection; in it was a letter to Yu Sheng that used the reign titles of the three Ming princes of the late dynasty, and it also cited Fang Xiaobiao's Records of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 當是時，文字禁網嚴，都御史趙申喬奏劾南山集語悖逆，遂逮下獄。

translations.literal: At that time the net of literary prohibition was strict; Censor-in-Chief Zhao Shenqiao memorialized that the language of the Southern Mountain Collection was rebellious, and Mingshi was arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time literary prohibitions were severe; Censor-in-Chief Zhao Shenqiao memorialized that the language of the Southern Mountain Collection was rebellious, and Mingshi was arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 孝標已前卒，而苞與之同宗，又序南山集，坐是方氏族人及凡掛名集中者皆獲罪，繫獄兩載。

translations.literal: Xiaobiao had already died earlier, but Bao was of the same clan and had also written a preface to the Southern Mountain Collection; for this the Fang clansmen and all whose names appeared in the collection were punished and imprisoned for two years.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobiao had already died, but Bao was of the same clan and had written a preface to the collection; for this the Fang clansmen and all whose names appeared in it were punished and imprisoned for two years.

sentences.zh: 九卿覆奏，名世、雲鶚俱論死。

translations.literal: The Nine Ministers reported back; Mingshi and Yunhe were both sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers reported back; Mingshi and Yunhe were both sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 親族當連坐，聖祖矜全之。

translations.literal: His kin were liable to collective punishment, but the Sage Emperor showed mercy and spared them.
translations.idiomatic: His kin were liable to collective punishment, but the Kangxi Emperor showed mercy and spared them.

sentences.zh: 又以大學士李光地言，宥苞及其全宗。

translations.literal: On the word of Grand Secretary Li Guangdi, Bao and his entire clan were also pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Secretary Li Guangdi's recommendation, Bao and his entire clan were also pardoned.

sentences.zh: 申喬有清節，惟興此獄獲世譏雲。

translations.literal: Shenqiao had a reputation for integrity, yet for initiating this case he earned the world's reproach.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiao had a reputation for integrity, yet for initiating this case he earned the world's reproach.

sentences.zh: 名世為文善敘事，又著有​​孑遺錄，紀明末桐城兵變事，皆毀禁，後乃始傳云。

translations.literal: Mingshi's writing excelled at narrative; he also authored Records of the Survivors, recounting the military upheaval at Tongcheng at the end of the Ming—all were destroyed and banned, and only later did they begin to circulate.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshi's prose excelled at narrative; he also authored Records of the Survivors, recounting the military upheaval at Tongcheng at the end of the Ming—all were destroyed and banned, and only later did they begin to circulate.
